detail.sensitivity: Most sensitive to how fast utilities and developers can add power and cooling to sites.
detail.statement: Companies now size and cap their AI buildouts by gigawatts of available power, so electricity and site capacity increasingly limit how many accelerators they can actually deploy.
detail.title: Power capacity is becoming the binding limit on AI buildout

detail.falsifiableTrigger: A third co-design vendor wins a major custom-AI-chip program, or the two-firm share falls below 80% within 4 quarters.

detail.sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether hyperscalers build in-house design teams or a third co-design vendor emerges.
detail.statement: Hyperscalers' shift to custom AI chips runs almost entirely through two outside design firms, so the alternative to merchant GPUs is itself concentrated in those two suppliers.
detail.title: The custom-AI-chip alternative depends on two design houses

sensitivity: Most sensitive to when new memory fabrication capacity comes online.

falsifiableTrigger: AMD Data Center revenue growth (D2) stalls below the prior quarter, or its accelerator market-share-pct fails to rise above 7% within 4 quarters.

sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether AMD's rack-scale systems ramp on schedule.

falsifiableTrigger: Custom-ASIC share of AI accelerators (market-share-pct) stops rising above 28%, or ASIC unit growth falls below merchant-GPU growth in a year.

sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether custom chips reach volume production on schedule.

mechanism: Scarce accelerator supply keeps rental and resale prices firm even as new capacity arrives.

sensitivity: Most sensitive to the pace at which new accelerator supply reaches rental markets.

mechanism: US rules block or heavily tax sales of top accelerators to China, so a large slice of demand cannot be served.
rationale: China revenue collapsed to $4,550M from $9,659M with no Hopper shipments and no revenue yet from granted licenses, while a shift to case-by-case review offers only a partial and taxed reopening.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether granted China licenses convert into shipped revenue.

mechanism: NVIDIA lends buying power to small clouds and takes revenue share, so its reported demand partly rests on credit it extends.
rationale: NVIDIA scaled its revenue-sharing and backstop program to about 210,000 GPUs across Firmus and Sharon AI and raised $25B in bonds to fund it, tying more reported demand to credit it extends.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether financed clouds keep paying for and renting the GPUs.

sensitivity: Most sensitive to open Ethernet alternatives from other switch vendors.

falsifiableTrigger: flopsPerDollar fails to improve with Vera Rubin, or inference GPU demand growth stalls quarter over quarter.
mechanism: Each new generation lowers the cost to run a model, which makes more inference jobs worth putting on these GPUs.
rationale: NVIDIA reports its current generation delivers an order-of-magnitude lower cost per inference token with the next generation set to extend that, supporting wider workload pull.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether rival chips cut cost per token faster.

mechanism: Buyers pre-pay billions for memory they cannot cancel, so they are committed to building the accelerators that use it.
rationale: A memory supplier disclosed 16 non-cancelable five-year take-or-pay deals backed by more than $22B, including nearly $18B in cash deposits, hard evidence that future demand is prepaid rather than speculative.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to any cancellation or renegotiation of these prepaid memory deals.

rationale: Buyer interest from Alibaba, ByteDance and DeepSeek grows and mid-tier licensing moved to case-by-case under a sub-50% cap, but shipments stay trivial and China revenue sits at $4,550M with no license revenue yet.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether approved licenses actually turn into shipments.

falsifiableTrigger: AI-server memory and NVMe costs (hbmSupplyCapex) stop rising or fall quarter over quarter as supply catches up.
mechanism: Memory and storage prices are climbing fast, so each AI server costs more to build.
rationale: Memory lead times stretched to 32 to 40-plus weeks with prices up about 90%, rack component costs rising 2 to 3% per week, and memory contract prices doubling, all pushing up server build cost.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to when new memory fabrication capacity comes online.

falsifiableTrigger: Any of the four ramps (releaseCadence) slips past H2 2026, or 2H26 output misses plan.
mechanism: Four major chip makers move their new accelerators into volume around the same time, lifting total supply.
rationale: Multiple sources confirm next-generation accelerators from several vendors moving into volume around the second half of 2026, though AMD's rack-scale system slips its full ramp into 2027.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to manufacturing delays in any single vendor's ramp.

falsifiableTrigger: A single AMD design win (designWins) accounts for over 25% of DC GPU revenue, or a named mega-deal is canceled within 4 quarters.
mechanism: A few very large customer commitments make up most of AMD's accelerator growth, so its fortunes ride on those partners.
rationale: AMD's growth leans on a Meta commitment of up to 6 gigawatts, a Rackspace deal and a projected single-product line worth about a quarter of data-center sales, concentrating upside in a few partners.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to any single named mega-deal being canceled or delayed.

falsifiableTrigger: Crescent Island sampling (releaseCadence) slips past 2H 2026, or LPDDR5X inference parts fail to reach volume within 4 quarters.
mechanism: Using standard memory instead of scarce high-bandwidth memory lets an inference chip skip the packaging queue.
rationale: Intel's Crescent Island inference GPU using standard memory instead of high-bandwidth memory stays on track for second-half 2026 sampling, keeping the alternative supply route open.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the standard-memory parts reach volume.

falsifiableTrigger: TSMC gross margin (grossMargin) falls quarter over quarter, or CoWoS drops below full booking in 2026.
mechanism: AI orders across many chip types keep TSMC's factories full, giving it room to raise prices.
rationale: TSMC lifted gross margin to 67.7%, raised full-year revenue guidance above 40% and increased capex, with AI demand broadening across many chip types keeping capacity full.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to any broad slowdown in AI chip orders.

falsifiableTrigger: Hyperscaler 2026 capex guidance (hyperscalerCapexRevision) is cut quarter over quarter, or a top hyperscaler announces an AI capex reduction.
mechanism: Hyperscalers spend far ahead of AI revenue, so weak returns could trigger a spending cut that hits chip orders.
rationale: Hyperscaler capex is being revised up toward roughly $725B for 2026 with Meta sizing multi-gigawatt buildouts, even as fresh analyst doubt calls the spending possibly unsustainable, keeping the pullback risk live but untriggered.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to visible returns on AI investment.

falsifiableTrigger: NVIDIA non-GAAP gross margin (grossMargin) falls below 70% in a quarter during the Rubin ramp.
mechanism: Buyers keep paying premium prices, so NVIDIA holds its margin near three-quarters even while launching new chips.
rationale: NVIDIA reported non-GAAP gross margin of 75.0% and guided the next quarter to the same level, far above AMD's 55%, showing buyers still pay premium prices during a ramp.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to margin dilution during the Rubin production ramp.

falsifiableTrigger: Top-three CoWoS customerConcentration falls below 85%, or a fourth buyer takes double-digit share within 4 quarters.
mechanism: Three buyers take most of TSMC's advanced-packaging output, so one cutting orders would leave capacity hard to refill.
rationale: Fresh figures put the top three packaging clients above 85% of TSMC output, with NVIDIA near 60% and AMD near 11%, confirming extreme buyer concentration.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether a fourth large buyer enters packaging.

falsifiableTrigger: Contracted backlog value (rpoBacklog) shrinks quarter over quarter, or new commitments shorten below one year.
mechanism: Buyers sign multi-year purchase deals, so more compute demand is locked in years ahead.
rationale: Multi-year deals keep lengthening: five-year memory take-or-pay contracts, a CoreWeave backlog jumping to $99.4B including a Meta deal running to 2032, and a Broadcom backlog of $73B.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to any cancellation or shortening of these long contracts.

falsifiableTrigger: A leading model provider reports revenue (apiArr) growth stalling quarter over quarter while compute commitments keep growing.
mechanism: Model makers commit to heavy compute, but this cycle offers little proof their sales are rising to match.
rationale: Model makers keep locking in long-term compute but this cycle shows no revenue figures proving their sales rise to match, and fresh doubt warns the spending may be unsustainable.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether model providers disclose rising paid revenue.

falsifiableTrigger: A flagship Chinese model still needs smuggled NVIDIA GPUs (exportControlExposure), or domestic-ASIC clusters fail to scale past 50,000 chips within 4 quarters.
mechanism: Chinese chips now train frontier-scale models, cutting the need for imported NVIDIA GPUs.
rationale: A Chinese lab pretrained a 1.6-trillion-parameter model on more than 50,000 domestic non-NVIDIA accelerators, a frontier-scale demonstration that cuts the need for imported GPUs.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether domestic chips overcome memory and software limits at scale.

falsifiableTrigger: A major neocloud posts a net profit, or its contracted backlog (rpoBacklog) falls quarter over quarter.
mechanism: Neoclouds book fast-rising revenue but spend even more on GPUs and debt, so their losses grow.
rationale: CoreWeave revenue grew about 168% to $5.1B while its net loss widened to $1.2B and its backlog climbed to $99.4B, the pattern of rising sales and deeper losses in hard numbers.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether these firms can turn backlog into profit.

falsifiableTrigger: AI buildouts stop being sized in gigawatts, or planned power capacity growth stalls for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Companies plan and cap their AI sites by available power, so electricity limits how many chips they can install.
rationale: Buildouts are consistently sized in power terms this cycle, from Meta's 7-gigawatt 2026 plan to named projects at 140 and 360 megawatts, showing electricity increasingly frames deployment scale.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to the pace of new power and grid capacity.

falsifiableTrigger: A third co-design vendor wins a major custom-AI-chip program, or the two-firm share falls below 80% within 4 quarters.
mechanism: Nearly all hyperscaler custom chips are designed by just two firms, so the merchant-GPU alternative is itself concentrated.
rationale: Two firms still hold an estimated 95% of custom AI chip co-design, and an early-stage Anthropic-Samsung talk is not yet a competing win, so the alternative to merchant GPUs stays concentrated.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to a third design house winning a major program.

falsifiableTrigger: B200 rpoBacklog falls below 2M units for two consecutive quarters
mechanism: Customers order far more NVIDIA GPUs than the company can build, so backlogs stretch out and cloud rental supply stays scarce.
rationale: Record DC revenue up 92% year-over-year, Q2 guide of $91B, a B200 backlog of ~3.6M units, and near-zero H100 availability all show orders still exceed what NVIDIA can ship.
sensitivity: Would weaken if backlog shrinks or DC revenue growth stalls quarter over quarter.

falsifiableTrigger: HBM leadTimes ease to available-on-demand before end of the 2027 supply window
mechanism: Memory makers cannot produce enough high-bandwidth memory, so the shortage of that chip, not packaging, sets the ceiling on how many GPUs sell.
rationale: Findings confirm both clauses precisely: CoWoS packaging gap narrows ~20% to ~10% by end-2026 while HBM3E/HBM4 stay sold out through 2027 and Micron caps GPU availability on supply not demand.
sensitivity: Would break if HBM supply catches demand while packaging tightens instead.

falsifiableTrigger: AMD accelerator market-share-pct fails to rise above 7% through 2027
mechanism: Large buyers place real Instinct orders with AMD, so its datacenter revenue climbs even while its overall share stays small.
rationale: AMD lands Meta (up to 6GW), OpenAI, and Rackspace design wins with DC-GPU revenue up ~114% to ~$15B, though its accelerator share is still only ~5-7% versus NVIDIA's ~80%.
sensitivity: Would weaken if MI400/MI455 slips further or Meta and OpenAI commitments shrink.

falsifiableTrigger: ASIC market-share-pct growth falls back below GPU growth for two consecutive quarters
mechanism: Hyperscalers build their own inference chips and route more internal work onto them, trimming the growth of merchant GPU orders.
rationale: Custom ASIC shipments grow 44.6% versus GPU's 16.1%, custom silicon already ~two-thirds of AI compute, and ASIC is forecast to surpass GPU by 2028, though these chips stay captive and GPUs still hold ~60% of AWS builds.
sensitivity: Would weaken if custom silicon stays captive and merchant-GPU share holds.

falsifiableTrigger: gpuSpotPrice for H100 or GB200 drops more than 20% within a quarter
mechanism: Scarce GPU supply and NVIDIA's dominant share let cloud providers hold rental prices firm despite new capacity coming online.
rationale: GB200 rents at ~$10.50/GPU/hr and H100 holds ~$2-11/GPU-hr with NVIDIA at ~70-80% share underpinning pricing, showing rental levels have not cracked.
sensitivity: Would weaken if 2H-2026 supply wave pushes spot rents down sharply.

falsifiableTrigger: exportControlExposure eases so China DC revenue recovers above prior levels within two quarters
mechanism: US rules block most advanced GPUs from China, so a large slice of potential demand cannot legally be served.
rationale: NVIDIA China revenue halved to $4,550M with no DC Hopper shipped and Blackwell banned, and AMD took ~$440M in charges, showing controls still bind even as case-by-case H200 licenses hint at partial relief.
sensitivity: Would weaken if broad H200 licenses restore China revenue.

falsifiableTrigger: Vendor-financed GPU commitments in rpoBacklog exceed 300,000 units within two quarters
mechanism: NVIDIA lends or guarantees money to clouds that then spend it buying NVIDIA chips, so part of its demand rests on its own financing.
rationale: NVIDIA launched a revenue-sharing/credit-support model and now backstops ~210K GPUs across Firmus and Sharon AI on top of CoreWeave and Lambda deals, raising $25B in bonds, deepening the circular-financing concern.
sensitivity: Would weaken if NVIDIA winds down backstops and neoclouds self-fund.

falsifiableTrigger: customerConcentration for the top three direct customers falls below prior shares next fiscal year
mechanism: A handful of big buyers account for a rising share of NVIDIA sales, so losing one would dent revenue heavily.
rationale: Three direct customers made up 21%, 17%, and 16% of Q1FY27 revenue, and for FY2026 one hit 22% and another 14%, up from prior 12/11/11%, with the top four exceeding half of revenue.
sensitivity: Would weaken if the buyer base broadens and top-customer shares fall.

falsifiableTrigger: NVIDIA DC Ethernet switch market-share-pct slips from #1 within two quarters
mechanism: NVIDIA sells its switches packaged with its GPUs, so buying the chips pulls in the networking and locks customers into its full system.
rationale: NVIDIA became the #1 datacenter Ethernet switch vendor by revenue in Q1 2026 with Spectrum-X and Quantum bundled alongside Blackwell and GB300, extending the systems moat beyond prior reaffirmation.
sensitivity: Would weaken if rivals win back switching share or bundling unwinds.

falsifiableTrigger: Cost-per-token gains stall so tokenEconomics improves less than one generation cycle
mechanism: Each new NVIDIA generation makes a token cheaper to compute, so more inference work becomes affordable and lands on its GPUs.
rationale: Grace Blackwell cuts cost per token by an order of magnitude with Vera Rubin extending the lead and delivering up to 10x performance per megawatt, while inference costs broadly fell 30-50% per year.
sensitivity: Would weaken if per-token cost gains flatten or shift to rival chips.

falsifiableTrigger: Prepaid HBM commitments in rpoBacklog shrink or deposits are refunded within a quarter
mechanism: Buyers pay billions of non-refundable deposits for years of HBM, so the accelerators that memory feeds are effectively pre-committed.
rationale: Micron signed 16 non-cancelable five-year take-or-pay HBM deals backed by over $22B cash (~$18B deposits) and HBM is sold out under non-cancellable contracts, while NVIDIA's total supply commitments reached $145B.
sensitivity: Would weaken if take-or-pay deals are renegotiated or deposits fall.

falsifiableTrigger: exportControlExposure changes lift the sub-50% China cap or clear Blackwell within two quarters
mechanism: Washington allows only certain older chips into China through individual permits capped below half of US sales, so any reopening stays partial.
rationale: BIS moved H200/MI325X-class to case-by-case with a 25% tariff and a sub-50% cap, China signaled Alibaba/ByteDance/DeepSeek may buy H200, ~$10B in licenses were approved, but Blackwell stays banned and licenses show no revenue yet.
sensitivity: Would break if full reopening or a higher cap is granted.

falsifiableTrigger: AMD or non-NVIDIA designWins in production inference keep expanding for two consecutive quarters
mechanism: Rival software stacks now run popular AI models well enough that some customers move workloads off NVIDIA despite CUDA's head start.
rationale: AMD's ROCm GEAK kernel lifted DeepSeek-V4 throughput 2.10x and cut time-to-first-token 3.71x on MI355, AMD claims 33% lower TCO than B200, and Chinese labs plus Meituan ran large models off non-NVIDIA chips, chipping at software lock-in.
sensitivity: Would reaffirm if rival stacks stall and customers stay on CUDA.

falsifiableTrigger: Memory hbmSupplyCapex expansion pulls DRAM/NVMe prices down within two quarters
mechanism: Scarce, pricier memory and NVMe raise what it costs to build each AI server, squeezing buyer budgets and vendor margins.
rationale: Memory lead times run 32-40+ weeks with prices up 90% since late 2025, AI-server rack costs rise 2-3% per week (10-15% above baseline), HBM4 prices are set to double into 2027, and GDDR6 spot tripled.
sensitivity: Would weaken if new memory capacity cuts prices in late 2026.

falsifiableTrigger: releaseCadence slips push a major vendor's 2H-2026 ramp into 2027
mechanism: Several vendors ramp new accelerators in the same half-year, so total available AI compute supply jumps in 2H 2026.
rationale: Vera Rubin, AMD Helios, Trainium 3, and Google TPU are cited as reaching mass production together in 2H26, with Vera Rubin ramping Q3 2026, AMD MI450 in H2 2026, and Meta MTIA production in September 2026.
sensitivity: Would weaken if manufacturing delays stagger the ramps.

falsifiableTrigger: AMD customerConcentration eases as its buyer base broadens over the next two quarters
mechanism: A few very large customer commitments drive most of AMD's datacenter accelerator growth, so any single cancellation hits hard.
rationale: AMD's growth rides Meta's up-to-6GW commitment, OpenAI interest, and MI400 alone at ~$7.2B, while AMD itself warns of continued dependence on a small number of customers.
sensitivity: Would weaken if AMD wins many mid-size customers and reduces reliance on mega-deals.

falsifiableTrigger: Crescent Island releaseCadence slips its customer sampling past the 2H 2026 quarter
mechanism: Intel builds an inference chip on cheaper standard memory, so it sidesteps the packaging and HBM shortages that gate rival GPUs.
rationale: Intel Crescent Island uses up to 480GB LPDDR5X instead of HBM specifically to avoid packaging and HBM contention, with customer sampling guided to 2H 2026.
sensitivity: Would weaken if the part slips badly or fails to reach volume.

falsifiableTrigger: TSMC grossMargin declines for two consecutive quarters as capacity loosens
mechanism: AI orders from many chip types fill TSMC's factories, so it stays sold out and can charge more, lifting its margins.
rationale: AI demand spreading into ASICs, networking, and PMICs tightens TSMC across nodes, and TSMC posted 67.7% gross margin (+9.1pp), +36% revenue, a raised >40% FY growth guide, and $60-64B capex.
sensitivity: Would weaken if AI order breadth narrows and TSMC utilization drops.

falsifiableTrigger: A hyperscalerCapexRevision cuts 2026 or 2027 AI capex guidance within two quarters
mechanism: Cloud giants spend far ahead of proven AI returns, so if payoffs disappoint they can cut orders sharply and hit chip suppliers.
rationale: Hyperscaler capex jumped 77% to ~$725B, early-July sentiment turned to doubt calling the jump possibly unsustainable, and chip stocks fell on AI-spending jitters July 16, making the pullback risk more visible.
sensitivity: Would weaken if returns evidence firms and capex guides hold or rise.

falsifiableTrigger: NVIDIA grossMargin guidance drops below 70% in a coming quarter
mechanism: Strong pricing and mix let NVIDIA keep about 75 cents of gross profit per revenue dollar even while launching new products.
rationale: NVIDIA reported Q1FY27 non-GAAP gross margin of 75.0% and guided Q2 to the same, holding near three-quarters through the Blackwell and Vera Rubin ramps.
sensitivity: Would weaken if new-product ramp costs or rising memory prices compress margin.

falsifiableTrigger: Top-buyer customerConcentration in CoWoS output falls below 85% within a year
mechanism: A handful of buyers reserve nearly all of TSMC's advanced-packaging lines, so smaller players are largely shut out of that supply.
rationale: The top three CoWoS clients take over 85% of TSMC output, with NVIDIA alone at ~60% (~595K wafers) and AMD ~11%, confirming a tight concentration of advanced packaging.
sensitivity: Would weaken if new packaging capacity spreads output across more buyers.

falsifiableTrigger: Aggregate rpoBacklog duration shortens as new commitments turn shorter-dated over two quarters
mechanism: Buyers and suppliers sign multi-year commitments, so order books now stretch several years into the future.
rationale: Micron signed five-year take-or-pay deals, CoreWeave's backlog rose to $99.4B including a $21B Meta commitment through 2032, Broadcom holds a $73B AI backlog, and CoWoS is booked through 2027.
sensitivity: Would weaken if buyers shift to shorter contracts or backlogs shrink.

falsifiableTrigger: apiArr growth at a leading model provider stalls or reverses over two quarters
mechanism: Top model makers grow paid usage revenue rapidly, so the money funding GPU buildouts increasingly rests on real customer sales.
rationale: Anthropic reached $30B+ ARR (from $1B in Jan 2025) and OpenAI hit $25B, with Anthropic's Claude now generally available in Azure, showing model-provider revenue scaling fast enough to back compute spend and reversing the prior weakened read.
sensitivity: Would weaken if ARR growth flattens or churn rises.

falsifiableTrigger: Chinese domestic accelerator designWins for frontier training stall over the next two quarters
mechanism: Chinese firms train frontier-scale models on home-built accelerators, so banned NVIDIA GPUs lose some of the demand they would have served.
rationale: Meituan trained the 1.6-trillion-parameter LongCat-2.0 on over 50,000 domestic non-NVIDIA accelerators using 35T tokens, a concrete large-model training run without NVIDIA chips, while Chinese custom ASICs remain more than two years out.
sensitivity: Would weaken if domestic training runs prove one-off or performance lags badly.

falsifiableTrigger: A neocloud's marginalBuyerFinancing debt load or net loss narrows for two consecutive quarters
mechanism: Neoclouds book fast-rising GPU rental revenue but borrow heavily and spend more than they earn, so losses and debt keep growing.
rationale: CoreWeave revenue grew 168% to $5.1B while net loss widened from $937M to $1.2B, and its debt reached $24.86B against $3.5B equity (5.4:1), up 16.1% in one quarter.
sensitivity: Would weaken if neoclouds reach profitability or deleverage.

falsifiableTrigger: A top hyperscaler cuts its 2027 gigawatt power target below its 2026 level
mechanism: Companies plan AI capacity around available electricity in gigawatts, so power supply, not chips, increasingly sets how big a buildout can be.
rationale: Buildouts are sized in gigawatts and megawatts, with Meta at 7GW for 2026 doubling in 2027, Firmus at 360MW for 170K GPUs, Japan's factory at 140MW, and new systems touted for 10x performance per megawatt.
sensitivity: Would weaken if power procurement stops gating expansion plans.

falsifiableTrigger: Broadcom-plus-Marvell market-share-pct of custom ASIC co-design falls below 90% within a year
mechanism: Nearly all hyperscaler custom chips are co-designed by just two firms, so the custom-silicon path funnels through Broadcom and Marvell.
rationale: Broadcom and Marvell hold ~95% of the custom AI ASIC co-design market and Broadcom's $73B backlog targets $100B by 2027, though Anthropic's early talks with Samsung hint at slight diversification.
sensitivity: Would weaken if new design houses like Samsung win meaningful custom-chip work.

detail.mechanism: Hyperscalers pull AI-server and networking gear through contract makers like Wistron, so their record monthly sales show the buildout is shipping, not just booked.

falsifiableTrigger: B200 rpoBacklog falls below 2M units for two consecutive quarters.

rationale: Data-center revenue hit a record $75.2B up 92% with Q2 guided to $91B, a B200 backlog near 3.6M units, and memory plus packaging still capping what can ship.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to a sudden loosening of high-bandwidth memory and advanced-packaging supply.

falsifiableTrigger: HBM leadTimes ease to available-on-demand before the end of the 2027 supply window.
mechanism: Memory makers cannot add high-bandwidth output fast enough, so memory now sets the ceiling on how many accelerators vendors can finish.
rationale: Memory stays sold out through 2027 while packaging expands as the TSMC gap narrows toward 10% and ASE and Hanmi add capacity, matching the standing claim even though TSMC still calls packaging very tight.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to the pace of new high-bandwidth memory fab capacity coming online.

falsifiableTrigger: AMD accelerator market-share-pct fails to rise above 7% through 2027.
mechanism: Large buyers place multi-gigawatt Instinct orders to secure a second supplier, turning roadmap promises into booked datacenter volume.
rationale: AMD locked gigawatt-scale commitments from Microsoft, OpenAI, Meta and Oracle and grew data-center revenue 57%, though its accelerator share still sits at only 5-7%.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the mega-deal commitments convert into shipped revenue on schedule.

falsifiableTrigger: ASIC market-share-pct growth falls back below GPU growth for two consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Hyperscalers move steady inference work onto their own chips, taking growth that would otherwise go to merchant GPUs.
rationale: Forecasts put custom-chip growth at 44.6% versus 16.1% for merchant GPUs, custom silicon already runs about two-thirds of AI compute, Meta's MTIA enters production, and Broadcom carries a $73B backlog.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to how much inference volume hyperscalers can move onto captive silicon.

falsifiableTrigger: gpuSpotPrice for H100 or GB200 drops more than 20% within a quarter.
mechanism: Demand keeps rented GPUs fully booked, so cloud operators hold or raise hourly rates even as new capacity arrives.

rationale: H100 rental prices are up 24% from their late-2025 low and top-end GB200 and B200 rentals hold firm, so added supply has not cracked pricing.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to the speed at which new rental capacity outruns rental demand.

falsifiableTrigger: exportControlExposure eases so China DC revenue recovers above prior levels within two quarters.
mechanism: Policy blocks the top China products and licenses, so a large share of would-be demand cannot be served.

rationale: NVIDIA scaled a revenue-share and rent-back program backing about 210,000 GPUs at Firmus and Sharon AI, funded by a $25B bond raise, tightening the loop between its own credit and reported demand.

falsifiableTrigger: customerConcentration for the top three direct customers falls below prior shares next fiscal year.
mechanism: A handful of buyers drive most sales, so one of them slowing orders would dent revenue sharply.

falsifiableTrigger: NVIDIA DC Ethernet switch market-share-pct slips from #1 within two quarters.
mechanism: Selling networking bundled with GPUs raises the cost of switching away, deepening a full-system lock-in.
rationale: NVIDIA took the top spot in data-center Ethernet switching by pairing its networking with Blackwell and is adding optical products, but no finding compares networking growth to compute, so the standing caveat still holds.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether buyers adopt standalone networking from rivals.

falsifiableTrigger: Cost-per-token gains stall so tokenEconomics improves less than one generation cycle.
mechanism: Each generation lowers the cost to run a model, so more use cases become affordable and land on NVIDIA hardware.
rationale: Inference token costs are falling sharply each year and NVIDIA cites an order-of-magnitude lower cost per token with its newest systems, widening the workloads that pay off on its GPUs.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether each new chip generation keeps cutting cost per token.

falsifiableTrigger: Prepaid HBM commitments in rpoBacklog shrink or deposits are refunded within a quarter.
mechanism: Buyers put billions of non-refundable cash behind multi-year memory contracts, so much of the buildout is committed rather than speculative.

sensitivity: Most sensitive to any customer walking away from a prepaid memory contract.

sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether Chinese buyers actually take delivery under the granted licenses.

sensitivity: Most sensitive to when new memory capacity arrives to relieve prices.

sensitivity: Most sensitive to any one mega-partner delaying or shrinking its order.

sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the standard-memory design performs well enough to win real workloads.

mechanism: Demand across many chip categories keeps TSMC's lines full, giving it room to raise prices and hold high margins.
rationale: TSMC lifted its gross margin to 67.7% and raised full-year revenue guidance above 40% as AI demand spreads across chip types and fills capacity, with packaging so tight it limits customer growth.

rationale: Fresh market doubt about AI-spending returns pressured chip stocks even as hyperscalers keep raising capex, so the risk of a future pullback stands without yet materializing.

falsifiableTrigger: NVIDIA grossMargin guidance drops below 70% in a coming quarter.
mechanism: Buyers keep paying premium prices, so margins stay near three-quarters even during a product ramp.
rationale: NVIDIA held a 75% gross margin this quarter and guided the next quarter to the same level, far above AMD's mid-50s, while ramping new products.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to competitive pricing pressure and the cost of ramping new chips.

falsifiableTrigger: Top-buyer customerConcentration in CoWoS output falls below 85% within a year.
mechanism: A few buyers hold most packaging slots, so one of them cutting orders leaves capacity that is hard to refill quickly.
rationale: The top three packaging clients take over 85% of TSMC's output with NVIDIA alone near 60%, concentrating scarce advanced-packaging supply in a few buyers.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether any dominant packaging buyer scales back orders.

falsifiableTrigger: Aggregate rpoBacklog duration shortens as new commitments turn shorter-dated over two quarters.
mechanism: Buyers sign longer-dated commitments, so a growing share of compute demand is locked in years ahead.
rationale: Micron signed five-year memory deals, CoreWeave's backlog reached $99.4B with a Meta commitment running to 2032, and Broadcom carries a multi-year AI backlog, pushing order books further into the future.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to buyers shifting back toward shorter contracts.

falsifiableTrigger: A leading model provider reports revenue (apiArr) growth stalling quarter over quarter while compute commitments keep growing.
mechanism: Model providers earn fast-growing subscription and API sales that pay for the compute they contract, rather than spending on hope.
rationale: Anthropic's revenue reached $30B-plus, up thirtyfold in fifteen months, with Claude now in production on NVIDIA hardware in Azure, showing model-provider sales rising fast behind their compute spending.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether model-provider revenue keeps outgrowing their compute bills.

falsifiableTrigger: Chinese domestic accelerator designWins for frontier training stall over the next two quarters.
mechanism: Chinese firms train large models on domestic chips, reducing the country's need for imported GPUs.
rationale: Meituan trained a 1.6-trillion-parameter model on roughly 50,000 domestic accelerators with no NVIDIA chips, and Chinese labs are building custom silicon, showing home-grown hardware starting to train frontier models.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to how fast domestic chips and their software close the capability gap.

falsifiableTrigger: A neocloud's marginalBuyerFinancing debt load or net loss narrows for two consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Neoclouds book record sales but spend even faster on debt-funded GPUs, so losses widen alongside revenue.
rationale: CoreWeave's revenue grew about 168% to $5.1B while its net loss widened to $1.2B and its debt kept climbing, matching the pattern of fast growth with deepening losses.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether these buyers can turn revenue growth into positive cash flow.

falsifiableTrigger: A top hyperscaler cuts its 2027 gigawatt power target below its 2026 level.
mechanism: Firms plan buildouts around available electricity, so power and grid gear increasingly cap how many accelerators can be deployed.
rationale: Forecasts see 40% of AI datacenters power-constrained by 2027, buyers now size projects in gigawatts and megawatts, and power-transformer lead times run about 128 weeks.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to how fast new power and grid infrastructure comes online.

falsifiableTrigger: Broadcom-plus-Marvell market-share-pct of custom ASIC co-design falls below 90% within a year.
mechanism: Nearly all hyperscaler custom chips are designed by two outside houses, so the merchant-GPU alternative is itself narrowly sourced.
rationale: Broadcom and Marvell together still hold about 95% of custom AI chip co-design, so the alternative to merchant GPUs remains concentrated in two firms.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to new design houses entering custom-silicon work.

falsifiableTrigger: Wistron odmMonthlyAiRevenue falls year-over-year for two consecutive months.
mechanism: Contract server makers only book record revenue when AI systems physically ship, so their sales confirm real deliveries.
rationale: Wistron posted record June revenue up 53.9% on AI-server and networking shipments as suppliers report an order boom spilling into the second half of 2026, confirming volume is actually shipping.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to the flow of hyperscaler server orders into contract makers.

falsifiableTrigger: A neocloud's marginalBuyerFinancing debt-to-equity rises above 6:1 within two quarters.
mechanism: Neoclouds borrow heavily to buy GPUs, leaving little equity cushion if revenue or asset values fall.
rationale: CoreWeave carries $18.81B of debt against $3.5B of equity, a 5.4:1 ratio with total debt up 16% in a quarter, confirming these operators fund fleets mostly with debt on thin equity.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to lenders' willingness to keep funding GPU purchases.

detail.falsifiableTrigger: Co-packaged optics adoption stalls below 5% of AI optical modules through 2027.
detail.mechanism: Faster optical links let clusters scale, so whoever controls the new optics supply shapes how quickly big systems can be built.
detail.sensitivity: Most sensitive to how fast co-packaged optics yields and volumes ramp.
detail.statement: The move to co-packaged optics is reshaping how AI networking gear is built and supplied, tying cluster wiring to a fast-changing optics roadmap.
detail.title: Optical networking shifts to co-packaged optics as a supply lever

detail.falsifiableTrigger: A named US fab or packaging project slips its build milestone past 2027.
detail.mechanism: New US fabs and packaging plants add a second geography for accelerator supply, easing reliance on a single region over time.
detail.sensitivity: Most sensitive to construction timelines and whether US capacity comes online as planned.
detail.statement: NVIDIA and its partners are committing to build AI hardware inside the United States at very large scale, adding fabrication and packaging capacity outside Taiwan.
detail.title: US onshoring broadens the AI hardware supply base

falsifiableTrigger: B200 rpoBacklog falls below 2 million units for two consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Buyers order accelerators years ahead while packaging and memory limit output, so orders keep sitting above what NVIDIA can deliver.
rationale: NVIDIA data-center revenue hit a record $75.2B, up 92% year over year, with next-quarter guidance of $91B, a B200 order book of about 3.6 million units, and named Rubin buildouts in Japan, Indonesia and across major clouds, while packaging and memory still cap what can ship.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to hyperscaler capital-spending plans holding at current levels.

falsifiableTrigger: HBM leadTimes ease to available-on-demand and CoWoS lead times fall below 26 weeks before the end of 2027.
mechanism: Accelerators need both stacked memory and advanced packaging slots, so whichever of the two is scarcer sets the ceiling on how many units vendors can book.
note: supply-constraint-binding: applied: corroborated secondary reversal (8 distinct publishers; pending filing checkpoint)
rationale: Memory is still sold out through 2027, but packaging did not ease as expected: TSMC says advanced packaging is fully booked through 2027 with 52-78 week lead times and calls the demand gap very big through 2029-2030, so packaging remains a hard cap alongside memory rather than a loosening one.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the CoWoS ramp to 125,000-130,000 wafers a month lands on schedule.

falsifiableTrigger: AMD accelerator market-share-pct fails to rise above 7% through 2027.
mechanism: Buyers short of NVIDIA supply sign large multi-year commitments with AMD, which turns its roadmap into shipped share.
rationale: AMD data-center revenue reached $5.78B, up 57% year over year, with gigawatt-scale commitments from Microsoft, OpenAI, Meta and Oracle, a new Anthropic deal for up to 2 gigawatts of MI450, and Helios racks shipping to customers in the second half of 2026.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to AMD's thin share of advanced packaging, which it must split between its server CPUs and its accelerators.

falsifiableTrigger: ASIC market-share-pct growth falls back below GPU growth for two consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Hyperscalers building their own inference chips serve internal workloads with silicon they control instead of buying merchant GPUs.
rationale: Custom chips are forecast to grow 44.6% in 2026 against 16.1% for merchant GPUs and to reach 27.8% of AI servers, Meta puts four new in-house accelerators into production in September 2026, and custom silicon reportedly already consumes about two-thirds of AI compute.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to the fact that in-house chips stay captive to their makers and cannot be rented out, which limits how far they displace merchant demand.

falsifiableTrigger: gpuSpotPrice for H100 or GB200 drops more than 20% within a quarter.
mechanism: New capacity arrives slower than rental demand grows, so hourly prices stay firm instead of falling as fleets expand.
rationale: Rental prices held or rose: median H100 on-demand is $3.85 an hour with GPU prices up 24% from the November 2025 low, Lambda lists H100 at $3.99 and B200 at $6.69, and CoreWeave charges $10.50 per GPU-hour for GB200, with H100 availability extremely low.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to the second-half 2026 wave of new accelerators landing all at once and loosening rental supply.

falsifiableTrigger: exportControlExposure eases so China DC revenue recovers above prior levels within two quarters.
mechanism: Licence rules, tariffs and enforcement keep the largest non-US buying pool from taking delivery, so a big slice of willing demand never becomes revenue.
rationale: China data-center compute stayed effectively closed: NVIDIA China revenue fell to $4,550M from $9,659M, no Hopper data-center shipments occurred, H200 licenses granted since February have booked no revenue, shipments are called trivial, Blackwell is still banned, and NVIDIA more than halved its list of authorised Asian buyers.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the case-by-case H200 licences start converting into actual shipments.

falsifiableTrigger: Vendor-financed GPU commitments in rpoBacklog exceed 300,000 units within two quarters.
mechanism: When the chip seller supplies the money and guarantees the rent, reported orders partly reflect its own credit rather than independent buyer budgets.
rationale: NVIDIA raised $25B in bonds on June 15 2026 to scale a revenue-share and backstop programme now covering roughly 210,000 GPUs at Firmus and Sharon AI after CoreWeave and Lambda support deals, and AMD committed up to $5B of equity to Anthropic alongside its compute deal, so a second vendor now finances its own customer.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to how much of total bookings these backstopped buyers represent, still small next to the 3.6 million unit B200 book.

falsifiableTrigger: customerConcentration for the top three direct customers falls below prior shares next fiscal year.
mechanism: A handful of buyers place most of the orders, so one of them slowing or switching to its own chips removes a large block of revenue at once.
rationale: Three direct NVIDIA customers were 21%, 17% and 16% of revenue in Q1 FY2027, and in FY2026 one customer was 22% and another 14% with the top four above half of revenue, while the vendor-financing programme may add further concentration in a few neoclouds.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to broadening into enterprise, sovereign and neocloud buyers such as the Japan and Indonesia projects.

falsifiableTrigger: NVIDIA DC Ethernet switch market-share-pct slips from #1 within two quarters.
mechanism: Selling switches, links and accelerators as one rack makes swapping in another vendor's chip a whole-system change rather than a part swap.
rationale: NVIDIA took the top revenue spot in data-center Ethernet switching in Q1 2026 on Spectrum-X and Quantum sold with Blackwell and GB300, and its rack systems keep cutting cost per token, but no finding compares networking growth with compute growth, so the stronger claim stays unsupported.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to rival rack-scale systems such as AMD's Helios landing at the same customers.

falsifiableTrigger: Cost-per-token gains stall so tokenEconomics improves less than one generation cycle.
mechanism: Each generation cuts the cost of serving a token, which makes uses that were too expensive worth running and enlarges total demand.
rationale: NVIDIA says Vera Rubin reaches one-tenth the cost per million tokens versus the prior generation and 10x more throughput per megawatt, an enterprise buyer cites up to 10x performance per megawatt versus the gear it replaces, and open-source inference costs have fallen 30-50% a year since 2023.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the claimed gains, largely vendor-stated, hold in independent customer measurements.

falsifiableTrigger: Prepaid HBM commitments in rpoBacklog shrink or deposits are refunded within a quarter.
mechanism: Buyers who pay cash up front and cannot cancel have already committed to the accelerators that memory will go into.
rationale: Micron holds 16 non-cancelable five-year take-or-pay agreements backed by more than $22B of cash and commitments including nearly $18B of deposits, all 2026 memory output is pre-sold under non-cancellable contracts, and Microsoft, Google and Meta have used reserves to lock long-term supply.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether buyers would rather forfeit deposits than take delivery if AI returns disappoint.

falsifiableTrigger: exportControlExposure changes lift the sub-50% China cap or clear Blackwell within two quarters.
mechanism: Case-by-case licences, a 25% tariff, security conditions and a cap at under half of US sales leave a legal channel that almost no volume actually flows through.
rationale: The licence path exists but is not converting: about $10B of H200 licences to roughly ten firms have produced only trivial shipments, no revenue has been booked since February, Chinese orders of over 2 million units face about 700,000 units of inventory, Blackwell stays banned, and NVIDIA cut its authorised Asian buyer list by more than half.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether approved licences translate into shipped units in the next quarter or stay trivial.

falsifiableTrigger: AMD or non-NVIDIA designWins in production inference keep expanding for two consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Once rival software runs the workloads customers actually use, price and supply advantages start to outweigh the cost of switching.
rationale: Rivals keep winning production work despite the software gap: Anthropic committed to up to 2 gigawatts of AMD accelerators, Meta to up to 6 gigawatts, Rackspace signed a phased 30 MW deployment, AMD kernel work lifted a frontier model's throughput 2.10x, and a Chinese team trained a 1.6-trillion-parameter model on about 50,000 non-NVIDIA chips.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether these gigawatt commitments turn into deployed clusters rather than announcements.

falsifiableTrigger: Memory hbmSupplyCapex expansion pulls DRAM/NVMe prices down within two quarters.
mechanism: Memory is a large share of an AI server's bill of materials, so sharp memory price rises lift the cost of every rack built.
rationale: Memory pricing kept climbing: server memory contract prices are seen rising more than 25% quarter over quarter in Q3 2026, HBM4 contract prices may roughly double into 2027, DRAM lead times run 30-40 plus weeks with prices up about 90% since late 2025, rack component costs are inflating 2-3% a week, and AMD raised consumer GPU bundle prices about 10% citing memory.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to new memory fabrication capacity coming online in late 2026 and easing prices.

falsifiableTrigger: releaseCadence slips push a major vendor's 2H-2026 ramp into 2027.
mechanism: Several vendors ramping new parts at once adds units to the market, but any one vendor's manufacturing slip removes its share of that addition.
rationale: The wave is real but slipping in part: NVIDIA's Vera Rubin ramps in Q3 2026 and Helios ships to Microsoft in the second half, yet AMD's rack-scale MI455X only reaches engineering samples in the second half with mass production pushed to Q2 2027 on manufacturing delays.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to packaging and memory allocation, which caps how much of the ramp can actually be built.

falsifiableTrigger: AMD customerConcentration eases as its buyer base broadens over the next two quarters.
mechanism: When a few gigawatt-scale contracts carry most of the growth, one partner rescheduling swings the whole revenue line.
rationale: AMD's growth still rides a short list of very large partners - Microsoft, OpenAI at 6 gigawatts, Meta at up to 6 gigawatts, Oracle's 50,000-GPU cluster and now Anthropic at up to 2 gigawatts with a $5B equity investment attached - and AMD itself says it expects continued customer concentration.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to smaller deals such as the Rackspace 30 MW deployment multiplying into a wider buyer base.

falsifiableTrigger: Crescent Island releaseCadence slips its customer sampling past the 2H 2026 quarter.
mechanism: Using ordinary memory on a standard package skips the two scarcest inputs, so these chips can be built without competing for packaging or stacked memory slots.
rationale: Intel's Crescent Island is still on its stated path, detailed at Computex with up to 480GB of standard memory instead of high-bandwidth memory specifically to avoid packaging and memory contention, and guided to customer sampling in the second half of 2026.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether sampling turns into named customers, since none are disclosed yet.

falsifiableTrigger: TSMC grossMargin declines for two consecutive quarters as capacity loosens.
mechanism: When many kinds of AI chips compete for the same fabrication and packaging slots, the foundry runs full and can charge more.
rationale: TSMC posted a 67.7% gross margin, up 9.1 points year over year, with revenue up 36% and full-year growth guidance raised to above 40%, while AI demand spreading into custom chips, networking and power parts tightens capacity across nodes plus packaging, and TSMC lifted 2026 capex to $60-64B.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to the large capacity additions now being built, which could loosen the squeeze from late 2026.

falsifiableTrigger: A hyperscalerCapexRevision cuts 2026 or 2027 AI capex guidance within two quarters.
mechanism: If AI spending does not earn its keep, buyers cut capital budgets and accelerator orders fall with them.
note: hyperscaler-ai-spending-may-outrun-near-term-returns: applied: corroborated secondary reversal (5 distinct publishers; pending filing checkpoint)
rationale: The pullback did not happen: Alphabet raised 2026 capex to $195-205B, its second increase this year, with cloud revenue up 82% and backlog up more than $50B in a quarter, CoreWeave roughly doubled its capex plan, and the four largest US buyers track toward about $725B; only market jitters and analyst doubt point the other way.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to how the spending is funded, with Alphabet posting its first negative free cash flow while issuing equity and notes.

falsifiableTrigger: NVIDIA grossMargin guidance drops below 70% in a coming quarter.
mechanism: Buyers with no ready substitute pay premium prices, so margin holds even while new products carry early ramp costs.
rationale: NVIDIA's non-GAAP gross margin was 75.0% in Q1 FY2027 with next-quarter guidance held at the same level, far above AMD at 55% guided to about 56%, TSMC at 67.7% and Intel guided at 37.5%.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to memory input costs, with server memory contract prices set to rise more than 25% in the third quarter.

falsifiableTrigger: Top-buyer customerConcentration in CoWoS output falls below 85% within a year.
mechanism: When three buyers absorb nearly all packaging output, losing one leaves specialised capacity with almost no one else able to take it.
rationale: The top three advanced-packaging clients still take over 85% of TSMC output, with NVIDIA at about 60% and AMD about 11%, and AMD must split its slice between its server CPUs and its accelerators.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to outside packaging houses adding capacity that widens the customer base beyond the top three.

falsifiableTrigger: Aggregate rpoBacklog duration shortens as new commitments turn shorter-dated over two quarters.
mechanism: Buyers facing scarce supply sign longer contracts to reserve future capacity, which pushes the average life of order books further out.
rationale: Long-dated books grew: Google Cloud backlog rose more than $50B in a quarter to $514B with just over half converting within 24 months, CoreWeave's backlog reached $99.4B including a $21B Meta commitment running to 2032, Micron signed 16 five-year take-or-pay deals, and Broadcom carries a $73B AI backlog.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether long-dated commitments are firm or can be renegotiated if returns disappoint.

falsifiableTrigger: A leading model provider reports revenue (apiArr) growth stalling quarter over quarter while compute commitments keep growing.
mechanism: Rising paid usage of AI models gives the buyers of compute real sales to fund their contracts with.
rationale: Anthropic reached over $30B of annualised revenue as of April 2026, up from $1B in January 2025, and its models now run in production on Microsoft's cloud, though its compute commitments now include vendor equity of up to $5B from a chip supplier.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to how much of a model provider's compute is funded by its own sales versus supplier equity and credit.

falsifiableTrigger: Chinese domestic accelerator designWins for frontier training stall over the next two quarters.
mechanism: Once local chips can train frontier-scale models, Chinese buyers need fewer imported GPUs to keep up.
rationale: Meituan pretrained a 1.6-trillion-parameter model entirely on more than 50,000 domestic non-NVIDIA superpods across over 35 trillion tokens, and Chinese labs including Zhipu and DeepSeek are designing their own inference chips, though viable in-house silicon is judged more than two years away.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to the gap between demonstrated capability and demand, with Chinese firms still ordering over 2 million NVIDIA H200 units for 2026.

falsifiableTrigger: A neocloud's marginalBuyerFinancing debt load or net loss narrows for two consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Buying GPU fleets with borrowed money brings revenue in fast but interest and depreciation arrive faster still.
rationale: CoreWeave's revenue grew about 168% from $1.9B to $5.1B while its net loss widened from $937M to $1.2B, with total debt of $24.86B up 16.1% in a quarter, even as it raised 2026 capex to $31-35B and booked a $99.4B backlog.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether long-dated contracts such as the $21B Meta commitment convert into cash before debt costs bite.

falsifiableTrigger: A top hyperscaler cuts its 2027 gigawatt power target below its 2026 level.
mechanism: Accelerators cannot run without electricity and the grid gear to deliver it, so available power sets how many chips can actually be switched on.
rationale: Buildouts are now sized in gigawatts - Meta plans 7 gigawatts in 2026 and roughly double in 2027, AMD deals are stated in gigawatts, a Japan project is described by its 140 megawatts - while Gartner expects 40% of AI data centers to be power-constrained by 2027 and power transformer lead times average 128 weeks.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to efficiency gains, since new racks claim up to 10x more throughput per megawatt and stretch each available watt.

falsifiableTrigger: Broadcom-plus-Marvell market-share-pct of custom ASIC co-design falls below 90% within a year.
mechanism: Hyperscalers lack the in-house chip design capacity to go it alone, so their alternative to merchant GPUs runs through the same two partners.
rationale: Broadcom and Marvell together still hold an estimated 95% of custom AI chip co-design, with Broadcom alone carrying a $73B AI backlog and targeting $100B of annual AI chip revenue by 2027.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to buyers routing designs elsewhere, as with early talks between a model provider and Samsung on a 2nm custom chip.

falsifiableTrigger: Wistron odmMonthlyAiRevenue falls year-over-year for two consecutive months.
mechanism: Contract manufacturers only book revenue when finished servers leave the factory, so their monthly sales track real shipments rather than announcements.
rationale: Wistron posted record June 2026 revenue of NT$321.82B, up 53.9% year over year and 10.9% month over month on AI-server and networking shipments, with supply-chain players reporting an order boom running into the second half.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to memory and packaging shortages holding back finished-system output.

falsifiableTrigger: A neocloud's marginalBuyerFinancing debt-to-equity rises above 6:1 within two quarters.
mechanism: Debt-funded fleets leave a thin equity cushion, so a dip in rental demand or a refinancing squeeze hits the operator quickly.
rationale: CoreWeave has raised $18.81B of debt against $3.5B of equity, a 5.4:1 ratio, with total debt of $24.86B up 16.1% in one quarter, while it plans $31-35B of 2026 capex, roughly double its 2025 spend.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to supplier backstops, since the chip vendor now guarantees to rent back idle GPUs at fixed rates.

falsifiableTrigger: Co-packaged optics adoption stalls below 5% of AI optical modules through 2027.
mechanism: Putting the optics next to the switch chip ties cluster wiring to a single fast-moving optics roadmap and its suppliers.
rationale: Co-packaged optics is set to grow from about 0.5% of AI optical modules in 2026 to about 35% by 2030, with NVIDIA's Spectrum-X Photonics due in the second half of 2026 and Quantum-X shipping early in 2026, and NVIDIA already leading data-center Ethernet switching.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to the 2026 shipment schedule for the first co-packaged switch products.

falsifiableTrigger: A named US fab or packaging project slips its build milestone past 2027.
mechanism: Building fabrication and packaging outside Taiwan spreads production across more sites and reduces reliance on one island.
rationale: NVIDIA plans up to $500B of AI infrastructure produced in the United States with TSMC, Foxconn, Wistron, Corning, Lumentum, Coherent and Amkor, alongside a $5B investment in Intel to build custom processors with its high-speed links, while Intel also adds capacity in Ireland.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether announced dollar totals turn into working capacity, since advanced packaging remains concentrated at TSMC.

detail.falsifiableTrigger: Google Cloud or CoreWeave rpoBacklog fails to grow sequentially for two consecutive quarters.
detail.mechanism: Customers sign for capacity that does not exist yet, so signed contracts pile up ahead of the revenue that recognises them.
detail.sensitivity: Most sensitive to how much of the backlog is cancellable and how fast delivery capacity catches up.
detail.statement: Cloud providers are booking compute contracts far faster than they can deliver them, so their reported backlogs now show demand better than their quarterly sales do.
detail.title: Cloud backlog conversion becomes the demand proof point

detail.falsifiableTrigger: A top hyperscaler returns to positive free cash flow while holding 2027 capex guidance for two consecutive quarters.
detail.mechanism: When spending outruns operating cash, buyers must raise outside money, which makes their orders depend on credit markets staying open.
detail.sensitivity: Most sensitive to borrowing costs and investor appetite for AI-related debt and equity.
detail.statement: The largest cloud buyers are turning to debt and share issuance to pay for AI capacity instead of funding it from cash generated by their businesses.
detail.title: Hyperscalers now borrow to fund the buildout

detail.falsifiableTrigger: A new accelerator generation delivers less than a 1.5x perfPerWatt gain over its predecessor.
detail.mechanism: More output per watt and per package means a fixed supply of power and packaging slots produces more usable compute each generation.
detail.sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether vendor-stated efficiency claims hold up in independent measurement.
detail.statement: Each new generation of AI racks does far more work per megawatt, which lets buyers add capacity even when power and packaging are capped.
detail.title: Efficiency gains stretch scarce power and packaging

sensitivity: Most sensitive to the second-half 2026 wave of new racks landing faster than demand absorbs it.
