falsifiableTrigger: NVIDIA DC Ethernet switch market-share-pct slips from #1 within two quarters.
mechanism: Selling the switches and the accelerators as one system makes it costlier for a buyer to swap in someone else's chips without redoing the cluster wiring.
rationale: NVIDIA took the top revenue spot in data-center Ethernet switching, and Spectrum-6 landed named first customers including CoreWeave, Microsoft, Nebius, SpaceXAI and Tesla, with photonics claimed at five times better power efficiency across 100,000-GPU deployments.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to open Ethernet alternatives winning large clusters on price.

falsifiableTrigger: Cost-per-token gains stall so tokenEconomics improves less than one generation cycle.
mechanism: When each answer costs less to produce, buyers run far more of them, so cheaper compute grows total chip demand instead of shrinking it.
rationale: Open-source inference costs have fallen 30-50% a year with token prices dropping far faster on some measures, NVIDIA claims an order-of-magnitude lower cost per token with NVLink systems, and AT&T is now burning about a trillion tokens a month.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether falling prices per token keep converting into higher total token volume.

falsifiableTrigger: Prepaid HBM commitments in rpoBacklog shrink or deposits are refunded within a quarter.
mechanism: Buyers who put cash down years ahead for memory have already paid for the accelerators that memory goes into, so that demand is committed rather than hoped for.
rationale: Micron holds 16 non-cancelable five-year take-or-pay deals backed by over $22B including nearly $18B of cash deposits, and HBM suppliers have sold out 2026 output under non-cancellable contracts with hyperscalers locking multi-year supply.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether any large depositor walks away and forfeits its prepayment.

falsifiableTrigger: exportControlExposure changes lift the sub-50% China cap or clear Blackwell within two quarters.
mechanism: Licenses only turn into sales if buyers, tariffs and inventory all line up, and right now they do not, so a paper reopening delivers no revenue.
rationale: The licensing door is open on paper - roughly ten Chinese firms cleared for up to 75,000 chips each and about $10B of approved licenses - but actual shipments stay trivial, no revenue has been booked, a 25% tariff applies, Blackwell is still banned, and enforcement raids are widening.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the first real H200 shipments actually clear customs and book revenue.

falsifiableTrigger: AMD or non-NVIDIA designWins in production inference keep expanding for two consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Customers stay on NVIDIA when porting their software is painful, and each rival software release that closes the gap lowers that cost of leaving.
rationale: AMD's software stack posted 3.3x inference and 2.4x training gains over its prior release and a 2.10x throughput jump on a leading open model, while Anthropic, OpenAI, Meta, Oracle and Rackspace committed to Instinct in production, so software is less of a barrier than before.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the announced rival deployments actually run production workloads at scale.

falsifiableTrigger: Memory hbmSupplyCapex expansion pulls DRAM/NVMe prices down within two quarters.
mechanism: Memory is a big share of an AI server's bill of materials, so sharp memory price rises push up the cost of every rack and squeeze whoever cannot pass it on.
rationale: Server memory contract prices are set to rise more than 25% in one quarter, DRAM lead times stretch to 32-40 weeks with prices up about 90% since late 2025, AI-server rack component costs are inflating 2-3% a week, and AMD is raising Radeon bundle prices about 10% on memory costs.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to how quickly new memory fab capacity arriving from late 2026 relieves prices.

falsifiableTrigger: releaseCadence slips push a major vendor's 2H-2026 ramp into 2027.
mechanism: Several vendors reach volume production in the same half, so total accelerator units available to buyers steps up at once.
rationale: NVIDIA's Vera Rubin enters production ramp in the third quarter, AMD's Helios reached full production with shipments starting the same quarter, and next-generation parts from AWS and Google are moving to mass production together, though AMD's rack-scale volume ramp slips toward 2027.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to packaging and memory allocation, which can hold back a ramp even when the chip is ready.

falsifiableTrigger: AMD customerConcentration eases as its buyer base broadens over the next two quarters.
mechanism: A few enormous contracts carry nearly all of the growth, so one partner delaying or cancelling swings AMD's data-center line hard.
rationale: AMD's pipeline is a short list of very large commitments - Anthropic at 2 gigawatts, OpenAI at 6 gigawatts, Meta at up to 6 gigawatts, Microsoft and Oracle - and AMD itself says it expects continued customer concentration, with an equity investment tying one of those buyers to it.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether smaller enterprise and cloud buyers pick up Instinct in volume.

falsifiableTrigger: Crescent Island releaseCadence slips its customer sampling past the 2H 2026 quarter.
mechanism: Using ordinary memory instead of stacked memory removes the advanced-packaging step that gates everyone else, so this chip can be built with capacity that is not fought over.
rationale: Intel's Crescent Island still targets second-half 2026 customer sampling using up to 480GB of standard LPDDR5X rather than high-bandwidth memory, explicitly to avoid packaging and memory contention.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the lower memory bandwidth is good enough for real inference jobs.

falsifiableTrigger: TSMC grossMargin declines for two consecutive quarters as capacity loosens.
mechanism: When many kinds of chips chase the same fab and packaging slots, the foundry can choose the best-paying work and lift prices.
rationale: TSMC posted a 67.7% gross margin, up 9.1 points year over year, raised full-year growth guidance to above 40% and lifted capex to $60-64B, while demand spreading into ASICs, networking and power chips tightens capacity across nodes and packaging.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to a slowdown in AI orders that would leave newly added capacity underused.

falsifiableTrigger: A hyperscalerCapexRevision cuts 2026 or 2027 AI capex guidance within two quarters.
mechanism: If the money spent on AI capacity does not come back as revenue, buyers cut orders, but cloud revenue and profit are so far rising alongside the spending.
rationale: Rather than pulling back, Alphabet raised 2026 capex to $195-205B for a second time and reported cloud revenue up 82% with operating income at $8.8B, CoreWeave roughly doubled its capex plan, and the four largest buyers track toward about $725B; only market jitters and analyst worry point the other way.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to cloud revenue growth stalling while capex commitments stay locked in.

falsifiableTrigger: NVIDIA grossMargin guidance drops below 70% in a coming quarter.
mechanism: Buyers keep paying premium prices because supply is short and alternatives are limited, so margin holds even through a costly product transition.
rationale: NVIDIA reported a 75.0% non-GAAP gross margin and guided the next quarter to the same level, far above AMD at 55% guided to 56% and Intel in the low 40s.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to memory cost inflation and the cost of ramping the next generation.

falsifiableTrigger: Top-buyer customerConcentration in CoWoS output falls below 85% within a year.
mechanism: A very small number of buyers fill the packaging lines, so if one cuts orders there is no queue of other customers ready to take the slots.
rationale: The top three packaging customers still take more than 85% of TSMC output, with NVIDIA at about 60% and AMD about 11%, and AMD must split its slice between server processors and accelerators.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether custom-chip and networking customers grow into meaningful packaging buyers.

falsifiableTrigger: Aggregate rpoBacklog duration shortens as new commitments turn shorter-dated over two quarters.
mechanism: Buyers who fear being short of compute sign longer contracts, so the order book stretches further into the future than the delivery schedule.
rationale: Google Cloud's backlog jumped more than $50B in a quarter to $514B with only just over half converting within 24 months, CoreWeave's backlog reached $99.4B including a Meta commitment running to 2032, and Micron's take-or-pay deals run five years.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether new bookings keep their long tenor as capacity loosens.

falsifiableTrigger: A leading model provider reports revenue (apiArr) growth stalling quarter over quarter while compute commitments keep growing.
mechanism: Model providers pay for compute out of subscription and interface sales, so rising sales make their compute commitments look funded rather than speculative.
rationale: Anthropic's annual run-rate revenue passed $30B in April 2026 from $1B in January 2025, its models are in production on Azure, and it has signed multi-gigawatt compute deals it says are needed to meet customer demand.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether model-provider revenue growth keeps pace with commitments that now run into the tens of billions.

falsifiableTrigger: Chinese domestic accelerator designWins for frontier training stall over the next two quarters.
mechanism: Once local chips can train a frontier model, buyers blocked from imports have a working substitute and stop queuing for licensed foreign parts.
rationale: Meituan trained a 1.6-trillion-parameter model on more than 50,000 domestic accelerators with no NVIDIA chips across 35 trillion tokens, and Chinese labs are commissioning their own inference chips, though viable in-house silicon is judged more than two years out.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to memory supply and software maturity on the domestic stack.

falsifiableTrigger: A neocloud's marginalBuyerFinancing debt load or net loss narrows for two consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Buying GPU fleets on credit means interest and depreciation grow faster than rental revenue, so sales records come with bigger losses.
rationale: CoreWeave's revenue grew about 168% to $5.1B while its net loss widened from $937M to $1.2B, even as it raised 2026 capex to $31-35B.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to rental prices, which decide whether the fleet ever earns back its cost.

falsifiableTrigger: A top hyperscaler cuts its 2027 gigawatt power target below its 2026 level.
mechanism: A site can only run as many accelerators as it has electricity and electrical gear for, so power and transformers now set the ceiling on deployments.
rationale: Buildouts are now sized in gigawatts - Meta at 7 gigawatts in 2026 and roughly double in 2027, AMD deals quoted at 2 and 6 gigawatts - while Gartner expects 40% of AI data centers to be power-constrained by 2027 and transformer lead times average 128 weeks.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to grid connection timing and transformer delivery, which move slower than chip supply.

falsifiableTrigger: Broadcom-plus-Marvell market-share-pct of custom ASIC co-design falls below 90% within a year.
mechanism: Custom chips still mostly go through two design partners, so their capacity and pricing gate the alternative to merchant GPUs unless new partners appear.
rationale: Broadcom and Marvell still hold an estimated 95% of custom AI chip co-design, but Anthropic is in early talks with Samsung to build a custom chip on a 2nm process and Chinese labs are pursuing their own designs, so the two-house channel is starting to face alternatives.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether new design partners such as Samsung convert early talks into shipping silicon.

falsifiableTrigger: Wistron odmMonthlyAiRevenue falls year-over-year for two consecutive months.
mechanism: Contract manufacturers only bill when finished servers leave the factory, so their monthly revenue is a direct check that orders are turning into hardware.
rationale: Wistron posted record June 2026 revenue of NT$321.82B, up 53.9% year over year and 10.9% month over month on AI-server and networking shipments, with supply-chain players reporting an order boom into the second half.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to component shortages that can hold finished racks in the factory.

falsifiableTrigger: A neocloud's marginalBuyerFinancing debt-to-equity rises above 6:1 within two quarters.
mechanism: GPU fleets are bought with borrowed money secured on the chips, so a thin equity cushion leaves little room if rental income or resale values fall.
rationale: CoreWeave has raised $18.81B of debt against $3.5B of equity, a 5.4 to 1 ratio, with total debt of $24.86B up 16.1% in a single quarter, while it doubles capex plans.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to credit conditions and to how lenders value used accelerators as collateral.

falsifiableTrigger: Co-packaged optics adoption stalls below 5% of AI optical modules through 2027.
mechanism: Putting the optics into the switch package cuts power per link, so cluster wiring gets tied to a new and narrow set of packaging suppliers.
rationale: Co-packaged optics is set to climb from about 0.5% of AI optical modules in 2026 to roughly 35% by 2030, NVIDIA's photonics switches ship this year with named first customers, and Taiwanese packaging houses are newly competing for silicon photonics work.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to yield and serviceability of packaged optics in live clusters.

falsifiableTrigger: A named US fab or packaging project slips its build milestone past 2027.
mechanism: Vendors are funding fabs and packaging lines outside Taiwan, which adds a second place these parts can be made if the first is disrupted.
rationale: NVIDIA plans up to $500B of US-built AI infrastructure with TSMC, Foxconn, Wistron and Amkor; Micron committed $250B to US memory manufacturing through 2035 and broke ground in New York on July 9, 2026; Intel added EUR 5B of capacity and grew foundry revenue 31%.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to construction and qualification timelines, since announcements run years ahead of output.

falsifiableTrigger: Google Cloud or CoreWeave rpoBacklog fails to grow sequentially for two consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Cloud sellers sign contracts faster than they can build capacity, so the unshipped order book grows and shows demand earlier than the revenue line does.
rationale: Google Cloud's backlog grew more than $50B sequentially to $514B with just over half due to convert within 24 months while cloud revenue accelerated to 82% growth, and CoreWeave's backlog climbed to $99.4B from $66.8B a month earlier.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether booked contracts actually convert to revenue on schedule.

falsifiableTrigger: A top hyperscaler returns to positive free cash flow while holding 2027 capex guidance for two consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Spending has outgrown what operating cash can cover, so buyers raise debt and equity to keep building, which links future orders to open capital markets.
rationale: Alphabet funded its June-quarter buildout with $49.6B of equity issuance and $20.3B of notes and reported its first ever negative free cash flow of $5.9B, while NVIDIA raised $25B of bonds to finance customer purchases and CoreWeave keeps leveraging up.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to borrowing costs and investor appetite for financing AI capacity.

falsifiableTrigger: A new accelerator generation delivers less than a 1.5x perfPerWatt gain over its predecessor.
mechanism: Each generation does more work for the same electricity, so a site with a fixed power budget can buy more useful compute without new grid capacity.
rationale: NVIDIA's newest systems are stated at up to 10 times the performance per megawatt of the gear they replace, its photonics networking claims five times better power efficiency, and the prior generation step measured about 1.6 times better performance per watt.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether vendor efficiency claims hold up in real deployments rather than benchmarks.

detail.falsifiableTrigger: HBM leadTimes shorten and suppliers report unsold capacity for two consecutive quarters before end-2027.
detail.mechanism: Every accelerator needs several stacks of high-bandwidth memory, so when memory makers are sold out the chip vendors cannot build more units no matter how many orders they hold.
detail.sensitivity: Most sensitive to how fast new memory capacity from the three suppliers converts into shipped stacks.
detail.statement: Stacked memory, not chips or packaging alone, now decides how many accelerators NVIDIA and AMD can actually deliver.
detail.title: Memory supply is the new choke point on accelerator shipments

detail.falsifiableTrigger: Memory supplier gross margin falls for two consecutive quarters as contract prices flatten.
detail.mechanism: Scarce memory lets suppliers set the price, so a larger slice of what a buyer pays for an AI server ends up as memory-maker profit.
detail.sensitivity: Most sensitive to new memory fabs coming online and restoring buyer bargaining power.
detail.statement: Memory suppliers are earning extraordinary margins on AI parts, shifting profit from the server builders toward the memory makers.
detail.title: Memory makers capture a growing share of AI server profit

detail.falsifiableTrigger: No new sovereign or enterprise cluster above 10,000 GPUs is announced for two consecutive quarters.
detail.mechanism: Governments and large companies buying their own clusters add order flow that does not depend on the top few cloud operators.
detail.sensitivity: Most sensitive to public funding decisions and to whether these projects secure power and packaging allocation.
detail.statement: National projects and large enterprises are now placing accelerator orders big enough to matter alongside the cloud giants.
detail.title: Sovereign and enterprise buyers become a new demand tier

detail.falsifiableTrigger: Intel data-center revenue growth falls below 10% year over year for two consecutive quarters.
detail.mechanism: Better factory yields and named external customers let Intel sell more server silicon and manufacturing capacity, widening the supply base beyond two vendors.
detail.sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether foundry yield gains hold as volumes rise.
detail.statement: Intel's data-center and foundry businesses are growing again with better margins, adding a third source of AI-adjacent supply.
detail.title: Intel returns as a data-center supplier

falsifiableTrigger: B200 rpoBacklog falls below 2 million units for two consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Buyers place multi-year orders faster than memory and packaging suppliers can build the parts NVIDIA needs to fill them.
rationale: NVIDIA data-center revenue hit a record $75.2B up 92% year over year, B200 orders reached about 3.6 million units, and memory and packaging remain sold out, so orders keep running ahead of what NVIDIA can ship.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to memory and packaging supply loosening enough to clear the order book.

falsifiableTrigger: HBM leadTimes ease to available-on-demand and CoWoS lead times fall below 26 weeks before the end of 2027.
mechanism: Every accelerator needs both stacked memory and advanced packaging, so whichever is scarcer sets the ceiling on total shipments.
note: supply-constraint-binding: deferred: secondary-only reversal (2 distinct publishers < 3)
rationale: Stacked memory is sold out through 2026 and much of 2027, TSMC packaging carries 52 to 78 week waits and is booked into 2027, even as packaging capacity climbs toward 130,000 wafers a month, so both limits still cap shipments.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to memory and packaging capacity additions arriving faster than demand.

falsifiableTrigger: AMD accelerator market-share-pct fails to rise above 7% through 2027.
mechanism: Large multi-year customer commitments feed later shipments that show up as datacenter accelerator share gains.
rationale: AMD still holds only about 5 to 7 percent share, but gigawatt-scale wins with Anthropic, OpenAI, Meta and Oracle plus data-center revenue up 57 percent point to that share converting soon.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the announced gigawatt commitments turn into shipped and recognized revenue.

falsifiableTrigger: ASIC market-share-pct growth falls back below GPU growth for two consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Hyperscalers move inference work onto their own cheaper chips, taking growth that would otherwise go to merchant GPUs.
rationale: Custom chips are set to grow about 45 percent in 2026 versus 16 percent for merchant GPUs, custom silicon already covers a large slice of total compute, and Meta is putting new in-house accelerators into production.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether captive custom chips can match merchant GPU software and performance at scale.

falsifiableTrigger: gpuSpotPrice for H100 or GB200 drops more than 20% within a quarter.
mechanism: Tight supply keeps rental demand above available capacity, so hourly prices stay firm.
rationale: Rental prices are holding, with H100 up about 24 percent from its late-2025 low and current cloud rates steady, even as more supply arrives.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to a fast supply ramp arriving before demand absorbs it.

falsifiableTrigger: exportControlExposure eases so China DC revenue recovers above prior levels within two quarters.
mechanism: License rules block or delay the chips Chinese buyers want, removing that revenue from the served market.
rationale: NVIDIA's China revenue fell by more than half to $4.55B with no Hopper shipments, H200 sales stayed trivial, and the top chip's export stayed banned, so policy is cutting real addressable demand.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to US and China policy shifts on which chips may ship.

falsifiableTrigger: Vendor-financed GPU commitments in rpoBacklog exceed 300,000 units within two quarters.
mechanism: NVIDIA funds the buyers who then order its chips, so its own credit props up part of its reported demand.
rationale: NVIDIA scaled a revenue-sharing and backstop program covering about 210,000 GPUs across Firmus and Sharon AI and issued $25B of bonds, so more reported demand rests on NVIDIA-extended credit.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to how large the vendor-financed share of orders grows relative to cash-funded orders.

falsifiableTrigger: customerConcentration for the top three direct customers falls below prior shares next fiscal year.
mechanism: A few large buyers place most orders, so any one slowing or moving to in-house chips would dent demand sharply.
rationale: Three direct customers were 21, 17 and 16 percent of NVIDIA's revenue and the top four were more than half, so concentration stays high.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to a single top hyperscaler cutting orders or switching to its own silicon.

falsifiableTrigger: NVIDIA DC Ethernet switch market-share-pct slips from #1 within two quarters.
mechanism: Selling networking together with GPUs makes the full system harder to swap out for standalone chips.
rationale: NVIDIA became the revenue leader in datacenter Ethernet switches for the first time and is shipping new Spectrum networking with marquee cloud customers, deepening the bundled-system tie.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to open networking standards letting buyers mix rival switches with any accelerator.

falsifiableTrigger: Cost-per-token gains stall so tokenEconomics improves less than one generation cycle.
mechanism: Lower cost per token makes more AI use cases affordable, expanding the work that runs on NVIDIA GPUs.
rationale: NVIDIA's newest generation cut inference cost per token about tenfold, and open-source inference costs keep falling fast, pulling more workloads onto its chips.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether each new generation keeps cutting cost per token.

falsifiableTrigger: Prepaid HBM commitments in rpoBacklog shrink or deposits are refunded within a quarter.
mechanism: Binding prepaid contracts commit buyers to take the memory and chips regardless of later conditions.
rationale: Micron signed 16 non-cancelable five-year take-or-pay memory deals backed by more than $22B, and NVIDIA lifted total prepaid supply commitments toward $145B, locking future accelerator demand in place.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether customers can walk away from or renegotiate the prepaid deals.

falsifiableTrigger: exportControlExposure changes lift the sub-50% China cap or clear Blackwell within two quarters.
mechanism: Case-by-case licenses and a hard cap let only a trickle of chips through while the best parts stay blocked.
rationale: China access stayed limited to case-by-case H200-class licenses under a sub-50 percent cap with only about ten cleared buyers and the top chip still banned, matching the capped-reopening picture.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to policy moves that raise the cap or approve the banned top-tier chip.

falsifiableTrigger: AMD or non-NVIDIA designWins in production inference keep expanding for two consecutive quarters.
mechanism: As rival software matures and cuts cost, customers can move workloads off NVIDIA despite the switching effort.
rationale: AMD posted large inference and training software gains, won production commitments from Anthropic, OpenAI and Meta, and showed a lower total cost of ownership than NVIDIA, so the software lock-in is holding customers less tightly than before.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to how fast rival software stacks close the ease-of-use gap with CUDA.

falsifiableTrigger: Memory hbmSupplyCapex expansion pulls DRAM/NVMe prices down within two quarters.
mechanism: Scarce memory and storage bid up prices for the parts that make up most of an AI server's bill of materials.
rationale: AI-server rack component costs are climbing 2 to 3 percent a week, standard memory prices jumped roughly 90 percent, spot DDR4 rose over 17 percent in a month, and stacked-memory contract prices are set to double.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to new memory capacity arriving and easing prices.

falsifiableTrigger: releaseCadence slips push a major vendor's 2H-2026 ramp into 2027.
mechanism: Several vendors ramping new accelerators at once adds to the total pool of available compute.
rationale: NVIDIA Vera Rubin, AMD Helios, AWS Trainium3 and Google TPU are all lined up for mass production in the second half of 2026, though AMD's next rack part slipped its full ramp toward 2027.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to production delays and shared memory and packaging constraints across vendors.

falsifiableTrigger: AMD customerConcentration eases as its buyer base broadens over the next two quarters.
mechanism: A small set of very large buyers drives most of AMD's accelerator volume, so each one carries outsized weight.
rationale: AMD's growth rests on a handful of gigawatt-scale commitments from Microsoft, OpenAI, Meta, Oracle and Anthropic, and AMD itself expects continued customer concentration.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether any one mega-customer delays or cancels.

falsifiableTrigger: Crescent Island releaseCadence slips its customer sampling past the 2H 2026 quarter.
mechanism: Using standard memory instead of stacked memory lets the chip skip the advanced packaging that is in short supply.
rationale: Intel's Crescent Island stayed on track to sample in the second half of 2026 using standard LPDDR5X memory up to 480GB, sidestepping the packaging and stacked-memory crunch.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether standard-memory parts deliver enough performance to attract buyers.

falsifiableTrigger: TSMC grossMargin declines for two consecutive quarters as capacity loosens.
mechanism: AI demand across many chip types keeps TSMC's lines full, giving it room to raise prices.
rationale: TSMC's gross margin rose more than 9 points to about 68 percent with packaging sold out and lead times stretched, showing broad AI demand filling capacity and lifting prices.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to a broad AI demand slowdown that frees up capacity.

falsifiableTrigger: A hyperscalerCapexRevision cuts 2026 or 2027 AI capex guidance within two quarters.
mechanism: Buyers are committing cash to capacity years ahead of the revenue it is meant to generate, exposing them to a pullback if returns lag.
rationale: Combined hyperscaler capital spending jumped toward $650 to $725B with fresh doubt about the payoff, so the risk that spending outruns returns still stands even as budgets rise.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether AI revenue growth keeps pace with the rising spend.

falsifiableTrigger: NVIDIA grossMargin guidance drops below 70% in a coming quarter.
mechanism: Strong pricing power and product mix keep margins high even through the cost bump of new product ramps.
rationale: NVIDIA held its gross margin at 75 percent and guided the next quarter to the same level while ramping new products, far above rivals in the 50s.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to competition or rising memory and packaging costs squeezing margins.

falsifiableTrigger: Top-buyer customerConcentration in CoWoS output falls below 85% within a year.
mechanism: A handful of buyers pre-book most packaging capacity, leaving little for anyone else.
rationale: The top three packaging clients take more than 85 percent of TSMC's output, with NVIDIA near 60 percent and AMD about 11 percent.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to new packaging capacity opening room for more buyers.

falsifiableTrigger: Aggregate rpoBacklog duration shortens as new commitments turn shorter-dated over two quarters.
mechanism: Signing multi-year commitments extends how far into the future booked demand reaches.
rationale: Buyers signed longer-dated deals including Micron's five-year take-or-pay contracts and CoreWeave's Meta commitment through 2032, pushing out the average life of order books.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to buyers shifting toward shorter contracts if confidence wavers.

falsifiableTrigger: A leading model provider reports revenue (apiArr) growth stalling quarter over quarter while compute commitments keep growing.
mechanism: Fast-growing model revenue funds the compute commitments, tying buildout to actual paying usage.
rationale: Anthropic's annual revenue run-rate grew from about $1B to over $30B in roughly a year, and one enterprise is already processing about a trillion tokens a month, so heavy compute spending rests on real and rising sales.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether model revenue keeps climbing with compute spend.

falsifiableTrigger: Chinese domestic accelerator designWins for frontier training stall over the next two quarters.
mechanism: Export bans push Chinese labs to build and use domestic accelerators for the training that NVIDIA can no longer serve.
rationale: Meituan trained a large trillion-parameter model on more than 50,000 Chinese domestic accelerators without any NVIDIA chips, showing home-grown silicon now handles frontier training.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether domestic chips keep matching frontier training needs.

falsifiableTrigger: A neocloud's marginalBuyerFinancing debt load or net loss narrows for two consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Heavy interest and depreciation on debt-funded GPU fleets grow faster than the revenue they generate.
rationale: CoreWeave grew revenue 168 percent to $5.1B while its net loss widened from $937M to $1.2B, confirming record revenue alongside deepening losses.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to rental prices and borrowing costs versus fleet expansion.

falsifiableTrigger: A top hyperscaler cuts its 2027 gigawatt power target below its 2026 level.
mechanism: Limited power and long-lead grid gear cap how much compute can actually be switched on.
rationale: Analysts expect 40 percent of AI datacenters to be power-constrained by 2027, transformer lead times reached 128 weeks, and buyers now size deals in gigawatts like Meta's 7GW plan.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to grid buildout and power-equipment lead times.

falsifiableTrigger: Broadcom-plus-Marvell market-share-pct of custom ASIC co-design falls below 90% within a year.
mechanism: Hyperscalers rely on these two design houses to turn their chip ideas into working silicon.
rationale: Broadcom and Marvell together still hold about 95 percent of custom AI chip co-design, so the custom-chip path runs almost entirely through two firms.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to a new design partner entering or hyperscalers building in-house design teams.

falsifiableTrigger: Wistron odmMonthlyAiRevenue falls year-over-year for two consecutive months.
mechanism: Contract server makers only book revenue when finished AI systems actually ship, so record sales track real shipments.
rationale: Wistron posted record June revenue of NT$321.82B, up about 54 percent year over year, confirming AI-server orders are shipping in volume.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to a slowdown in AI-server order flow.

falsifiableTrigger: A neocloud's marginalBuyerFinancing debt-to-equity rises above 6:1 within two quarters.
mechanism: Neoclouds borrow to buy fleets, so a small equity base sits under a large pile of debt.
rationale: CoreWeave carried $18.81B of debt against $3.5B of equity, a 5.4-to-1 ratio, with total debt rising 16 percent in a quarter, confirming debt-heavy funding with thin equity.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to lender appetite and the cost of refinancing the debt.

falsifiableTrigger: Co-packaged optics adoption stalls below 5% of AI optical modules through 2027.
mechanism: Moving optics onto the switch package changes who supplies AI networking gear and how it is built.
rationale: Co-packaged optics is still early at about 0.5 percent of AI optical modules but is set to reach 35 percent by 2030, with NVIDIA's photonics switch and Taiwan packagers moving into it.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to yield and reliability of the new packaged-optics designs.

falsifiableTrigger: A named US fab or packaging project slips its build milestone past 2027.
mechanism: Building fabs, packaging and assembly inside the US adds capacity outside the current Asia concentration.
rationale: NVIDIA committed up to $500B of US AI hardware with partners, Micron pledged $250B of US memory, and Wistron opened a Texas plant, widening domestic supply at large scale.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to construction timelines and whether the pledged projects actually break ground.

falsifiableTrigger: Google Cloud or CoreWeave rpoBacklog fails to grow sequentially for two consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Signed contracts pile up ahead of the capacity to serve them, so backlog grows as a sign of real committed demand.
rationale: Google Cloud's backlog grew $50B in a quarter to $514B and CoreWeave's rose from about $67B to $99B, showing cloud providers booking compute far faster than they can deliver.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether new bookings keep outpacing deliveries.

falsifiableTrigger: A top hyperscaler returns to positive free cash flow while holding 2027 capex guidance for two consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Capacity spending now exceeds operating cash, so buyers raise debt and equity to cover the gap.
rationale: Alphabet funded its quarter with $49.6B of equity and $20.3B of notes and posted its first-ever negative free cash flow, showing the largest buyers turning to outside financing instead of cash.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to capital-market conditions and how long spending outruns cash flow.

falsifiableTrigger: A new accelerator generation delivers less than a 1.5x perfPerWatt gain over its predecessor.
mechanism: Doing far more compute per megawatt means each scarce unit of power and packaging yields more usable capacity.
rationale: NVIDIA's Vera Rubin racks deliver about ten times the work per megawatt of the prior generation, letting buyers add capacity even where power and packaging are capped.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether each new generation keeps posting large efficiency jumps.

falsifiableTrigger: HBM leadTimes shorten and suppliers report unsold capacity for two consecutive quarters before end-2027.
mechanism: Each accelerator needs stacked memory, so when that memory is short it, not the chip, sets how many can ship.
rationale: Micron said its stacked-memory shipments are capped by supply not demand and that this gates NVIDIA and AMD GPU availability, with the shortage running into 2027 and 2028.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to how fast memory makers expand stacked-memory output.

falsifiableTrigger: Memory supplier gross margin falls for two consecutive quarters as contract prices flatten.
mechanism: Scarce memory lets suppliers charge much higher prices, moving profit from server builders to memory makers.
rationale: Micron's data-center memory revenue more than doubled at an 87 percent gross margin and stacked-memory contract prices are set to double, shifting profit toward the memory makers.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to memory supply catching up and cooling contract prices.

falsifiableTrigger: No new sovereign or enterprise cluster above 10,000 GPUs is announced for two consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Governments and large enterprises now place clusters big enough to add a new source of accelerator demand.
rationale: A Japanese national project ordered 27,500 Rubin GPUs, an Indonesia factory plans up to 170,000 GPUs, and a large pharma firm is deploying multiple flagship systems, so national and enterprise orders now matter alongside the cloud giants.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to national funding and enterprise AI budgets holding up.

falsifiableTrigger: Intel data-center revenue growth falls below 10% year over year for two consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Rising data-center sales and improving margins bring Intel back as a third source of AI-adjacent supply.
rationale: Intel's data-center and AI revenue grew 59 percent to $6.3B, its gross margin rose to about 40 percent from 27.5 percent, foundry revenue grew 31 percent, and it signed an external foundry customer.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to Intel sustaining product competitiveness and foundry ramp execution.

detail.falsifiableTrigger: New vendor equity-for-compute deals in marginalBuyerFinancing stop appearing for two consecutive quarters.
detail.mechanism: A vendor funds a customer that then commits to buy the vendor's chips, so part of demand depends on the vendor's own money.
detail.sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether these funded customers can pay from their own revenue rather than vendor capital.
detail.statement: Merchant accelerator vendors are now buying equity stakes in the AI firms that buy their chips, tying reported demand to vendor-funded customers beyond NVIDIA alone.
detail.title: chipmakers take equity in their own customers

detail.falsifiableTrigger: Standard DRAM S10 spot prices fall for two consecutive months as suppliers restore non-AI capacity.
detail.mechanism: Memory makers shift capacity to high-margin AI parts, starving other products and driving their prices up.
detail.sensitivity: Most sensitive to how much memory capacity stays diverted to AI parts.
detail.statement: The stacked-memory shortage is spreading into standard memory and raising prices on consumer and general-purpose graphics parts.
detail.title: memory crunch spills into consumer and general-purpose parts

falsifiableTrigger: B200 rpoBacklog falls below 2 million units for two consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Buyers keep placing orders faster than NVIDIA can build and ship systems, so the order book grows even as revenue sets records.
rationale: NVIDIA posted record data-center revenue of $75.2 billion, up 92% year over year, guided the next quarter to $91 billion, carries a roughly 3.6 million unit B200 order book, and has begun the Vera Rubin production ramp with purchase orders in hand from almost all major customers.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to a pullback in the handful of very large cloud buyers who place most of the orders.

falsifiableTrigger: HBM leadTimes ease to available-on-demand and CoWoS lead times fall below 26 weeks before the end of 2027.
mechanism: Every accelerator needs both stacked memory and advanced packaging, so whichever of the two is scarcer sets the ceiling on how many units vendors can ship.
rationale: Stacked memory is sold out through 2026 with much of 2027 pre-booked and no sign of easing, while TSMC advanced packaging carries 52 to 78 week lead times and is booked into 2027 even as capacity climbs toward 130,000 wafers a month, so both limits still cap shipments.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to how fast new memory and packaging capacity actually comes online versus the pace of order growth.

falsifiableTrigger: AMD accelerator market-share-pct fails to rise above 7% through 2027.
mechanism: Large named buyers signing multi-gigawatt AMD deployments turn AMD's roadmap into contracted volume that would otherwise have gone to NVIDIA.
rationale: AMD data-center revenue reached $5.78 billion, up 57% year over year, its rack-scale Helios system hit full production with shipments starting in the third quarter of 2026, and it added Anthropic at up to 2 gigawatts alongside Meta, OpenAI, Oracle and Microsoft commitments, though its accelerator share is still only about 5 to 7%.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether AMD's rack-scale systems ship on schedule rather than slipping into 2027.

falsifiableTrigger: ASIC market-share-pct growth falls back below GPU growth for two consecutive quarters.
mechanism: When a cloud buyer builds its own inference chip, the workloads it moves in-house no longer need a bought-in accelerator.
rationale: Custom AI chips are forecast to grow 44.6% in 2026 against 16.1% for merchant GPUs, hyperscaler in-house silicon spending is projected above $25 billion in 2026, Meta's four new in-house accelerators enter production in September 2026 explicitly to cut GPU purchases, and Broadcom carries a $73 billion AI backlog.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether in-house chips can handle frontier training rather than only inference.

falsifiableTrigger: gpuSpotPrice for H100 or GB200 drops more than 20% within a quarter.
mechanism: Scarce accelerators mean renters bid against each other, so added capacity gets absorbed before it can push hourly prices down.
rationale: Rental prices held or rose rather than fell: cloud GPU prices are up 24% from their November 2025 low, median H100 on-demand sits near $3.85 an hour across providers, and NVIDIA held a 75.0% gross margin with the same level guided for the next quarter.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to a wave of new rental capacity landing faster than workloads grow to fill it.

falsifiableTrigger: exportControlExposure eases so China DC revenue recovers above prior levels within two quarters.
mechanism: Licence rules and tariffs block sales into a large buying market, so orders that exist there never turn into shipped revenue.
rationale: NVIDIA reported no data-center Hopper shipments to China against $4.6 billion a year earlier, China revenue fell to $4,550 million, approved H200 shipments remain trivial with a 25% tariff, NVIDIA more than halved its list of authorised Asian buyers, and AMD took about $440 million of China-related charges.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether case-by-case licences start producing real shipment volume rather than paper approvals.

falsifiableTrigger: Vendor-financed GPU commitments in rpoBacklog exceed 300,000 units within two quarters.
mechanism: When the chip seller funds or guarantees the buyer's purchase, reported demand partly reflects the seller's own money rather than independent customer budgets.
rationale: NVIDIA scaled its revenue-share and backstop programme to roughly 210,000 GPUs across Firmus and Sharon AI, funded by a $25 billion bond raise, on top of earlier CoreWeave and Lambda support deals, and AMD committed up to $5 billion of equity to Anthropic alongside its compute deal.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the financed buyers can pay from their own revenue once support ends.

falsifiableTrigger: customerConcentration for the top three direct customers falls below prior shares next fiscal year.
mechanism: With half of sales resting on four buyers, one buyer trimming orders or switching to its own chip removes a large slice of revenue at once.
rationale: NVIDIA disclosed three direct customers at 21%, 17% and 16% of revenue, with the four largest above half of revenue in the prior fiscal year and rising from 12%/11%/11%, while its backstop deals push more demand toward a few vendor-financed clouds and Meta moves inference to its own chips.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to how quickly sovereign and enterprise buyers grow into a genuine third leg of demand.

falsifiableTrigger: NVIDIA DC Ethernet switch market-share-pct slips from #1 within two quarters.
mechanism: Selling the switches and the accelerators as one tested system makes swapping in a rival chip a whole-cluster redesign rather than a part swap.
rationale: NVIDIA took the top revenue spot in data-center Ethernet switching for the first time in the first quarter of 2026 on bundled Spectrum-X and Quantum gear, and named CoreWeave, Microsoft, Nebius and Tesla among first Spectrum-6 customers with photonics claimed at 5x better power efficiency across deployments above 100,000 GPUs.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to open rack and networking standards that let buyers mix suppliers inside one cluster.

falsifiableTrigger: Cost-per-token gains stall so tokenEconomics improves less than one generation cycle.
mechanism: Each drop in the price of serving a token makes more uses affordable, so buyers run more work rather than spend less.
rationale: The newest generation cuts inference cost per token about tenfold against the prior generation on Google Cloud, open-model serving costs keep falling sharply year over year, and heavy users such as AT&T now burn on the order of a trillion tokens a month.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether cheaper serving raises total spending or simply lets buyers cut their bills.

falsifiableTrigger: Prepaid HBM commitments in rpoBacklog shrink or deposits are refunded within a quarter.
mechanism: Buyers who have already paid cash deposits for memory they cannot cancel will go on to buy the accelerators that memory is meant for.
rationale: Micron holds 16 non-cancelable five-year take-or-pay agreements backed by more than $22 billion of commitments including nearly $18 billion of cash deposits, memory makers have sold out 2026 output under non-cancellable contracts, and order books now extend into 2028.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether contract terms are ever renegotiated when buyers' own demand softens.

falsifiableTrigger: exportControlExposure changes lift the sub-50% China cap or clear Blackwell within two quarters.
mechanism: Licences let a limited set of Chinese buyers purchase older parts, but the volume cap and tariff hold actual sales far below what those buyers want.
rationale: Licensing stayed case-by-case with the sub-50% cap and a 25% tariff, about ten Chinese firms are cleared for up to 75,000 chips each against roughly $10 billion of approved licences, first shipments have begun but remain trivial, and the newest generation stays banned.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to a policy change that raises the cap or clears the current top-end parts.

falsifiableTrigger: AMD or non-NVIDIA designWins in production inference keep expanding for two consecutive quarters.
mechanism: As rival software stacks run mainstream models well, the cost of moving off NVIDIA falls and price differences start to decide purchases.
rationale: Anthropic committed to up to 2 gigawatts of AMD accelerators, AMD reports software gains of 3.3x in inference and 2.4x in training over its prior release plus a 2.10x throughput improvement on a leading open model, and a Chinese team pretrained a 1.6-trillion-parameter model entirely on non-NVIDIA hardware.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether rival software holds up in day-to-day production, not just in vendor benchmarks.

falsifiableTrigger: Memory hbmSupplyCapex expansion pulls DRAM/NVMe prices down within two quarters.
mechanism: Memory is a large slice of an AI server's bill of materials, so a sharp rise in memory prices lifts the cost of every rack built.
rationale: AI-server rack component costs are inflating about 2% to 3% a week and sit 10% to 15% above baseline on memory and storage scarcity, memory component prices are up about 90% since late 2025, server memory contract prices are forecast up more than 25% quarter over quarter, and stacked-memory contract prices may roughly double into 2027.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to when the new memory fabs coming online in late 2026 actually add sellable output.

falsifiableTrigger: releaseCadence slips push a major vendor's 2H-2026 ramp into 2027.
mechanism: A supply wave only lands if every vendor's ramp happens at once, so one major vendor slipping thins out the added volume.
rationale: NVIDIA's next generation is ramping in the third quarter of 2026 and several vendors are moving to mass production together, but AMD's rack-scale part is reported to see only engineering samples and low volume in the second half of 2026 with mass production and first production tokens pushed to the second quarter of 2027, and its ramp is described as extending into the second half of 2027.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to AMD's rack-scale manufacturing schedule holding rather than sliding further.

falsifiableTrigger: AMD customerConcentration eases as its buyer base broadens over the next two quarters.
mechanism: When a handful of contracts carry most of the growth, one partner delaying or shrinking its build removes a large part of the forecast.
rationale: AMD's disclosed accelerator demand rests on a short list of very large commitments including Anthropic at 2 gigawatts, OpenAI at 6 gigawatts, Meta at up to 6 gigawatts and Oracle's 50,000-GPU cluster, and AMD itself states it depends on a small number of customers for a substantial share of business.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether mid-sized buyers pick up AMD parts alongside the marquee names.

falsifiableTrigger: Crescent Island releaseCadence slips its customer sampling past the 2H 2026 quarter.
mechanism: A chip built with ordinary memory does not need the scarce stacked memory or advanced packaging, so it can be made on capacity that is not oversubscribed.
rationale: Intel's inference chip still uses standard low-power memory of up to 480GB instead of stacked memory specifically to avoid advanced-packaging and memory contention, and its customer sampling target remains the second half of 2026 with no slip reported.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the lower memory bandwidth is good enough for real inference workloads.

falsifiableTrigger: TSMC grossMargin declines for two consecutive quarters as capacity loosens.
mechanism: When demand fills many different production lines at once, the foundry can choose the most profitable orders and raise prices.
rationale: TSMC reported a 67.7% gross margin, up 9.1 points year over year, raised full-year revenue growth guidance above 40% and lifted 2026 capex to $60-64 billion, while trade reporting says AI demand spreading into custom chips, networking and power parts is tightening both 8-inch and 12-inch nodes as well as packaging and giving foundries pricing power.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to a broad AI spending pause that empties several node families at the same time.

falsifiableTrigger: A hyperscalerCapexRevision cuts 2026 or 2027 AI capex guidance within two quarters.
mechanism: Spending that outruns the cash a business generates has to be justified by future profit, and investors who doubt that will press buyers to slow down.
note: hyperscaler-ai-spending-may-outrun-near-term-returns: applied: corroborated secondary reversal (4 distinct publishers; pending filing checkpoint)
rationale: Alphabet reported its first-ever negative free cash flow of $5.9 billion while raising 2026 capex to $195-205 billion, its shares fell about 6% on the news alongside other AI-linked names, chip stocks sold off on spending doubts in mid-July, and analysts warned a 67% jump in AI capex to $650 billion may be unsustainable.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether cloud revenue keeps accelerating fast enough to cover the higher spending.

falsifiableTrigger: NVIDIA grossMargin guidance drops below 70% in a coming quarter.
mechanism: Buyers keep paying full price because they cannot get equivalent systems elsewhere, so the vendor keeps the margin even through a product changeover.
rationale: NVIDIA held a 75.0% non-GAAP gross margin with the next quarter guided at the same level even while ramping new products, against AMD at 55% guided to about 56% and Intel at 40.4%.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to rising memory input costs and to price competition from rival rack-scale systems.

falsifiableTrigger: Top-buyer customerConcentration in CoWoS output falls below 85% within a year.
mechanism: When three buyers take almost all of a specialised production line, there is no queue of other customers ready to take the slots if one cuts back.
rationale: The top three advanced-packaging clients take over 85% of TSMC output with NVIDIA alone at about 60% or roughly 595,000 wafers and AMD at about 11%, and AMD must split its small allocation between server processors and accelerators.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether outside packaging houses build enough capacity to serve a wider set of buyers.

falsifiableTrigger: Aggregate rpoBacklog duration shortens as new commitments turn shorter-dated over two quarters.
mechanism: Buyers who fear they cannot get capacity later sign longer contracts now, which stretches the average life of the order book.
rationale: Google Cloud's backlog rose more than $50 billion in a quarter to $514 billion with only just over half expected to convert within 24 months, CoreWeave holds a $21 billion Meta commitment running to 2032, and memory take-or-pay contracts run five years with order books into 2028.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to supply loosening, which would remove the reason to book years ahead.

falsifiableTrigger: A leading model provider reports revenue (apiArr) growth stalling quarter over quarter while compute commitments keep growing.
mechanism: Model providers can only keep signing multi-year compute contracts if their own sales grow fast enough to pay for them.
rationale: Anthropic's annual revenue run rate reached over $30 billion as of April 2026 from $1 billion in January 2025 and it is committing to gigawatt-scale compute while citing customer demand, but this cycle offers only that one dated revenue figure and no comparable numbers from other model providers.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to how much of the reported revenue run rate is recurring rather than one-off.

falsifiableTrigger: Chinese domestic accelerator designWins for frontier training stall over the next two quarters.
mechanism: Domestic chips that can train large models remove a technical barrier, but appetite for imported parts stays high until domestic supply reaches the same scale.
rationale: ADJUSTED: China's home-grown accelerators can now train frontier-scale models without NVIDIA chips, but Chinese buyers still order far more NVIDIA parts than are available, so the displacement is proven in capability and not yet in volume. Two findings show a 1.6-trillion-parameter model pretrained on more than 50,000 domestic accelerators across over 35 trillion tokens, while Chinese firms ordered more than two million restricted NVIDIA parts for 2026 against roughly 700,000 units of inventory and domestic labs' own chips are judged more than two years away.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to how much domestic manufacturing capacity China can add for its own accelerators.

falsifiableTrigger: A neocloud's marginalBuyerFinancing debt load or net loss narrows for two consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Buying GPU fleets on borrowed money creates interest and depreciation costs that grow with the fleet, so revenue growth does not close the loss.
rationale: CoreWeave revenue grew about 168% from $1.9 billion to $5.1 billion while its net loss widened from $937 million to $1.2 billion, its total debt rose 16.1% in one quarter to $24.86 billion, and it roughly doubled planned capital spending to $31-35 billion for 2026.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to rental prices holding up long enough for the installed fleet to pay for itself.

falsifiableTrigger: A top hyperscaler cuts its 2027 gigawatt power target below its 2026 level.
mechanism: Accelerators cannot run without electricity and the grid gear to deliver it, so power and site readiness set the pace of installation.
rationale: Gartner projects 40% of AI data centers will be power-constrained by 2027 as data-center electricity roughly doubles from about 485 to about 950 terawatt-hours, power transformer lead times average 128 weeks with prices up 77% since 2019, and buyers now describe their plans in gigawatts such as Meta's 7 gigawatts for 2026 and a 140 megawatt national project.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to efficiency gains that let each megawatt carry more work.

falsifiableTrigger: Broadcom-plus-Marvell market-share-pct of custom ASIC co-design falls below 90% within a year.
mechanism: Designing a large AI chip needs rare engineering teams, so buyers seeking an alternative to merchant GPUs mostly queue at the same two firms.
rationale: Broadcom and Marvell together still hold an estimated 95% of custom AI chip co-design, and the only visible alternatives are early: talks between a model provider and Samsung and Chinese labs' in-house efforts judged more than two years out.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to a third design partner winning a named frontier chip programme.

falsifiableTrigger: Wistron odmMonthlyAiRevenue falls year-over-year for two consecutive months.
mechanism: Contract manufacturers only book revenue when finished servers leave the factory, so their monthly sales track real shipments rather than orders.
rationale: Wistron posted record June 2026 revenue of NT$321.82 billion, up 53.9% year over year and 10.9% month over month on AI-server and networking shipments, opened a 324,000-square-foot plant in Texas to build AI systems, and supply-chain players report an order boom running into the second half of 2026.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to component shortages that stall assembly even when orders are in hand.

falsifiableTrigger: A neocloud's marginalBuyerFinancing debt-to-equity rises above 6:1 within two quarters.
mechanism: Fleets bought with borrowed money leave a thin equity cushion, so a dip in rental income quickly threatens debt payments.
rationale: CoreWeave has raised $18.81 billion of debt against $3.5 billion of equity, a 5.4 to 1 ratio, with total debt up 16.1% in a single quarter to $24.86 billion, and NVIDIA is backstopping further purchases with rent-back guarantees for smaller clouds.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to borrowing costs and to how long contracted rental income runs.

falsifiableTrigger: Co-packaged optics adoption stalls below 5% of AI optical modules through 2027.
mechanism: Putting the optics into the switch package changes who builds the parts and adds a new packaging step that cluster wiring now depends on.
rationale: Co-packaged optics is projected to grow from about 0.5% of AI optical modules in 2026 to about 35% by 2030 with NVIDIA photonics switches shipping through 2026, first customers are named for the newest photonics Ethernet platform, and Taiwan packaging houses are newly competing for silicon photonics work.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to yield and serviceability of packaged optics in live clusters.

falsifiableTrigger: A named US fab or packaging project slips its build milestone past 2027.
mechanism: New plants inside the United States add places to make and assemble AI hardware outside Taiwan, spreading the supply base.
rationale: NVIDIA plans up to $500 billion of US-built AI infrastructure with named partners, Wistron opened a Texas plant building those systems, Micron committed $250 billion to US memory manufacturing through 2035 and broke ground in New York on July 9, 2026, and TSMC announced an incremental $100 billion US investment.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether announced projects reach production rather than stopping at groundbreaking.

falsifiableTrigger: Google Cloud or CoreWeave rpoBacklog fails to grow sequentially for two consecutive quarters.
mechanism: When a provider cannot build capacity fast enough, signed contracts pile up in the backlog and show demand earlier than reported sales do.
rationale: Google Cloud's backlog jumped more than $50 billion in one quarter to $514 billion while revenue grew 82% year over year to $24.8 billion, and CoreWeave's contracted backlog rose from $66.8 billion to $99.4 billion within months, so bookings are outrunning deliveries.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to how much of the backlog is cancellable and how fast it converts to revenue.

falsifiableTrigger: A top hyperscaler returns to positive free cash flow while holding 2027 capex guidance for two consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Once spending exceeds the cash the business throws off, buyers must raise outside money, which makes future orders depend on capital markets staying open.
rationale: Alphabet funded its quarter with $49.6 billion of equity issuance and $20.3 billion of senior unsecured notes and posted its first-ever negative free cash flow of $5.9 billion while raising 2026 capex to $195-205 billion, against combined hyperscaler spending on track for roughly $725 billion.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to borrowing costs and to investor tolerance for negative free cash flow.

falsifiableTrigger: A new accelerator generation delivers less than a 1.5x perfPerWatt gain over its predecessor.
mechanism: More work per megawatt lets a buyer with a fixed power budget install more useful capacity without new substations.
rationale: The newest rack-scale system is claimed to deliver 10x more throughput per megawatt than the prior generation and up to 10x the performance per megawatt of the equipment it replaces at an enterprise site, independent figures put the current generation at roughly 1.6x the efficiency of the one before, and new photonics networking claims 5x better power efficiency.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to the gap between vendor-claimed efficiency and what independent testing shows.

falsifiableTrigger: HBM leadTimes shorten and suppliers report unsold capacity for two consecutive quarters before end-2027.
mechanism: Each accelerator needs a fixed amount of stacked memory, so the number of memory stacks suppliers can build sets the number of accelerators that can be finished.
rationale: Micron says stacked-memory shipment growth is capped by supply rather than end demand and directly gates NVIDIA and AMD accelerator availability, memory is sold out through 2027 with order books into 2028, a major supplier says constraints may persist through 2027, and analysts see no sign of easing with shortages possibly intensifying in 2027 and 2028.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to yield on the next memory generation and how fast new packaging lines at memory makers open.

falsifiableTrigger: Memory supplier gross margin falls for two consecutive quarters as contract prices flatten.
mechanism: Scarce memory lets suppliers set prices, so more of the money paid for each AI server ends up with the memory makers instead of the system builders.
rationale: Micron's data-center segment reported $11.5 billion of revenue at an 87% gross margin and up 103% quarter over quarter, stacked-memory contract prices are forecast to roughly double into 2027, a supplier is seeking up to a 20% contract price rise for the third quarter, and rack component costs are climbing 2% to 3% a week on memory scarcity.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to new memory capacity arriving and turning today's shortage into competition on price.

falsifiableTrigger: No new sovereign or enterprise cluster above 10,000 GPUs is announced for two consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Governments and large companies buying their own clusters add a source of orders that does not depend on the big cloud providers.
rationale: A Japanese national project with the trade ministry will deploy 27,500 next-generation GPUs across 140 megawatts, a 360 megawatt campus in Indonesia is planned with up to 170,000 GPUs, a pharmaceutical company is installing a second eight-system cluster, AMD launched a part aimed at sovereign and scientific buyers, and a hosting provider signed a phased 30 megawatt deployment.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to government funding cycles and to whether announced projects are actually financed.

falsifiableTrigger: Intel data-center revenue growth falls below 10% year over year for two consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Growing server-chip sales and outside foundry work give Intel the cash and the customers to stay a third supplier of AI-adjacent hardware.
rationale: Intel's data-center and AI segment revenue rose 59% year over year to $6.3 billion, foundry revenue rose 31% to $5.8 billion, gross margin improved to 40.4% from 27.5% with about 41.0% guided next quarter, revenue beat consensus by 11.64% with guidance above expectations, and it added a named external foundry customer plus a EUR 5 billion Ireland expansion.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether external foundry customers grow beyond small first deals.

falsifiableTrigger: New vendor equity-for-compute deals in marginalBuyerFinancing stop appearing for two consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Taking a stake in a customer gives the chip seller a hand in whether that customer can afford its next order, so demand and vendor money become linked.
rationale: AMD committed a strategic equity investment of up to $5 billion in Anthropic alongside its compute deal, NVIDIA agreed to invest $5 billion in Intel common stock tied to custom processors for its platforms, and NVIDIA raised $25 billion of bonds to fund compute-for-revenue-share deals now covering roughly 210,000 GPUs.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether these investees raise independent outside funding for later purchases.

falsifiableTrigger: Standard DRAM S10 spot prices fall for two consecutive months as suppliers restore non-AI capacity.
mechanism: Memory makers move production lines to the most profitable AI parts, which leaves less standard memory for consumer and general-purpose products and pushes their prices up.
rationale: AMD is raising graphics card bundle prices about 10% citing tight memory with graphics memory spot prices roughly tripled since late 2025, standard DDR4 spot prices hit $81.20 above their prior peak while DDR5 broke $50 for the first time, and suppliers are cutting standard and embedded output to favour high-margin AI memory.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to when new memory fabs add enough output to refill the standard product lines.

sensitivity: Most sensitive to how fast new packaging and memory capacity actually comes online versus the 2027 order book.

falsifiableTrigger: AMD accelerator market-share-pct fails to rise above 7% through 2027.
mechanism: Buyers who cannot get enough NVIDIA parts sign large AMD commitments, and those commitments turn into shipped racks once AMD's rack-scale system reaches production.
rationale: AMD data-center revenue reached $5.78 billion, up 57% year over year, and it put Helios into production with named commitments from Anthropic at up to 2 gigawatts, OpenAI at 6 gigawatts, Meta at up to 6 gigawatts, Oracle, Microsoft and Rackspace, though share is still only about 5-7% and one report puts full MI455X mass production in Q2 2027.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to AMD's share of scarce packaging output, which it must split between its server processors and its accelerators.

falsifiableTrigger: ASIC market-share-pct growth falls back below GPU growth for two consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Large cloud buyers move their steady inference work onto chips they design themselves, which takes growth away from the merchant accelerators they would otherwise buy.
rationale: Forecasts put custom-chip growth at 44.6% against 16.1% for merchant GPUs in 2026 with custom systems at 27.8% of the market, hyperscaler in-house silicon spending is projected above $25 billion, Meta's new in-house inference chips enter production in September 2026, and Broadcom carries a $73 billion order book; NVIDIA's projected share falls from 87% to 75%.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether in-house chips stay captive to their owners or become rentable to outside customers.

falsifiableTrigger: gpuSpotPrice for H100 or GB200 drops more than 20% within a quarter.
mechanism: New capacity arrives more slowly than new workloads, so renters bid up the hourly rate instead of waiting for cheaper supply.
rationale: Median GB200 rental rose about 42% year over year to $18.77 per GPU-hour with H200 and B200 medians each up about 11%, cloud GPU prices are up 24% from their November 2025 low, and NVIDIA held a 75.0% gross margin with the same level guided ahead.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to a simultaneous multi-vendor supply wave landing while buyers pause new workloads.

falsifiableTrigger: exportControlExposure eases so China DC revenue recovers above prior levels within two quarters.
mechanism: Licence rules and tariffs keep the largest single foreign market mostly closed, so demand that exists there cannot be billed.
rationale: NVIDIA's China revenue fell to $4,550 million from $9,659 million with no data-center Hopper shipments in the quarter, licensed H200 volumes remain trivial despite about $10 billion of approvals, and NVIDIA more than halved its Asian buyer whitelist, while AMD carries roughly $440 million of related charges and a 25% tariff applies; the case-by-case shift is real but has produced no revenue.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether approved licences convert into actual shipments rather than staying on paper.

falsifiableTrigger: Vendor-financed GPU commitments in rpoBacklog exceed 300,000 units within two quarters.
mechanism: The chip seller supplies the money and the rent guarantee that let thinly funded buyers place orders, so some reported demand is the seller's own credit coming back as revenue.
rationale: NVIDIA raised $25 billion of bonds to scale a revenue-share and backstop programme now covering about 210,000 GPUs at Firmus and Sharon AI after earlier support for CoreWeave and Lambda, and secondary coverage flags that this concentrates demand in vendor-funded buyers.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the backed clouds can pay from real customer rentals rather than from the guarantee.

falsifiableTrigger: customerConcentration for the top three direct customers falls below prior shares next fiscal year.
mechanism: A handful of buyers place most of the orders, so one of them slowing down or switching to its own chips removes a large slice of revenue at once.
rationale: Three direct customers were 21%, 17% and 16% of NVIDIA revenue in the latest quarter, up from 12%/11%/11% two years earlier with the four largest now more than half of revenue, and the vendor-financing programme adds a further concentrated set of buyers.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to how fast the biggest buyers shift work onto chips they design in-house.

falsifiableTrigger: NVIDIA DC Ethernet switch market-share-pct slips from #1 within two quarters.
mechanism: Selling the switches and the accelerators as one system means a buyer who swaps chip vendors must also rewire the cluster, which raises the cost of leaving.
rationale: NVIDIA took the top revenue spot in data-center Ethernet switching for the first time on the back of networking bundled with Blackwell and GB300, and its next switch generation already names CoreWeave, Microsoft, Nebius, SpaceXAI and Tesla as first deployers with claimed 5x better power efficiency at over 100,000-GPU scale.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to open rack-scale standards work that would let rival accelerators reuse the same wiring.

falsifiableTrigger: Cost-per-token gains stall so tokenEconomics improves less than one generation cycle.
mechanism: When each answer costs less to produce, workloads that were too expensive become worth running, so total chip hours rise even as the price per answer falls.
rationale: The newest Rubin systems are quoted at one-tenth the inference cost per token of the prior generation, open-model token prices have fallen sharply year after year, and usage is scaling with it, with AT&T described as burning about a trillion tokens a month.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to rivals matching cost per token, since the pull-in effect helps whoever is cheapest rather than NVIDIA specifically.

falsifiableTrigger: Prepaid HBM commitments in rpoBacklog shrink or deposits are refunded within a quarter.
mechanism: Buyers who put cash down years ahead and cannot cancel have already paid for the memory, so they have strong reason to build the servers that use it.
rationale: Micron has signed 16 non-cancelable five-year take-or-pay agreements backed by more than $22 billion of cash and commitments including nearly $18 billion of deposits, suppliers sold out all 2026 output under non-cancellable contracts, and NVIDIA's own supply commitments including prepayments rose to $145 billion.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether a buyer would rather forfeit deposits than take delivery if its own demand disappoints.

falsifiableTrigger: exportControlExposure changes lift the sub-50% China cap or clear Blackwell within two quarters.
mechanism: Licences let a limited set of buyers purchase older parts under a volume ceiling, so China sales can restart but cannot return to their former size.
rationale: The case-by-case licence policy with its roughly 25% tariff and sub-50% cap remains in force, about ten Chinese firms are cleared for up to 75,000 chips each against roughly $10 billion of approved licences, first H200 shipments have begun but stay trivial and have generated no revenue, and Blackwell is still banned.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the volume cap or the tariff moves, since either alone decides how much can ship.

falsifiableTrigger: AMD or non-NVIDIA designWins in production inference keep expanding for two consecutive quarters.
mechanism: As rival software gets close enough to run the same production workloads, the cost of moving falls and price and availability start to decide the purchase.
rationale: AMD's software stack now claims 3.3x faster inference and 2.4x faster training over its prior release with a tuned kernel lifting DeepSeek throughput 2.10x, and buyers acted on it with Anthropic, OpenAI, Meta, Microsoft, Oracle and Rackspace all committing to Instinct, while NVIDIA's projected share falls from 87% toward 75%.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the announced gigawatt commitments turn into working production clusters rather than pilots.

falsifiableTrigger: Memory hbmSupplyCapex expansion pulls DRAM/NVMe prices down within two quarters.
mechanism: Memory and storage are a large part of an AI server's bill of materials, so their price rises lift the cost of every rack a buyer installs.
rationale: Server rack component costs are running up 2-3% a week and sit 10-15% above baseline on memory and storage scarcity, server memory contract prices are forecast up more than 25% in the quarter, memory component prices are up about 90% since late 2025, and next-generation contract prices for stacked memory are forecast to roughly double into 2027.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to when new memory fabrication capacity actually starts shipping bits.

falsifiableTrigger: releaseCadence slips push a major vendor's 2H-2026 ramp into 2027.
mechanism: Four vendors hitting production in the same half adds accelerator units to the market at the same time rather than in sequence.
rationale: NVIDIA's Vera Rubin entered production ramp in Q3 2026, AMD's Helios reached full production with shipments starting Q3 2026, Meta's new in-house inference chips enter production in September 2026, and supply-chain reporting has Vera Rubin, Helios, Trainium 3 and Google's chips all moving to mass production together, though one report puts AMD's own high-volume ramp in Q2 2027.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to shared inputs, since all four ramps draw on the same packaging and stacked-memory supply.

falsifiableTrigger: AMD customerConcentration eases as its buyer base broadens over the next two quarters.
mechanism: A handful of gigawatt-scale agreements carry nearly all the growth, so one partner delaying or cancelling moves AMD's whole accelerator line.
rationale: AMD's disclosed accelerator demand is a short list of very large commitments - Anthropic up to 2 gigawatts, OpenAI 6 gigawatts, Meta up to 6 gigawatts, Oracle's 50,000-GPU cluster and Microsoft - and AMD itself warns it depends on a small number of customers, while its own product launch disclosed no order quantities.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to the financing health of the model builders behind the largest commitments.

falsifiableTrigger: Crescent Island releaseCadence slips its customer sampling past the 2H 2026 quarter.
mechanism: Using ordinary memory on a simpler package lets a chip ship without a slot in the packaging and stacked-memory queue that limits everyone else.
rationale: Intel's Crescent Island inference chip still uses standard low-power memory rather than stacked memory specifically to avoid advanced-packaging and memory contention, and it remains guided to customer sampling in the second half of 2026 with no slip reported.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the cheaper memory delivers enough speed for real inference work at scale.

falsifiableTrigger: TSMC grossMargin declines for two consecutive quarters as capacity loosens.
mechanism: When many different chip types compete for the same lines at once, the foundry can fill every node and charge more for a slot.
rationale: TSMC reported a 67.7% gross margin, up 9.1 points year over year, raised full-year growth guidance to above 40%, lifted capital spending to $60-64 billion, and says its packaging shortage is limiting customer growth with a very large gap through 2029-2030, while demand spreads beyond GPUs into custom chips, networking and power parts across both mature and advanced nodes.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to a broad cut in AI capital spending, which would empty several node queues at the same time.

falsifiableTrigger: A hyperscalerCapexRevision cuts 2026 or 2027 AI capex guidance within two quarters.
mechanism: Spending grows faster than the cash the same businesses throw off, so the buildout depends on investors staying willing to fund it.
rationale: The four largest US cloud buyers plan about $725 billion of 2026 capital spending, up 77%, and Alphabet's second raise this year to $195-205 billion came with its first-ever negative free cash flow of $5.9 billion; its shares fell about 6% on the day and other AI-linked names fell with it, while analysts publicly questioned whether the spending is sustainable.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to cloud revenue growth holding up, since a single soft quarter would turn the spending into a visible loss.

falsifiableTrigger: NVIDIA grossMargin guidance drops below 70% in a coming quarter.
mechanism: Buyers accept the asking price because supply is short and no rival ships an equivalent system in volume, so cost increases pass through.
