rationale: AMD's announced accelerator commitments sit with a handful of buyers: OpenAI at 6 gigawatts, Meta at up to 6 gigawatts, Anthropic at up to 2 gigawatts, an Oracle cluster of 50,000 GPUs and a July 20 Microsoft expansion. AMD itself says it depends on a small number of customers for a substantial portion of its business, and the launch of its new accelerator family disclosed no order quantities or revenue guidance beyond those named partners.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the enterprise variants and sovereign products bring in a wider set of smaller buyers over the next few quarters.

falsifiableTrigger: Crescent Island releaseCadence slips its customer sampling past the 2H 2026 quarter.
mechanism: Using ordinary memory instead of stacked memory lets a chip skip the two scarcest steps in the chain, so it can be built when others cannot.
rationale: Intel's inference part is still guided to customer sampling in the second half of 2026 and still uses standard low-power memory of up to 480 gigabytes instead of stacked memory, specifically to avoid contention for advanced packaging and high-bandwidth memory. No shipment, order or customer has been reported.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether standard memory stays available; the same shortage is already spreading into ordinary memory parts.

falsifiableTrigger: TSMC grossMargin declines for 2 consecutive quarters as capacity loosens.
mechanism: When accelerators, custom chips, networking and power parts all queue for the same fabs, TSMC can fill every line and charge more for a slot.
rationale: TSMC reported a 67.7% gross margin, up 9.1 points year over year, with revenue up 36% and full-year growth guidance raised to above 40% from over 30%, citing very strong AI-server and high-performance computing demand. It also says packaging capacity is so tight it is limiting customer growth with a very big demand gap through 2029 to 2030, raised 2026 capital spending to $60 to $64 billion, and announced an incremental $100 billion US investment.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to competing packaging routes; Intel is targeting production at roughly half the cost of TSMC's advanced packaging in 2027.

falsifiableTrigger: A hyperscalerCapexRevision cuts 2026 or 2027 AI capex guidance within 2 quarters.
mechanism: Cloud buyers are spending far ahead of the revenue the equipment earns, so any disappointment pushes them to slow orders to protect cash.
rationale: The four largest US cloud buyers plan about $725 billion of 2026 capital spending, up about 77% from roughly $410 billion, and Alphabet raised its own guidance twice to $195 to $205 billion. Investors treated the increase as a cost rather than growth: Alphabet fell about 6% on results day alongside other AI-infrastructure names, chip stocks fell on July 16 with Micron down almost 6%, analysts warned the jump may be unsustainable, Alphabet posted its first-ever negative free cash flow of $5.9 billion, and AMD shares fell more than 8% on a capital-spending overshoot.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to cloud revenue growth; Google Cloud accelerating to 82% is the main argument that the spending is earning its keep.

falsifiableTrigger: NVIDIA grossMargin guidance drops below 70% in a coming quarter.
mechanism: Buyers keep paying NVIDIA's asking price even as it introduces new products, so the gap between its cost and its price stays wide.
rationale: NVIDIA reported a 75.0% non-GAAP gross margin with the next quarter guided at the same level, well above AMD at 55 to 56 percent and Intel at 40.4% GAAP and 41.8% non-GAAP. AMD also notes its accelerator revenue carries a gross margin slightly below its own corporate average, which sits far below NVIDIA's.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to memory and storage input costs, which are rising fast enough to squeeze margins if they cannot be passed on.

falsifiableTrigger: Top-buyer customerConcentration in CoWoS output falls below 85% within a year.
mechanism: A handful of buyers have reserved almost all the packaging output, so if one cancels there is no queue of other customers ready to take the slots.
rationale: Three separate accounts now put the top three packaging customers at more than 85% of TSMC output, with NVIDIA at roughly 60% or about 595,000 wafers and AMD at about 11% or 105,000 wafers, and NVIDIA booking more than half of the 2026 to 2027 expansion. Capacity is described as pre-booked at more than 85% for both 2026 and 2027.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether smaller custom-chip designers book capacity as alternative packaging routes at Intel, Samsung and Amkor mature.

falsifiableTrigger: Aggregate rpoBacklog duration shortens as new commitments turn shorter-dated over 2 quarters.
mechanism: Buyers who cannot get capacity today sign contracts stretching years out, so the average contract in the order book keeps getting longer.
rationale: Google Cloud's backlog rose more than $50 billion sequentially to $514 billion with just over half expected to convert within 24 months, meaning almost half runs beyond two years. CoreWeave's contracted backlog reached $99.4 billion including a $21 billion Meta commitment running to 2032, Micron signed 16 non-cancelable five-year agreements, and Broadcom carries a $73 billion AI backlog targeting $100 billion of annual revenue by 2027.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether long-dated bookings survive; they are promises, and a buyer under pressure can renegotiate them.

falsifiableTrigger: A leading model provider reports revenue (apiArr) growth stalling quarter over quarter while compute commitments keep growing.
mechanism: Model providers pay for compute out of subscription and interface sales, so rising sales mean their orders rest on customers rather than on borrowed hope.
rationale: Anthropic's annual recurring revenue reached more than $30 billion as of April 2026, up from $1 billion in January 2025, and its chief compute officer says access to compute is central to meeting customer demand. Anthropic also committed to up to 2 gigawatts of AMD accelerators, but no other model provider reported revenue this cycle, so the thesis rests on a single company.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to how thin the evidence base is; one company's figures currently carry the whole thesis.

falsifiableTrigger: Chinese domestic accelerator designWins for frontier training stall over the next 2 quarters.
mechanism: Chinese buyers cut off from NVIDIA parts fund and buy home-grown accelerators instead, so domestic suppliers grow into the gap the ban creates.
rationale: Two accounts confirm Meituan pretrained a 1.6-trillion-parameter model on more than 50,000 domestic accelerators across over 35 trillion tokens without NVIDIA chips. Domestic vendors are now also scaling commercially, with Moore Threads guiding first-half revenue up 135.1% to 149.4% and Hygon up 55.6% to 70.2%, while Chinese firms still ordered over two million restricted NVIDIA parts against roughly 700,000 units available and Chinese labs' own custom chips are judged more than two years out.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to memory access inside China, which the model builders themselves name as their main remaining limit.

falsifiableTrigger: A neocloud's marginalBuyerFinancing debt load or net loss narrows for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Renting out GPUs bought with borrowed money brings in sales quickly but the interest and depreciation grow faster, so losses widen alongside revenue.
rationale: CoreWeave's full-year revenue grew about 168% from $1.9 billion to $5.1 billion while its net loss widened from $937 million to $1.2 billion, the exact pattern the thesis describes. It also carries a $21 billion Meta commitment to 2032 even as Meta's own compute unit emerges as a potential rival.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to rental rates on older hardware, which have fallen to about $3 to $4 per GPU-hour on public price pages.

falsifiableTrigger: A top hyperscaler cuts its 2027 gigawatt power target below its 2026 level.
mechanism: A site can only run as many accelerators as its electricity supply allows, so buyers plan in megawatts and the grid sets how much hardware they can install.
rationale: Buyers now describe their plans in gigawatts rather than chips: Meta plans 7 gigawatts in 2026 and roughly double in 2027, SpaceX went from 400 megawatts to 1.4 gigawatts and guides above 2 gigawatts by year-end, Anthropic committed to 2 gigawatts and SK Telecom to a 2-gigawatt cloud. Power limits are now shaping the products themselves, with reported cuts to the next flagship's memory and power specification attributed partly to what sites can supply.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to efficiency gains; racks that do 10 times more work per megawatt stretch the same power much further.

falsifiableTrigger: Broadcom-plus-Marvell market-share-pct of custom ASIC co-design falls below 90% within a year.
mechanism: Hyperscalers need an outside partner to turn a chip idea into silicon, and until now only two firms could do that work at this scale.
rationale: Broadcom and Marvell are still estimated at about 95% of custom accelerator co-design, but two credible entrants appeared this cycle: MediaTek says its second-generation data-center chip stays on schedule for 2028 mass production using Intel packaging and runs a dual-vendor strategy, and Anthropic is in early talks with Samsung to build a custom chip on a 2-nanometre process. Neither ships yet, so the concentration holds today while the path away from it has widened.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the new entrants actually ship; both current challengers are years from volume.

falsifiableTrigger: Wistron odmMonthlyAiRevenue falls year-over-year for 2 consecutive months.
mechanism: Contract manufacturers only book revenue when finished servers leave the factory, so their monthly sales show what actually shipped rather than what was ordered.
rationale: Wistron posted record June revenue of NT$321.82 billion, up 53.9% year over year and 10.9% month over month, on AI-server and networking shipments. Server supply-chain players separately report an order boom spilling into the second half of 2026, and Wistron opened a 324,000-square-foot plant in Fort Worth to build NVIDIA systems.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to component shortages; memory lead times of 32 to 40-plus weeks could stall assembly regardless of orders.

falsifiableTrigger: A neocloud's marginalBuyerFinancing debt-to-equity rises above 6:1 within 2 quarters.
mechanism: Neoclouds borrow against the GPUs they buy, so the fleet grows with debt and a small drop in rental income threatens the interest payments.
rationale: CoreWeave has raised $18.81 billion of debt against $3.5 billion of equity, a 5.4-to-1 ratio, with total debt of $24.86 billion up 16.1% in a single quarter. Its net loss also widened to $1.2 billion, and NVIDIA has separately extended backstop and revenue-sharing support to CoreWeave and Lambda, which points to how thin the equity cushion is.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to long-term customer contracts; large multi-year commitments are what lenders are underwriting.

falsifiableTrigger: Co-packaged optics adoption stalls below 5% of AI optical modules through 2027.
mechanism: Putting the optics inside the switch package cuts power and cabling but ties cluster wiring to a new manufacturing step with its own capacity limits.
rationale: Co-packaged optics is projected to rise from about 0.5% of AI optical modules in 2026 to about 35% by 2030, with NVIDIA's photonics switches due in the second half of 2026 and early 2026 respectively. Taiwanese packaging houses are newly competing for silicon photonics work as data-center architectures upgrade, NVIDIA claims 5x better power efficiency from its photonics Ethernet, and it signed a long-term Corning partnership adding three US plants and a tenfold increase in US optical connectivity capacity.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to packaging capacity for photonics, a step that competes for the same specialised suppliers as accelerator packaging.

falsifiableTrigger: A named US fab or packaging project slips its build milestone past 2027.
mechanism: Committing money to American fabs, packaging and optics plants creates a second place these parts can be made, reducing dependence on one island.
rationale: NVIDIA plans to produce up to $500 billion of AI infrastructure in the United States with TSMC, Foxconn, Wistron, Corning, Lumentum, Coherent and Amkor, and Wistron has opened a 324,000-square-foot Texas plant. TSMC added an incremental $100 billion US investment, Micron committed $250 billion through 2035 targeting 40% of output domestically and broke ground in New York on July 9, Corning is adding three plants and over 3,000 jobs, and Intel raised its capital plan above $20 billion while ramping its newest node.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to construction and qualification timelines; announcements today produce no parts for several years.

falsifiableTrigger: Google Cloud or CoreWeave rpoBacklog fails to grow sequentially for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Cloud sellers sign contracts faster than they can install capacity, so the unfilled order book grows faster than the sales line and shows demand earlier.
rationale: Google Cloud's backlog jumped more than $50 billion in one quarter to $514 billion from $462 billion, far outpacing its reported revenue of $24.8 billion, which itself accelerated to 82% growth from 63% and 48% in the two prior quarters. CoreWeave's backlog rose to $99.4 billion from $66.8 billion in about a month, and supply-chain players report orders spilling into the second half of 2026.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to how much of the backlog converts on schedule; just over half of Google's is expected within 24 months.

falsifiableTrigger: A top hyperscaler returns to positive free cash flow while holding 2027 capex guidance for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Building capacity now costs more than the businesses generate in cash, so the buyers raise debt and sell shares to cover the gap.
rationale: Alphabet funded its quarter with $49.6 billion of equity issuance and $20.3 billion of senior unsecured notes and reported its first-ever negative free cash flow of $5.9 billion. NVIDIA raised $25 billion of bonds in June to fund customer purchases at scale, and CoreWeave roughly doubled its capital plan to $31 to $35 billion following increases by Meta, Google and Microsoft.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to borrowing costs and investor patience; shares fell about 6% when one buyer raised its spending plan.

falsifiableTrigger: A new accelerator generation delivers less than a 1.5x perfPerWatt gain over its predecessor.
mechanism: Each generation does more work for the same electricity, so a site with fixed power can serve more customers without adding megawatts.
rationale: NVIDIA's newest rack is claimed to deliver 10 times more throughput per megawatt than the previous generation, and its enterprise systems up to 10 times the performance per megawatt of the equipment they replace. An independent comparison puts the current generation at roughly a 1.6x efficiency gain over the prior one, its photonics Ethernet claims 5x better power efficiency, and SK hynix reports 2.5 times better performance per watt on its newest flash.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether vendor claims hold in the field; independent measurement shows a 1.6x gain where the vendor claims 10x per megawatt at rack level.

falsifiableTrigger: HBM leadTimes shorten and suppliers report unsold capacity for 2 consecutive quarters before end-2027.
mechanism: Every accelerator needs a fixed amount of stacked memory, so the total memory supply divided by memory per chip sets how many chips can be built.
rationale: Morgan Stanley finds no sign the memory shortage is easing and flags it intensifying in 2027 and 2028, Micron says conditions stay tight beyond calendar 2027 with order books into 2028, and SK Hynix's chief executive says constraints could persist through 2027. The clearest proof is that NVIDIA has reportedly cut the memory on its next flagship from 288 gigabytes to 192 gigabytes, with two accounts naming memory supply as the reason and describing it as a way to raise total output from a fixed memory pool.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to memory capacity additions; Samsung is raising output 50% in 2026 and SK Hynix has started mass production of the next generation.

falsifiableTrigger: Memory supplier grossMargin falls for 2 consecutive quarters as contract prices flatten.
mechanism: Memory is the scarcest part in the rack, so its makers set the price and the builders who need it absorb the increase out of their own margin.
rationale: Micron's data-center segment reported $11.5 billion of revenue, up 103% quarter over quarter, at an 87% gross margin, far above any server builder. Contract prices for the newest stacked memory are forecast to roughly double into 2027, all three suppliers locked 2026 output at high-teen to low-twenties percent price increases, and Samsung is seeking up to a further 20% rise with quotes valid for only 72 hours.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to new memory capacity arriving; announced expansions do not ship parts until late 2026 at the earliest.

falsifiableTrigger: No new sovereign or enterprise cluster above 10,000 GPUs is announced for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Governments and large companies now buy clusters at a scale that used to be reserved for cloud giants, adding a third source of orders.
rationale: A Japanese national project developed with the trade ministry will deploy 27,500 Rubin accelerators and 13,750 processors across 140 megawatts, SK Telecom will build a 2-gigawatt cloud in Korea, and Bristol Myers Squibb is deploying eight enterprise systems as a second cluster. AMD split its new family specifically to serve sovereign and high-performance computing buyers, and named AT&T and Cisco among its deployment partners.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to allocation; these buyers only get parts if the top handful of cloud customers leave supply on the table.

falsifiableTrigger: Intel data-center revenue growth falls below 10% year over year for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Better factory yields and named outside customers let Intel sell both processors and manufacturing services again, adding a third supplier to the chain.
rationale: Intel's data-center and AI segment posted $6.3 billion of revenue, up 59% year over year with $2.5 billion of operating income, foundry revenue reached $5.8 billion up 31%, and GAAP gross margin rose to 40.4% from 27.5%. It guided the next quarter to $15.8 to $16.8 billion above expectations, signed Fortinet as a named external foundry customer, announced a EUR 5 billion Ireland expansion, and won a Google order for more than 3 million units of its advanced packaging.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether its packaging suits accelerators; one account says its bridge approach fits custom chips better than high-bandwidth GPUs.

falsifiableTrigger: New vendor equity-for-compute deals in marginalBuyerFinancing stop appearing for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: The chip maker puts money into the buyer, so part of the customer's purchasing power comes from the seller and the two balance sheets become linked.
rationale: AMD committed up to $5 billion of equity in Anthropic alongside its 2-gigawatt compute agreement, confirmed by two AMD disclosures. NVIDIA invested an undisclosed amount in Safe Superintelligence alongside a compute commitment, will invest $5 billion in Intel common stock at $23.28 a share, and offers startups compute in exchange for a share of future revenue, with two initial partners covering more than 200,000 accelerators.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether these customers raise outside money; independent funding would break the link.

falsifiableTrigger: Standard DRAM S10 spot prices fall for 2 consecutive months as suppliers restore non-AI capacity.
mechanism: Memory makers move wafers to the highest-priced AI parts, so ordinary memory becomes scarce and everything built with it costs more.
rationale: AMD is raising graphics card bundle prices about 10% in July on tight memory and graphics memory spot prices that have roughly tripled since late 2025. Standard memory spot prices set new highs, with 16GB DDR4 at $81.20 up 17.5% in a month above the prior $79 peak and DDR5 breaking $50 for the first time, makers are cutting standard output to favour AI parts, and enterprise contracts now get priority flash allocation over retail.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to when new fabrication capacity comes online, which reporting puts at late 2026 at the earliest.

falsifiableTrigger: No new multi-year accelerator-to-memory supply partnership is announced for 2 consecutive quarters through 2027.
mechanism: Rather than buy memory on the open market, accelerator makers sign direct multi-year deals with the suppliers to reserve output before rivals can.
rationale: NVIDIA entered a long-term partnership with SK hynix to secure next-generation memory supply and jointly develop stacked memory, folded into a partnership NVIDIA describes as more than $500 billion covering memory supply, factory construction and cloud capacity. All three memory makers have begun full-scale development of 16-high next-generation stacks specifically for NVIDIA, targeting delivery by the fourth quarter of 2026.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether these agreements convert from letters of intent into signed, enforceable contracts.

falsifiableTrigger: The leading supplier's HBM market-share-pct falls below 50% within 4 quarters as rivals ship volume.
mechanism: One supplier makes most of the stacked memory, so whoever holds a contract with that supplier can build AI servers and whoever does not, cannot.
rationale: Three accounts now put SK Hynix at 56.4% of the stacked memory market overall, about 62% of the next-generation product, and roughly two thirds of NVIDIA's next-generation supply. Microsoft, Google and Meta have used capital reserves to lock long-term contracts, keeping that supply concentrated at the hyperscale tier.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to Samsung and Micron ramping their own next-generation output; Samsung is raising capacity 50% in 2026.

falsifiableTrigger: No new diversion prosecution or whitelist reduction is reported for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Prosecutions and shorter approved-buyer lists raise the cost and risk of reselling restricted chips, so the informal routes close.
rationale: Taiwanese prosecutors expanded a criminal probe into smuggling NVIDIA chips into China through Super Micro servers, raiding the company's Taiwan office and affiliates and detaining employees, tied to US charges alleging some $2.5 billion of servers shipped without a licence. NVIDIA separately more than halved the number of authorised Asian buyers under a new compliance whitelist.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to the size of the unmet demand behind the wall; Chinese firms ordered over two million parts against roughly 700,000 units available.

falsifiableTrigger: CoWoS lead times stay above 52 weeks through the end of 2027 while the supply gap fails to narrow below 15%.
mechanism: Packaging capacity can be added by building more lines, while memory needs new fabs and long production cycles, so the two constraints ease at different speeds.
rationale: Two accounts now put the packaging shortfall at about 10% in mid-2026, narrowed from about 20%, against TSMC capacity of roughly 120,000 to 140,000 wafers a month and industry capacity of 170,000 to 200,000. Yet lead times stay at 52 to 78 weeks with lines booked through 2027, TSMC says the gap runs through 2029 to 2030, while memory shows no easing at all with analysts flagging worse shortages in 2027 and 2028.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to alternative packaging routes; outside suppliers quote 26 to 39 weeks against TSMC's 52 to 78.

falsifiableTrigger: NAND contract prices for server drives fall for 2 consecutive quarters while Rubin deployments keep growing.
mechanism: The new rack design adds a large drive pool next to each accelerator, so every system shipped pulls far more flash than the previous generation did.
rationale: The newest generation's context memory tier is expected to pull flash demand from about 35 million terabytes this year to more than 100 million next year, with each unit carrying 576 drives for 9,600 terabytes, described as adding an Apple-sized source of demand. Enterprise contracts are already getting priority allocation over retail, and the industry has published a first standard for a high-bandwidth flash tier.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to how fast the new generation actually deploys, since the demand jump depends on those racks shipping in volume.

falsifiableTrigger: Every major cloud provider publishes list rates for its newest rack-scale systems for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Providers keep their scarcest new systems off the public page and sell them through negotiation, so the listed rates only cover older hardware.
rationale: Lambda's rendered price tables on August 5 showed no H200, GB200, GB300 or B300 line items, making B200 its newest publicly rentable part, and it quotes terms of a year or more only as custom pricing. Its catalogue also lists only NVIDIA parts with no AMD instances, while CoreWeave and RunPod still publish rates for the older H100 generation.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to supply; once the newest racks are plentiful, providers have less reason to hide the price.

falsifiableTrigger: NVIDIA accelerator market-share-pct stabilises or rises for 2 consecutive quarters while rival shipments grow.
mechanism: The whole accelerator market is growing faster than NVIDIA can supply it, so rivals absorb the overflow and NVIDIA's slice shrinks while its sales rise.
rationale: One projection has NVIDIA's accelerator share falling from a 2024 peak of 87% to 81% in 2025 and 75% in 2026, and two other accounts put it at about 70% and 70 to 80 percent, while its data-center revenue set a record at $75.2 billion. The picture is not unanimous: one low-confidence account still describes NVIDIA at as much as 90% share in a given quarter, so the direction is supported but the level is disputed.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to how share is measured; published figures for the same period range from 70% to 90%.

falsifiableTrigger: A major buyer returns to purchasing loose accelerators rather than vendor racks for a flagship cluster within 2 quarters.
mechanism: Both vendors now sell a complete rack with its own networking and software, so buyers choose between whole systems and cannot mix parts easily.
rationale: AMD launched Helios, its first production rack with 72 accelerators, 31 terabytes of memory and 2.9 exaFLOPS per rack, explicitly positioned against NVIDIA's 72-accelerator rack, and named OpenAI, Meta, Anthropic, Microsoft and Oracle as adopters. NVIDIA's own 72-accelerator rack entered production ramp across the major clouds, and both vendors now market rack-level comparisons, with AMD claiming 15% better compute and 30% more tokens per dollar than NVIDIA's rack.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to open rack standards; AMD is co-developing rack-scale standards with Meta that would loosen the bundle.

falsifiableTrigger: Power transformer lead times fall below 80 weeks for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: A data centre cannot energise until its transformers and switchgear arrive, so long waits for that equipment delay the site regardless of chip supply.
rationale: No finding this cycle reports transformer or grid-equipment lead times at all. The power constraints that did appear are about electricity supply and site capacity rather than electrical gear: power shortages are cited as prompting NVIDIA to lower product power ratings, and site power limits are named alongside memory as the reason the next flagship's memory was cut. The named binding constraints this cycle are memory, packaging and available power, not the equipment that connects a site to the grid.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether anyone reports the numbers; the thesis has now gone two cycles without a single lead-time observation.

falsifiableTrigger: Median newest-generation gpuSpotPrice falls while prior-generation rates rise for 2 consecutive months.
mechanism: Buyers chase whatever generation is newest, so older hardware competes on price while the newest carries whatever premium the seller can negotiate.
rationale: Prior-generation quotes are spread out and drifting lower: RunPod lists H100 at $2.99 per GPU-hour, Lambda at $3.99, and CoreWeave at $49.24 per 8-GPU instance on demand against $19.71 spot, while separate coverage tracks H100 rates falling from $7 to $10 an hour at launch to about $2 to $4. Meanwhile the newest parts are absent from public price pages and a new Blackwell server is priced near $500,000 against $150,000 to $180,000 for a used 8-GPU H100 server.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to the missing half of the picture; the newest systems are not publicly priced, so the premium itself is inferred rather than observed.

falsifiableTrigger: Alternative packaging upstreamLeadTimes rise above 52 weeks, or no accelerator maker places advanced-packaging volume outside TSMC for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Chip designers facing year-long waits at TSMC place work with rival packaging houses that quote half the wait, so volume starts leaving the incumbent.
rationale: Google has committed to order more than 3 million units of Intel's bridge packaging for its next chip, with delivery expected in 2028, the first concrete volume commitment outside TSMC. Intel's yield on that process has reportedly climbed above 90% targeting 2027 production at roughly half TSMC's cost, NVIDIA is reportedly weighing a shift of some output to Intel, Samsung and Amkor quote 26 to 39 weeks against TSMC's 52 to 78, and ASE and Hanmi are adding packaging capacity.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to technical fit; Intel's bridge approach is described as better suited to custom chips than to high-bandwidth GPUs, and Intel holds only about 13.7% of 2.5D capacity against TSMC's roughly 70%.

falsifiableTrigger: AMD's share of CoWoS output in pkgCapacityOrderSpread rises above 15% within 2 quarters.
mechanism: AMD has one fixed pool of packaging slots and two product lines that need them, so filling one line empties the other.
rationale: AMD still holds about 11% of TSMC packaging output, roughly 105,000 wafers, against NVIDIA at about 60%, and must split that allocation between its server processors and its accelerators, so each processor slot used cannot go to an accelerator. No finding this cycle shows AMD's allocation rising.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to alternative packaging routes at Samsung, Amkor and Intel, which could relieve the trade-off without TSMC allocating more.

falsifiableTrigger: The next flagship ships with its originally planned 288GB memory configuration within 2 quarters of launch.
mechanism: When memory is the limit, putting less of it in each accelerator lets the vendor build more accelerators from the same pool, so the product shrinks instead of the shipment count.
rationale: Two publishers now report the same cut: the mainstream next flagship drops to 192 gigabytes in an 8-high stack from a 288-gigabyte 12-high design, well below the 1-terabyte 16-high configuration previewed at the 2025 developer conference. Both name constrained memory supply as the driver, one describing the cut as a way to raise total output from a fixed memory pool, alongside data-centre power limits, with reported chip power at about 1,800 watts for the mainstream variant.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to sourcing; both accounts rest on supply-chain reports rather than any statement from NVIDIA.

falsifiableTrigger: The first Korean AI factory misses its 2027 target or the partnership is not converted from letters of intent into signed contracts within 2 quarters.
mechanism: Tying factory construction, memory supply and cloud capacity into one Korean partnership puts a full stack of the buildout in a second country.
rationale: NVIDIA's own investor materials now describe the SK partnership as a more-than-$500-billion initiative covering factory construction, next-generation memory supply and cloud deployment across Asia-Pacific, with the first factory targeted for 2027 and SK Telecom building a 2-gigawatt cloud on NVIDIA's platform with SK hynix memory. SK Hynix separately approved a 7.09 trillion won, or $4.83 billion, packaging plant in Cheongju, and the arrangement is also cited in coverage of NVIDIA's $750 billion of pending agreements.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to contract conversion; the headline figure still rests on letters of intent rather than signed orders.

falsifiableTrigger: No accelerator or system vendor announces a shipping product using the high-bandwidth flash specification within 4 quarters.
mechanism: A flash tier next to the accelerator holds data that would otherwise need stacked memory, so systems can grow without competing for the scarcest part.
rationale: SK hynix and Sandisk released the first high-bandwidth flash specification through the Open Compute Project, covering capacities up to 512 gigabytes in 8-high and 16-high stacks and three performance grades from about 0.4 to 3.0 terabytes per second, with Google and Tenstorrent joining the consortium. In parallel, the newest NVIDIA rack design already builds around large drive pools, with each context-memory unit carrying 576 drives, and SK hynix reports 2.5 times better performance per watt on its latest flash.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to flash supply itself, which is already tightening as the newest racks pull demand from 35 million to over 100 million terabytes.

falsifiableTrigger: AMD software releases deliver less than a 1.5x measured inference gain over the prior release for 2 consecutive releases.
mechanism: Software tuning lifts the speed of accelerators AMD has already sold, so its competitive case improves before any new hardware ships.
rationale: AMD reports a 2.10x end-to-end throughput gain and a 3.71x cut in time-to-first-token on its current accelerator from an optimised kernel, and claims 3.3x inference and 2.4x training gains in its newest software release. Its rack volume still lags: shipments start in the third quarter of 2026 with the ramp into the second half of 2027, and one supply-chain account puts first production output at the second quarter of 2027.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to who is measuring; every figure so far comes from AMD's own testing rather than an independent benchmark.

detail.falsifiableTrigger: SpaceX nameplate compute fails to exceed 2 gigawatts by the end of 2026 or its quarterly AI capex falls below $10 billion for 2 consecutive quarters.
detail.mechanism: A single non-cloud buyer taking a large slice of one vendor's output leaves less for everyone else and ties that vendor's shipment plan to one customer's construction schedule.
detail.sensitivity: Most sensitive to how the company funds this spending, since $15.8 billion a quarter on AI infrastructure is not covered by an announced revenue base.
detail.statement: SpaceX has built its compute fleet from 400 megawatts to 1.4 gigawatts in a year, spent $15.8 billion on AI infrastructure in a single quarter, and says it will build exclusively on NVIDIA while expecting a very significant share of NVIDIA's 2027 output.
detail.title: A rocket company becomes a top-tier accelerator buyer

detail.falsifiableTrigger: Intel's share of 2.5D packaging capacity fails to rise above 20% within 4 quarters, or its bridge packaging misses 2027 mass production.
detail.mechanism: Moving packaging work to a second supplier only relieves the shortage if every step behind that supplier can scale, and here one sole-source component is already fully booked.
detail.sensitivity: Most sensitive to the sourcing quality; the yield and cost figures come from secondary coverage with no confirmation from Intel or its customers.
detail.statement: Intel's bridge packaging is winning volume orders, but a single supplier of its silicon capacitors is already fully booked and the technology is described as a better fit for custom chips than for high-bandwidth accelerators.
detail.title: The alternative packaging route has its own choke point

falsifiableTrigger: B200 rpoBacklog falls below 2 million units for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Buyers keep committing to more accelerators than NVIDIA can build, so orders stack up ahead of deliveries.
rationale: A single new buyer, SpaceX, says it will take a very significant share of NVIDIA's 2027 output and has already leased multibillion-dollar capacity to Google and Anthropic, on top of a 3.6 million unit B200 order book and record data-center sales.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to a small number of very large buyers holding or cancelling their forward orders.

falsifiableTrigger: HBM leadTimes ease to available-on-demand and CoWoS lead times fall below 26 weeks before the end of 2027.
mechanism: Stacked memory and advanced packaging both sit ahead of chip assembly, so whichever is scarcer sets how many systems ship.
rationale: Memory stays tight through 2027 and NVIDIA is now testing four alternative memory specifications for its next flagship, while advanced packaging lines are booked through 2027.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to memory makers adding usable capacity faster than accelerator demand grows.

falsifiableTrigger: AMD accelerator market-share-pct fails to rise above 7% through 2027.
mechanism: Named gigawatt commitments and a shipping rack give buyers a second supplier they can actually order from, but volume arrives later than the announcements.
rationale: AMD beat its quarter at $11.5 billion revenue, put its rack system into production with Anthropic taking up to 2 gigawatts and Microsoft deploying at scale, yet one report still puts NVIDIA at as much as 90% of the market and AMD disclosed no order backlog.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the 2027 volume ramp lands on time.

falsifiableTrigger: ASIC market-share-pct growth falls back below GPU growth for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Every workload a cloud runs on its own chip is a rack it does not buy from a merchant vendor.
rationale: Google has ordered more than 3 million units of Intel bridge packaging for its next in-house chip for 2028 delivery, and MediaTek's first accelerator enters production in the fourth quarter of 2026 with more than $2 billion of expected revenue.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether in-house chips reach volume production on their announced dates.

falsifiableTrigger: gpuSpotPrice for H100 or GB200 drops more than 20% within a quarter.
mechanism: As more rental supply comes online, providers compete on price for the same hardware and quotes drift apart.
rationale: Published rental rates for the same card now vary more than threefold across providers, from $1.42 to $4.50 an hour, and the prior-generation H100 is quoted at $2.99 to $3.99, so rental prices are spreading out rather than holding firm.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to how much older-generation capacity is freed up as new racks arrive.

falsifiableTrigger: exportControlExposure eases so China DC revenue recovers above prior levels within 2 quarters.
mechanism: Licence rules decide which buyers a vendor may sell to, so policy sets the size of the market it can serve.
rationale: China data-center revenue is still down to $4,550 million from $9,659 million a year earlier, licensed shipments remain trivial, and NVIDIA assumes no China compute revenue in its outlook.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to any change in which chip classes regulators will license.

falsifiableTrigger: Vendor-financed GPU commitments in rpoBacklog exceed 300,000 units within 2 quarters.
mechanism: When the seller guarantees the buyer's money, reported orders partly reflect the seller's own credit rather than independent demand.
rationale: The backstop and revenue-share programme still covers roughly 210,000 accelerators across two clouds, with a discussed $350 billion facility for one model maker and an undisclosed stake taken in another customer.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether backed customers can refinance on their own terms.

falsifiableTrigger: customerConcentration for the top three direct customers falls below prior shares next fiscal year.
mechanism: When a handful of buyers take most of the output, one of them pausing removes a large slice of sales at once.
rationale: One buyer now expects a very significant percentage of next year's output, while three direct customers already account for 21%, 17% and 16% of revenue.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether new buyer tiers grow fast enough to dilute the top accounts.

falsifiableTrigger: NVIDIA DC Ethernet switch market-share-pct slips from #1 within 2 quarters.
mechanism: Selling the wiring with the compute makes it costlier for a buyer to swap in someone else's accelerator.
rationale: NVIDIA still holds the top revenue spot in data-center Ethernet switching and has now tied up long-term US optical manufacturing with Corning, but no finding compares networking growth with compute growth.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to buyers standardising on open networking they can source elsewhere.

falsifiableTrigger: Cost-per-token gains stall so tokenEconomics improves less than one generation cycle.
mechanism: Lower cost per answer makes more uses worth running, so cheaper serving pulls in extra work rather than cutting spend.
rationale: The newest systems are quoted at one tenth the cost per million tokens of the prior generation, and one large buyer expects about 90% of its fleet to serve inference or be rented out.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether cost-per-answer keeps falling with each new generation.

falsifiableTrigger: Prepaid HBM commitments in rpoBacklog shrink or deposits are refunded within a quarter.
mechanism: Customers who have already paid deposits for memory have committed to the systems that memory goes into.
rationale: Sixteen non-cancelable five-year memory agreements backed by more than $22 billion of cash and deposits still stand, and memory for 2026 remains sold out with order books stretching into 2028.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether any large deposit is renegotiated or written off.

falsifiableTrigger: exportControlExposure changes lift the sub-50% China cap or clear Blackwell within 2 quarters.
mechanism: A licence-by-licence process with a hard ceiling lets some sales through while keeping the total small.
rationale: The case-by-case licence policy, the cap at under half of comparable US sales and the 25% tariff are unchanged, shipments are still described as trivial, and licensed sales have produced no revenue.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the newest chip generation is ever cleared for sale.

falsifiableTrigger: Memory hbmSupplyCapex expansion pulls DRAM/NVMe prices down within 2 quarters.
mechanism: Memory is a large slice of each server's bill of materials, so its price sets what a finished rack costs.
rationale: Memory stays tight through 2027, rack component costs are running 2% to 3% higher per week, and even a professional graphics card has risen 55% in sixteen months.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to new memory fabs coming online and easing contract prices.

falsifiableTrigger: releaseCadence slips push a major vendor's 2H-2026 ramp into 2027.
mechanism: Each vendor's ramp is set by its own packaging and memory allocation, so new supply arrives in stages rather than together.
rationale: AMD's rack reached production with third-quarter shipments and a full new product family launched, while one supply-chain account still puts real volume at the second quarter of 2027 and a third designer's first chip only enters production in the fourth quarter of 2026.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to manufacturing delays at any one vendor.

falsifiableTrigger: AMD customerConcentration eases as its buyer base broadens over the next 2 quarters.
mechanism: When a few partners carry most of the volume, each one's schedule decides the whole growth path.
rationale: The named commitments are still a handful of very large ones, now anchored by up to 2 gigawatts for Anthropic starting in the first half of 2027, and AMD disclosed no order backlog figure to show a broader buyer base.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether smaller buyers start placing volume orders.

falsifiableTrigger: Crescent Island releaseCadence slips its customer sampling past the 2H 2026 quarter.
mechanism: Using ordinary memory instead of stacked memory takes a chip out of the queue for the scarcest parts.
rationale: Intel's standard-memory inference chip is still guided only to customer sampling in the second half of 2026, with no new evidence this cycle of volume or customers.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether standard-memory parts are fast enough for real serving work.

falsifiableTrigger: TSMC grossMargin declines for 2 consecutive quarters as capacity loosens.
mechanism: When many kinds of AI chips compete for the same factory slots, the factory can pick its price.
rationale: TSMC's margin reached 67.7% with full-year growth guidance raised above 40%, its packaging lines are booked through 2027, and it says the demand gap runs to 2029-2030.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to rival packaging capacity pulling volume away.

falsifiableTrigger: A hyperscalerCapexRevision cuts 2026 or 2027 AI capex guidance within 2 quarters.
mechanism: Spending lands years before the revenue it is meant to earn, so any doubt about payback shows up first in share prices and then in order plans.
rationale: AMD's shares fell more than 8% purely because it spent $808 million of capital against an expected $298 million, and one buyer put roughly $15.8 billion into AI compute in a single quarter, so investors are now punishing spending rather than rewarding it.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether AI revenue growth keeps pace with capital spending.

falsifiableTrigger: NVIDIA grossMargin guidance drops below 70% in a coming quarter.
mechanism: Buyers pay a premium for the leading system, which keeps the seller's margin high even during a product changeover.
rationale: NVIDIA's margin is still 75.0% with the same level guided ahead, while AMD runs at about 56% and says its accelerator sales earn slightly below its own average.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to rising memory input costs eating into margin.

falsifiableTrigger: Top-buyer customerConcentration in CoWoS output falls below 85% within a year.
mechanism: A few buyers reserve nearly all the packaging slots, so their orders alone decide whether the lines stay full.
rationale: Advanced packaging is pre-booked at more than 85% for both 2026 and 2027, with one buyer holding roughly 60% of 2026 capacity.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to any large buyer moving work to a rival packaging house.

falsifiableTrigger: Aggregate rpoBacklog duration shortens as new commitments turn shorter-dated over 2 quarters.
mechanism: Buyers book capacity years ahead to secure it, so the order book stretches further into the future than sales do.
rationale: New multibillion-dollar capacity leases with Google and Anthropic add to a $514 billion cloud backlog, a purchase commitment running through 2032 and five-year memory contracts.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to buyers switching to shorter contracts once supply loosens.

falsifiableTrigger: A leading model provider reports revenue (apiArr) growth stalling quarter over quarter while compute commitments keep growing.
mechanism: Real and rising sales from AI services give buyers the cash flow to keep paying for compute.
rationale: One buyer reported AI revenue of $2.6 billion in the quarter, up 213% on the prior quarter and 247% on the year, alongside a model provider at more than $30 billion of annual revenue.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether revenue growth keeps pace with compute commitments.

falsifiableTrigger: Chinese domestic accelerator designWins for frontier training stall over the next 2 quarters.
mechanism: Home-grown parts can do the work, but they cannot yet be built in the quantities Chinese buyers want.
rationale: The 1.6-trillion-parameter model trained on more than 50,000 domestic accelerators still stands as proof of capability, while Chinese orders of more than two million restricted parts against roughly 700,000 units of inventory show the volume gap is unchanged.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to how fast domestic manufacturing capacity grows.

falsifiableTrigger: A neocloud's marginalBuyerFinancing debt load or net loss narrows for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Buying fleets on credit means interest and depreciation grow at least as fast as the rental income they produce.
rationale: CoreWeave's revenue grew about 168% to $5.1 billion while its net loss widened from $937 million to $1.2 billion, with debt up 16.1% in one quarter.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to rental rates holding up long enough to cover fleet costs.

falsifiableTrigger: A top hyperscaler cuts its 2027 gigawatt power target below its 2026 level.
mechanism: Sites can only energise so many megawatts, so available power caps how much hardware can actually run.
rationale: Power shortages are now cited as a reason to lower a flagship accelerator's power rating to 1,800 watts, and one buyer measures its own fleet in gigawatts, going from 400 megawatts to 1.4 gigawatts in a year.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to how quickly new grid connections are delivered.

falsifiableTrigger: Broadcom-plus-Marvell market-share-pct of custom ASIC co-design falls below 90% within a year.
mechanism: If only two firms can co-design custom chips, the alternative to merchant parts is as concentrated as the thing it replaces.
rationale: MediaTek has raised its accelerator share target to 15-20%, expects more than $2 billion of revenue this year with its first chip in production in the fourth quarter of 2026 and a second in 2028, so a third design house is now taking custom work.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the newer entrant actually ships volume rather than announcing targets.

falsifiableTrigger: Wistron odmMonthlyAiRevenue falls year-over-year for 2 consecutive months.
mechanism: Contract manufacturers only book revenue when finished systems leave the factory, so their monthly sales track real deliveries.
rationale: The most recent monthly figure remains a record NT$321.82 billion, up 53.9% on the year, with supply-chain reports of an order boom running into the second half, and no newer monthly data this cycle.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to component shortages stalling final assembly.

falsifiableTrigger: A neocloud's marginalBuyerFinancing debt-to-equity rises above 6:1 within 2 quarters.
mechanism: Fleets bought with borrowed money leave a thin equity cushion if rental income falls short.
rationale: CoreWeave still carries $18.81 billion of debt against $3.5 billion of equity, a 5.4-to-1 ratio, while raising its own 2026 spending plan to $31-35 billion.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to credit staying cheap and available.

falsifiableTrigger: Co-packaged optics adoption stalls below 5% of AI optical modules through 2027.
mechanism: Building the optics into the switch package ties cluster wiring to a small set of optics suppliers and their roadmap.
rationale: NVIDIA and Corning committed to a tenfold increase in US optical connectivity capacity with three new plants, on top of adoption forecast to rise from about 0.5% of AI optical modules in 2026 to about 35% by 2030.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to reliability problems pushing buyers back to pluggable optics.

falsifiableTrigger: A named US fab or packaging project slips its build milestone past 2027.
mechanism: New domestic plants add supply that does not depend on a single island's factories.
rationale: A new long-term optical manufacturing partnership adds three US plants and more than 3,000 jobs, alongside plans to produce up to $500 billion of AI infrastructure in the United States and a $250 billion domestic memory commitment.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to construction and staffing schedules holding.

falsifiableTrigger: Google Cloud or CoreWeave rpoBacklog fails to grow sequentially for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Providers sign contracts faster than they can build capacity, so the order book runs ahead of reported sales.
rationale: Cloud backlog stands at $514 billion after a sequential rise of more than $50 billion, a neocloud backlog reached $99.4 billion, and fresh multibillion-dollar leases were signed this cycle.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to how much of the booked work actually converts to revenue.

falsifiableTrigger: A top hyperscaler returns to positive free cash flow while holding 2027 capex guidance for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Spending has outgrown the cash the core businesses throw off, so the gap is filled with borrowing and share sales.
rationale: Alphabet funded its quarter with $49.6 billion of equity issuance and $20.3 billion of notes and posted its first negative free cash flow of $5.9 billion, with 2026 spending plans still rising across the group.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to borrowing costs and investor appetite for the debt.

falsifiableTrigger: A new accelerator generation delivers less than a 1.5x perfPerWatt gain over its predecessor.
mechanism: More work per megawatt lets a buyer add capacity without adding power or packaging slots.
rationale: A new compact module is claimed at up to 25 times the work of the prior mainstream part, the newest racks at 10 times the throughput per megawatt, and even flash storage at 2.5 times the performance per watt.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether each generation keeps delivering large efficiency steps.

falsifiableTrigger: HBM leadTimes shorten and suppliers report unsold capacity for 2 consecutive quarters before end-2027.
mechanism: Each accelerator needs a fixed amount of stacked memory, so the memory pool sets the unit count.
rationale: Tight memory has pushed NVIDIA to weigh four alternative memory specifications for its next flagship and to cut its memory per accelerator from 288 to 192 gigabytes, which is a supply limit reshaping the product itself.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to yields on the newest stacked-memory generation.

falsifiableTrigger: Memory supplier grossMargin falls for 2 consecutive quarters as contract prices flatten.
mechanism: Scarcity gives memory suppliers the pricing power, so more of each server's value settles with them.
rationale: Micron's data-center segment earned an 87% gross margin on $11.5 billion of revenue, and memory suppliers are still selling out at double-digit price increases.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to new memory capacity arriving and breaking the shortage.

falsifiableTrigger: No new sovereign or enterprise cluster above 10,000 GPUs is announced for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Governments and large companies now order at a size that used to belong only to the big clouds.
rationale: A Korean carrier will build a 2-gigawatt AI cloud under a partnership described as more than $500 billion, adding to a Japanese national project of 27,500 accelerators and a pharmaceutical company's second system.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether these projects convert from letters of intent into signed orders.

falsifiableTrigger: Intel data-center revenue growth falls below 10% year over year for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Growing chip sales plus outside orders for its packaging give Intel a second way to serve AI buildouts.
rationale: Intel's data-center revenue rose 59% to $6.3 billion, it guided the next quarter to $15.8-16.8 billion at about 42% margin, and a cloud buyer ordered more than 3 million units of its packaging.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to yields and delivery on its 2027 packaging ramp.

falsifiableTrigger: New vendor equity-for-compute deals in marginalBuyerFinancing stop appearing for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: When a supplier invests in its buyer, part of the buyer's purchasing power comes from the supplier itself.
rationale: AMD's commitment of up to $5 billion in Anthropic alongside a compute deal and NVIDIA's undisclosed stake in a model maker remain the standing examples, with no new stake announced this cycle.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether these customers can raise money from outside investors.

falsifiableTrigger: Standard DRAM S10 spot prices fall for 2 consecutive months as suppliers restore non-AI capacity.
mechanism: Suppliers move capacity to the highest-paying AI parts, so everything else gets scarcer and dearer.
rationale: A professional graphics card now lists at $13,250, up 55% in about sixteen months, on top of a roughly 10% bundle price rise blamed on memory and graphics memory spot prices roughly tripling since late 2025.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to suppliers restarting standard memory lines.

falsifiableTrigger: No new multi-year accelerator-to-memory supply partnership is announced for 2 consecutive quarters through 2027.
mechanism: Reserving memory output years ahead is the only way to guarantee the parts that limit shipments.
rationale: The long-term memory partnership with SK hynix carries into a Korean AI cloud built on that supplier's newest memory, and three suppliers are jointly developing the next stacked-memory generation for NVIDIA.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether memory stays scarce enough to be worth locking up.

falsifiableTrigger: The leading supplier's HBM market-share-pct falls below 50% within 4 quarters as rivals ship volume.
mechanism: One supplier controls most of the scarcest part, so its allocation decides who can build systems.
rationale: SK Hynix still holds about 62% of the newest stacked-memory supply and provides roughly two-thirds of NVIDIA's, while the largest clouds have locked in long-term contracts.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to rival suppliers qualifying their newest memory at scale.

falsifiableTrigger: No new diversion prosecution or whitelist reduction is reported for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Prosecutions and shorter approved-buyer lists remove the middlemen that informal shipments relied on.
rationale: The criminal probe into diverted servers widened to raids and detentions tied to about $2.5 billion of unlicensed shipments, and the authorised Asian buyer list was more than halved.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to enforcement attention staying on this trade.

falsifiableTrigger: CoWoS lead times stay above 52 weeks through the end of 2027 while the supply gap fails to narrow below 15%.
mechanism: Packaging capacity can be added by building more lines, while memory capacity takes longer and is already sold out.
rationale: The packaging shortfall has narrowed to about 10% from about 20% with industry capacity around 170,000 to 200,000 wafers a month, while memory stays tight through 2027 and lines remain booked through 2027.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether new packaging lines reach usable yields on schedule.

falsifiableTrigger: NAND contract prices for server drives fall for 2 consecutive quarters while Rubin deployments keep growing.
mechanism: The newest racks add a large drive pool, so each system now pulls far more flash than before.
rationale: The industry published a first high-bandwidth flash specification with capacities up to 512 gigabytes per stack, while the new storage tier is expected to lift flash demand from about 35 million terabytes to more than 100 million next year and enterprise contracts already get priority over retail.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to flash makers adding capacity ahead of the new rack ramp.

falsifiableTrigger: Every major cloud provider publishes list rates for its newest rack-scale systems for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Providers move scarce new capacity to negotiated contracts, so it disappears from published rate cards.
rationale: One provider's public pages showed no rates at all for four newer part types on 5 August, with its newest listed part still the B200, while a rival publishes rates for the newest systems at $7.39 an hour.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to how quickly new capacity becomes plentiful enough to sell off the shelf.

falsifiableTrigger: NVIDIA accelerator market-share-pct stabilises or rises for 2 consecutive quarters while rival shipments grow.
mechanism: Rivals can only take share once their systems ship in volume, and that volume has not arrived yet.
note: nvidia-s-share-slips-while-its-sales-still-grow: applied: corroborated secondary reversal (4 distinct publishers; pending filing checkpoint)
rationale: A fresh report puts NVIDIA at as much as 90% of the market in any given quarter and describes AMD as a small challenger, which cuts against the earlier projection of a slide from 87% to 75%.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to how quickly rival racks and in-house chips reach volume.

falsifiableTrigger: A major buyer returns to purchasing loose accelerators rather than vendor racks for a flagship cluster within 2 quarters.
mechanism: Vendors now sell compute, networking and software as one cabinet, so buyers compare finished systems.
rationale: AMD launched a full family plus its own processors and software with a cloud deploying its racks at scale, and compares itself to NVIDIA on whole-rack measures such as 15% more compute and 30% more tokens per dollar.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to open rack standards letting buyers mix parts again.

falsifiableTrigger: Power transformer lead times fall below 80 weeks for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: If sites cannot get electrical gear, new capacity waits on equipment rather than on chips.
rationale: No finding this cycle reports transformer or grid equipment lead times, while the power limit now shows up inside the product as lower power ratings on the next flagship at 1,800 watts.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether anyone reports current grid equipment delivery times at all.

falsifiableTrigger: Median newest-generation gpuSpotPrice falls while prior-generation rates rise for 2 consecutive months.
mechanism: Scarce new hardware commands the premium while older parts compete on price as they become plentiful.
rationale: One provider's ladder runs $7.39 for the newest part down to $2.99 for the prior generation, and a new server costs about $500,000 against $150,000 to $180,000 for a used prior-generation one.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to how fast newest-generation capacity becomes widely available.

falsifiableTrigger: Alternative packaging upstreamLeadTimes rise above 52 weeks, or no accelerator maker places advanced-packaging volume outside TSMC for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Shorter waits and lower cost elsewhere pull packaging orders away from the incumbent.
rationale: A cloud buyer ordered more than 3 million units of Intel's bridge packaging for 2028 delivery, Intel reports a growing backlog with 2027 high-volume production, and rival routes still quote 26 to 39 weeks against 52 to 78.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether alternative lines hit production yields in 2027.

falsifiableTrigger: AMD's share of CoWoS output in pkgCapacityOrderSpread rises above 15% within 2 quarters.
mechanism: A fixed allocation of packaging slots means every processor packaged is an accelerator not packaged.
rationale: AMD still holds only about 11% of the packaging output, roughly 105,000 wafers, and must split it between its server processors and its accelerators.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to AMD winning a larger packaging allocation or moving work outside.

falsifiableTrigger: The next flagship ships with its originally planned 288GB memory configuration within 2 quarters of launch.
mechanism: With a fixed pool of memory, giving each accelerator less lets the vendor build more of them.
rationale: Two more reports put the next flagship's memory at 192 gigabytes in an eight-high stack, down from 288 in a twelve-high one, with tight memory named as the driver, and four alternative memory specifications now under review.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the newest stacked-memory generation passes validation.

falsifiableTrigger: The first Korean AI factory misses its 2027 target or the partnership is not converted from letters of intent into signed contracts within 2 quarters.
mechanism: Tying construction, memory supply and cloud capacity in one place concentrates a large share of the buildout there.
rationale: The partnership is now described as a more than $500 billion initiative with the first plant targeted for 2027 and a carrier building a 2-gigawatt AI cloud on local memory.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the letters of intent become binding contracts.

falsifiableTrigger: No accelerator or system vendor announces a shipping product using the high-bandwidth flash specification within 4 quarters.
mechanism: A standard flash tier gives system builders extra capacity without drawing on the scarce stacked-memory pool.
rationale: The first high-bandwidth flash specification is now published through an industry body, covering up to 512 gigabytes per stack and speeds from about 0.4 to 3.0 terabytes a second, with two more members joining the group.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether flash is fast enough to stand in for stacked memory in real workloads.

falsifiableTrigger: AMD software releases deliver less than a 1.5x measured inference gain over the prior release for 2 consecutive releases.
mechanism: Software tuning lifts the value of hardware already installed, so it improves the offer before new racks ship.
rationale: AMD again claims 15% better compute and 30% more tokens per dollar than the rival system and reports large software speedups, while its biggest deployment only begins in the first half of 2027.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to independent testing confirming the claimed speedups.

falsifiableTrigger: SpaceX nameplate compute fails to exceed 2 gigawatts by the end of 2026 or its quarterly AI capex falls below $10 billion for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: A buyer spending at hyperscale rates adds a new top-tier claim on each year's accelerator output.
rationale: SpaceX confirmed 1.4 gigawatts of compute against 400 megawatts a year earlier, about $15.8 billion of AI capital spending in the quarter, exclusivity with NVIDIA, AI revenue of $2.6 billion and a target above 2 gigawatts by year end.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether its AI revenue keeps funding the spending.

falsifiableTrigger: Intel's share of 2.5D packaging capacity fails to rise above 20% within 4 quarters, or its bridge packaging misses 2027 mass production.
mechanism: A single booked-out supplier of one component caps how much of the alternative packaging can actually be built.
rationale: The sole silicon capacitor supplier for Intel's bridge packaging is already fully booked, Intel holds only about 13.7% of this packaging capacity against about 70% for TSMC, and substrate mass production is not expected before 2027 at 50% initial yields.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to a second source qualifying for that component.

detail.falsifiableTrigger: MediaTek market-share-pct of AI accelerators fails to exceed 5% within 4 quarters, or its first chip misses Q4 2026 production.
detail.mechanism: A new design partner gives cloud buyers another route to their own chips, spreading work that two firms used to share.
detail.sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the first chip actually reaches volume production on schedule.
