falsifiableTrigger: B200 rpoBacklog falls below 2 million units for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Buyers keep committing to more accelerators than NVIDIA can build, so its order book and revenue guidance keep climbing faster than it can ship.
rationale: NVIDIA posted record data-center revenue of $75.2 billion, up 92% year over year, guided the next quarter to $91.0 billion, is negotiating more than $750 billion of potential infrastructure agreements, and SpaceX says it will build only on NVIDIA and expects a very significant share of 2027 output, while the B200 order book stood near 3.6 million units.
sensitivity: A cut in hyperscaler capital spending plans.

falsifiableTrigger: HBM leadTimes ease to available-on-demand and CoWoS lead times fall below 26 weeks before the end of 2027.
mechanism: Every accelerator needs both stacked memory and an advanced package, so whichever of the two is scarcer sets the ceiling on shipments.
rationale: Advanced packaging is still sold out at 52 to 78 week waits with bookings into 2027, and high-bandwidth memory is still described as sold out with tightness running past 2027, so both limits still cap what vendors can ship even though the packaging shortfall narrowed to about 10%.
sensitivity: How fast new memory fabs and packaging lines actually come online.

falsifiableTrigger: AMD accelerator market-share-pct fails to rise above 7% through 2027.
mechanism: Large buyers are signing multi-year commitments with a second accelerator vendor, which turns AMD into a real alternative once its racks ship in volume.
rationale: AMD's data-center revenue jumped 107% year over year to $6.7 billion, its filings now name OpenAI and Meta at up to 6 gigawatts each, Anthropic at 2 gigawatts and Microsoft deploying at scale, and its rack system reached production with third-quarter shipments, while its share is still small against NVIDIA and real volume waits on 2027.
sensitivity: Whether the rack ramp holds its 2027 schedule.

falsifiableTrigger: ASIC market-share-pct growth falls back below GPU growth for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Cloud operators that design their own inference chips buy fewer merchant accelerators for the same workloads.
rationale: Custom chips are still growing much faster than merchant GPUs at 44.6% against 16.1%, Meta's own parts enter production in September, and Google has ordered more than 3 million advanced packages for its next in-house chip, yet merchant GPUs still make up about 60% of one large cloud's build.
sensitivity: Whether in-house chips can handle training as well as inference.

falsifiableTrigger: gpuSpotPrice for H100 or GB200 drops more than 20% within a quarter.
mechanism: Scarce supply lets sellers hold prices, so added capacity gets absorbed before it can push rates down.
rationale: Retail listings still show prior-generation cards near $30,000 and the newer part above $35,000, the newest rack systems are quoted only privately rather than discounted, and NVIDIA held a 75% gross margin, so prices are not sagging as supply grows.
sensitivity: A sudden wave of second-hand fleets coming to market.

falsifiableTrigger: exportControlExposure eases so China DC revenue recovers above prior levels within 2 quarters.
mechanism: Licensing rules bar the strongest parts from the largest non-US market, so a share of real demand cannot be served at all.
rationale: NVIDIA's China revenue fell to $4,550 million from $9,659 million, it books no China data-center compute in its outlook, approved shipments remain trivial, it more than halved its authorised Asian buyer list, and AMD still flags the same restrictions as a risk.
sensitivity: Any policy move that clears the newest generation for China.

falsifiableTrigger: Vendor-financed GPU commitments in rpoBacklog exceed 300,000 units within 2 quarters.
mechanism: When the seller guarantees the buyer's purchase, reported demand partly reflects the seller's own credit rather than independent budgets.
rationale: NVIDIA has scaled a backstop and revenue-sharing programme covering roughly 210,000 GPUs at Firmus and Sharon AI after earlier support for CoreWeave and Lambda, is discussing a $350 billion facility for one customer's chip purchases, invested in another customer, and raised $25 billion of bonds to fund the programme.
sensitivity: Whether backstopped customers can refinance on their own.

falsifiableTrigger: customerConcentration for the top three direct customers falls below prior shares next fiscal year.
mechanism: A handful of buyers account for most of the revenue, so one of them slowing orders moves the whole result.
rationale: Three direct customers were 21%, 17% and 16% of NVIDIA revenue in the latest quarter, the prior year already showed one at 22% and another at 14%, SpaceX expects a very significant share of 2027 output, and vendor-financed neoclouds add more of the same few names.
sensitivity: Whether sovereign and enterprise buyers grow fast enough to dilute the top few.

falsifiableTrigger: NVIDIA DC Ethernet switch market-share-pct slips from #1 within 2 quarters.
mechanism: Selling the switches and the accelerators as one system raises the cost of swapping in a rival part.
rationale: NVIDIA became the revenue leader in data-center Ethernet switching for the first time, its newest switch generation launched with named cloud customers, and it claims large efficiency and cost-per-token gains from selling network and compute together, but no finding compares networking growth with compute growth.
sensitivity: Whether buyers keep choosing open networking standards for large clusters.

falsifiableTrigger: Cost-per-token gains stall so tokenEconomics improves less than one generation cycle.
mechanism: Cheaper output per query makes more uses affordable, so total spending on serving models rises even as unit prices fall.
rationale: The newest generation is claimed to cut inference cost per token roughly tenfold against the prior rack, open-model serving costs keep falling sharply each year, one telecom buyer is burning about a trillion tokens a month, and SpaceX expects about 90% of its fleet to serve inference.
sensitivity: Whether cheaper serving actually converts into paid usage.

falsifiableTrigger: Prepaid HBM commitments in rpoBacklog shrink or deposits are refunded within a quarter.
mechanism: Buyers who have already paid deposits on memory they cannot cancel have a strong reason to build the accelerators that use it.
rationale: Micron holds 16 non-cancelable five-year take-or-pay agreements backed by more than $22 billion including nearly $18 billion of cash deposits, all 2026 stacked-memory output is pre-sold under non-cancellable contracts, and order books now run into 2028.
sensitivity: Whether any large buyer walks away and forfeits its deposits.

falsifiableTrigger: exportControlExposure changes lift the sub-50% China cap or clear Blackwell within 2 quarters.
mechanism: Licences are granted one deal at a time with a hard ceiling, so China can reopen without ever becoming a large market again.
rationale: The licensing rule remains case-by-case with a cap under half of US sales and a roughly 25% tariff, about ten Chinese firms hold roughly $10 billion of approved licences, first shipments have begun but stay trivial, and China revenue is still far below its earlier level.
sensitivity: Any change to the newest generation's ban.

falsifiableTrigger: Memory hbmSupplyCapex expansion pulls DRAM/NVMe prices down within 2 quarters.
mechanism: Memory is a large slice of each server's bill of materials, so its price rises straight into the cost of every rack.
rationale: Memory lead times have stretched to 32 to 40-plus weeks with prices up about 90% since late 2025, server memory contracts are forecast up more than 25% in the third quarter, rack component costs are running 2% to 3% higher every week, and AMD says its accelerator margin already sits below its company average.
sensitivity: When new memory fabs start shipping volume.

falsifiableTrigger: releaseCadence slips push a major vendor's 2H-2026 ramp into 2027.
mechanism: Several vendors start producing new accelerators in the same half-year, but each ramps on its own schedule so the extra supply arrives in steps.
rationale: NVIDIA's newest rack is in production ramp from the third quarter, AMD's rack reached production with third-quarter shipments, and several in-house parts move to mass production together, yet one supply-chain account still puts AMD's real volume at the second quarter of 2027 and Meta's own parts start only in September.
sensitivity: Manufacturing delays at any one vendor.

falsifiableTrigger: AMD customerConcentration eases as its buyer base broadens over the next 2 quarters.
mechanism: Nearly all of AMD's accelerator growth sits in a few named agreements, so one of them changing size moves the whole line.
rationale: AMD's own filing names just two customers each planning up to 6 gigawatts, a third at 2 gigawatts, and the company itself warns of continued customer concentration, while its disclosed long-term contracted obligations are only $222 million.
sensitivity: Whether mid-sized buyers start placing orders.

falsifiableTrigger: Crescent Island releaseCadence slips its customer sampling past the 2H 2026 quarter.
mechanism: A chip built with ordinary memory does not need the scarce stacked memory or the scarce advanced package, so it can be made on capacity nobody is fighting over.
rationale: Intel's inference chip is still described as using standard low-power memory instead of stacked memory precisely to avoid the packaging and memory squeeze, with customer sampling still guided to the second half of 2026 and no volume yet.
sensitivity: Whether ordinary memory gives enough bandwidth for real inference jobs.

falsifiableTrigger: TSMC grossMargin declines for 2 consecutive quarters as capacity loosens.
mechanism: When demand from many kinds of AI chips fills every line, the foundry can raise prices instead of chasing volume.
rationale: TSMC reported a 67.7% gross margin, up 9.1 points, raised full-year growth guidance from over 30% to more than 40%, says packaging tightness is limiting customer growth with a demand gap running to 2029-2030, and lifted 2026 capital spending to $60-64 billion.
sensitivity: How quickly rival packaging capacity absorbs the overflow.

falsifiableTrigger: A hyperscalerCapexRevision cuts 2026 or 2027 AI capex guidance within 2 quarters.
mechanism: Spending is rising far faster than the cash these businesses generate, so a disappointing payback would force budgets down and orders with them.
rationale: The four largest US cloud buyers plan about $725 billion of 2026 spending, up 77%, Alphabet raised guidance again and reported its first negative free cash flow of $5.9 billion, its shares fell about 6% on the news, and analysts warned the spending pace may be unsustainable.
sensitivity: Whether cloud revenue keeps accelerating alongside the spending.

falsifiableTrigger: NVIDIA grossMargin guidance drops below 70% in a coming quarter.
mechanism: Buyers keep paying premium prices for the leading part, so new-product start-up costs do not dent the margin.
rationale: NVIDIA held a 75.0% gross margin and guided the next quarter to the same level while ramping its newest platform, against AMD near 54% and Intel near 40%.
sensitivity: How much rising memory costs eat into the margin.

falsifiableTrigger: Top-buyer customerConcentration in CoWoS output falls below 85% within a year.
mechanism: A few customers hold nearly all the booked slots, so if one cancels there is no queue of other buyers ready to take that capacity.
rationale: Advanced packaging is pre-booked at more than 85% for 2026 and 2027, with one buyer holding roughly 60% of capacity and the top three more than 85%.
sensitivity: Whether smaller chip designers can win packaging slots.

falsifiableTrigger: Aggregate rpoBacklog duration shortens as new commitments turn shorter-dated over 2 quarters.
mechanism: Buyers who fear shortage sign longer contracts, so an increasing share of future output is spoken for years ahead of delivery.
rationale: Google's cloud backlog rose more than $50 billion in one quarter to $514 billion with only just over half converting within 24 months, one neocloud holds a purchase commitment running through 2032, memory buyers signed five-year take-or-pay deals, and a wafer supplier signed a ten-year agreement.
sensitivity: Whether shortages ease enough for buyers to stop pre-booking.

falsifiableTrigger: A leading model provider reports revenue (apiArr) growth stalling quarter over quarter while compute commitments keep growing.
mechanism: Model sellers with fast-rising revenue can pay for compute out of sales rather than out of fundraising.
rationale: Anthropic's annual run-rate reached over $30 billion from $1 billion fifteen months earlier, SpaceX reported AI revenue of $2.6 billion up 247% year over year, and Anthropic's compute lead ties its buying directly to serving customer demand.
sensitivity: Whether reported run-rates translate into collected cash.

falsifiableTrigger: Chinese domestic accelerator designWins for frontier training stall over the next 2 quarters.
mechanism: Local chips have proven they can train large models, but their output is still far too small to cover what Chinese buyers want.
rationale: A 1.6-trillion-parameter model was pretrained on more than 50,000 domestic accelerators, two Chinese chip makers guided first-half revenue growth of 135% and 56%, yet Chinese firms still ordered more than two million restricted foreign parts against about 700,000 units available and their own labs' silicon is judged more than two years away.
sensitivity: How fast domestic memory and packaging supply scales.

falsifiableTrigger: A neocloud's marginalBuyerFinancing debt load or net loss narrows for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Renting out GPUs bought with borrowed money produces revenue quickly but interest and depreciation grow faster than the margin.
rationale: CoreWeave's revenue grew about 168% to $5.1 billion while its net loss widened from $937 million to $1.2 billion, its debt reached $24.86 billion at a 5.4 to 1 debt-to-equity ratio, and it still raised 2026 spending plans to $31-35 billion.
sensitivity: Rental rates staying high enough to cover financing costs.

falsifiableTrigger: A top hyperscaler cuts its 2027 gigawatt power target below its 2026 level.
mechanism: A site with fixed electricity supply can only host so many racks, so power sets the number of accelerators that can run regardless of how many are built.
rationale: Buyers now describe their fleets in gigawatts, with one at 1.4 gigawatts heading to over 2 by year-end and about 10 by end-2027, another planning 7 gigawatts in 2026, and NVIDIA is reported to be lowering product power ratings and offering several power grades because sites cannot supply enough electricity.
sensitivity: How fast new generation and grid connections are approved.

falsifiableTrigger: Broadcom-plus-Marvell market-share-pct of custom ASIC co-design falls below 90% within a year.
mechanism: New entrants winning cloud design slots spread the custom-chip work across more suppliers, so the alternative to merchant GPUs becomes less concentrated.
rationale: The two incumbent design firms are still credited with about 95% of custom AI chip co-design, but MediaTek raised its accelerator share target to 15-20% with a first chip in production in the fourth quarter of 2026 and over $2 billion of expected 2026 revenue, and Anthropic is in early talks with Samsung about its own chip.
sensitivity: Whether the new entrant's first chip actually ships on time.

falsifiableTrigger: Wistron odmMonthlyAiRevenue falls year-over-year for 2 consecutive months.
mechanism: Contract manufacturers only book revenue when finished systems leave the factory, so their monthly sales track real deliveries rather than orders.
rationale: Foxconn posted July revenue of NT$946.51 billion, up 54.19% year over year and its first month above NT$900 billion on cloud and networking products, following Wistron's record June revenue up 53.9% on AI-server and networking shipments.
sensitivity: Whether rising component prices inflate the revenue figures without more units.

falsifiableTrigger: A neocloud's marginalBuyerFinancing debt-to-equity rises above 6:1 within 2 quarters.
mechanism: GPU fleets are bought with borrowed money against contracted rentals, so a small drop in utilisation quickly threatens the thin equity underneath.
rationale: CoreWeave has raised $18.81 billion of debt against $3.5 billion of equity, a 5.4 to 1 ratio, with total debt up 16.1% in a single quarter, while it doubles its annual spending and smaller operators lean on vendor backstops.
sensitivity: Credit market appetite for GPU-backed lending.

falsifiableTrigger: Co-packaged optics adoption stalls below 5% of AI optical modules through 2027.
mechanism: Putting the optics inside the switch package changes who builds the part and ties cluster wiring to a new and fast-moving supply chain.
rationale: Co-packaged optics is projected to grow from about 0.5% of AI optical modules in 2026 to about 35% by 2030, is entering commercialisation with Taiwanese assembly houses newly competing for the work, NVIDIA's photonic switch claims 5x better power efficiency, and Corning is expanding US optical capacity tenfold.
sensitivity: Whether the new packages reach acceptable yields.

falsifiableTrigger: A named US fab or packaging project slips its build milestone past 2027.
mechanism: Building fabrication, packaging and assembly inside the United States adds capacity that does not depend on a single island.
rationale: NVIDIA plans up to $500 billion of US-built AI infrastructure with named partners, opened a Texas system plant, and announced a US optical manufacturing expansion, while TSMC added a $100 billion US commitment, Micron committed $250 billion through 2035 and MediaTek approved $5 billion of US financing.
sensitivity: Whether US sites can be staffed and powered on schedule.

falsifiableTrigger: Google Cloud or CoreWeave rpoBacklog fails to grow sequentially for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Providers cannot deliver capacity as fast as customers sign for it, so the signed but undelivered pile shows demand better than quarterly sales.
rationale: Google's cloud backlog jumped from $462 billion to $514 billion in a quarter while its cloud revenue accelerated to 82% growth, one neocloud's contracted backlog rose from $66.8 billion to $99.4 billion, and a smaller provider disclosed $2.8 billion of new multi-year contracts.
sensitivity: Whether backlog actually converts on the stated 24-month schedule.

falsifiableTrigger: A top hyperscaler returns to positive free cash flow while holding 2027 capex guidance for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Capital spending has outgrown operating cash, so buyers now raise outside money to keep building.
rationale: Alphabet funded the quarter with $49.6 billion of equity issuance and $20.3 billion of notes and reported its first-ever negative free cash flow of $5.9 billion, while NVIDIA itself raised $25 billion of bonds to finance customer purchases.
sensitivity: The cost of debt for large technology borrowers.

falsifiableTrigger: A new accelerator generation delivers less than a 1.5x perfPerWatt gain over its predecessor.
mechanism: More work per megawatt lets a fixed power budget carry more useful computing, so output grows even when sites and packaging are capped.
rationale: The newest rack is claimed to deliver ten times the throughput per megawatt of the prior one, an enterprise system claims ten times the performance per megawatt of what it replaces, the prior generation showed about a 1.6x efficiency step, and a new flash generation claims 2.5 times better performance per watt.
sensitivity: Whether vendor efficiency claims hold up in independent testing.

falsifiableTrigger: HBM leadTimes shorten and suppliers report unsold capacity for 2 consecutive quarters before end-2027.
mechanism: With a fixed pool of stacked memory, the amount of memory each accelerator carries decides how many accelerators can be built at all.
rationale: NVIDIA is reported to have cut its next flagship's memory from 288GB to 192GB with limited memory named as the reason, is assessing four alternative memory specifications because supply is tight, and suppliers say the shortage shows no sign of easing and may run into 2028.
sensitivity: How fast new memory capacity and higher stacks qualify.

falsifiableTrigger: Memory supplier grossMargin falls for 2 consecutive quarters as contract prices flatten.
mechanism: Memory is scarce and sole-sourced in places, so its suppliers set prices and take profit that used to sit with system builders.
rationale: Micron's data-center segment posted $11.5 billion of revenue at an 87% gross margin, all three suppliers locked 2026 contracts at high-teen to low-twenties percent price increases, stacked-memory contract prices are forecast to roughly double into 2027, and AMD's accelerator margin sits below its company average.
sensitivity: When added memory capacity ends the shortage.

falsifiableTrigger: No new sovereign or enterprise cluster above 10,000 GPUs is announced for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Governments and large companies are now buying clusters big enough to compete for the same scarce supply as the cloud giants.
rationale: A Japanese national project will deploy 27,500 accelerators across 140 megawatts with government involvement, a Korean carrier is building a 2-gigawatt AI cloud, a pharmaceutical company is installing a second large system, and AMD launched a chip aimed specifically at sovereign and scientific buyers.
sensitivity: Whether public funding for these projects survives budget cycles.

falsifiableTrigger: Intel data-center revenue growth falls below 10% year over year for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Growing server revenue and a foundry winning outside customers give buyers a third supplier for AI-adjacent parts and packaging.
rationale: Intel's data-center segment grew 59% year over year to $6.3 billion, gross margin rose to 40.4% from 27.5%, it guided the next quarter above expectations, its foundry revenue grew 31% to $5.8 billion with narrowing losses and capital spending above $20 billion, and Google has ordered more than 3 million of its advanced packages.
sensitivity: Whether its newest process yields hold as volume rises.

falsifiableTrigger: New vendor equity-for-compute deals in marginalBuyerFinancing stop appearing for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: When the chip seller owns part of the buyer, some reported demand is funded by the seller rather than by an independent customer budget.
rationale: AMD committed up to $5 billion of equity in Anthropic alongside its compute deal, NVIDIA invested an undisclosed amount in Safe Superintelligence alongside a platform commitment, holds a $5 billion stake in Intel, and offers startups compute for a share of future revenue.
sensitivity: Whether these stakes are ever written down.

falsifiableTrigger: Standard DRAM S10 spot prices fall for 2 consecutive months as suppliers restore non-AI capacity.
mechanism: Memory makers move wafers to the highest-priced AI parts, which starves consumer and general-purpose products and lifts their prices.
rationale: AMD is raising graphics card bundle prices about 10% on tight memory with graphics memory spot prices roughly tripled since late 2025, standard memory spot prices broke prior peaks, suppliers are cutting older memory output to favour AI parts, and enterprise contracts are taking priority over retail drives.
sensitivity: When new fabs let suppliers refill the non-AI lines.

falsifiableTrigger: No new multi-year accelerator-to-memory supply partnership is announced for 2 consecutive quarters through 2027.
mechanism: Chip designers deal straight with memory makers to reserve output rather than compete for it later on the open market.
rationale: NVIDIA entered a long-term partnership with SK hynix to secure next-generation memory and jointly develop it, three suppliers began full-scale development of a taller stack specifically for NVIDIA, and Micron signed a ten-year wafer agreement with upfront financial support.
sensitivity: Whether memory supply loosens enough to make reservations unnecessary.

falsifiableTrigger: The leading supplier's HBM market-share-pct falls below 50% within 4 quarters as rivals ship volume.
mechanism: One supplier controls most of the scarce memory and the largest buyers have pre-booked it, so access to that one source decides who can build servers.
rationale: SK Hynix holds 56.4% of the stacked-memory market overall, about 62% of the next generation and roughly two-thirds of NVIDIA's supply, while Microsoft, Google and Meta have used their cash to lock long-term contracts.
sensitivity: Whether rival suppliers qualify their next-generation parts.

falsifiableTrigger: No new diversion prosecution or whitelist reduction is reported for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Prosecutions and shorter approved-buyer lists make the informal routes into China too risky to use.
rationale: Taiwanese prosecutors expanded a criminal smuggling probe, raiding a server maker's offices and detaining employees over roughly $2.5 billion of servers allegedly shipped without licences, and NVIDIA more than halved its list of authorised Asian buyers.
sensitivity: Whether enforcement attention holds once cases conclude.

falsifiableTrigger: CoWoS lead times stay above 52 weeks through the end of 2027 while the supply gap fails to narrow below 15%.
mechanism: Packaging capacity can be added by building more lines, while memory needs new wafer fabs and yield learning, so the two limits ease at very different speeds.
rationale: The packaging shortfall is now put at about 10% in mid-2026 against about 20% in late 2025 with capacity heading toward 120,000 to 140,000 wafers a month and roughly 200,000 including outside partners, yet lines are still booked through 2027 at 52 to 78 weeks while memory tightness is expected to run through 2027 with no easing.
sensitivity: How much of the new packaging capacity is already pre-booked.

falsifiableTrigger: NAND contract prices for server drives fall for 2 consecutive quarters while Rubin deployments keep growing.
mechanism: Each new rack now ships with a very large drive pool, so flash demand grows with deployments and competes for the same limited output.
rationale: The newest generation's storage tier is expected to lift flash demand from about 35 million terabytes to more than 100 million next year with each unit carrying 576 drives, enterprise contracts already take priority over retail, rack costs are climbing 2% to 3% a week partly on drive scarcity, and the industry has published a first standard for a new flash tier.
sensitivity: How quickly flash makers add capacity.

falsifiableTrigger: Every major cloud provider publishes list rates for its newest rack-scale systems for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: When the newest systems are scarce, sellers negotiate each deal privately instead of publishing a rate anyone can take.
rationale: On 5 August one large provider's public pricing showed no H200, GB200, GB300 or B300 at all, leaving B200 as its newest publicly rentable part, longer terms are quoted only as custom pricing, and its catalogue carries no rival-vendor instances, while retail card prices remain published.
sensitivity: Whether supply loosens enough to bring the newest parts back onto public price pages.

falsifiableTrigger: NVIDIA accelerator market-share-pct stabilises or rises for 2 consecutive quarters while rival shipments grow.
mechanism: The overall market is growing faster than NVIDIA's own output can, so rivals absorb the extra growth while NVIDIA's sales still rise.
rationale: Share estimates cluster lower at roughly 70% to 80%, with one projection falling from 87% in 2024 to 75% in 2026, even as NVIDIA posted record data-center revenue up 92%, though one low-confidence account still puts it near 90%.
sensitivity: How quickly rival racks reach real volume.

falsifiableTrigger: A major buyer returns to purchasing loose accelerators rather than vendor racks for a flagship cluster within 2 quarters.
mechanism: Vendors now sell a complete rack with its own wiring and software, so buyers compare finished systems rather than individual chips.
rationale: AMD put a 72-accelerator rack into production and pitches it against NVIDIA's rack on tokens per dollar and overall performance, NVIDIA's own 72-accelerator rack is in production ramp, and the next NVIDIA design is described as an eight-rack system of 72 accelerators each.
sensitivity: Whether open rack standards let buyers mix parts again.

falsifiableTrigger: Power transformer lead times fall below 80 weeks for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: If sites are limited by how much electricity they can draw rather than by waiting for switchgear, the delay sits with the utility connection rather than with the equipment order.
rationale: This cycle's power evidence points to electricity supply itself rather than equipment delivery, with NVIDIA reported to be lowering product power ratings and offering several power grades because sites cannot supply enough power, and buyers sizing fleets in gigawatts, while no finding reports transformer or grid-gear lead times.
sensitivity: Whether any operator names electrical equipment as the reason a site slipped.

falsifiableTrigger: Median newest-generation gpuSpotPrice falls while prior-generation rates rise for 2 consecutive months.
mechanism: Scarcity sits with whatever just launched, so the price premium follows the newest hardware while older parts settle to a lower level.
rationale: Retail listings show the newer card at $35,998 against about $30,000 for the prior generation, a new top-end server runs about $500,000 against $150,000 to $180,000 used, and the newest parts are absent from public rental pages so their premium is negotiated rather than posted.
sensitivity: How quickly the newest systems reach broad availability.

falsifiableTrigger: Alternative packaging upstreamLeadTimes rise above 52 weeks, or no accelerator maker places advanced-packaging volume outside TSMC for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Much shorter quoted waits elsewhere give chip makers a reason to move some packaging work away from the incumbent.
rationale: Google has committed to more than 3 million units of Intel's bridge packaging for its next in-house chip, Intel reports very high demand and a growing backlog targeting high-volume production in 2027 at reportedly above 90% yield, alternative suppliers quote 26 to 39 weeks against 52 to 78 at TSMC, and other assembly houses are adding capacity.
sensitivity: Whether alternative packages qualify for high-bandwidth parts.

falsifiableTrigger: AMD's share of CoWoS output in pkgCapacityOrderSpread rises above 15% within 2 quarters.
mechanism: A fixed number of packaging slots must cover two product lines, so every processor packaged uses a slot an accelerator cannot have.
rationale: AMD is reported to hold about 11% of the packaging output, roughly 105,000 wafers, against one buyer at about 60%, and must split that allocation between its server processors and its accelerators, with capacity pre-booked above 85% for 2026 and 2027.
sensitivity: Whether AMD can move one of the two lines to another packaging supplier.

falsifiableTrigger: The next flagship ships with its originally planned 288GB memory configuration within 2 quarters of launch.
mechanism: Putting less memory on each accelerator lets a fixed memory pool cover more units, so the shortage shows up as smaller products rather than only fewer of them.
rationale: Two accounts now report the mainstream next flagship cut to 192GB in an 8-high stack from 288GB, with limited memory and site power named as the drivers, successive roadmap downgrades including cancelling the four-die package, and NVIDIA assessing four alternative memory specifications because supply is tight.
sensitivity: Whether taller memory stacks pass validation in time.

falsifiableTrigger: The first Korean AI factory misses its 2027 target or the partnership is not converted from letters of intent into signed contracts within 2 quarters.
mechanism: Tying construction, memory supply and cloud capacity into one programme concentrates a large share of the buildout in one country.
rationale: NVIDIA's own investor material now describes the SK partnership as a $500-billion-plus programme covering AI factory construction, memory supply and cloud across Asia-Pacific with the first factory targeted for 2027, a Korean carrier will build a 2-gigawatt AI cloud, and SK hynix approved a $4.83 billion packaging plant, though the original announcement rested on letters of intent.
sensitivity: Whether the letters of intent become signed contracts.

falsifiableTrigger: No accelerator or system vendor announces a shipping product using the high-bandwidth flash specification within 4 quarters.
mechanism: A flash tier fast enough to sit near the processor absorbs work that would otherwise need scarce stacked memory.
rationale: SK hynix and Sandisk published the first high-bandwidth flash specification through an open industry body covering up to 512GB stacks and about 0.4 to 3.0 terabytes a second with Google and Tenstorrent joining, a new flash generation claims 2.5 times better performance per watt, and the newest racks already carry 576 drives each.
sensitivity: Whether flash bandwidth is good enough for real training and serving jobs.

falsifiableTrigger: AMD software releases deliver less than a 1.5x measured inference gain over the prior release for 2 consecutive releases.
mechanism: Software tuning lifts what today's installed accelerators can do without waiting for new hardware to ship.
rationale: AMD reports a 2.10x end-to-end throughput gain and a 3.71x latency cut from a software kernel on current parts, plus 3.3x inference and 2.4x training gains over the prior software release, while one supply-chain account still puts its volume ramp at the second quarter of 2027.
sensitivity: Whether independent testing reproduces the claimed gains.

falsifiableTrigger: SpaceX nameplate compute fails to exceed 2 gigawatts by the end of 2026 or its quarterly AI capex falls below $10 billion for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: A single non-cloud buyer spending at this rate takes a meaningful slice of the same limited accelerator output the cloud giants are competing for.
rationale: SpaceX ended the quarter at 1.4 gigawatts of compute against 400 megawatts a year earlier, spent about $15.8 billion of the quarter's capital on AI infrastructure, said it will build only on NVIDIA and expects a very significant share of 2027 output, reported AI revenue of $2.6 billion up 247%, and holds multibillion-dollar capacity leases with Google and Anthropic.
sensitivity: Whether its AI revenue keeps funding the spending.

falsifiableTrigger: Intel's share of 2.5D packaging capacity fails to rise above 20% within 4 quarters, or its bridge packaging misses 2027 mass production.
mechanism: The alternative route depends on one small supplier and unproven substrate yields, so it cannot absorb much of the overflow yet.
rationale: Intel's bridge packaging is winning volume with a multi-million-unit cloud order and a growing backlog, but its sole silicon capacitor supplier is already fully booked, its share of this packaging class is only about 13.7% against roughly 70% for TSMC, substrate mass production is not expected before 2027 at about 50% initial yield, and the technique is described as better suited to custom chips.
sensitivity: Whether a second capacitor supplier is qualified.

falsifiableTrigger: MediaTek market-share-pct of AI accelerators fails to exceed 5% within 4 quarters, or its first chip misses Q4 2026 production.
mechanism: A third design house winning cloud customers gives buyers another route to custom silicon beyond the two incumbents.
rationale: MediaTek raised its accelerator share target to 15-20% from 10-15%, expects more than $2 billion of AI data-centre chip revenue in 2026 with its first chip entering production in the fourth quarter and a second in 2028, and approved $5 billion of financing, though an analyst notes its 2024 share was under 1% and calls the target very high.
sensitivity: Whether its first chip reaches production on schedule.

falsifiableTrigger: Used prior-generation server prices fall more than 40% within 2 quarters, or published prior-generation rental rates drop below $2.00 per GPU-hour.
mechanism: Older hardware costs a fraction of new and is available now, so buyers who cannot get or afford the newest systems keep running it.
rationale: A new top-end server is priced around $500,000 against roughly $150,000 to $180,000 for a used prior-generation eight-accelerator server, prior-generation cards still list in stock near $30,000, and public rental catalogues still lead with prior-generation parts.
sensitivity: How fast newest-generation supply becomes freely available.

detail.falsifiableTrigger: Wafer suppliers report spare 300mm capacity or falling wafer prices for 2 consecutive quarters.
detail.mechanism: Every new memory fab and packaging line draws on the same finite output of blank silicon wafers, so wafer supply caps how fast that new capacity can actually run.
detail.sensitivity: Whether wafer makers add capacity before the new memory fabs start pulling volume in 2027.
detail.statement: Silicon wafer makers are running their lines at full utilisation, prices are rising and buyers are signing decade-long deals, so the squeeze now reaches one step further back than memory itself.
detail.title: Silicon wafer supply tightens behind the memory crunch

detail.falsifiableTrigger: AMD's reported remaining performance obligations stay below $1 billion for 2 consecutive quarters while new gigawatt commitments keep being announced.
detail.mechanism: Announced deployment intentions can be resized or delayed until they turn into signed, non-cancellable contracts that show up as reported obligations.
detail.sensitivity: Whether the 2027 rack deployments convert into disclosed contract value.
detail.statement: AMD has announced multi-gigawatt customer commitments while reporting only $222 million of contracted obligations beyond one year, so most of its pipeline is still intent rather than firm order.
detail.title: AMD's announced gigawatt deals are not yet booked orders

falsifiableTrigger: B200 rpoBacklog falls below 2 million units for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Buyers order accelerators faster than NVIDIA can build and ship them, so orders keep piling up ahead of deliveries.
rationale: NVIDIA posted record data-center revenue of $75.2 billion, up 92% year over year, guided the next quarter to $91 billion, still carries a multi-million-unit order book, and is negotiating more than $750 billion of infrastructure agreements while server suppliers report orders spilling into the second half.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to a pause in large cloud and model-builder orders.

falsifiableTrigger: HBM leadTimes ease to available-on-demand and CoWoS lead times fall below 26 weeks before the end of 2027.
mechanism: Every accelerator needs both a packaging slot and stacked memory, so whichever is scarcer sets the shipment ceiling.
rationale: Packaging is still sold out with 52 to 78 week waits and bookings into 2027, and memory suppliers can meet only 60% to 70% of requested volume for the next accelerator generation, so both limits still cap shipments.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to how fast new memory and packaging capacity actually comes online.

falsifiableTrigger: AMD accelerator market-share-pct fails to rise above 7% through 2027.
mechanism: Large buyers want a second supplier, so AMD wins volume commitments once its rack-scale system is real.
rationale: AMD's data-center revenue reached $6.7 billion, up 107% year over year, it guided the next quarter to about $13.0 billion, its rack system is in production, and two named customers each intend to deploy up to 6 gigawatts, yet its share stays small against a rival at roughly 90%.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the rack ramp holds its schedule rather than slipping into 2027.

falsifiableTrigger: ASIC market-share-pct growth falls back below GPU growth for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Cloud buyers design their own inference chips to cut the price they pay for merchant accelerators.

sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether in-house parts can handle training as well as inference.

falsifiableTrigger: gpuSpotPrice for a current-generation part drops more than 20% within a quarter.

falsifiableTrigger: exportControlExposure eases so China DC revenue recovers above prior levels within 2 quarters.

falsifiableTrigger: Vendor-financed GPU commitments in rpoBacklog exceed 300,000 units within 2 quarters.
mechanism: The seller lends or guarantees the money its buyers use to purchase its own chips, so reported demand partly reflects its own credit.
rationale: NVIDIA is backstopping customer purchases, discussing a $350 billion facility for one buyer, running a revenue-share programme covering roughly 210,000 accelerators across two small clouds, and taking a stake in another customer.

falsifiableTrigger: customerConcentration for the top three direct customers falls below prior shares next fiscal year.

falsifiableTrigger: NVIDIA DC Ethernet switch market-share-pct slips from #1 within 2 quarters.

falsifiableTrigger: Cost-per-token gains stall so tokenEconomics improves less than one generation cycle.

rationale: The newest platform is quoted at one tenth the cost per token of the prior generation, open-model serving costs keep falling sharply each year, one carrier is burning about a trillion tokens a month, and a large new buyer expects roughly 90% of its fleet to serve inference.

falsifiableTrigger: Prepaid HBM commitments in rpoBacklog shrink or deposits are refunded within a quarter.

falsifiableTrigger: exportControlExposure changes lift the sub-50% China cap or clear Blackwell within 2 quarters.

falsifiableTrigger: Memory hbmSupplyCapex expansion pulls DRAM/NVMe prices down within 2 quarters.
mechanism: Memory is a large slice of every AI server's parts cost, so its price directly moves the build price of the machine.
rationale: Memory lead times have stretched to 32 to 40-plus weeks with prices up about 90% since late 2025, server memory contract prices are set to rise more than 25% in the quarter, rack costs are climbing 2% to 3% a week, and one supplier is seeking a 20% contract increase.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether buyers keep paying rather than trimming orders.

falsifiableTrigger: releaseCadence slips push a major vendor's 2H-2026 ramp into 2027.
mechanism: Each vendor hits production on its own schedule, so new supply arrives in steps rather than in a single flood.

sensitivity: Most sensitive to manufacturing delays at any one vendor.

falsifiableTrigger: AMD customerConcentration eases as its buyer base broadens over the next 2 quarters.
mechanism: A few very large agreements carry most of AMD's accelerator growth, so its results rise and fall with those partners.
rationale: AMD's own filing names two customers each intending up to 6 gigawatts, a third committing up to 2 gigawatts, and the company repeats that a small number of customers drive a large part of its business.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether any one of the named partners delays its deployment.

falsifiableTrigger: Crescent Island releaseCadence slips its customer sampling past the 2H 2026 quarter.
mechanism: Using ordinary memory lets a chip skip the scarce stacked-memory and advanced-packaging queues entirely.
rationale: Intel's inference part still uses standard low-power memory instead of stacked memory to avoid the packaging and memory squeeze, and it is still guided to customer sampling in the second half of 2026.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the lower memory speed is good enough for real inference work.

falsifiableTrigger: TSMC grossMargin declines for 2 consecutive quarters as capacity loosens.
mechanism: When demand from many chip types fills the same factories, the foundry can charge more for every slot.
rationale: TSMC reported a 67.7% gross margin with revenue up 36% and raised full-year growth guidance above 40%, says packaging tightness is limiting customer growth into 2029-2030, and lifted capital spending to $60-64 billion plus a further $100 billion US commitment.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to a slowdown in any one of the demand streams filling those lines.

falsifiableTrigger: A hyperscalerCapexRevision cuts 2026 or 2027 AI capex guidance within 2 quarters.
mechanism: Buyers are spending far ahead of the profits the new capacity has produced, so weak returns would force them to cut orders.

falsifiableTrigger: NVIDIA grossMargin guidance drops below 70% in a coming quarter.
mechanism: Buyers accept premium prices because no rival system matches the product, so margin survives the cost of new ramps.
rationale: NVIDIA held a 75.0% gross margin and guided the next quarter at the same level, far above AMD at 54% and Intel at 40.4% on the same measure basis.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to rising memory input costs and to credible rival systems.

falsifiableTrigger: Top-buyer customerConcentration in CoWoS output falls below 85% within a year.
mechanism: A few buyers reserve nearly all the packaging slots, so a cancellation by one leaves capacity with no ready replacement.
rationale: The top three customers still hold more than 85% of advanced-packaging output with one buyer at roughly 60%, and capacity is pre-booked at more than 85% for both 2026 and 2027.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether smaller buyers can take up released slots.

falsifiableTrigger: Aggregate rpoBacklog duration shortens as new commitments turn shorter-dated over 2 quarters.
mechanism: Buyers who fear shortage sign longer contracts, which pushes more of tomorrow's demand into today's order books.
rationale: One cloud backlog rose more than $50 billion in a quarter to $514 billion with just over half converting within 24 months, another holds a purchase commitment running to 2032, memory deals run five years, a wafer deal runs ten, and a network provider signed multi-year contracts worth over $2.8 billion.

falsifiableTrigger: A leading model provider reports revenue (apiArr) growth stalling quarter over quarter while compute commitments keep growing.

rationale: One model provider's annual revenue run rate reached more than $30 billion from $1 billion fifteen months earlier, another large buyer reported AI revenue of $2.6 billion up 247% year over year, and a model provider's compute chief ties frontier work directly to securing more capacity.

falsifiableTrigger: Chinese domestic accelerator designWins for frontier training stall over the next 2 quarters.

sensitivity: Most sensitive to how much domestic manufacturing capacity comes online.

falsifiableTrigger: A neocloud's marginalBuyerFinancing debt load or net loss narrows for 2 consecutive quarters.

falsifiableTrigger: A top hyperscaler cuts its 2027 gigawatt power target below its 2026 level.

falsifiableTrigger: Broadcom-plus-Marvell market-share-pct of custom ASIC co-design falls below 90% within a year.

sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the newest entrant actually ships on schedule.

falsifiableTrigger: Wistron odmMonthlyAiRevenue falls year-over-year for 2 consecutive months.

falsifiableTrigger: A neocloud's marginalBuyerFinancing debt-to-equity rises above 6:1 within 2 quarters.

falsifiableTrigger: Co-packaged optics adoption stalls below 5% of AI optical modules through 2027.

falsifiableTrigger: A named US fab or packaging project slips its build milestone past 2027.

rationale: NVIDIA plans up to $500 billion of US-built AI infrastructure with named partners, a contract builder opened a 324,000 square foot Texas plant, TSMC added $100 billion of US investment, a memory maker committed $250 billion through 2035, and an optics partner is opening three new plants.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to construction timelines and to skilled staffing.

falsifiableTrigger: Google Cloud or CoreWeave rpoBacklog fails to grow sequentially for 2 consecutive quarters.

sensitivity: Most sensitive to how much of the backlog actually converts on schedule.

falsifiableTrigger: A top hyperscaler returns to positive free cash flow while holding 2027 capex guidance for 2 consecutive quarters.

sensitivity: Most sensitive to borrowing costs and to investor appetite for funding the buildout.

falsifiableTrigger: A new accelerator generation delivers less than a 1.5x perfPerWatt gain over its predecessor.
mechanism: Each generation does more work for the same electricity, so a fixed power budget buys more useful compute.
rationale: The newest rack claims ten times the work per megawatt of the prior generation, an enterprise system claims ten times the performance per megawatt of what it replaces, the previous step delivered about 1.6 times, a new flash generation claims 2.5 times better performance per watt, and a space module claims up to 25 times the processing of an older part.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether vendor efficiency claims hold in real deployments.

falsifiableTrigger: HBM leadTimes shorten and suppliers report unsold capacity for 2 consecutive quarters before end-2027.

sensitivity: Most sensitive to yields on the newest memory stacks.

falsifiableTrigger: Memory supplier grossMargin falls for 2 consecutive quarters as contract prices flatten.

sensitivity: Most sensitive to new memory capacity arriving and breaking the pricing power.

falsifiableTrigger: Intel data-center revenue growth falls below 10% year over year for 2 consecutive quarters.

falsifiableTrigger: New vendor equity-for-compute deals in marginalBuyerFinancing stop appearing for 2 consecutive quarters.

falsifiableTrigger: The leading supplier's HBM market-share-pct falls below 50% within 4 quarters as rivals ship volume.

falsifiableTrigger: NAND contract prices for server drives fall for 2 consecutive quarters while Rubin deployments keep growing.

sensitivity: Most sensitive to how quickly flash makers add capacity.

falsifiableTrigger: Every major cloud provider publishes list rates for its newest rack-scale systems for 2 consecutive quarters.

falsifiableTrigger: NVIDIA accelerator market-share-pct stabilises or rises for 2 consecutive quarters while rival shipments grow.

sensitivity: Most sensitive to how fast rival supply actually ships.

falsifiableTrigger: A major buyer returns to purchasing loose accelerators rather than vendor racks for a flagship cluster within 2 quarters.
mechanism: Both vendors now sell finished racks with their own networking and software, so buyers compare whole systems instead of individual chips.
rationale: AMD's 72-accelerator rack reached full production with named adopters and a claimed 30% advantage in output per dollar, NVIDIA's 72-accelerator rack is ramping across major clouds, and a large new buyer says it will deploy whole rack systems both on the ground and in orbit.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to open rack standards that would let buyers mix parts again.

falsifiableTrigger: Power transformer lead times fall below 80 weeks for 2 consecutive quarters.

sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether grid-equipment delivery data reappears in future cycles.

falsifiableTrigger: Median newest-generation gpuSpotPrice falls while prior-generation rates rise for 2 consecutive months.

falsifiableTrigger: Alternative packaging upstreamLeadTimes rise above 52 weeks, or no accelerator maker places advanced-packaging volume outside TSMC for 2 consecutive quarters.

falsifiableTrigger: AMD's share of CoWoS output in pkgCapacityOrderSpread rises above 15% within 2 quarters.

falsifiableTrigger: The next flagship ships with its originally planned 288GB memory configuration within 2 quarters of launch.

falsifiableTrigger: The first Korean AI factory misses its 2027 target or the partnership is not converted from letters of intent into signed contracts within 2 quarters.

sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the letters of intent become signed contracts.

falsifiableTrigger: No accelerator or system vendor announces a shipping product using the high-bandwidth flash specification within 4 quarters.

sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether flash speed is close enough to substitute in real workloads.

falsifiableTrigger: AMD software releases deliver less than a 1.5x measured inference gain over the prior release for 2 consecutive releases.

sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether its AI revenue keeps funding the spending.

falsifiableTrigger: MediaTek market-share-pct of AI accelerators fails to exceed 5% within 4 quarters, or its first chip misses Q4 2026 production.

sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether its first chip reaches production on time.

falsifiableTrigger: Used prior-generation server prices fall more than 40% within 2 quarters, or published prior-generation rental rates drop below $2.00 per GPU-hour.

sensitivity: Most sensitive to how much cheaper each new generation makes the same work.

falsifiableTrigger: Wafer suppliers report spare 300mm capacity or falling wafer prices for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: New memory fabs all need the same blank wafers, so the squeeze moves one step further back in the chain.
rationale: A major wafer maker says its lines are effectively at full utilisation with constraints already appearing on some advanced 300 millimetre products, spot prices are rising with more increases expected, buyers are stretching contracts from about three years to five to eight, and a memory maker put $500 million into a ten-year supply agreement.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to how fast wafer makers add new lines.

falsifiableTrigger: AMD's reported remaining performance obligations stay below $1 billion for 2 consecutive quarters while new gigawatt commitments keep being announced.

rationale: AMD reported only $222 million of contracted obligations beyond one year, of which $144 million falls within 12 months, disclosed no backlog figure while describing strong customer pull, and its filing frames the multi-gigawatt commitments as intentions to deploy.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the named partners convert intent into signed purchase orders.

detail.falsifiableTrigger: No hardwired inference product reaches customer shipment within 4 quarters, or inference workloads stay on general accelerators for 2 consecutive quarters after launch.
detail.mechanism: A chip built for one fixed model runs it far more cheaply than a flexible accelerator, so cost-sensitive inference work can move off general parts.
detail.sensitivity: Most sensitive to how often models change, since hardwired parts lose their advantage when weights are updated.
detail.statement: Accelerator vendors are buying startups that burn model weights straight into silicon, a cheaper approach to running finished models that could take work away from general-purpose accelerators.
detail.title: Hardwired inference chips emerge as a new rival to general accelerators

detail.falsifiableTrigger: Non-cloud owners stop signing new rental or lease agreements for 2 consecutive quarters, or rented share of their fleets falls below 50%.
detail.mechanism: Owners who bought more capacity than they need rent the surplus, which turns their own purchases into a supply source for other buyers.
detail.sensitivity: Most sensitive to rental prices staying high enough to justify holding the fleet.
detail.statement: Companies that bought accelerators for their own use are now renting much of that capacity to others, adding a new layer of supply between the chip vendors and end users.
detail.title: Compute owners outside the big clouds start renting capacity out

falsifiableTrigger: B200 rpoBacklog falls below 2 million units for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Buyers commit to more accelerators than the memory and packaging chain can build, so orders keep stacking up ahead of deliveries.
rationale: Demand still runs ahead of what NVIDIA can build: data-center revenue hit a record $75.2 billion with guidance to $91.0 billion, the B200 order book stood near 3.6 million units, more than $750 billion of potential infrastructure agreements are in negotiation, and SpaceX expects a very significant share of 2027 output, while memory suppliers can cover only 60 to 70 percent of the volume NVIDIA asked for.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to a large buyer cancelling or deferring committed orders.

falsifiableTrigger: HBM leadTimes ease to available-on-demand and CoWoS lead times fall below 26 weeks before the end of 2027.
mechanism: Every accelerator needs both a packaging slot and stacked memory, so whichever is scarcer sets the shipment ceiling.
rationale: Both limits still bind: advanced packaging is sold out with 52 to 78 week lead times and bookings into 2027, stacked memory for 2026 is effectively gone, memory suppliers can meet only 60 to 70 percent of NVIDIA's request, and tight memory is forecast to run through 2027.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to memory yield gains and new packaging lines arriving faster than planned.

falsifiableTrigger: AMD accelerator market-share-pct fails to rise above 7% through 2027.
mechanism: AMD wins large commitments and ships a complete rack, but its production ramp lands a year later than the orders, so share moves slowly.
rationale: ADJUSTED: AMD's data-center sales nearly doubled to $6.7 billion in the second quarter of 2026 and its Helios racks are in production with Anthropic, OpenAI, Meta and Microsoft named, yet its accelerator share stays near 5 to 10 percent against NVIDIA at roughly 90 percent because volume shipments only ramp through 2027.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether Helios volume arrives in 2026 or slips to the second quarter of 2027.

falsifiableTrigger: ASIC market-share-pct growth falls back below GPU growth for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Large cloud buyers build their own inference chips and move volume off bought accelerators to cut cost per workload.
rationale: Custom silicon keeps taking growth: forecasts put custom-chip growth at 44.6 percent against 16.1 percent for merchant GPUs with custom systems at 27.8 percent of the market, Meta's own parts enter production in September, Microsoft is negotiating capacity for more than 300,000 of its own chips for 2027, and Google ordered more than 3 million advanced packages for its next chip.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether in-house parts reach volume production on schedule.

falsifiableTrigger: gpuSpotPrice for a current-generation part drops more than 20% within a quarter.
mechanism: Scarce new hardware keeps rental rates firm because buyers cannot get enough capacity to bid prices down.
rationale: Published rates for current parts still hold up, with the newest rentable cards quoted at $5.89 to $7.39 an hour and older cards far lower, though the gap between providers is wide, from $1.71 to $6.00 an hour for the same AMD card, so levels hold while the spread widens.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to a wave of new rack deliveries landing at rental providers at once.

falsifiableTrigger: exportControlExposure eases so China DC revenue recovers above prior levels within 2 quarters.
mechanism: Licence rules and buyer whitelists bar the largest foreign market, so a block of otherwise willing demand cannot be served.
rationale: Policy still caps the reachable market: NVIDIA booked no Hopper data-center shipments to China against $4.6 billion a year earlier, China revenue fell to $4,550 million, the company assumes no China data-center revenue at all, it more than halved the Asian customers cleared to buy its chips, and AMD still carries export-control charges and restrictions on its China parts.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to a policy change that clears higher-end parts or lifts the volume cap.

falsifiableTrigger: Vendor-financed GPU commitments in rpoBacklog exceed 300,000 units within 2 quarters.
mechanism: NVIDIA guarantees or funds its own buyers' purchases, so part of reported demand rests on credit the seller extends.
rationale: Vendor support keeps widening: NVIDIA signed memorandums with six large financial firms to mobilise more than $500 billion of outside capital for its customers, is discussing a $350 billion facility and a debt backstop for OpenAI, backs roughly 210,000 GPUs at Firmus and Sharon AI after support deals with CoreWeave and Lambda, and invested in Safe Superintelligence.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether backed customers can refinance on their own terms.

falsifiableTrigger: customerConcentration for the top three direct customers falls below prior shares next fiscal year.
mechanism: A handful of buyers place most of the orders, so one of them slowing down moves the whole revenue line.
rationale: Three direct customers were 21, 17 and 16 percent of NVIDIA revenue in the latest quarter, following a year in which the four largest were more than half of sales, and new arrangements add concentration, with SpaceX expecting a very significant share of 2027 output and vendor-financed neoclouds taking a growing block.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to sovereign and enterprise buyers growing large enough to dilute the top few.

falsifiableTrigger: NVIDIA DC Ethernet switch market-share-pct slips from #1 within 2 quarters.
mechanism: Selling the switches and cabling with the accelerators makes the whole cluster harder to swap out for a rival part.
rationale: NVIDIA took the top revenue spot in data-center Ethernet switching for the first time, named CoreWeave, Microsoft, Nebius, SpaceX and Tesla as first customers for its newest switch, claims five times better network power efficiency across clusters above 100,000 GPUs, and is expanding US optical manufacturing with Corning, but no finding compares networking growth with compute growth.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to buyers standardising on open networking that works with any accelerator.

falsifiableTrigger: Cost-per-token gains stall so tokenEconomics improves less than one generation cycle.
mechanism: Each cheaper generation makes workloads that were too costly worth running, so lower prices expand rather than shrink the market.
rationale: The newest generation cuts inference cost per token roughly tenfold against the prior one, open-model serving costs keep falling sharply year after year, and AT&T is described as burning about a trillion tokens a month, so cheaper tokens keep drawing in more work.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the next generation repeats the same size of cost cut.

falsifiableTrigger: Prepaid HBM commitments in rpoBacklog shrink or deposits are refunded within a quarter.
mechanism: Buyers who put cash down years ahead for memory have already paid for the accelerators that memory will go into.
rationale: Micron holds 16 non-cancelable five-year take-or-pay agreements backed by more than $22 billion including nearly $18 billion of cash deposits, suppliers sold out all 2026 output under non-cancellable contracts at high-teen to low-twenties price rises, and order books now extend into 2028.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to any renegotiation or refund of the prepaid deposits.

falsifiableTrigger: exportControlExposure changes lift the sub-50% China cap or clear Blackwell within 2 quarters.
mechanism: Approvals come one buyer at a time under a volume cap and a tariff, so the market reopens only part way.
rationale: The rules are unchanged and the ceiling still holds: licensing moved to case-by-case for the mid-tier parts with a 25 percent tariff and a cap under half of US sales, about ten Chinese firms are cleared for up to 75,000 chips each with roughly $10 billion of licences approved, yet shipments remain trivial, top-end parts stay banned and China revenue sits at $4,550 million.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether approved licences turn into actual shipments.

falsifiableTrigger: Memory hbmSupplyCapex expansion pulls DRAM/NVMe prices down within 2 quarters.
mechanism: Memory is a large slice of each server bill, so its price rises pass straight through into what a rack costs to build.
rationale: Costs keep climbing: Micron says it can supply only about half of demand and calls memory the top constraint for large customers, memory component lead times have stretched to 32 to 40-plus weeks with prices up about 90 percent since late 2025, server memory prices are set to rise 18 percent in the quarter, and rack component costs are inflating 2 to 3 percent a week, although one contract builder says high memory prices have not yet slowed customer spending.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to new memory fabs coming online and easing contract prices.

falsifiableTrigger: releaseCadence slips push a major vendor's 2H-2026 ramp into 2027.
mechanism: Each vendor's ramp depends on its own packaging and memory allocation, so the new parts arrive one after another rather than together.
rationale: The wave still lands in stages: NVIDIA's newest rack entered production ramp in the third quarter, AMD's rack reached production with third-quarter shipment start ramping into the second half of 2027 and one account puts real volume at the second quarter of 2027, Meta's in-house parts enter production in September, and AMD's sovereign variant ships in early 2027.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to further manufacturing delays at any one vendor.

falsifiableTrigger: AMD customerConcentration eases as its buyer base broadens over the next 2 quarters.
mechanism: A handful of very large commitments carry the growth, so one of them changing plans swings the whole business.
rationale: AMD's own filings now name the concentration: OpenAI and Meta each intend to deploy up to 6 gigawatts under multi-year agreements with warrant incentives, Anthropic takes up to 2 gigawatts starting in the first half of 2027, and the risk factors state a small number of customers will keep making up a substantial part of revenue.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether enterprise and sovereign buyers add volume outside the named few.

falsifiableTrigger: Crescent Island releaseCadence slips its customer sampling past the 2H 2026 quarter.
mechanism: Using ordinary memory lets a chip skip the queue for stacked memory and advanced packaging that limits everyone else.
rationale: Intel's inference chip still uses standard low-power memory rather than stacked memory to avoid the packaging and memory queue, with customer sampling guided to the second half of 2026 and capacities up to 480 gigabytes; no finding this cycle shows shipments or design wins.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether any named customer actually adopts the part.

falsifiableTrigger: TSMC grossMargin declines for 2 consecutive quarters as capacity loosens.
mechanism: Demand from accelerators, custom chips, networking and power parts fills the same lines, so the maker can hold firm on price.
rationale: TSMC's July revenue rose 44.7 percent year over year, it raised full-year growth guidance to slightly above 40 percent and capex to $60-64 billion, reported a 67.7 percent gross margin, and says packaging tightness is limiting customer growth with the demand gap running to 2029-2030.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to customers moving volume to rival foundries and packaging houses.

falsifiableTrigger: A hyperscalerCapexRevision cuts 2026 or 2027 AI capex guidance within 2 quarters.
mechanism: Buyers are spending far ahead of the revenue the capacity earns, so a disappointing payback would cut future orders.
rationale: Spending keeps rising, at about $725 billion across the four largest buyers, up 77 percent, but investors are treating it as a cost: Alphabet fell about 6 percent on its raised budget, chip stocks fell on spending jitters, analysts warned the jump may be unsustainable, and AMD shares fell more than 8 percent on a capital-spending overshoot.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to cloud revenue growth keeping pace with the spending.

falsifiableTrigger: NVIDIA grossMargin guidance drops below 70% in a coming quarter.
mechanism: Buyers pay a premium for the leading system, so the maker keeps a wide margin even while ramping new products.
rationale: NVIDIA's gross margin was 75.0 percent with the next quarter guided to the same level, well above AMD at 54 to 56 percent and Intel at about 40 to 42 percent.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to rising memory input costs and to price competition from rival racks.

falsifiableTrigger: Top-buyer customerConcentration in CoWoS output falls below 85% within a year.
mechanism: A few buyers hold nearly all the booked slots, so capacity freed by any one of them has no ready replacement.
rationale: Advanced packaging is pre-booked above 85 percent for 2026 and 2027 with the top three customers holding more than 85 percent of capacity, NVIDIA alone at roughly 60 percent, and reporting now puts NVIDIA's 2026 reservation at 800,000 to 850,000 wafers, over half the year's total.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to smaller chip designers securing their own packaging allocations.

falsifiableTrigger: Aggregate rpoBacklog duration shortens as new commitments turn shorter-dated over 2 quarters.
mechanism: Buyers who fear shortages sign longer contracts, which pushes a growing share of demand years into the future.
rationale: Commitments keep stretching out: Google Cloud's backlog rose more than $50 billion to $514 billion with just over half converting within 24 months, CoreWeave holds a Meta commitment running through 2032, a wafer maker signed a 10-year supply deal, wafer buyers are moving contracts from about three years to five to eight years, and SpaceX has multibillion-dollar multi-year capacity leases.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to supply loosening enough that buyers stop pre-booking.

falsifiableTrigger: A leading model provider reports revenue (apiArr) growth stalling quarter over quarter while compute commitments keep growing.
mechanism: Model sellers fund their compute contracts out of fast-growing sales rather than out of hope, which makes their orders more likely to stick.
rationale: Revenue keeps climbing behind the spending: Anthropic's annualised revenue passed $30 billion from $1 billion 15 months earlier, SpaceX reported AI revenue of $2.6 billion up 247 percent year over year, and Anthropic frames compute access as central to serving customer demand.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to price competition pulling down what customers pay per token.

falsifiableTrigger: Chinese domestic accelerator designWins for frontier training stall over the next 2 quarters.
mechanism: Blocked buyers turn to home-grown parts, which proves the capability long before local output can cover the volume they want.
rationale: The picture is unchanged: a 1.6-trillion-parameter model was pretrained on more than 50,000 domestic accelerators across over 35 trillion tokens, Chinese suppliers are scaling fast with Moore Threads guiding first-half revenue up about 135 to 149 percent and holding a 56.95 percent gross margin, yet Chinese firms ordered more than two million restricted NVIDIA parts for 2026 against roughly 700,000 units of inventory and domestic labs' own chips are judged more than two years out.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to how fast domestic suppliers can raise production volume.

falsifiableTrigger: A neocloud's marginalBuyerFinancing debt load or net loss narrows for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Buying fleets on borrowed money means depreciation and interest grow faster than the rental income they produce.
rationale: CoreWeave's revenue grew about 168 percent to $5.1 billion while its net loss widened from $937 million to $1.2 billion, its debt reached $24.86 billion against $3.5 billion of equity, and it still raised 2026 capital spending to $31-35 billion.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to rental rates holding while borrowing costs stay affordable.

falsifiableTrigger: A top hyperscaler cuts its 2027 gigawatt power target below its 2026 level.
mechanism: Sites can only host as many accelerators as they can power and cool, so electricity sets the deployment ceiling.
rationale: Power now shapes the products themselves: NVIDIA is reported to be lowering power specifications on its next flagship and cutting its memory partly because sites cannot supply enough electricity, Meta plans 7 gigawatts in 2026 and roughly double in 2027, SpaceX sizes its fleet in gigawatts to over 2 by year end and about 10 by end-2027, and a Texas connection queue of roughly 474 GW yields only about 1.2 GW of actual additions.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to how quickly new generation and grid connections are approved.

falsifiableTrigger: Broadcom-plus-Marvell market-share-pct of custom ASIC co-design falls below 90% within a year.
mechanism: New design partners and direct foundry deals give buyers routes to custom chips that do not pass through the two incumbent firms.
rationale: The two-firm grip is loosening: MediaTek raised its accelerator share target to 15-20 percent with a first chip in production in the fourth quarter of 2026 and more than $2 billion of expected 2026 revenue, Anthropic is in early talks with Samsung for a custom chip, and Microsoft is negotiating foundry capacity directly for its own part, even though the two incumbents are still estimated at about 95 percent of co-design work.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the new entrants deliver working chips on schedule.

falsifiableTrigger: Wistron odmMonthlyAiRevenue falls year-over-year for 2 consecutive months.
mechanism: Contract builders bill only when systems actually ship, so their monthly sales are a direct check on real deliveries.
rationale: Contract makers keep setting records: Foxconn's July revenue reached NT$946.51 billion, up 54.19 percent year over year and its first month above NT$900 billion, Wistron posted record June revenue up 53.9 percent with AI servers now 95 percent of its server business, and TSMC's July revenue rose 44.7 percent.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to component shortages stalling assembly regardless of orders.

falsifiableTrigger: A neocloud's marginalBuyerFinancing debt-to-equity rises above 6:1 within 2 quarters.
mechanism: Fleets bought on borrowed money leave a thin equity cushion, so a dip in rental income quickly threatens the lenders.
rationale: CoreWeave carries $18.81 billion of debt against $3.5 billion of equity, a 5.4 to 1 ratio, with total debt up 16.1 percent in a quarter, while it doubles capital spending to $31-35 billion and NVIDIA works to mobilise more than $500 billion of outside capital for customers like it.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to credit conditions and to the resale value of used accelerators.

falsifiableTrigger: Co-packaged optics adoption stalls below 5% of AI optical modules through 2027.
mechanism: Putting the optics into the switch package ties cluster wiring to a new supply chain that has to scale alongside the accelerators.
rationale: Co-packaged optics is still early but moving: adoption is set to rise from about 0.5 percent of AI optical modules in 2026 toward about 35 percent by 2030, NVIDIA's photonics switch is due in the second half of 2026 and claims five times better power efficiency, Taiwanese packaging houses are newly competing for silicon photonics work, and NVIDIA and Corning are expanding US optical capacity tenfold.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to yield and reliability of the packaged optical parts.

falsifiableTrigger: A named US fab or packaging project slips its build milestone past 2027.
mechanism: Building fabs, packaging and optical plants inside the United States adds supply that does not depend on Taiwan.
rationale: The US build-out keeps growing: NVIDIA plans up to $500 billion of US-made AI infrastructure with named partners, Wistron opened a Texas plant, Corning is adding three plants and a tenfold rise in US optical capacity, Micron committed $250 billion through 2035 targeting 40 percent domestic output and put $500 million into a Texas wafer plant, TSMC added a $100 billion US commitment, and Intel raised $15 billion of equity for capacity.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to construction timelines and to whether the announced money is actually spent.

falsifiableTrigger: Google Cloud or CoreWeave rpoBacklog fails to grow sequentially for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Providers sign contracts faster than they can build capacity, so the order book shows demand earlier than reported sales do.
rationale: Booked work keeps outrunning delivery: Google Cloud's backlog rose more than $50 billion sequentially to $514 billion while its revenue grew 82 percent, CoreWeave's contracted backlog reached $99.4 billion from $66.8 billion a month earlier, Akamai signed more than $2.8 billion of multi-year cloud contracts this year, and AMD reports strong Helios pull ahead of forecast without disclosing any backlog figure.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to how much of the booked work actually converts into billed revenue.

falsifiableTrigger: A top hyperscaler returns to positive free cash flow while holding 2027 capex guidance for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Spending has outgrown the cash the businesses throw off, so buyers now raise debt and equity to keep building.
rationale: Alphabet funded its quarter with $49.6 billion of equity issuance and $20.3 billion of notes and posted its first negative free cash flow of $5.9 billion, Intel raised up to $17.25 billion of stock for capacity, MediaTek approved $5 billion of US financing, and NVIDIA is arranging outside capital platforms of more than $500 billion for buyers.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to interest rates and to investors' willingness to keep funding the build.

falsifiableTrigger: A new accelerator generation delivers less than a 1.5x perfPerWatt gain over its predecessor.
mechanism: More work per megawatt lets buyers add capability inside a fixed power and packaging budget.
rationale: New systems still do far more per unit of power, with the newest rack claiming ten times the throughput per megawatt of the prior one, enterprise systems claiming up to ten times the performance per megawatt of what they replace, a measured 1.6 times gain between the last two card generations, and a flash generation claiming 2.5 times better performance per watt, though NVIDIA is also lowering power specifications because sites are short of electricity.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the next generation keeps improving work per megawatt.

falsifiableTrigger: HBM leadTimes shorten and suppliers report unsold capacity for 2 consecutive quarters before end-2027.
mechanism: Each accelerator needs a fixed stack of memory, so the memory a supplier can deliver sets how many chips get built.
rationale: Memory now decides output: suppliers can meet only 60 to 70 percent of NVIDIA's requested volume for its next flagship, Micron says it can supply about half of demand and calls memory the number one constraint with no line of sight to balance, tight supply is forecast through 2027, and AMD's next accelerator raises memory per chip by 50 percent, though Samsung and SK Hynix yields reaching about 80 percent point to eventual relief.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to yield improvements converting into extra shipped memory.

falsifiableTrigger: Memory supplier grossMargin falls for 2 consecutive quarters as contract prices flatten.
mechanism: Memory is scarce and priced by its makers, so a rising share of what a server sells for lands with them rather than the builder.
