rationale: Micron's data-center segment posted $11.5 billion of revenue up 103 percent sequentially at an 87 percent gross margin, next-generation memory contract prices are forecast to roughly double into 2027, Samsung is seeking up to a 20 percent contract price rise with quotes valid only 72 hours, and server memory contract prices are set to rise more than 25 percent in the quarter.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to new memory capacity arriving and breaking the pricing power.

falsifiableTrigger: No new sovereign or enterprise cluster above 10,000 GPUs is announced for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Governments and large companies now order clusters big enough to matter, which spreads demand beyond the cloud giants.
rationale: National and enterprise orders keep landing: a Japanese national project takes 27,500 accelerators across 140 megawatts developed with the trade ministry, SK Telecom will build a 2-gigawatt AI cloud in Korea, Bristol Myers Squibb deployed a second enterprise cluster, AMD launched a variant aimed at sovereign work, and AT&T and Cisco appear as named partners.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to public funding decisions and to whether announcements become deliveries.

falsifiableTrigger: Intel data-center revenue growth falls below 10% year over year for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Better yields and a recovering server line let Intel sell chips, packaging and foundry work into the same demand wave.
rationale: Intel's data-center revenue grew 59 percent to $6.3 billion, foundry revenue rose 31 percent to $5.8 billion, gross margin improved to 40.4 percent from 27.5 percent, it guided the next quarter above expectations, raised its investment plan above $20 billion and then sold up to $17.25 billion of stock, while its packaging backlog is growing with a Google order for more than 3 million units.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether its packaging reaches high-volume production in 2027 as promised.

falsifiableTrigger: New vendor equity-for-compute deals in marginalBuyerFinancing stop appearing for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Vendors put money into the firms that buy their chips, so reported demand partly rests on capital the seller supplied.
rationale: The pattern continues on both sides: AMD committed up to $5 billion of equity in Anthropic alongside the compute deal and attached warrants to the OpenAI and Meta agreements, while NVIDIA invested an undisclosed amount in Safe Superintelligence and $5 billion in Intel common stock.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the funded customers can raise money elsewhere.

falsifiableTrigger: Standard DRAM S10 spot prices fall for 2 consecutive months as suppliers restore non-AI capacity.
mechanism: Makers move wafers to the highest-priced AI memory, which starves ordinary parts and lifts their prices.
rationale: The spillover is broadening: AMD raised graphics bundle prices about 10 percent on tight memory with spot prices for its graphics memory roughly tripled since late 2025, standard memory spot prices are above their prior peak, makers are cutting standard output to favour AI parts, enterprise contracts get priority on flash allocation over retail, and stacked memory displaces standard memory at a 3-to-1 ratio worsening to 4-to-1.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to new fabs restoring standard memory output.

falsifiableTrigger: No new multi-year accelerator-to-memory supply partnership is announced for 2 consecutive quarters through 2027.
mechanism: Accelerator makers contract straight with memory suppliers to reserve output rather than compete for it later on the open market.
rationale: Direct deals keep coming: NVIDIA entered a long-term partnership with SK hynix to secure next-generation memory and jointly develop it, SK Telecom's 2-gigawatt cloud pairs NVIDIA accelerators with SK hynix memory, three suppliers began full-scale development of the next memory stack for NVIDIA, and Micron signed a 10-year wafer agreement with upfront financial support to protect its own inputs.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to memory supply loosening enough that reservations stop being necessary.

falsifiableTrigger: The leading supplier's HBM market-share-pct falls below 50% within 4 quarters as rivals ship volume.
mechanism: A second supplier reaching comparable yields gives buyers a real alternative and dilutes the leader's grip on who can build servers.
note: stacked-memory-supply-sits-with-one-dominant-maker: applied: corroborated secondary reversal (4 distinct publishers; pending filing checkpoint)
rationale: The single-source picture is easing: Samsung's yield on the next memory generation reached close to 80 percent from below 60 percent, about four months early, SK Hynix sits at a similar level, and Samsung aims to lift its share to roughly 38 percent by year end, against the leader's 56.4 percent overall and about 62 percent of the next generation, while the largest cloud buyers still hold long-term contracts.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the challenger's yields translate into qualified shipped volume.

falsifiableTrigger: No new diversion prosecution or whitelist reduction is reported for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Prosecutions and shorter approved-buyer lists raise the cost of reselling restricted chips, which closes the informal route.
rationale: Enforcement remains active: Taiwanese prosecutors expanded a criminal smuggling probe and raided a server maker's Taiwan office and affiliates, detaining employees, tied to US charges over some $2.5 billion of servers shipped without a licence, while NVIDIA more than halved the Asian customers cleared to buy its chips.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether smuggling shifts to routes outside Taiwan's reach.

falsifiableTrigger: CoWoS lead times stay above 52 weeks through the end of 2027 while the supply gap fails to narrow below 15%.
mechanism: Packaging capacity is growing but demand is growing with it, so the shortfall is not closing as steadily as the earlier estimate implied.
note: packaging-tightness-starts-to-ease-while-memory-does-not: applied: corroborated secondary reversal (4 distinct publishers; pending filing checkpoint)
rationale: The easing half of the claim is now contested: one account puts the packaging shortfall at about 10 percent in mid-2026, but newer reporting still puts the gap at about 20 percent for 2026 even as monthly capacity rises toward 130,000 to 140,000 wafers, with lines booked through 2027 and TSMC farming a front-end step out to partners, while memory shows no easing at all.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to which shortfall estimate later reporting confirms.

falsifiableTrigger: NAND contract prices for server drives fall for 2 consecutive quarters while Rubin deployments keep growing.
mechanism: The newest racks add a large drive pool per system, so every deployment multiplies flash demand.
rationale: The new storage tier keeps pulling flash: demand tied to it is projected to rise from about 35 million terabytes this year to more than 100 million next year with each unit carrying 576 drives, enterprise contracts are getting priority over retail, rack component costs are rising 2 to 3 percent a week partly on drive scarcity, and the industry has published a first high-bandwidth flash specification.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to flash makers adding capacity ahead of the rack ramp.

falsifiableTrigger: Every major cloud provider publishes list rates for its newest rack-scale systems for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Providers hold their scarcest systems back for negotiated contracts, so list pages understate what the newest hardware costs.
rationale: Lambda's published pages still show no listing for the newer parts, with its newest publicly rentable card being the B200 and longer terms quoted only as custom pricing, while RunPod does publish rates for newer cards including the B300 and H200, so public pages show only part of what leading capacity costs.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to supply loosening enough that providers post rates publicly again.

falsifiableTrigger: NVIDIA accelerator market-share-pct stabilises or rises for 2 consecutive quarters while rival shipments grow.
mechanism: The market grows faster than one supplier can serve, so rivals absorb the extra growth without taking existing business.
rationale: Share estimates keep drifting down, from a 2024 peak of 87 percent to 81 percent and 75 percent for 2026, with another source at about 70 percent as custom chips grow 44.6 percent against 16.1 percent for merchant GPUs, while revenue set a record $75.2 billion; one report still puts NVIDIA as high as 90 percent, so the level is disputed even though the direction is not.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to how quickly rival racks and custom chips reach volume.

falsifiableTrigger: A major buyer returns to purchasing loose accelerators rather than vendor racks for a flagship cluster within 2 quarters.
mechanism: Vendors sell accelerators, networking and software as one rack, so buyers compare finished systems rather than individual chips.
rationale: Both vendors now sell complete 72-accelerator racks: AMD's Helios reached production with named adopters and is compared directly against NVIDIA's rack on tokens per dollar, NVIDIA's newest rack is in production ramp across several clouds, Microsoft will deploy Helios at scale on Azure, SpaceX will build exclusively on NVIDIA racks, and NVIDIA's next design is described in eight-rack scale-up units.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to open rack standards letting buyers mix parts from different vendors.

falsifiableTrigger: ERCOT data-center additions exceed 5 GW over the next 4 quarters as the pause lifts.
mechanism: Sites wait years for a grid connection or a policy decision before they can energise, so electrical access rather than hardware sets the start date.
rationale: ADJUSTED: New AI sites are held up mainly by grid connection queues and state-level pauses rather than by chip supply, with a Texas connection queue of roughly 474 gigawatts where about 90 percent of requests are data centres yet only about 1.2 gigawatts of additions are forecast over the next year and up to $8 billion of lost data-centre revenue attributed to the pause; no finding this cycle reports transformer lead times.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to state policy and to how fast connection queues are cleared.

falsifiableTrigger: Median newest-generation gpuSpotPrice falls while prior-generation rates rise for 2 consecutive months.
mechanism: Scarcity sits with whatever just launched, so the price premium follows the newest hardware while older parts compete on price.
rationale: Published rates step down cleanly by generation, at $7.39 an hour for the newest card, $5.89 for the one before, $4.39 and $2.99 for older parts on the same page, with older cards spread from $1.71 to $6.00 across providers and used prior-generation hardware selling well below new.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to how fast the newest racks reach rental providers in volume.

falsifiableTrigger: Alternative packaging upstreamLeadTimes rise above 52 weeks, or no accelerator maker places advanced-packaging volume outside TSMC for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Shorter quoted waits elsewhere pull work away from the incumbent when its lines are fully booked.
rationale: The spread is now backed by orders: Google committed to more than 3 million units of Intel's bridge packaging for its next chip, Intel reports very high demand and a growing backlog targeting high-volume production in 2027, MediaTek's second accelerator uses it, alternative routes quote 26 to 39 weeks against 52 to 78 at TSMC, TSMC itself is outsourcing a front-end step to partners, and other packaging houses are adding capacity.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to yields on the alternative packaging holding up at volume.

falsifiableTrigger: AMD's share of CoWoS output in pkgCapacityOrderSpread rises above 15% within 2 quarters.
mechanism: A fixed packaging allocation shared between two product lines means every processor packaged costs an accelerator.
rationale: AMD still holds roughly 11 percent of packaging output, about 105,000 wafers, and must split it between its server processors and its accelerators, within capacity that is more than 85 percent pre-booked for 2026 and 2027 and dominated by NVIDIA at roughly 60 percent.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to AMD winning extra allocation or moving work to another packaging house.

falsifiableTrigger: The next flagship ships with its originally planned 288GB memory configuration within 2 quarters of launch.
mechanism: With a fixed pool of memory, putting less in each accelerator is the only way to ship more of them.
rationale: Multiple accounts now describe the same cut: the mainstream next flagship drops to 192 gigabytes in an 8-high stack from 288 in a 12-high, far below the 1 terabyte previewed, driven by memory scarcity and site power limits, with samples testing 192 and 256 gigabyte options and some reverting to the prior memory generation, and four alternative specifications under assessment.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to memory yields improving before the flagship locks its specification.

falsifiableTrigger: The first Korean AI factory misses its 2027 target or the partnership is not converted from letters of intent into signed contracts within 2 quarters.
mechanism: Tying construction, memory supply and cloud capacity together in one country creates a second cluster of the buildout outside the United States.
rationale: The Korean partnership is firming up: NVIDIA describes a more than $500 billion initiative covering AI factory construction, next-generation memory supply and cloud deployment with the first factory targeted for 2027, SK Telecom will build a 2-gigawatt AI cloud on NVIDIA hardware with local memory, and SK hynix approved a 7.09 trillion won packaging investment, though the wider deal was formalised through letters of intent.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the letters of intent become binding contracts.

falsifiableTrigger: No accelerator or system vendor announces a shipping product using the high-bandwidth flash specification within 4 quarters.
mechanism: A cheaper flash tier holds data that would otherwise need scarce stacked memory, so it adds capacity without competing for the same supply.
rationale: The first high-bandwidth flash specification is now published through an industry body, covering up to 512 gigabytes in tall stacks and three performance grades from about 0.4 to 3.0 terabytes a second with Google and Tenstorrent joining, the same supplier claims 2.5 times better performance per watt on its newest flash, and rack designs already pull flash demand from about 35 million to more than 100 million terabytes.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether a chip vendor actually builds the new flash tier into a product.

falsifiableTrigger: AMD software releases deliver less than a 1.5x measured inference gain over the prior release for 2 consecutive releases.
mechanism: Software tuning lifts what existing hardware delivers, so competitiveness improves before any new silicon ships.
rationale: AMD reports large software speedups now while volume waits: a tuned kernel improved end-to-end throughput 2.10 times and cut first-token latency 3.71 times on its current card, its software release claims 3.3 times inference and 2.4 times training gains, and it launched a new software platform alongside the new chips, yet rack volume only ramps through 2027.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether independent testing confirms the vendor's own numbers.

falsifiableTrigger: SpaceX nameplate compute fails to exceed 2 gigawatts by the end of 2026 or its quarterly AI capex falls below $10 billion for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: One buyer outside the traditional cloud group is now taking enough output to move a vendor's allocation decisions.
rationale: SpaceX confirmed the scale on its results call: 1.4 gigawatts of compute from 400 megawatts a year earlier with guidance above 2 gigawatts by year end and about 10 by end-2027, roughly $15.8 billion of quarterly capital spending on AI compute, AI revenue of $2.6 billion up 247 percent, an exclusive commitment to NVIDIA, and an expectation of a very significant share of NVIDIA's 2027 output.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether its AI revenue keeps funding the spending.

falsifiableTrigger: Intel's share of 2.5D packaging capacity fails to rise above 20% within 4 quarters, or its bridge packaging misses 2027 mass production.
mechanism: The alternative route depends on one supplier of a key component, so it inherits a bottleneck of its own as it scales.
rationale: The bottleneck holds: Intel's sole silicon capacitor supplier for its bridge packaging is already fully booked, the technology is described as better suited to custom chips than to high-bandwidth accelerators, Intel holds only about 13.7 percent of 2.5D capacity against roughly 70 percent for TSMC, and substrate mass production is expected in 2027 at initial yields around 50 percent, even as Intel reports a growing backlog.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to a second source qualifying for the scarce component.

falsifiableTrigger: MediaTek market-share-pct of AI accelerators fails to exceed 5% within 4 quarters, or its first chip misses Q4 2026 production.
mechanism: A third design partner gives cloud buyers another route to their own chips, which loosens the hold of the two incumbents.
rationale: MediaTek raised its share target to 15-20 percent from 10-15, expects more than $2 billion of data-centre chip revenue in 2026 with its first chip entering production in the fourth quarter developed with a large US cloud customer, approved $5 billion of financing, and keeps a second chip on track for 2028, though an analyst notes its 2024 share was under 1 percent and calls the target very high.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the first chip reaches production on schedule.

falsifiableTrigger: Used prior-generation server prices fall more than 40% within 2 quarters, or published prior-generation rental rates drop below $2.00 per GPU-hour.
mechanism: Older systems cost a fraction of new ones and still earn rent, so buyers keep them working instead of retiring them.
rationale: The price gap holds: a new top-end server runs about $500,000 against roughly $150,000 to $180,000 used, secondary hardware listings run $15,000 to $40,000 for the same card class depending on condition, and rental rates for older parts sit at $1.49 to $2.99 an hour against $7.39 for the newest.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to a flood of new capacity pushing older rental rates down.

falsifiableTrigger: Wafer suppliers report spare 300mm capacity or falling wafer prices for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: New memory fabs all draw on the same wafer suppliers, so building more memory capacity tightens the raw material behind it.
rationale: The squeeze reaches one step further back: GlobalWafers says its lines are effectively at full utilisation with constraints already appearing on some advanced products, spot prices for large wafers are rising with more increases expected, buyers are lengthening contracts from about three years to five to eight, and Micron signed a 10-year deal with $500 million of upfront support.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to wafer makers adding lines before the new memory fabs start up.

falsifiableTrigger: AMD's reported remaining performance obligations stay below $1 billion for 2 consecutive quarters while new gigawatt commitments keep being announced.
mechanism: Announced gigawatt intentions do not appear as contracted obligations, so the pipeline is still mostly intent rather than firm order.
rationale: AMD's filing still shows only $222 million of contracted obligations beyond one year as of late June, of which $144 million falls within 12 months, while its 10-Q describes OpenAI and Meta each intending to deploy up to 6 gigawatts, and management reports strong pull without disclosing any backlog figure.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the announced deployments convert into disclosed contracted obligations.

falsifiableTrigger: No hardwired inference product reaches customer shipment within 4 quarters, or inference workloads stay on general accelerators for 2 consecutive quarters after launch.
mechanism: Burning a finished model into silicon runs it far more cheaply than a general chip, so settled workloads can move off general accelerators.
rationale: AMD signed a definitive agreement to buy Taalas, a startup building inference silicon that hardwires model weights, with terms undisclosed and closing subject to approvals, frames inference as one of the fastest-growing parts of the market, plans to pair the technology with its own accelerators at system level, and notes such silicon could erode general accelerator demand in cost-sensitive inference.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to how often models change, since a fixed chip cannot follow a moving model.

falsifiableTrigger: Non-cloud owners stop signing new rental or lease agreements for 2 consecutive quarters, or rented share of their fleets falls below 50%.
mechanism: Owners who bought more compute than they use rent the surplus, which adds a layer of supply between chip vendors and end users.
rationale: SpaceX expects roughly 90 percent of its compute to serve inference or be rented out with only about 10 percent used for its own training, and holds multibillion-dollar capacity leases with Google and Anthropic, while a content-delivery firm grew its cloud infrastructure revenue 39 percent including GPU services on more than $2.8 billion of multi-year contracts; the big clouds' own custom chips stay captive and unavailable for rent.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether these owners' own workloads grow enough to absorb their fleets.

detail.falsifiableTrigger: Reported HBM4 yields fall back below 70% or contract prices keep rising for 2 consecutive quarters.
detail.mechanism: Higher yields turn the same wafers into more usable memory stacks, so output rises without any new factory.
detail.sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether yield gains hold once volume production scales.
detail.statement: Both large Korean memory makers have pushed yields on the newest stacked memory to about 80 percent, months ahead of plan, which points to more supply reaching accelerator makers than today's sold-out order books imply.
detail.title: Memory yields improve fast enough to promise relief

detail.falsifiableTrigger: No compute-financing platform closes a funded transaction within 2 quarters, or the memorandums lapse without binding agreements.
detail.mechanism: Outside funds lend against the accelerators themselves, which lets buyers order more than their own cash or the vendor's credit would allow.
detail.sensitivity: Most sensitive to credit conditions and to how lenders value used accelerators as collateral.
detail.statement: Large asset managers and banks are being lined up to finance accelerator purchases, moving part of the buildout's funding from chip vendors and cloud balance sheets onto third-party capital.
detail.title: Outside investors start funding the compute buildout

falsifiableTrigger: B200 rpoBacklog falls below 2 million units for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Buyers commit to multi-year compute purchases faster than memory, packaging and power allow NVIDIA to build systems, so orders queue up instead of clearing.
rationale: NVIDIA posted record data-center revenue of $75.2 billion, up 92% year over year, and guided the next quarter to $91 billion, while a 3.6 million unit order book, more than $750 billion of infrastructure agreements under negotiation, and SpaceX expecting a very large slice of 2027 output all point to orders still running ahead of what can be built.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to a hyperscaler cutting or deferring committed orders, which would drain the order book faster than shipments refill it.

falsifiableTrigger: HBM leadTimes ease to available-on-demand and CoWoS lead times fall below 26 weeks before the end of 2027.
mechanism: Every accelerator needs both stacked memory and an advanced package, so the scarcer of the two sets a hard ceiling on how many units vendors can ship.
rationale: Packaging is sold out with 52 to 78 week waits and bookings into 2027, and memory is now the harder limit: NVIDIA's suppliers can meet only 60 to 70 percent of requested volume for its next generation and Micron says it can supply about half of customer demand with no line of sight to balance.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to memory capacity additions landing earlier than the 2027 to 2028 timelines suppliers now give.

falsifiableTrigger: AMD accelerator market-share-pct fails to rise above 7% through 2027.
mechanism: AMD wins named anchor customers and ships complete racks, but its packaging and memory allocation limits volume until 2027, so credibility rises faster than share.
rationale: AMD's data-center revenue hit $6.7 billion, more than double a year earlier, and Helios racks reached production with OpenAI, Meta, Anthropic, Microsoft and Oracle named, yet its accelerator share is still put at 5 to 7 percent against NVIDIA near 90 percent and one account puts real volume output at the second quarter of 2027.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether AMD's 2027 volume ramp holds its schedule or slips another 2 quarters.

falsifiableTrigger: ASIC market-share-pct growth falls back below GPU growth for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Cloud operators build their own inference chips to cut cost per workload, so a growing share of new compute is filled in-house rather than bought from merchant vendors.
rationale: Custom silicon is projected to grow 44.6 percent against 16.1 percent for merchant GPUs, hyperscaler in-house spending is heading past $25 billion, Meta's new parts enter production in September, Microsoft is negotiating capacity for upward of 300,000 of its own chips for 2027, and Google has ordered more than 3 million advanced packages for its next chip.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to in-house chip programmes slipping their production dates, which would push the workloads back onto merchant parts.

falsifiableTrigger: gpuSpotPrice for a current-generation part drops more than 20% within a quarter.
mechanism: Supply of the newest systems stays scarce, so renters bid the current generation up while the discount lands on hardware that is a generation or two behind.
rationale: Published rental rates still step down cleanly by generation, with the newest publicly rentable part at $6.69 per GPU-hour against $3.99 for the prior generation and $2.79 for the one before, so current-generation pricing has not cracked even as older secondary-market cards ease from their earlier $25,000 to $40,000 range.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to a large block of new rack capacity reaching rental markets at once, which would break the scarcity premium.

falsifiableTrigger: exportControlExposure eases so China DC revenue recovers above prior levels within 2 quarters.
mechanism: Licence rules, tariffs and volume caps keep the largest non-US buyer group from purchasing at scale, removing that demand from what vendors can serve.
rationale: Licensing moved from denial to case-by-case for one chip class, yet NVIDIA booked no data-center shipments to China against $4.6 billion a year earlier, China revenue fell to $4,550 million, actual H200 shipments stay trivial under a 25 percent tariff, and AMD still carries export-control charges, so policy still caps the addressable market.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to licensed shipments actually converting to revenue, which has not happened in the 2 quarters since approvals began.

falsifiableTrigger: Vendor-financed GPU commitments in rpoBacklog exceed 300,000 units within 2 quarters.
mechanism: NVIDIA guarantees, funds or takes equity in the buyers of its own chips, so part of its reported demand rests on credit it extends rather than on independent customer cash.
rationale: NVIDIA's financing footprint widened again this cycle: a discussed $350 billion facility and lease backstop for one customer, roughly 210,000 GPUs backed under revenue-sharing deals, residual value guaranties covering about 4.25 gigawatts capped at $105 billion, an equity stake in a new model lab, and memorandums to mobilise over $500 billion of outside capital for its own buyers.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to a backstopped customer defaulting, which would turn a demand signal into a direct loss.

falsifiableTrigger: customerConcentration for the top three direct customers falls below prior shares next fiscal year.
mechanism: A handful of buyers absorb most of the output, so one of them slowing orders removes a large block of revenue at once.
rationale: Three direct customers were 21, 17 and 16 percent of revenue in the latest quarter, up from 12, 11 and 11 percent two years earlier with the top four now more than half of sales, and SpaceX says it expects a very significant percentage of 2027 output while one 20-year lease campus rests on a single customer.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to the sovereign and enterprise tier growing fast enough to dilute the top buyers' shares.

falsifiableTrigger: NVIDIA DC Ethernet switch market-share-pct slips from #1 within 2 quarters.
mechanism: Selling the switch fabric with the accelerators makes the cluster work as one tested product, so swapping in a rival chip means rebuilding the network too.
rationale: NVIDIA is still the revenue leader in data-center Ethernet switching on the back of networking bundled with its racks, with named first customers for its newest switch line, claimed 5x better power efficiency across clusters above 100,000 GPUs, and a long-term optical manufacturing partnership, but no finding this cycle compares networking growth against compute growth.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to open rack standards letting buyers mix accelerators and switches from different vendors.

falsifiableTrigger: Cost-per-token gains stall so tokenEconomics improves less than one generation cycle.
mechanism: Each generation cuts the price of serving a token, which makes workloads that were too expensive worth running and enlarges the pool of paying inference demand.
rationale: The newest generation is reported at ten times lower inference cost per token than its predecessor and one tenth the cost per million tokens of the generation before, open-model token prices keep falling sharply each year, and buyers are consuming at scale with one carrier burning about a trillion tokens a month.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to memory and power limits capping the per-generation efficiency step, which would stall the cost decline.

falsifiableTrigger: Prepaid HBM commitments in rpoBacklog shrink or deposits are refunded within a quarter.
mechanism: Buyers put cash down years ahead for memory that is only useful inside accelerators, so the deposits stand as a paid-for claim on future accelerator volume.
rationale: Micron holds 16 non-cancelable five-year take-or-pay agreements backed by more than $22 billion including nearly $18 billion of cash deposits, suppliers sold out 2026 output under non-cancellable contracts with all capacity pre-allocated, and order books now extend into 2028.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to any customer walking away from a deposit, which would show the commitments are softer than they read.

falsifiableTrigger: exportControlExposure changes lift the sub-50% China cap or clear Blackwell within 2 quarters.
mechanism: US licence caps limit what may be sold and Chinese instructions to park the hardware outside the mainland limit what buyers may actually use, so approvals do not turn into deliveries.
rationale: ADJUSTED: China's reopening to NVIDIA is now blocked from both sides, with Washington allowing only case-by-case licences under a sub-50 percent cap and a 25 percent tariff while Beijing tells approved buyers to keep the licensed hardware in Hong Kong to protect its own chipmakers, so shipments stay trivial and no revenue has yet been booked.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to Beijing lifting the Hong Kong storage instruction, which would let approved licences convert to revenue.

falsifiableTrigger: Memory hbmSupplyCapex expansion pulls DRAM/NVMe prices down within 2 quarters.
mechanism: Memory is a large and rising share of the parts bill, and buyers absorb the increase rather than cancel, so the extra cost comes out of the assembler's margin.
rationale: ADJUSTED: Memory and flash prices keep pushing up what every AI server costs, with component lead times at 32 to 40 weeks, prices up about 90 percent since late 2025 and rack costs inflating 2 to 3 percent a week, but the biggest contract builder says high memory prices have not slowed customer spending, so the pressure now lands on system builders' margins rather than on order volumes.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether buyers keep paying, since one large customer balking would turn a margin problem into a volume problem.

falsifiableTrigger: releaseCadence slips push a major vendor's 2H-2026 ramp into 2027.
mechanism: Each vendor's ramp waits on its own packaging and memory allocation, so the new supply arrives vendor by vendor instead of in one wave.
rationale: The staged picture holds: NVIDIA's newest rack entered production ramp in the third quarter with fourteen named server vendors, AMD's rack began shipping in the third quarter but ramps into the second half of 2027 with one account putting first production output at the second quarter of 2027, and Meta's own parts only enter production in September.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to memory qualification delays, which have already reshaped one flagship's configuration.

falsifiableTrigger: AMD customerConcentration eases as its buyer base broadens over the next 2 quarters.
mechanism: A few gigawatt-scale commitments make up most of AMD's accelerator pipeline, so each one carries an outsized share of both the growth and the risk.
rationale: AMD's filings now name two customers each intending to deploy up to 6 gigawatts under multi-year agreements with warrants tied to purchase milestones, plus up to 2 gigawatts from a third and a Microsoft expansion, while its own risk factors say a small number of customers will keep accounting for a substantial part of revenue.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to one anchor customer delaying its deployment, which would visibly dent AMD's whole accelerator ramp.

falsifiableTrigger: Crescent Island releaseCadence slips its customer sampling past the 2H 2026 quarter.
mechanism: Using standard memory removes the need for a scarce advanced package and a scarce memory stack, so the part can be built with capacity that is not fought over.
rationale: Intel's inference GPU still uses standard low-power memory of up to 480 gigabytes instead of stacked memory specifically to avoid packaging and stacked-memory contention, and it remains guided to customer sampling in the second half of 2026 with no slip reported this cycle.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the part performs well enough on real inference work to justify the bandwidth it gives up.

falsifiableTrigger: TSMC grossMargin declines for 2 consecutive quarters as capacity loosens.
mechanism: AI demand now fills accelerator, custom-chip, networking and power orders at the same fab, so capacity stays full across nodes and pricing holds.
rationale: TSMC reported a 67.7 percent gross margin, up 9.1 points year over year, raised full-year growth guidance to above 40 percent and capex to $60-64 billion, posted July revenue up 44.7 percent year over year, says the demand gap runs through 2029-2030, and even a second-tier foundry raised advanced prices 10 to 15 percent.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to a broad cut in AI capital budgets, which would empty several node families at once.

falsifiableTrigger: A hyperscalerCapexRevision cuts 2026 or 2027 AI capex guidance within 2 quarters.
mechanism: Cloud buyers are spending far ahead of the revenue the new capacity earns, so a disappointing return would force them to cut the orders that fund accelerator demand.
rationale: Combined 2026 spending is heading to roughly $725 billion, up about 77 percent, and the market reaction is turning: Alphabet's shares fell about 6 percent on its raised budget, chip stocks fell on spending doubts, analysts warned a 67 percent jump in AI capex may be unsustainable, and Alphabet reported its first-ever negative free cash flow of $5.9 billion.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to cloud revenue growth holding up, since one quarter of deceleration would validate the doubts.

falsifiableTrigger: NVIDIA grossMargin guidance drops below 70% in a coming quarter.
mechanism: Scarcity and a bundled system product let NVIDIA hold price while ramp costs rise, so the margin does not dip through the transition.
rationale: NVIDIA's gross margin was 75.0 percent with the next quarter guided to the same level, far above AMD at 56 percent and Intel at 41.8 percent, so buyers are still paying premium prices through a product transition.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to memory input costs, which suppliers expect to roughly double into 2027.

falsifiableTrigger: Top-buyer customerConcentration in CoWoS output falls below 85% within a year.
mechanism: A very small set of buyers has booked nearly all packaging output years ahead, so any one of them cancelling leaves capacity with no comparable buyer waiting.
rationale: The top three customers hold more than 85 percent of advanced-packaging output with NVIDIA at roughly 60 percent, capacity is pre-booked above 85 percent for both 2026 and 2027, and NVIDIA alone is reported to have reserved 800,000 to 850,000 wafers of 2026 capacity, over half the year's total.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to custom-chip designers taking a larger direct share of packaging bookings.

falsifiableTrigger: Aggregate rpoBacklog duration shortens as new commitments turn shorter-dated over 2 quarters.
mechanism: Buyers facing scarcity book capacity further ahead to secure a place in line, which stretches the average life of every supplier's order book.
rationale: Google Cloud's backlog rose more than $50 billion sequentially to $514 billion with only just over half converting within 24 months, one contract runs to 2032, memory deals are five-year take-or-pay, one campus lease runs 20 years, and wafer buyers are stretching contracts from about three years to five to eight.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to supply loosening, which would let buyers revert to shorter contracts.

falsifiableTrigger: A leading model provider reports revenue (apiArr) growth stalling quarter over quarter while compute commitments keep growing.
mechanism: Model providers earn rising sales from the capacity they rent, so their compute commitments are funded by revenue rather than by expectation alone.
rationale: Anthropic's annual run rate reached more than $30 billion, up from $1 billion in fifteen months, and SpaceX reported AI revenue of $2.6 billion, up 247 percent year over year, while Anthropic's compute chief ties its spending directly to meeting customer demand.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to the freshness of these disclosures, since the largest figure cited dates from April.

falsifiableTrigger: Chinese domestic accelerator designWins for frontier training stall over the next 2 quarters.
mechanism: Export limits push Chinese buyers to domestic parts, and state direction plus proven frontier training turns that from a workaround into a growing home market.
rationale: Beyond the 1.6-trillion-parameter model pretrained on more than 50,000 domestic accelerators, Chinese suppliers now show volume: Moore Threads guided first-half revenue up 135 to 149 percent and held a 56.95 percent gross margin while narrowing losses, Hygon guided 55 to 70 percent growth, and regulators are steering licensed buyers to support domestic chipmakers.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to memory access inside China, since domestic labs' own chips are still judged more than 2 years out.

falsifiableTrigger: A neocloud's marginalBuyerFinancing debt load or net loss narrows for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Fleet growth is funded with debt whose interest and depreciation land before the contracted revenue arrives, so faster growth deepens the reported loss.
rationale: CoreWeave's revenue grew about 168 percent from $1.9 billion to $5.1 billion while its net loss widened from $937 million to $1.2 billion, and its debt rose 16.1 percent in a single quarter to $24.86 billion.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to rental rates on the newest hardware, which decide whether the fleet ever out-earns its financing cost.

falsifiableTrigger: A top hyperscaler cuts its 2027 gigawatt power target below its 2026 level.
mechanism: Sites can only switch on the megawatts the grid delivers, so available power rather than chip supply sets how many accelerators actually run.
rationale: Power is now shaping the products themselves, with persistent shortages cited as driving NVIDIA to lower its flagship power specification to 1,800 watts, while buyers size plans in gigawatts, Meta at 7 gigawatts in 2026 and roughly double in 2027 and SpaceX guiding past 2 gigawatts, against a Texas queue of about 474 gigawatts that will add only about 1.2 gigawatts.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to efficiency gains per megawatt, which let the same power run more work.

falsifiableTrigger: Broadcom-plus-Marvell market-share-pct of custom ASIC co-design falls below 90% within a year.
mechanism: New design houses winning cloud customers spread the custom-chip work, so the alternative to merchant GPUs no longer runs through only two suppliers.
rationale: The two incumbent design firms are still put at about 95 percent of custom co-design, but a third designer now expects more than $2 billion of accelerator revenue in 2026 with its first chip in production in the fourth quarter and a share target raised to 15 to 20 percent, and one model lab is in early talks with a memory maker to build its own chip.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the newcomer's first chip actually reaches production in the fourth quarter of 2026.

falsifiableTrigger: Wistron odmMonthlyAiRevenue falls year-over-year for 2 consecutive months.
mechanism: Contract builders only book revenue when systems physically ship, so their monthly records confirm that orders are converting into hardware.
rationale: Wistron posted record June revenue of NT$321.82 billion, up 53.9 percent year over year, Foxconn's July revenue reached NT$946.51 billion, up 54.19 percent and its first month above NT$900 billion, TSMC's July revenue rose 44.7 percent, and Wistron says AI servers are now 95 percent of its server business.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to one large enterprise client, which Wistron says supplies most of its volume.

falsifiableTrigger: A neocloud's marginalBuyerFinancing debt-to-equity rises above 6:1 within 2 quarters.
mechanism: Neocloud operators borrow against the chips themselves instead of paying out of earnings, so every fleet expansion piles more debt onto a thin equity base.
rationale: CoreWeave has raised $18.81 billion of debt against $3.5 billion of equity, a 5.4 to 1 ratio, with total debt of $24.86 billion up 16.1 percent in one quarter, and vendor backstops rather than equity are filling the gap for smaller operators.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to lenders repricing chip-backed debt, which would stop the fleet growth outright.

falsifiableTrigger: Co-packaged optics adoption stalls below 5% of AI optical modules through 2027.
mechanism: Putting the optics inside the switch package cuts lasers and power per link, so cluster wiring now depends on optical engine yield and packaging capacity rather than on pluggable module supply.
rationale: Adoption is set to run from about 0.5 percent of AI optical modules in 2026 to about 35 percent by 2030, order books for the new switch platform are reported full through 2027 with supply tight into 2028, the platform claims 4x fewer lasers and 5x lower power, and Taiwanese assembly houses are newly competing for photonics packaging.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to optical engine yields, named as the key limit on expanding this supply.

falsifiableTrigger: A named US fab or packaging project slips its build milestone past 2027.
mechanism: Vendors and their suppliers are funding fabs, packaging and optics plants inside the United States, which adds capacity that does not depend on Taiwan.
rationale: Commitments keep landing: up to $500 billion of US-built AI infrastructure with named partners, a new 324,000-square-foot Texas plant, $250 billion of US memory investment targeting 40 percent domestic output, an added $100 billion foundry investment, a tenfold expansion of US optical capacity with three new plants, and a $15 billion share sale earmarked partly for capacity.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to construction and equipment schedules, since announced dollars do not equal running capacity.

falsifiableTrigger: Google Cloud or CoreWeave rpoBacklog fails to grow sequentially for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Providers sign contracts faster than they can build capacity, so the growing gap between bookings and delivered revenue is the clearest read on demand.
rationale: Google Cloud's backlog rose more than $50 billion sequentially to $514 billion while revenue grew 82 percent to $24.8 billion, CoreWeave's contracted backlog reached $99.4 billion from $66.8 billion months earlier, and even a mid-sized provider signed more than $2.8 billion of multi-year contracts year to date.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to how much of the backlog converts, since only just over half is expected within 24 months.

falsifiableTrigger: A top hyperscaler returns to positive free cash flow while holding 2027 capex guidance for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Capital budgets have outgrown operating cash flow, so the buildout is now funded by issuing debt and shares instead of by the businesses themselves.
rationale: Alphabet funded its quarter with $49.6 billion of equity issuance and $20.3 billion of notes and reported its first-ever negative free cash flow of $5.9 billion, while combined 2026 budgets run to about $725 billion, up roughly 77 percent, and outside financing platforms are being lined up for over $500 billion more.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to credit conditions, since dearer borrowing would force capex plans down.

falsifiableTrigger: A new accelerator generation delivers less than a 1.5x perfPerWatt gain over its predecessor.
mechanism: Each generation does more work inside the same power and package footprint, so buyers add capability without adding megawatts or packaging slots.
rationale: The newest rack is claimed at ten times the throughput per megawatt of its predecessor and up to ten times the performance per megawatt of the infrastructure it replaces, an independent measure puts the prior step at about 1.6 times, and adjacent parts also improve, with a flash generation claiming 2.5 times better performance per watt.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to vendor-claimed figures, since the one independently measured step came in at 1.6x, barely above the trigger.

falsifiableTrigger: HBM leadTimes shorten and suppliers report unsold capacity for 2 consecutive quarters before end-2027.
mechanism: Stacked memory production eats three to four times the wafer capacity of standard memory, so the memory pool rather than the logic die decides how many accelerators can be finished.
rationale: Suppliers can meet only 60 to 70 percent of the memory volume requested for NVIDIA's next generation, Micron says it can supply about half of customer demand and calls memory the number one constraint with no line of sight to balance, supply stays tight through 2027, and NVIDIA is testing four alternative memory specifications as a result.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to yield improvements converting into shipped parts rather than staying a laboratory number.

falsifiableTrigger: Memory supplier grossMargin falls for 2 consecutive quarters as contract prices flatten.
mechanism: Memory is scarce and cannot be substituted inside an AI server, so its suppliers set the price and take a larger cut of the value of every rack.
rationale: Micron's data-center segment posted $11.5 billion of revenue, up 103 percent quarter over quarter, at an 87 percent gross margin, contract prices are locked in at high-teen to low-twenties percent increases with all 2026 output pre-allocated, and next-generation memory prices are forecast to roughly double into 2027.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to new fab capacity arriving, which would end the pricing power quickly.

falsifiableTrigger: No new sovereign or enterprise cluster above 10,000 GPUs is announced for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Governments and large firms are buying clusters directly rather than renting, which adds a demand tier that does not depend on cloud capital budgets.
rationale: Japan's national project takes 27,500 accelerators across 140 megawatts, a Korean carrier will build a 2-gigawatt AI cloud, a pharmaceutical company deployed a second full system, AMD launched a variant aimed specifically at sovereign buyers, and a rival system vendor names a national research university and a state-backed group among its customers.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to national budget cycles, which can pause these projects faster than commercial orders.

falsifiableTrigger: Intel data-center revenue growth falls below 10% year over year for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Better yields and a packaging technology customers want are bringing outside orders back to Intel, so it supplies AI-adjacent capacity again rather than only competing for it.
rationale: Intel's data-center segment grew 59 percent year over year to $6.3 billion with $2.5 billion of operating income, gross margin rose to 40.4 percent from 27.5 percent, foundry revenue grew 31 percent to $5.8 billion, it raised a $15 billion share sale for capacity, and its packaging won an order of more than 3 million units from a large cloud buyer.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to its packaging reaching high-volume production in 2027 as promised.

falsifiableTrigger: New vendor equity-for-compute deals in marginalBuyerFinancing stop appearing for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Vendors take stakes in the firms that buy their chips, so part of the order book is bought with the vendor's own capital.
rationale: AMD committed a strategic equity investment of up to $5 billion in Anthropic alongside its compute deal and issued warrants tied to purchase milestones for two other buyers, while NVIDIA invested an undisclosed sum in a new model lab and holds a $5 billion stake in Intel tied to custom processors.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to accounting or regulatory scrutiny of these stakes, which would slow the practice quickly.

falsifiableTrigger: Standard DRAM S10 spot prices fall for 2 consecutive months as suppliers restore non-AI capacity.
mechanism: Memory makers move wafers to the highest-margin AI parts, so ordinary memory grows scarce and lifts prices on consumer and general-purpose hardware.
rationale: AMD raised graphics bundle prices about 10 percent citing tight memory with spot prices for that memory type roughly tripled since late 2025, older standard memory spot prices hit $81.20, up 17.5 percent in a month and above the prior peak, makers are cutting standard output to favour AI parts, and enterprise contracts now get flash allocation ahead of retail.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to new fab capacity coming online, which suppliers do not expect before late 2026.

falsifiableTrigger: No new multi-year accelerator-to-memory supply partnership is announced for 2 consecutive quarters through 2027.
mechanism: With memory scarce, accelerator makers contract directly with the memory suppliers to reserve future output rather than buying it on the open market.
rationale: NVIDIA entered a long-term partnership with SK hynix to secure next-generation memory and jointly develop it, all three large makers began full-scale development of a 16-high stack specifically for NVIDIA targeting fourth-quarter 2026 delivery, and Micron locked in five-year take-or-pay agreements with nearly $18 billion of deposits.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to memory supply loosening, which would remove the reason to lock output up in advance.

falsifiableTrigger: The leading supplier's HBM market-share-pct falls below 50% within 4 quarters as rivals ship volume.
mechanism: A second maker reaching comparable yields and adding capacity gives accelerator makers a real alternative source, so one supplier no longer decides who can build.
rationale: SK Hynix still holds 56.4 percent of the market and about 62 percent of next-generation supply, but its rival has pushed yields to close to 80 percent from below 60 percent about four months early, both Korean makers now sit at similar production efficiency, one aims to lift its share to about 38 percent by year-end, and it is adding 50 percent more capacity in 2026.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the rival's yields translate into qualified shipments to the largest accelerator buyer.

falsifiableTrigger: No new diversion prosecution or whitelist reduction is reported for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Prosecutions and a shorter approved-buyer list raise the cost and risk of reselling restricted hardware, which shuts the informal channels down.
rationale: Taiwanese prosecutors expanded a criminal smuggling probe, raiding a server maker's Taiwan office and affiliates and detaining employees over some $2.5 billion of servers alleged to have shipped without a licence, while NVIDIA more than halved the number of Asian customers authorised to buy its chips.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to enforcement attention holding, since these channels reopen quickly when scrutiny fades.

falsifiableTrigger: CoWoS lead times stay above 52 weeks through the end of 2027 while the supply gap fails to narrow below 15%.
mechanism: Capacity additions are being absorbed by demand as fast as they arrive, so the shortfall does not narrow even as wafer output rises.
rationale: The easing half of the claim is now contested: one account still puts the packaging gap at about 10 percent in mid-2026, but another reports the gap still at about 20 percent for 2026 with a key step being outsourced and NVIDIA reserving over half the year's capacity, packaging lines are described as booked through 2027, and memory has not eased at all.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to which gap estimate proves right, since the two published figures differ by a factor of two.

falsifiableTrigger: NAND contract prices for server drives fall for 2 consecutive quarters while Rubin deployments keep growing.
mechanism: The new storage tier adds a very large block of flash demand on top of existing buyers, so drives become the next part in short supply.
rationale: The newest generation's context-memory tier is expected to pull flash demand from about 35 million terabytes this year to more than 100 million next year, with each unit carrying 576 drives for 9,600 terabytes, enterprise contracts already taking allocation ahead of retail, and drive scarcity feeding rack costs rising 2 to 3 percent a week.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to how many of the new racks actually ship with the full storage tier.

falsifiableTrigger: Every major cloud provider publishes list rates for its newest rack-scale systems for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Scarce newest-generation capacity is sold through negotiated contracts rather than listed rates, so public pages stop showing the leading edge.
rationale: Across four separate fetches this cycle one provider's public pages still showed no rates for the newest rack-scale parts and no listings for the rival vendor's accelerators, with longer terms quoted only as custom pricing, so its newest publicly rentable part remains a generation behind what is deploying.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to newest-generation supply loosening, which would push those systems back onto public price pages.

falsifiableTrigger: NVIDIA accelerator market-share-pct stabilises or rises for 2 consecutive quarters while rival shipments grow.
mechanism: The overall market is growing faster than NVIDIA can ship, so rivals absorb the surplus growth without taking existing business away.
rationale: One projection has NVIDIA's accelerator share falling from a 2024 peak of 87 percent to 81 percent in 2025 and 75 percent in 2026 as custom chips grow 44.6 percent against 16.1 percent for merchant GPUs, even as its data-center revenue set a record at $75.2 billion; another account still puts its share as high as 90 percent, so the direction is clearer than the level.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to which share series is used, since published 2026 figures range from 75 to 90 percent.

falsifiableTrigger: A major buyer returns to purchasing loose accelerators rather than vendor racks for a flagship cluster within 2 quarters.
mechanism: Vendors now ship pre-integrated racks with their own networking and software, so buyers evaluate complete systems and cannot mix parts easily.
rationale: AMD's 72-accelerator rack with 31 terabytes of memory and 2.9 exaFLOPS is explicitly positioned against NVIDIA's 72-accelerator rack, NVIDIA's newest rack is deploying across five named clouds, NVIDIA is scaling to an eight-rack 576-accelerator system, and a third vendor has entered with its own rack-scale machine.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to open rack standards work, which several buyers are co-developing.

falsifiableTrigger: ERCOT data-center additions exceed 5 GW over the next 4 quarters as the pause lifts.
mechanism: Sites cannot switch on until the grid operator clears their connection, so the queue and the state pause rather than equipment orders set the pace of new capacity.
rationale: The Texas connection queue still holds roughly 474 gigawatts with about 90 percent of requests from data centres while only about 1.2 gigawatts of additions are forecast over the next year, and lost data-centre revenue from the pause is estimated at up to $8 billion by early 2027; again no finding this cycle reports transformer lead times.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to state policy on the connection pause, which is the single largest part of the delay.

falsifiableTrigger: Median newest-generation gpuSpotPrice falls while prior-generation rates rise for 2 consecutive months.
mechanism: Buyers pay up for the fastest hardware they can actually get, so the premium follows each launch and the older fleet competes on price.
rationale: Published rates step down by age at $6.69 for the newest listed part, $3.99 for the prior generation and $2.79 for the one before, while used prior-generation cards now ask roughly $20,877 to $27,999 against a $25,000 to $40,000 range from mid-2024 into early 2026.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to public listings staying available for the newest parts, which are increasingly quoted privately.

falsifiableTrigger: Alternative packaging upstreamLeadTimes rise above 52 weeks, or no accelerator maker places advanced-packaging volume outside TSMC for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Alternative packaging houses quote much shorter waits, so buyers place work there rather than sit in a year-and-a-half queue.
rationale: One cloud buyer has committed to more than 3 million units of Intel's bridge packaging for its next chip, a chip designer is using the same technology for its second accelerator, alternative routes quote 26 to 39 weeks against 52 to 78, an assembly house and a tool maker are adding capacity, TSMC is itself outsourcing a front-end step, and NVIDIA is weighing moving some output to Intel.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the alternative route suits high-bandwidth accelerators, which one account doubts.

falsifiableTrigger: AMD's share of CoWoS output in pkgCapacityOrderSpread rises above 15% within 2 quarters.
mechanism: Both product lines need the same scarce package, so AMD's allocation forces a direct swap between processors and accelerators.
rationale: AMD is still put at about 11 percent of advanced-packaging output, roughly 105,000 wafers, against NVIDIA's 60 percent, and must split that allocation between its server processors and its accelerators so each processor slot used cannot go to an accelerator.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to AMD qualifying an alternative packaging route, which would end the trade-off.

falsifiableTrigger: The next flagship ships with its originally planned 288GB memory configuration within 2 quarters of launch.
mechanism: With a fixed pool of memory, putting less in each accelerator lets more accelerators ship, so the shortage shows up as a smaller product rather than fewer units.
rationale: Several accounts now report the same cut, to 192 gigabytes in an 8-high stack from 288 in a 12-high stack and far below the 1 terabyte originally previewed, with limited memory named as the driver, NVIDIA testing 192 and 256 gigabyte options plus four alternative specifications, and some samples reverting to the prior memory generation.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to how much performance is lost, since one bank's research says performance drops sharply below 500 gigabytes of memory.

falsifiableTrigger: The first Korean AI factory misses its 2027 target or the partnership is not converted from letters of intent into signed contracts within 2 quarters.
mechanism: Tying memory supply, cloud capacity and construction into one Korean partnership puts a second full stack of the buildout outside the United States.
rationale: The partnership is now described by NVIDIA itself as a $500-billion-plus initiative covering AI factory construction, next-generation memory supply and cloud deployment across Asia-Pacific with the first factory targeted for 2027, a Korean carrier will build a 2-gigawatt AI cloud on NVIDIA hardware with local memory, and SK Hynix approved a $4.83 billion packaging plant, though the arrangement is still formalised through letters of intent.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to the letters of intent becoming binding contracts, which has not happened yet.

falsifiableTrigger: No accelerator or system vendor announces a shipping product using the high-bandwidth flash specification within 4 quarters.
mechanism: Flash sits on a separate production line from stacked memory, so building a bandwidth tier out of it adds capacity without competing for the scarce part.
rationale: The first technical specification for a high-bandwidth flash tier is now published through an open consortium, covering up to 512 gigabytes in 8-high and 16-high stacks and three grades from about 0.4 to 3.0 terabytes per second, with two large cloud and chip names joining, and the newest accelerator generation is already designing racks around huge drive pools.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to flash itself tightening, since enterprise demand is already crowding out retail supply.

falsifiableTrigger: AMD software releases deliver less than a 1.5x measured inference gain over the prior release for 2 consecutive releases.
mechanism: Software tuning lifts what today's installed accelerators deliver without waiting on new hardware, so competitiveness improves before volume does.
rationale: AMD reported a 2.10x end-to-end throughput gain and 3.71x faster first-token time on a current accelerator from software work alone, plus 3.3x inference and 2.4x training gains over the prior software release, while one account still puts its mass-production ramp at the second quarter of 2027.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to independent verification, since the speedups are vendor-measured on chosen workloads.

falsifiableTrigger: SpaceX nameplate compute fails to exceed 2 gigawatts by the end of 2026 or its quarterly AI capex falls below $10 billion for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: A privately funded buyer is adding gigawatts of compute at hyperscaler pace and buying from one vendor only, which makes it a top-tier claim on that vendor's output.
rationale: SpaceX ended the quarter at 1.4 gigawatts of nameplate compute from 400 megawatts a year earlier, spent about $15.8 billion of its $18.4 billion quarterly capex on AI infrastructure, guides past 2 gigawatts by year-end and about 10 gigawatts by end-2027, says it is exclusive to NVIDIA, and expects a very significant percentage of NVIDIA's 2027 output.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to its own AI revenue, currently $2.6 billion a quarter, continuing to fund spending of this size.

falsifiableTrigger: Intel's share of 2.5D packaging capacity fails to rise above 20% within 4 quarters, or its bridge packaging misses 2027 mass production.
mechanism: The alternative route depends on one booked-out component supplier and unproven substrate yields, so its capacity cannot scale as fast as the orders arriving for it.
rationale: Intel's bridge packaging is winning volume with high demand, a growing backlog and yields reported above 90 percent, but its sole silicon capacitor supplier is already fully booked, Intel holds only about 13.7 percent of 2.5D capacity against roughly 70 percent for TSMC, substrate mass production is not expected before 2027 at 50 percent initial yields, and the technology is called a better fit for custom chips than for high-bandwidth accelerators.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to a second silicon capacitor source appearing, which would remove the tightest link.

falsifiableTrigger: MediaTek market-share-pct of AI accelerators fails to exceed 5% within 4 quarters, or its first chip misses Q4 2026 production.
mechanism: A third design house winning cloud customers gives buyers another route to custom silicon, though it starts from a very small base.
rationale: MediaTek confirmed its share target of 15 to 20 percent, expects more than $2 billion of accelerator revenue in 2026 with its first chip entering production in the fourth quarter and a second in 2028, and approved $5 billion of financing, but an analyst notes its 2024 share was under 1 percent and calls the target very high, and it has denied one reported packaging timeline.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to the fourth-quarter 2026 production date holding, since everything else rests on that first chip.

falsifiableTrigger: Used prior-generation server prices fall more than 40% within 2 quarters, or published prior-generation rental rates drop below $2.00 per GPU-hour.
mechanism: Older systems cost a fraction of new ones while still earning meaningful rental rates, so they keep paying for themselves instead of being retired.
rationale: A new top-end server is still about $500,000 against roughly $150,000 to $180,000 for a used prior-generation one, used cards ask $20,877 to $27,999 versus a $25,000 to $40,000 range earlier, and the prior generation still rents at $3.99 an hour against $6.69 for the newest listed part.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to power costs, since older hardware does far less work per megawatt.

falsifiableTrigger: Wafer suppliers report spare 300mm capacity or falling wafer prices for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Stacked memory consumes several times the wafers of standard memory, so the memory build-out pulls the shortage one step upstream into blank wafers.
rationale: GlobalWafers says its 300mm, 200mm and 150mm lines are at effectively full utilisation with constraints already appearing on some advanced products, spot 300mm prices are rising with more increases expected, buyers are stretching contracts from about three years to five to eight, and one memory maker signed a 10-year agreement with $500 million of upfront support.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to new memory fabs starting up together, which the wafer maker expects to intensify pressure through the second half of 2027.

falsifiableTrigger: AMD's reported remaining performance obligations stay below $1 billion for 2 consecutive quarters while new gigawatt commitments keep being announced.
mechanism: Gigawatt announcements state intent while the filings show almost no contracted obligation, so the pipeline is not yet a firm order book.
rationale: AMD still reports only $222 million of remaining performance obligations on contracts longer than one year, of which $144 million falls within 12 months, and disclosed no dollar backlog at all while naming two customers each intending up to 6 gigawatts under agreements carrying warrant incentives.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to the first anchor deployment converting into a disclosed contracted obligation.

falsifiableTrigger: No hardwired inference product reaches customer shipment within 4 quarters, or inference workloads stay on general accelerators for 2 consecutive quarters after launch.
mechanism: Fixing a finished model into hardware removes the flexibility cost of a general accelerator, so inference workloads can run far cheaper on purpose-built parts.
rationale: AMD signed a definitive agreement to buy a startup that burns model weights into silicon, frames inference as one of the fastest-growing parts of the market, plans to pair the technology with its own accelerators at system level, and notes such silicon could erode merchant demand in cost-sensitive inference.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to how fast models change, since a hardwired chip loses its value once its model is superseded.

falsifiableTrigger: Non-cloud owners stop signing new rental or lease agreements for 2 consecutive quarters, or rented share of their fleets falls below 50%.
mechanism: Owners who bought accelerators for themselves rent the idle share to cover the cost, which turns private fleets into a new layer of sellable supply.
rationale: SpaceX expects roughly 90 percent of its compute to serve inference or be rented out with only about 10 percent used for its own training, and holds multibillion-dollar capacity leases with two other firms, while a content-delivery company grew its cloud infrastructure revenue 39 percent and signed more than $2.8 billion of multi-year contracts.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to rental prices, since a fall would make renting out less attractive than internal use.

falsifiableTrigger: Reported HBM4 yields fall back below 70% or contract prices keep rising for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Yield gains raise good units per wafer, but the wafer allocation itself is capped, so better yields do not add enough supply to loosen the shortage.
rationale: Both Korean makers have reached about 80 percent yields months early, but relief is not showing anywhere downstream: NVIDIA's suppliers can meet only 60 to 70 percent of requested volume, Micron says it can supply about half of demand with no line of sight to balance, and supply is expected to stay tight through 2027.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to wafer allocation, since stacked memory consumes three to four times the capacity of standard memory.

falsifiableTrigger: No compute-financing platform closes a funded transaction within 2 quarters, or the memorandums lapse without binding agreements.
mechanism: Third-party investors take the financing role that vendors and clouds have been carrying, which moves the funding of accelerator purchases off those balance sheets.
rationale: NVIDIA signed memorandums with six large asset managers and banks to set up compute-financing platforms intended to mobilise more than $500 billion of third-party capital, reported again in a second announcement, alongside residual value guaranties covering about 4.25 gigawatts capped at $105 billion, though the memorandums remain non-binding.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to the first platform actually closing a funded deal, since nothing signed so far is binding.

detail.falsifiableTrigger: Samsung foundry utilisation loosens or it reverses the 10-15% price increase within 2 quarters.
detail.mechanism: Buyers shut out of the leading foundry take their advanced work to the next supplier, which fills that supplier's lines and lets it raise prices too.
detail.sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the overflow work is AI-related or ordinary mobile demand returning.
detail.statement: Samsung's contract chipmaking business is now full enough that it raised prices 10 to 15 percent on new orders and cannot meet all the orders it receives, so AI demand is tightening capacity beyond the market leader.
detail.title: The second-largest foundry fills up and raises prices

detail.falsifiableTrigger: Cerebras fails to report CS-4 customer shipments within 2 quarters, or no named customer expands beyond its initial system within 4 quarters.
detail.mechanism: A whole-wafer processor avoids the packaging and memory stacking that limit conventional accelerators, so it can add inference capacity from a different supply chain.
detail.sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the claimed speed advantage holds on customer workloads rather than on chosen benchmarks.
detail.statement: Cerebras is shipping a rack-scale system built from three whole-wafer processors with named cloud and research customers, and it plugs into rival vendors' racks rather than replacing them outright.
detail.title: Wafer-scale machines join the rack contest

falsifiableTrigger: B200 rpoBacklog falls below 2 million units for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Buyers keep committing to more accelerators than the parts chain can build, so orders pile up faster than shipments clear them.
rationale: Record data-center revenue of $75.2 billion, up 92% year over year, with the next quarter guided to $91 billion, a B200 order book near 3.6 million units, more than $750 billion of infrastructure agreements under negotiation, and a new rack generation entering production ramp, all while memory suppliers can fill only 60 to 70 percent of the requested volume.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to a break in the order book at the largest cloud buyers, since a few customers carry most of the commitments.

falsifiableTrigger: HBM leadTimes ease to available-on-demand and CoWoS lead times fall below 26 weeks before the end of 2027.
mechanism: Two scarce inputs sit in series ahead of every accelerator, so whichever is tighter sets the shipment ceiling no matter how many wafers are started.
rationale: Advanced packaging remains sold out with 52 to 78 week waits and bookings into 2027 even as monthly capacity climbs toward 125,000 to 130,000 wafers, while high-bandwidth memory is sold out through 2027 with order books into 2028, one large maker can serve only about half of demand, and the packaging gap is still put near 20 percent for 2026.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to memory output per wafer, because stacked memory eats three to four times the wafer capacity of standard memory.

falsifiableTrigger: AMD accelerator market-share-pct fails to rise above 7% through 2027.
mechanism: A second supplier wins named commitments long before it can build enough racks, so its sales grow fast while its share of installed accelerators barely moves.
rationale: Second-quarter data-center revenue of $6.7 billion was up 107 percent year over year with the next quarter guided to about $13.0 billion of total revenue, the 72-accelerator rack reached full production with Anthropic, OpenAI, Meta, Microsoft and Oracle named, yet share estimates still sit at 5 to 7 percent against roughly 80 to 90 percent for the leader and the real volume ramp is placed at the second quarter of 2027.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to packaging and memory allocation, since the challenger holds only about a tenth of advanced packaging output.

falsifiableTrigger: ASIC market-share-pct growth falls back below GPU growth for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Large cloud buyers move their steady inference work onto chips they design themselves, which takes growth away from the parts they would otherwise buy.
rationale: Custom silicon is projected to grow 44.6 percent in 2026 against 16.1 percent for merchant accelerators and to reach 27.8 percent of the market, spending on it is put above $25 billion in 2026, Meta's four in-house parts enter production in September, Microsoft is negotiating capacity for upward of 300,000 of its own chips for 2027, and Google has ordered more than three million advanced packaging units for its next design.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether in-house parts can get packaging and memory slots of their own, since they compete for the same scarce supply.

falsifiableTrigger: gpuSpotPrice for a current-generation part drops more than 20% within a quarter.
mechanism: Rental capacity stays scarce enough to hold hourly rates while the resale market for loose cards clears at lower prices than during the earlier shortage.
rationale: ADJUSTED: Published rental rates for current and prior generation accelerators are holding or edging up while used-card asking prices have drifted below their earlier peaks.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to how much new rack capacity reaches rental providers, since added supply shows up first in hourly rates.

falsifiableTrigger: exportControlExposure eases so China DC revenue recovers above prior levels within 2 quarters.
mechanism: Government licence rules decide which parts may be sold into the largest single foreign market, so policy sets the size of the market a vendor is allowed to serve.
rationale: China revenue fell to $4,550 million from $9,659 million a year earlier, no Hopper parts shipped to China in the quarter against $4.6 billion a year before, licences granted from February 2026 have produced no revenue, the vendor assumes no China data-center revenue in its outlook, and the rival vendor still flags the same restrictions with prior-year inventory charges.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to both governments at once, since Beijing's guidance can block shipments even after Washington grants a licence.

falsifiableTrigger: Vendor-financed GPU commitments in rpoBacklog exceed 300,000 units within 2 quarters.
mechanism: The seller guarantees or funds its own buyers' purchases, so reported demand partly reflects credit the seller extended rather than money the buyers already had.
rationale: The vendor now backstops roughly 210,000 accelerators across two early partners after earlier support deals with CoreWeave and Lambda, raised $25 billion of bonds to fund the programme, and signed residual value guaranties covering about 4.25 gigawatts with a cumulative cap of $105 billion tied to one customer, even though it cut a separate proposed guarantee from $250 billion to under $120 billion.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to the credit standing of the backstopped buyers, since the guarantees only pay out if one of them fails.

falsifiableTrigger: customerConcentration for the top three direct customers falls below prior shares next fiscal year.
mechanism: A handful of buyers place most of the orders, so one of them slowing down removes a large slice of revenue at once.
rationale: Three direct customers accounted for 21, 17 and 16 percent of revenue in the latest quarter after one customer reached 22 percent for the prior fiscal year, one rocket company expects a very significant share of 2027 output, and a single 20-year lease customer anchors an exclusive campus arrangement.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to in-house chip programmes at those same buyers, which convert a top customer into a competitor.

falsifiableTrigger: NVIDIA DC Ethernet switch market-share-pct slips from #1 within 2 quarters.
mechanism: Selling the switching fabric with the accelerators makes the whole cluster one purchase, which raises the cost of swapping any single part for a rival.
