rationale: The vendor took the top revenue spot in data-center Ethernet switching for the first time in the first quarter of 2026 by pairing its switching with its accelerator racks, named first customers are deploying its newest switch line, and a new multi-year cloud expansion ships its racks on that same networking, but again no finding compares networking growth against compute growth.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to open rack standards from rivals, which would let buyers mix networking and accelerators from different vendors.

falsifiableTrigger: Cost-per-token gains stall so tokenEconomics improves less than one generation cycle.
mechanism: Each generation lowers the cost of producing a token, which makes workloads that were too expensive worth running and enlarges the served market.
rationale: The newest rack generation is reported to cut inference cost per token tenfold against the prior generation, published token prices have fallen sharply year after year, one telecom customer is described burning roughly a trillion tokens a month, and one large private buyer expects about 90 percent of its compute to serve inference or be rented out.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to rivals matching the cost-per-token gain, which would move the added workloads onto other hardware.

falsifiableTrigger: Prepaid HBM commitments in rpoBacklog shrink or deposits are refunded within a quarter.
mechanism: Buyers who put cash down years ahead on non-cancellable terms have already paid for the accelerators those parts will go into, so the orders behind them are hard to walk away from.
rationale: One memory maker holds 16 non-cancelable five-year take-or-pay agreements backed by more than $22 billion including nearly $18 billion of cash deposits, 2026 stacked-memory output is sold out under non-cancellable contracts, another supplier has finalised long-term agreements with about ten customers, and a wafer supplier signed a ten-year deal with upfront financial support.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to contract renegotiation if memory prices fall, since deposits only bind while the parts stay scarce.

falsifiableTrigger: exportControlExposure changes lift the sub-50% China cap or clear Blackwell within 2 quarters.
mechanism: Both governments impose their own conditions on the same shipments, so approvals on one side are cancelled out by restrictions on the other and almost nothing moves.
rationale: The January 2026 rule still allows only case-by-case licences under a sub-50 percent cap with a roughly 25 percent tariff, about ten approved buyers hold roughly $10 billion of licences yet shipments remain trivial, Beijing has told those buyers to keep the licensed hardware in Hong Kong, the newest generation stays banned, and the vendor has publicly denied any China-specific alternative part.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to Beijing's stance toward its own chipmakers, which currently keeps approved hardware out of the mainland.

falsifiableTrigger: Memory hbmSupplyCapex expansion pulls DRAM/NVMe prices down within 2 quarters.
mechanism: Memory is a large and rising share of what a server costs, and builders cannot pass all of it on, so the extra cost lands on their margins rather than on order volumes.
rationale: Memory component waits stretch to 32 to 40-plus weeks with prices up about 90 percent since late 2025, rack component costs inflate about 2 to 3 percent a week, server memory contract prices are seen rising more than 25 percent quarter over quarter with another supplier seeking up to a 20 percent increase, and the largest contract builder repeats that high memory prices have not slowed customer spending.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to when new memory fabs come online, since prices only ease once added output reaches buyers.

falsifiableTrigger: releaseCadence slips push a major vendor's 2H-2026 ramp into 2027.
mechanism: Each vendor hits volume on its own schedule, so the extra supply arrives in steps spread over more than a year instead of in one wave.
rationale: Next-generation parts from four vendors are still described as moving into mass production together and the leader's newest rack entered full-scale manufacturing in May 2026 with production shipments in the autumn, while the challenger's rack ships from the third quarter of 2026 but its real volume and first production output are placed at the second quarter of 2027, and one buyer's in-house parts only enter production in September.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to manufacturing delays at the trailing vendors, which push their volume further into 2027.

falsifiableTrigger: AMD customerConcentration eases as its buyer base broadens over the next 2 quarters.
mechanism: A handful of very large commitments carry nearly all the growth, so the pace of the ramp rises or falls with the decisions of a few partners.
rationale: Two named customers each intend to deploy up to six gigawatts under multi-year agreements carrying warrant incentives tied to purchase milestones, a third committed to up to two gigawatts, and the company's own filings repeat that a small number of customers will keep accounting for a substantial part of revenue.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether those commitments convert into firm orders, since reported obligations beyond one year remain small.

falsifiableTrigger: Crescent Island releaseCadence slips its customer sampling past the 2H 2026 quarter.
mechanism: Using ordinary memory on a simpler package lets an inference chip be built without a slot in the queue for stacked memory or advanced packaging.
rationale: The inference part is still described as using standard low-power memory up to 480 gigabytes instead of stacked memory specifically to avoid advanced-packaging and memory contention, with customer sampling still guided to the second half of 2026 and no slip reported this cycle.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether standard memory stays available, since that supply is also tightening as makers shift capacity to stacked parts.

falsifiableTrigger: TSMC grossMargin declines for 2 consecutive quarters as capacity loosens.
mechanism: Demand arriving from accelerators, custom chips, networking and power parts at once fills every node, which lets the maker choose the most profitable orders and charge more.
rationale: Second-quarter gross margin reached 67.7 percent, up 9.1 points year over year, with full-year revenue growth guidance raised to slightly above 40 percent and capital spending lifted to $60-64 billion, July revenue rose 44.7 percent year over year, packaging is described as so tight it limits customer growth, and even the second-largest foundry raised prices 10 to 15 percent.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to a pause in customer capital spending, because the same few buyers fill most of the leading-edge capacity.

falsifiableTrigger: A hyperscalerCapexRevision cuts 2026 or 2027 AI capex guidance within 2 quarters.
mechanism: Spending is rising far faster than the revenue it is meant to produce, so a disappointing payback would force buyers to cut orders.
rationale: The four largest US cloud buyers plan about $725 billion of 2026 capital spending, up roughly 77 percent from about $410 billion, one raised guidance twice to $195-205 billion and reported its first-ever negative free cash flow of $5.9 billion while its shares fell about 6 percent on the day, chip stocks fell on spending jitters, and analysts warned the jump may be unsustainable.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to cloud revenue growth, which is the only near-term evidence that the spending pays back.

falsifiableTrigger: NVIDIA grossMargin guidance drops below 70% in a coming quarter.
mechanism: Buyers keep paying the asking price because no rival ships an equivalent system in volume, so the maker keeps its margin even while new products ramp.
rationale: Non-GAAP gross margin was 75.0 percent with the following quarter guided to the same level, against roughly 56 percent at the nearest accelerator rival and 41.8 percent at the returning third supplier, so the premium holds through a product transition.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to input costs, since memory contract prices are rising faster than system prices.

falsifiableTrigger: Top-buyer customerConcentration in CoWoS output falls below 85% within a year.
mechanism: A few buyers book nearly all the packaging slots years ahead, so any cancellation leaves specialised capacity with no queue of smaller customers to absorb it.
rationale: The top three customers are again put at more than 85 percent of advanced-packaging output with the leading buyer at roughly 60 percent, capacity is pre-booked above 85 percent for both 2026 and 2027, and that buyer is reported to have reserved roughly 800,000 to 850,000 wafers of 2026 capacity, over half the year's total.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to alternative packaging routes, which would let smaller buyers form outside the main queue.

falsifiableTrigger: Aggregate rpoBacklog duration shortens as new commitments turn shorter-dated over 2 quarters.
mechanism: Buyers who cannot get parts today sign longer contracts to reserve future output, which stretches the average life of the order book.
rationale: One cloud backlog rose more than $50 billion sequentially to $514 billion with just over half expected to convert within 24 months, a neocloud holds a $21 billion commitment running to 2032, memory contracts run five years with cash deposits, wafer buyers are lengthening contracts from about three years to five to eight, one wafer deal runs ten years, and one campus lease runs twenty.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to supply easing, because buyers stop reserving years ahead once parts are available on demand.

falsifiableTrigger: A leading model provider reports revenue (apiArr) growth stalling quarter over quarter while compute commitments keep growing.
mechanism: Model providers pay for compute out of sales that are growing quickly, so their commitments rest on money coming in rather than on hoped-for demand.
rationale: One leading model provider's annual recurring revenue reached more than $30 billion as of April 2026, up from $1 billion in January 2025, and one large private compute owner reported AI revenues of $2.6 billion in the second quarter, up 247 percent year over year, but no other provider reports comparable figures this cycle.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to how few providers disclose revenue, since the case rests on one or two reported figures.

falsifiableTrigger: Chinese domestic accelerator designWins for frontier training stall over the next 2 quarters.
mechanism: Blocked buyers fund domestic chipmakers, which proves the hardware can train frontier models long before it can be built in the volumes those buyers want.
rationale: A 1.6-trillion-parameter model was pretrained on more than 50,000 domestic accelerators across over 35 trillion tokens, two domestic chipmakers guided first-half revenue up 135 to 149 percent and 56 to 70 percent with one holding 56.95 percent gross margin and cutting its loss almost to zero, yet Chinese firms still ordered over two million restricted foreign parts against roughly 700,000 units of inventory and domestic labs' own designs are judged more than two years out.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to domestic memory and packaging capacity, which limits how many of these accelerators can be built.

falsifiableTrigger: A neocloud's marginalBuyerFinancing debt load or net loss narrows for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Buying fleets on borrowed money produces revenue immediately but depreciation and interest arrive faster, so losses widen as the business grows.
rationale: The largest listed neocloud grew revenue about 168 percent from $1.9 billion to $5.1 billion while its net loss widened from $937 million to $1.2 billion, and its total debt rose 16.1 percent in a single quarter to $24.86 billion.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to rental rates, since the fleets must earn back their cost before the next generation arrives.

falsifiableTrigger: A top hyperscaler cuts its 2027 gigawatt power target below its 2026 level.
mechanism: Buyers now plan in gigawatts because they can get chips faster than they can get electricity and sites, so power sets how much they can install.
rationale: One buyer plans 7 gigawatts of compute in 2026 and roughly double in 2027, another went from 400 megawatts to 1.4 gigawatts in a year and guides above 2 gigawatts, power shortages are cited as the reason the next flagship part is being specified at lower power, a Texas connection queue holds roughly 474 gigawatts against about 1.2 gigawatts of forecast additions, and one vendor is in talks to invest in a developer of powered land.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to grid connection timelines, which sit outside any chip vendor's control.

falsifiableTrigger: Broadcom-plus-Marvell market-share-pct of custom ASIC co-design falls below 90% within a year.
mechanism: Cloud buyers need outside design help to build their own chips, and until now only two firms could supply it, but new entrants are winning programmes.
rationale: Two firms are still put at about 95 percent of custom accelerator co-design, but a third designer raised its share target to 15 to 20 percent with a first chip entering production in the fourth quarter of 2026 and revenue above $2 billion expected in 2026, and one model provider is in early talks with a memory maker to build its own part, so the two-supplier picture is loosening even as it holds for now.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the new entrant's first chip ships on time, since its share target rests on unproven volume.

falsifiableTrigger: Wistron odmMonthlyAiRevenue falls year-over-year for 2 consecutive months.
mechanism: Contract builders only book revenue when finished systems leave the factory, so their monthly sales measure shipments rather than promises.
rationale: One contract maker posted record June revenue of NT$321.82 billion, up 53.9 percent year over year, another crossed NT$900 billion for the first time in July at NT$946.51 billion, up 54.19 percent, the foundry posted July revenue up 44.7 percent, and one builder says AI servers are now 95 percent of its server business.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to component shortages, since a missing memory or storage part stops a whole system from shipping.

falsifiableTrigger: A neocloud's marginalBuyerFinancing debt-to-equity rises above 6:1 within 2 quarters.
mechanism: Accelerator fleets are bought with borrowed money against contracted rental income, which leaves a thin equity cushion if that income slips.
rationale: The largest listed neocloud has raised $18.81 billion of debt against $3.5 billion of equity, a 5.4 to 1 ratio, with total debt of $24.86 billion up 16.1 percent in one quarter.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to refinancing terms, because the debt matures faster than the hardware pays for itself.

falsifiableTrigger: Co-packaged optics adoption stalls below 5% of AI optical modules through 2027.
mechanism: Putting the optics inside the switch package cuts power and parts count, which ties cluster wiring to a new and still scarce manufacturing base.
rationale: Co-packaged optics is set to rise from about 0.5 percent of AI optical modules in 2026 toward about 35 percent by 2030, a switch platform claims 4 times fewer lasers and 5 times lower power at up to 409.6 terabits per second, order books are reported full through 2027 with supplies tight into 2028, and one vendor announced a long-term partnership to raise US optical capacity tenfold.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to optical engine yield and packaging capacity, both named as the limits on expanding output.

falsifiableTrigger: A named US fab or packaging project slips its build milestone past 2027.
mechanism: Vendors and their suppliers are funding fabs, packaging and component plants inside the United States, which adds capacity that does not depend on Taiwan.
rationale: One vendor plans up to $500 billion of US AI infrastructure with named partners, a contract builder opened a 324,000 square foot Texas plant, a memory maker committed $250 billion through 2035 targeting 40 percent domestic output and broke ground in New York, the foundry added an incremental $100 billion US investment, an optical partnership adds three new plants, and one supplier raised $15 billion of stock partly for capital spending.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to construction and equipment schedules, since announced money only adds supply once the plants run.

falsifiableTrigger: Google Cloud or CoreWeave rpoBacklog fails to grow sequentially for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Providers sign contracts faster than they can build capacity, so the order book grows ahead of billed revenue and shows demand earlier.
rationale: One cloud backlog reached $514 billion after rising more than $50 billion sequentially while its quarterly revenue grew 82 percent to $24.8 billion, a neocloud's contracted backlog reached $99.4 billion from $66.8 billion a month earlier and it signed a fresh multi-year expansion, and a smaller provider reported over $2.8 billion of year-to-date multi-year contracts.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to how much of the backlog converts on schedule, since only about half is expected within 24 months.

falsifiableTrigger: A top hyperscaler returns to positive free cash flow while holding 2027 capex guidance for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Spending has outgrown the cash the businesses throw off, so buyers issue debt and stock to keep building.
rationale: One cloud buyer funded its quarterly build-out with $49.6 billion of equity issuance and $20.3 billion of senior unsecured notes and reported its first-ever negative free cash flow of $5.9 billion, while combined 2026 spending across the four largest buyers is on track for about $725 billion, up about 77 percent, and one neocloud roughly doubled its own capital plan to $31-35 billion.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to borrowing costs and investor tolerance, since both decide how long this funding route stays open.

falsifiableTrigger: A new accelerator generation delivers less than a 1.5x perfPerWatt gain over its predecessor.
mechanism: More work per megawatt lets buyers raise output inside a fixed power and packaging budget instead of adding sites.
rationale: The newest rack is claimed to deliver ten times the throughput per megawatt of the prior generation and enterprise systems ten times the performance per megawatt of what they replace, the prior generational step measured about 1.6 times, a new switch line claims five times better power efficiency, a new flash generation claims 2.5 times better performance per watt, and a wafer-scale system claims ten times higher throughput per watt than its predecessor.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to vendor-reported figures, since several of the largest claims come from the sellers themselves.

falsifiableTrigger: HBM leadTimes shorten and suppliers report unsold capacity for 2 consecutive quarters before end-2027.
mechanism: Every accelerator needs a fixed stack of memory, so the number that can ship equals the memory available divided by the memory each one uses.
rationale: Suppliers can meet only 60 to 70 percent of the requested volume for the next flagship generation, one maker says it can supply no more than about half of demand and calls memory the number one constraint with no line of sight to balance, tight conditions are expected through 2027, and the shortage has already forced changes to accelerator memory specifications.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to how much wafer capacity makers shift to stacked memory, which costs three to four standard parts for each stacked one.

falsifiableTrigger: Memory supplier grossMargin falls for 2 consecutive quarters as contract prices flatten.
mechanism: Memory is scarce while system builders compete on price, so the pricing power and the profit sit with the memory suppliers.
rationale: One maker's data-center segment posted $11.5 billion of revenue, up 103 percent quarter over quarter, at an 87 percent gross margin, server memory contract prices are seen rising more than 25 percent quarter over quarter with another supplier seeking up to 20 percent, stacked-memory contract prices are forecast to roughly double into 2027, and South Korean semiconductor exports nearly tripled year over year to $26 billion in the first 20 days of August.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to new memory capacity coming online, which would end the pricing power quickly.

falsifiableTrigger: No new sovereign or enterprise cluster above 10,000 GPUs is announced for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Governments and large firms are now buying clusters directly instead of renting from the big clouds, which adds a buyer group that did not exist at this size before.
rationale: A Japanese national project will deploy 27,500 accelerators across 140 megawatts developed with the trade ministry, a Korean carrier will build a 2-gigawatt-scale national cloud, a pharmaceutical company is deploying eight of the newest systems as a second cluster, a rival launched a variant aimed specifically at sovereign and high-performance computing buyers, a wafer-scale vendor names a national research group and a university among customers, and quant trading firms are becoming a meaningful rental segment.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to public funding cycles, since national projects depend on budgets rather than commercial returns.

falsifiableTrigger: Intel data-center revenue growth falls below 10% year over year for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Better factory yields and cycle times let the company sell more server parts and outside manufacturing at higher margins, adding a third source of supply.
rationale: Data-center and AI revenue reached $6.3 billion, up 59 percent year over year, foundry revenue reached $5.8 billion, up 31 percent, gross margin rose to 40.4 percent from 27.5 percent a year earlier, the next quarter is guided to $15.8-16.8 billion above expectations, capital spending was raised above $20 billion, and a first named external foundry customer was signed.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether its packaging and next node hit their 2027 production targets, since the recovery is funded ahead of proof.

falsifiableTrigger: New vendor equity-for-compute deals in marginalBuyerFinancing stop appearing for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Chip sellers put money into the firms that buy their chips, so part of the reported demand is funded by the seller's own balance sheet.
rationale: One accelerator maker committed a strategic equity investment of up to $5 billion in a model provider alongside its deployment agreement, the market leader invested an undisclosed amount in another model provider, holds a $5 billion stake in a rival chipmaker, held preliminary talks about investing in or acquiring an inference-chip startup, and is in advanced talks to invest several hundred million dollars in a powered land developer.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to the value of those stakes, which falls at the same time the customers' orders would.

falsifiableTrigger: Standard DRAM S10 spot prices fall for 2 consecutive months as suppliers restore non-AI capacity.
mechanism: Makers move wafers to the memory that earns most, which starves the standard parts used in consumer and general-purpose products and lifts their prices.
rationale: Standard memory spot prices hit $81.20 for a 16GB DDR4 part, up 17.5 percent in a month and above the prior peak, DDR5 broke $50 for the first time, one vendor raised graphics card bundle prices about 10 percent citing tripled graphics memory spot prices, makers are cutting standard output to favour higher-margin parts, and enterprise contracts now get priority flash allocation over retail.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to new fab capacity, since only added output lets makers serve both markets at once.

falsifiableTrigger: No new multi-year accelerator-to-memory supply partnership is announced for 2 consecutive quarters through 2027.
mechanism: With memory sold out, chip makers contract directly with suppliers years ahead so their own output is not decided by someone else's allocation.
rationale: One vendor entered a long-term partnership with a memory maker to secure next-generation supply and jointly develop parts, three suppliers began full-scale development of a 16-high stack specifically for that vendor targeting fourth-quarter 2026 delivery, and a memory maker signed a ten-year wafer supply agreement with upfront financial support inside a raised $250 billion domestic plan.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to memory scarcity itself, since these deals stop being worth signing once supply is easy.

falsifiableTrigger: The leading supplier's HBM market-share-pct falls below 50% within 4 quarters as rivals ship volume.
mechanism: One supplier held most of the stacked-memory output, but a rival reaching similar yields turns a single source into two.
rationale: The leading supplier is put at 56.4 to 58 percent of the stacked-memory market and about 62 percent of the newest generation, but the second maker has pushed its yield on that generation to close to 80 percent about four months early, aims to lift its share to roughly 38 percent by year-end 2026 and is reported raising capacity 50 percent, so the single-source picture is loosening even as the largest cloud buyers keep locking long-term contracts.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to qualification at the largest accelerator maker, since share only moves once its parts are approved.

falsifiableTrigger: No new diversion prosecution or whitelist reduction is reported for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Prosecutions and shorter approved-buyer lists raise the cost of reselling restricted parts, which closes the informal routes that used to carry them.
rationale: Taiwanese prosecutors expanded a criminal probe into chip smuggling, raiding a server maker's local office and affiliates and detaining employees in a case tied to charges alleging some $2.5 billion of servers were shipped without a licence, and the chip vendor more than halved the number of Asian customers authorised to buy under a new compliance whitelist.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to enforcement outside Taiwan, since diverted hardware can be routed through other jurisdictions.

falsifiableTrigger: CoWoS lead times stay above 52 weeks through the end of 2027 while the supply gap fails to narrow below 15%.
mechanism: Packaging capacity is being added faster than memory capacity, but the two most recent estimates of the remaining packaging gap point in opposite directions.
rationale: ADJUSTED: Advanced packaging capacity keeps expanding but reports now disagree on whether the shortfall has narrowed to about 10 percent or is still near 20 percent, with lines booked through 2027, while memory shows no easing at all.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to which gap estimate holds up, since 10 percent and 20 percent imply very different shipment ceilings.

falsifiableTrigger: NAND contract prices for server drives fall for 2 consecutive quarters while Rubin deployments keep growing.
mechanism: The new rack design adds a large drive pool per system, so each unit shipped consumes far more flash than the generation before it.
rationale: The newest generation's context memory tier is expected to pull flash demand from about 35 million terabytes this year to more than 100 million next year with each unit carrying 576 drives, enterprise contracts now get priority allocation over retail, flash scarcity is named alongside memory as the driver of rack costs rising 2 to 3 percent a week, and one maker expects tight conditions beyond calendar 2027.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to how fast the new generation deploys, since the demand step only lands as those racks ship.

falsifiableTrigger: Every major cloud provider publishes list rates for its newest rack-scale systems for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Providers sell their scarcest newest systems through negotiated contracts instead of listed rates, so published prices cover only older hardware.
rationale: One provider's public pages across four separate captures from July to August 2026 still list no H200, GB200, GB300 or B300 line items and no rival accelerator options, with longer terms quoted only as custom pricing, so its newest publicly rentable part remains a B200 at $6.69 per hour.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to supply of the newest racks, since list pricing returns once capacity is no longer allocated.

falsifiableTrigger: NVIDIA accelerator market-share-pct stabilises or rises for 2 consecutive quarters while rival shipments grow.
mechanism: The overall market is growing faster than one vendor can supply it, so rivals absorb the extra growth without taking existing business away.
rationale: One estimate has share falling from a 2024 peak of 87 percent to 75 percent in 2026 and others put it at roughly 70 to 80 percent, while a further account still describes as much as 90 percent in a given quarter, and revenue set a record at $75.2 billion, up 92 percent year over year, so the direction holds but the level remains disputed.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to how share is measured, since published estimates for the same period range from 70 to 90 percent.

falsifiableTrigger: A major buyer returns to purchasing loose accelerators rather than vendor racks for a flagship cluster within 2 quarters.
mechanism: Vendors now sell the whole cabinet with its networking and software, so buyers compare finished systems rather than individual chips.
rationale: The challenger launched a 72-accelerator rack with 31TB of memory and 2.9 exaFLOPS positioned directly against the leader's 72-accelerator rack, the leader's newest rack entered production ramp with a reported 576-accelerator scale-up of eight racks, and a wafer-scale entrant now ships a rack-scale system that pairs with rival racks rather than replacing them.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to open rack standards, which would let buyers mix parts from several vendors in one cabinet.

falsifiableTrigger: ERCOT data-center additions exceed 5 GW over the next 4 quarters as the pause lifts.
mechanism: New sites wait in connection queues and state-level pauses, so the grid rather than the chip supply decides when capacity comes online.
rationale: The Texas connection queue still holds roughly 474 gigawatts with about 90 percent of requests from data centres while only about 1.2 gigawatts of additions are forecast between the second quarter of 2026 and the first quarter of 2027, lost data-centre revenue from the pause is estimated at up to $8 billion, and one vendor is now investing in already-powered land, but again no finding reports transformer lead times.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to state policy, since the pause and the queue are administrative rather than physical limits.

falsifiableTrigger: Median newest-generation gpuSpotPrice falls while prior-generation rates rise for 2 consecutive months.
mechanism: Buyers who cannot get the newest racks fall back to the previous generation, which lifts the older rate instead of letting it drift lower.
rationale: The newest publicly listed part held flat at $6.69 per hour while the prior-generation part rose from $3.99 on August 19 to $4.29 on August 21, so the premium moved toward older hardware rather than away from it, even though used card asking prices of roughly $21,000 to $28,000 sit below the earlier $25,000 to $40,000 range.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to how few newest-generation rates are published at all, since the comparison rests on one provider's page.

falsifiableTrigger: Alternative packaging upstreamLeadTimes rise above 52 weeks, or no accelerator maker places advanced-packaging volume outside TSMC for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Buyers facing year-long waits at the leading packaging house place work with suppliers who quote half the wait, which spreads the work across more sites.
rationale: One cloud buyer committed to more than three million units of a rival's bridge packaging for delivery in 2028, that rival reports very high demand and a growing backlog targeting 2027 volume, alternative routes quote 26 to 39 weeks against 52 to 78, two assembly houses are adding capacity, the market leader is now outsourcing a front-end packaging step to outside partners, and one accelerator maker is weighing moving some output to the rival.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the alternative routes suit high-bandwidth accelerators, since one is described as a better fit for custom chips.

falsifiableTrigger: AMD's share of CoWoS output in pkgCapacityOrderSpread rises above 15% within 2 quarters.
mechanism: One fixed pool of packaging slots must cover two product lines, so building more of one directly reduces the other.
rationale: The company is again put at roughly 11 percent of advanced-packaging output, about 105,000 wafers, inside a pool where the top three customers hold more than 85 percent, and must split that allocation between its server processors and its accelerators so each processor slot used cannot go to an accelerator.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to alternative packaging routes, which would let one of the two product lines move off the contested pool.

falsifiableTrigger: The next flagship ships with its originally planned 288GB memory configuration within 2 quarters of launch.
mechanism: Putting less memory on each accelerator lets a fixed pool of memory cover more units, so the shortage changes what the product is rather than only how many ship.
rationale: Multiple accounts now report the next flagship variant cut to 192GB in an 8-high stack from 288GB in a 12-high stack and far below a 1TB design previewed earlier, with supply constraints and power limits named as the reasons, testing at 192GB and 256GB with some samples reverting to the prior memory generation, and four alternative memory specifications under assessment since the third quarter of 2026.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to performance loss, since one analysis says performance drops sharply below 500GB of memory.

falsifiableTrigger: The first Korean AI factory misses its 2027 target or the partnership is not converted from letters of intent into signed contracts within 2 quarters.
mechanism: Tying construction, memory supply and cloud capacity into one country's industrial base makes that country a second place where the buildout physically happens.
rationale: The partnership is now described as a $500-billion-plus initiative covering factory construction, next-generation memory supply and cloud deployment across Asia-Pacific with the first facility targeted for 2027, a Korean carrier will build a 2-gigawatt-scale national cloud, a memory maker approved a 7.09 trillion won packaging investment, and South Korean semiconductor exports nearly tripled year over year to $26 billion in the first 20 days of August.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to conversion, since the headline figure still rests on letters of intent rather than signed contracts.

falsifiableTrigger: No accelerator or system vendor announces a shipping product using the high-bandwidth flash specification within 4 quarters.
mechanism: A standard flash tier gives system builders a cheaper memory layer that draws on a different supply chain than the sold-out stacked memory.
rationale: Two suppliers published the first high-bandwidth flash specification through an open standards body covering capacities to 512GB in 8-high and 16-high stacks and three performance grades from about 0.4 to 3.0 terabytes per second, with a cloud buyer and a chip designer joining the group, the newest generation's flash tier already carries 576 drives per unit, and a new flash generation claims 2.5 times better performance per watt.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to flash supply itself, which is already being pulled tight by the same rack generation.

falsifiableTrigger: AMD software releases deliver less than a 1.5x measured inference gain over the prior release for 2 consecutive releases.
mechanism: Software tuning raises what today's installed accelerators can do without waiting for new hardware, so competitiveness improves before shipments do.
rationale: An optimised kernel improved end-to-end throughput 2.10 times and cut time-to-first-token 3.71 times on a current accelerator, the software stack is claimed at 3.3 times inference and 2.4 times training over the prior release and was relaunched as a named platform, while the new rack's mass production and first output are placed at the second quarter of 2027.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to independent verification, since the speedup figures come from the vendor's own testing.

falsifiableTrigger: SpaceX nameplate compute fails to exceed 2 gigawatts by the end of 2026 or its quarterly AI capex falls below $10 billion for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: A buyer outside the traditional cloud group is spending at cloud scale and has committed to a single vendor, which moves a large block of output to one customer.
rationale: Nameplate compute reached 1.4 gigawatts from 1.0 a quarter earlier and 400 megawatts a year earlier with guidance above 2 gigawatts by year-end and about 10 gigawatts by end-2027, quarterly capital spending was about $18.4 billion of which roughly $15.8 billion went to AI compute, AI revenue reached $2.6 billion up 247 percent year over year, and management confirmed exclusivity to one vendor while expecting a very significant share of its 2027 output.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to how it funds the spend, since its AI revenue is still small next to its quarterly capital outlay.

falsifiableTrigger: Intel's share of 2.5D packaging capacity fails to rise above 20% within 4 quarters, or its bridge packaging misses 2027 mass production.
mechanism: The alternative route depends on a single fully booked component supplier and a substrate that is not in volume yet, so it inherits a bottleneck of its own.
rationale: The bridge packaging route reports yields above 90 percent, very high demand and a growing backlog targeting 2027 volume at roughly half the leading route's cost, but its sole silicon capacitor supplier is already fully booked, substrate mass production is expected only in 2027 with initial yields targeted at 50 percent, the owner holds roughly 13.7 percent of 2.5D capacity against about 70 percent for the leader, and the technology is described as better suited to custom chips than to high-bandwidth accelerators.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to that one capacitor supplier, since nothing else in the route can substitute for it.

falsifiableTrigger: MediaTek market-share-pct of AI accelerators fails to exceed 5% within 4 quarters, or its first chip misses Q4 2026 production.
mechanism: A third design house winning cloud programmes gives buyers another route to custom silicon that does not run through the two incumbents.
rationale: The entrant raised its accelerator share target to 15 to 20 percent from 10 to 15 percent, sizes the 2027 market at $80 billion, expects more than $2 billion of 2026 revenue with a first chip entering production in the fourth quarter of 2026 and a second in 2028, and approved a $5 billion financing budget, but an analyst notes its 2024 share was under 1 percent and calls the target very high.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to the first chip reaching production on time, since the share target has no shipped volume behind it yet.

falsifiableTrigger: Used prior-generation server prices fall more than 40% within 2 quarters, or published prior-generation rental rates drop below $2.00 per GPU-hour.
mechanism: Older systems cost a fraction of new ones to buy and still rent out, so their economics keep them in service rather than retired.
rationale: A new top-end server is priced at about $500,000 against roughly $150,000 to $180,000 for a used prior-generation eight-accelerator server, published rentals still list the older part at $3.99 to $4.29 per hour and an older one at $2.79 against $6.69 for the newest listed system, and used cards ask roughly $21,000 to $28,000.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to how fast new capacity arrives, since abundant new racks would pull rental demand off older hardware.

falsifiableTrigger: Wafer suppliers report spare 300mm capacity or falling wafer prices for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: New memory fabs need blank wafers before they can produce anything, so the squeeze moves one step further back up the chain.
rationale: One wafer maker says its 300mm, 200mm and 150mm lines are effectively at full utilisation with constraints already appearing on some advanced 300mm products, spot prices are rising with further increases expected and pressure seen intensifying through the second half of 2027, buyers are rebuilding safety stock and lengthening contracts from about three years to five to eight, and one ten-year agreement carries upfront financial support from the customer.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to how many memory fabs start at once, since they all draw on the same wafer supply.

falsifiableTrigger: AMD's reported remaining performance obligations stay below $1 billion for 2 consecutive quarters while new gigawatt commitments keep being announced.
mechanism: Gigawatt announcements describe intent, while the reported obligation figure counts only what customers are contractually bound to pay, and the two are far apart.
rationale: The company reported only $222 million of remaining performance obligations on contracts longer than one year as of June 27, 2026, of which $144 million falls within twelve months, and disclosed no dollar backlog on its call, while its filings describe two customers each intending to deploy up to six gigawatts under agreements carrying warrant incentives.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to the first firm purchase orders behind those deployments, which would close the gap quickly.

falsifiableTrigger: No hardwired inference product reaches customer shipment within 4 quarters, or inference workloads stay on general accelerators for 2 consecutive quarters after launch.
mechanism: Fixing a finished model into hardware removes the flexibility a general accelerator pays for, which makes running that model cheaper.
rationale: One accelerator vendor signed a definitive agreement to acquire a startup that burns model weights into silicon, framing inference as one of the fastest-growing segments and planning to pair the technology with its own accelerators at system level, its own materials note such silicon could erode general accelerator demand in cost-sensitive inference, and the market leader held preliminary talks with another inference-chip startup.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to how fast models change, since a hardwired part is worth little once its model is superseded.

falsifiableTrigger: Non-cloud owners stop signing new rental or lease agreements for 2 consecutive quarters, or rented share of their fleets falls below 50%.
mechanism: Owners who bought more capacity than they need for themselves rent the surplus out, which puts a new layer of supply between the chip vendors and end users.
rationale: One large private owner expects roughly 90 percent of its compute to serve inference or be rented to others with only about 10 percent used for its own training, and holds multibillion-dollar capacity leases with two other firms, while a content delivery provider reported cloud infrastructure revenue of $99 million, up 39 percent, including accelerator services.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to their own workload growth, since capacity they start using themselves stops being available to rent.

falsifiableTrigger: Reported HBM4 yields fall back below 70% or contract prices keep rising for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Better yield raises output per wafer, but the wafers allocated to stacked memory are capped, so higher yield has not closed the gap.
rationale: Both large Korean makers have reached about 80 percent yield on the newest stacked memory roughly four months early, yet suppliers can still meet only 60 to 70 percent of requested volume for the next flagship generation, one maker says it can supply no more than about half of demand with no line of sight to balance, and supply is expected to stay tight through 2027.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to wafer allocation rather than yield, since each stacked part consumes three to four standard parts' worth of capacity.

falsifiableTrigger: No compute-financing platform closes a funded transaction within 2 quarters, or the memorandums lapse without binding agreements.
mechanism: Third-party capital pays for the accelerators, which moves the funding burden away from the chip vendor and the cloud balance sheets.
rationale: One vendor signed memorandums with six large asset managers and banks to set up compute-financing platforms intended to mobilise more than $500 billion of third-party capital for its customers, and it cut its own proposed guarantee on one campus from $250 billion to less than $120 billion, shifting part of the funding off its balance sheet, though the memorandums are described as non-binding.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to conversion into binding agreements, since nothing is funded while the arrangements remain memorandums.

falsifiableTrigger: Samsung foundry utilisation loosens or it reverses the 10-15% price increase within 2 quarters.
mechanism: Overflow demand that the leading foundry cannot take fills the second supplier's lines, which lets it raise prices too.
rationale: The second-largest contract chipmaker raised prices 10 to 15 percent on new orders in July 2026 as AI demand tightened capacity, its advanced line runs at full capacity making logic chips and its own memory base dies and it cannot meet all orders, and it expects AI and high-performance computing to exceed 30 percent of foundry revenue this year, up from 15 to 20 percent in late 2025, from a 7 percent global share against more than 70 percent for the leader.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to leading-edge capacity at the market leader, since this supplier fills up mainly on what spills over.

falsifiableTrigger: Cerebras fails to report CS-4 customer shipments within 2 quarters, or no named customer expands beyond its initial system within 4 quarters.
mechanism: Building the processor on a whole wafer sidesteps the stacked-memory and packaging queues that limit conventional racks, and it slots alongside them rather than replacing them.
rationale: The vendor unveiled a rack-scale system of three whole-wafer processors delivering 750 petaFLOPS with first shipments beginning this quarter, claims up to 30 times more tokens per second per user against accelerator systems and 10 times higher throughput per watt than its predecessor, and names a model provider, a sovereign group, a university and a cloud among customers while supporting pairing with rival racks.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to shipped volume, since the performance claims come from the vendor and no customer count is given.

detail.falsifiableTrigger: No new vendor-guaranteed or vendor-funded data-centre site above 1 gigawatt is announced for 2 consecutive quarters.
detail.mechanism: Chips cannot be installed without powered sites, so the vendor puts its own money and guarantees behind land and grid access to keep its shipments from stalling.
detail.sensitivity: Most sensitive to the credit standing of the tenants, since the guarantees only pay out if a tenant defaults.
detail.statement: The leading accelerator vendor is now guaranteeing data-centre leases and investing in powered land so that sites exist for its own hardware to fill.
detail.title: Chip vendors start buying the land and power behind their customers

detail.falsifiableTrigger: A hyperscaler raises AI capex guidance and its shares rise on the day for 2 consecutive quarters.
detail.mechanism: When investors mark a company down for spending more, management faces a direct cost for raising budgets further, which slows the pace of new commitments.
detail.sensitivity: Most sensitive to reported cloud revenue growth, which is what lets investors read the spending as an investment instead of a cost.
detail.statement: Share prices are falling on the days companies raise their AI spending plans, which puts a new brake on how far buyers can push their budgets.
detail.title: Investors now treat bigger AI budgets as a cost

falsifiableTrigger: B200 rpoBacklog falls below 2 million units for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Buyers order more accelerators than the parts chain can build, so NVIDIA sells everything it can make and revenue tracks supply rather than appetite.
rationale: NVIDIA posted record data-center revenue of $75.2 billion, up 92% year over year, and guided the next quarter to $91 billion, while its memory suppliers can fill only 60% to 70% of the volume it asked for and the prior order book stood at about 3.6 million units, so orders keep running ahead of what the company can build.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to stacked-memory and packaging availability, since those set the ceiling on how much NVIDIA can ship.

falsifiableTrigger: HBM leadTimes ease to available-on-demand and CoWoS lead times fall below 26 weeks before the end of 2027.
mechanism: Every accelerator needs both a packaging slot and a stack of memory, so whichever is scarcer sets the shipment count no matter how many chips are fabricated.
rationale: Advanced packaging is sold out with 52 to 78 week waits and lines booked through 2027, while Micron says it can supply only about half of customer demand and calls standard memory the top constraint its largest customers face, so both limits are still binding.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to how fast new packaging lines and memory fabs come online relative to accelerator orders.

falsifiableTrigger: AMD accelerator market-share-pct fails to rise above 7% through 2027.
mechanism: AMD wins named anchor customers and ships a competitive rack, but its packaging and memory allocation limits volume, so share moves only as fast as supply allows.
rationale: AMD's data-center revenue reached $6.7 billion in the second quarter, more than doubling year over year, and its 72-accelerator racks are in production with Anthropic, OpenAI, Meta, Microsoft and Oracle named, yet it is still described at roughly 5 to 7 percent of the accelerator market against NVIDIA near 90 percent, with real volume only arriving in 2027.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the 2027 volume ramp holds its schedule after the reported manufacturing delay.

falsifiableTrigger: ASIC market-share-pct growth falls back below GPU growth for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Cloud buyers move their steady inference work onto chips they design themselves, so each in-house part they deploy is a merchant accelerator they do not buy.
rationale: In-house chips are projected to grow 44.6% in 2026 against 16.1% for merchant accelerators, Meta's four new parts enter production in September, Microsoft is negotiating capacity for upward of 300,000 of its own accelerators for 2027, and Google has ordered more than 3 million units of alternative packaging for its next-generation part.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether in-house parts reach volume production on time and whether their owners keep buying merchant parts alongside them.

falsifiableTrigger: gpuSpotPrice for a current-generation part drops more than 20% within a quarter.
mechanism: Renting stays expensive because capacity is scarce, while second-hand cards compete against newer parts and so lose value faster than rental rates do.
rationale: The newest publicly listed part held at $6.69 per hour while the prior-generation card moved from $3.99 on August 19 to $4.29 on August 21, and used-card asking prices of roughly $21,000 to $28,000 sit below the earlier $25,000 to $40,000 range, matching the thesis as written.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to how quickly newly built capacity reaches the rental market.

falsifiableTrigger: exportControlExposure eases so China DC revenue recovers above prior levels within 2 quarters.
mechanism: Government rules bar the strongest parts from the second-largest buying market, so a large block of willing buyers cannot be served at any price.
rationale: NVIDIA's China revenue fell to $4.55 billion from $9.66 billion a year earlier, it assumes no China data-center revenue in its outlook, licensed shipments remain trivial, and AMD continues to flag the same restrictions after prior-year charges on its restricted part.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to licence policy changes on both the American and Chinese side.

falsifiableTrigger: Vendor-financed GPU commitments in rpoBacklog exceed 300,000 units within 2 quarters.
mechanism: When the seller guarantees the buyer's leases or debt, reported demand partly reflects the seller's own balance sheet rather than independent buying power.
rationale: ADJUSTED: NVIDIA still underwrites a large share of its own demand, but the support is shifting from direct chip credit toward data-centre lease guarantees and outside investor money, with one proposed customer guarantee cut from $250 billion to under $120 billion even as it capped a new site guarantee at $105 billion and signed platforms meant to raise over $500 billion from third parties.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether outside investors actually fund the announced platforms or the memorandums lapse.

falsifiableTrigger: customerConcentration for the top three direct customers falls below prior shares next fiscal year.
mechanism: A handful of buyers take most of the output, so one of them slowing orders or switching to its own chips removes a large slice of revenue at once.
rationale: Three direct customers accounted for 21%, 17% and 16% of NVIDIA revenue in the latest quarter, up from a year earlier when four customers passed half of revenue, and SpaceX says it expects a very significant share of 2027 output while one campus is tied to a single 20-year tenant.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether new buyer tiers grow fast enough to dilute the largest accounts.

falsifiableTrigger: NVIDIA DC Ethernet switch market-share-pct slips from #1 within 2 quarters.
mechanism: Selling the wiring with the computers makes the whole system one purchase, so a buyer swapping vendors has to replace the network as well as the chips.
rationale: NVIDIA took the top revenue spot in data-centre Ethernet switching for the first time by pairing its networking with its accelerators, its newest switch line names CoreWeave, Microsoft, Nebius, SpaceX and Tesla as first customers, and a new neocloud expansion ships that networking with the racks; still no finding compares networking growth with compute growth.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to open networking standards that let buyers mix vendors inside one cluster.

falsifiableTrigger: Cost-per-token gains stall so tokenEconomics improves less than one generation cycle.
mechanism: Falling cost per answer makes uses that were too expensive worth running, so cheaper serving adds workloads instead of shrinking spending.
rationale: The newest generation is credited with ten times lower cost per token than the one before it, open-model serving costs have fallen 30 to 50 percent a year since 2023, and one telecom buyer is described as consuming roughly a trillion tokens a month.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether each new generation keeps delivering large cost-per-answer gains.

falsifiableTrigger: Prepaid HBM commitments in rpoBacklog shrink or deposits are refunded within a quarter.
mechanism: Buyers who have already paid cash they cannot get back have every reason to take delivery, so the memory orders behind future accelerators are hard to walk away from.
rationale: Micron holds sixteen non-cancelable five-year take-or-pay agreements backed by more than $22 billion of commitments including nearly $18 billion of cash deposits, the 2026 stacked-memory supply is sold out under non-cancellable contracts, and one Korean supplier says it has finalised long-term agreements with about ten customers.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether any large buyer tries to renegotiate or write off a prepaid contract.

falsifiableTrigger: exportControlExposure changes lift the sub-50% China cap or clear Blackwell within 2 quarters.
mechanism: Both governments limit the same trade from opposite ends, so approvals on paper do not turn into shipments or revenue.
rationale: Licences remain case-by-case under a cap of under 50 percent of American shipments plus a roughly 25 percent tariff, actual shipments are still called trivial with no revenue booked, and Chinese regulators have told approved buyers to keep the licensed hardware in Hong Kong.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether Beijing lets licensed hardware cross into the mainland.

falsifiableTrigger: Memory hbmSupplyCapex expansion pulls DRAM/NVMe prices down within 2 quarters.
mechanism: Memory is a large and rising slice of each server's bill of materials, so its price increases land on the builder's margin while buyers keep ordering.
rationale: Memory component waits stretch to 32 to 40 weeks with prices up about 90 percent since late 2025, rack costs are inflating 2 to 3 percent a week, server memory contract prices are expected to rise 18 to more than 25 percent in the third quarter, and the largest contract builder repeats that high memory prices have not slowed customer spending.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to when new memory fabs start producing at volume.

falsifiableTrigger: releaseCadence slips push a major vendor's 2H-2026 ramp into 2027.
mechanism: Each vendor hits volume production on its own schedule, so new supply arrives in a sequence of ramps rather than one step change.
rationale: NVIDIA's newest rack entered production ramp in the third quarter of 2026 with shipments forecast for the autumn, AMD's rack reached production with third-quarter shipments but its real volume ramp is put at the second quarter of 2027, and Meta's in-house parts only enter production in September, so the wave still lands in stages.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to manufacturing delays at any one vendor in the sequence.

falsifiableTrigger: AMD customerConcentration eases as its buyer base broadens over the next 2 quarters.
mechanism: A handful of very large commitments carry almost all of AMD's accelerator growth, so one of them slipping moves the whole segment.
rationale: AMD's own filing names OpenAI and Meta each intending to deploy up to 6 gigawatts under multi-year agreements with warrants tied to purchase milestones, Anthropic adds up to 2 gigawatts, and the company repeats that a small number of customers will keep making up a substantial part of revenue.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the announced gigawatt commitments convert into firm orders on schedule.

falsifiableTrigger: Crescent Island releaseCadence slips its customer sampling past the 2H 2026 quarter.
mechanism: Using ordinary memory instead of stacked memory removes the two scarcest inputs from the build, so this design can ship on capacity that is not fought over.
rationale: Intel's inference part is still guided to customer sampling in the second half of 2026 and is described as using standard low-power memory of up to 480 gigabytes instead of stacked memory precisely to avoid competing for packaging and stacked-memory supply, with no shipping product yet reported.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the part samples on time and whether its lower memory speed is good enough for real serving work.

falsifiableTrigger: TSMC grossMargin declines for 2 consecutive quarters as capacity loosens.
mechanism: Demand from several kinds of AI chips at once fills every node, so the foundry can choose its customers and hold prices firm.
rationale: TSMC reported a 67.7% gross margin, raised full-year revenue growth guidance to slightly above 40% and lifted capital spending to $60-64 billion, July revenue rose 44.7% year over year, and it says packaging tightness is limiting customer growth with the gap staying wide for years.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to any broad slowdown in AI orders that would leave capacity unfilled.

falsifiableTrigger: A hyperscalerCapexRevision cuts 2026 or 2027 AI capex guidance within 2 quarters.
mechanism: Spending is being pulled forward faster than the revenue it is meant to serve, so a disappointing payback would force the buyers to cut orders.
rationale: The four largest cloud buyers plan about $725 billion of 2026 spending, up roughly 77 percent, Alphabet reported its first ever negative free cash flow of $5.9 billion and fell about 6 percent on the day it raised guidance, analysts warned the jump may be unsustainable, and AMD shares fell more than 8 percent on a capital-spending overshoot.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether cloud and model revenue keeps growing fast enough to justify the spending.

falsifiableTrigger: NVIDIA grossMargin guidance drops below 70% in a coming quarter.
mechanism: Scarcity and a full-system product let NVIDIA price above its rivals, so its margin holds even as new products carry early manufacturing costs.
rationale: NVIDIA reported a 75.0% non-GAAP gross margin and guided the following quarter to the same level, far above AMD at 56% and Intel near 42%, so buyers are still paying premium prices during a product changeover.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to rising memory input costs and to competitive pricing once rival racks reach volume.

falsifiableTrigger: Top-buyer customerConcentration in CoWoS output falls below 85% within a year.
mechanism: A small group books nearly all the packaging line time, so if one of them cancelled there would be no comparable buyer able to take that slot.
rationale: The top three customers hold more than 85 percent of advanced-packaging output with NVIDIA alone at roughly 60 percent, capacity is pre-booked above 85 percent for 2026 and 2027, and NVIDIA is reported to have reserved 800,000 to 850,000 wafers of 2026 capacity, over half the year's total.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether smaller accelerator programmes grow big enough to absorb freed capacity.

falsifiableTrigger: Aggregate rpoBacklog duration shortens as new commitments turn shorter-dated over 2 quarters.
mechanism: Buyers who fear they cannot get capacity later sign for it years ahead, so the average length of the order book keeps stretching.
rationale: Google Cloud's committed order book rose more than $50 billion in a quarter to $514 billion with only just over half converting within 24 months, a neocloud holds a purchase commitment running to 2032, one campus sits under a 20-year lease, and wafer buyers are stretching contracts from about three years to five to eight.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to any easing of scarcity that would let buyers wait instead of pre-booking.

falsifiableTrigger: A leading model provider reports revenue (apiArr) growth stalling quarter over quarter while compute commitments keep growing.
mechanism: Compute commitments are being funded out of sales that are themselves growing quickly, so the buildout rests on paying customers rather than on hope.
rationale: Anthropic's annualised revenue reached more than $30 billion from $1 billion fifteen months earlier, SpaceX reported AI revenue of $2.6 billion up 247 percent year over year, and Google Cloud revenue accelerated 82 percent to $24.8 billion with operating income of $8.8 billion.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether these revenue growth rates hold as the base gets larger.

falsifiableTrigger: Chinese domestic accelerator designWins for frontier training stall over the next 2 quarters.
mechanism: Barred from the best foreign parts, Chinese buyers fund home-grown accelerators, and each proven training run makes the switch easier for the next buyer.
rationale: A 1.6-trillion-parameter model was pretrained entirely on more than 50,000 domestic accelerators across over 35 trillion tokens, and two Chinese suppliers now show real commercial traction, with one guiding first-half revenue up 135 to 149 percent and holding a 56.95 percent gross margin while cutting its loss by 95.73 percent and another guiding growth of 56 to 70 percent.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to domestic memory and software gaps, which are still described as the limiting factors.

falsifiableTrigger: A neocloud's marginalBuyerFinancing debt load or net loss narrows for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Buying fleets on credit front-loads interest and depreciation, so revenue growth and losses rise together.
rationale: CoreWeave's revenue grew about 168 percent from $1.9 billion to $5.1 billion while its net loss widened from $937 million to $1.2 billion, exactly the pattern the thesis describes.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to rental prices and to how quickly new contracts convert into cash.

falsifiableTrigger: A top hyperscaler cuts its 2027 gigawatt power target below its 2026 level.
mechanism: A site can only run as many accelerators as its electricity supply allows, so power availability now decides deployment size before chip supply does.
rationale: Buyers now describe their plans in gigawatts, with Meta at 7 gigawatts for 2026 and roughly double in 2027 and SpaceX at 1.4 gigawatts heading past 2, NVIDIA is reported to be lowering product power ratings because sites cannot supply enough electricity, and a Texas connection queue of roughly 474 gigawatts is expected to add only about 1.2 gigawatts of data-centre capacity in a year.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to grid connection approvals and to how much work each new generation does per megawatt.

falsifiableTrigger: Broadcom-plus-Marvell market-share-pct of custom ASIC co-design falls below 90% within a year.
mechanism: New entrants win chip programmes that used to have only two possible partners, so the concentration behind custom silicon slowly loosens.
rationale: The two incumbent design firms are still put at about 95 percent of the custom co-design market, but MediaTek has raised its share target to 15 to 20 percent with a first chip entering production in the fourth quarter of 2026 and over $2 billion of 2026 revenue expected, Anthropic is in early talks with Samsung about its own chip, and Google's newest award may be moving work between the two incumbents rather than adding to them.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether new entrants convert announced programmes into shipping volume, which one analyst doubts given a sub-1 percent starting share.

falsifiableTrigger: Wistron odmMonthlyAiRevenue falls year-over-year for 2 consecutive months.
mechanism: Contract builders bill only for machines they actually ship, so their monthly sales are a direct check that orders are turning into hardware.
rationale: Foxconn's July revenue reached NT$946.51 billion, up 54.19 percent year over year and its first month above NT$900 billion, Wistron posted a record June up 53.9 percent, TSMC's July revenue rose 44.7 percent, and Wistron says AI servers are now 95 percent of its server business.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to component shortages that could delay assembly even when orders exist.

falsifiableTrigger: A neocloud's marginalBuyerFinancing debt-to-equity rises above 6:1 within 2 quarters.
mechanism: Fleets bought with borrowed money leave little owner capital between an earnings shortfall and the lenders.
rationale: CoreWeave has raised $18.81 billion of debt against $3.5 billion of equity, a 5.4 to 1 ratio, with total debt of $24.86 billion up 16.1 percent in one quarter.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to borrowing costs and to whether contracted revenue arrives on schedule.

falsifiableTrigger: Co-packaged optics adoption stalls below 5% of AI optical modules through 2027.
mechanism: Putting the optics next to the switch chip cuts power and parts count, so cluster wiring now depends on an optics roadmap with its own capacity limits.
rationale: The new switch platform claims four times fewer lasers and five times lower power at up to 409.6 terabits per second, adoption is projected to rise from about 0.5 percent of AI optical modules in 2026 to about 35 percent by 2030, order books are reported full through 2027 with supply tight into 2028, and NVIDIA and Corning are expanding American optical manufacturing tenfold.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to optical engine yields and to packaging capacity, both named as expansion bottlenecks.

falsifiableTrigger: A named US fab or packaging project slips its build milestone past 2027.
mechanism: Vendors and their suppliers are funding fabrication, packaging and components inside the United States, which adds capacity that does not depend on Taiwan.
rationale: NVIDIA plans up to $500 billion of American AI infrastructure with named partners, Wistron opened a 324,000 square foot Texas plant, Micron committed $250 billion to American memory manufacturing through 2035, TSMC added $100 billion of American investment, Corning is adding three plants, and Intel raised $15 billion of equity partly for capital spending.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to construction and staffing schedules, since announcements lead output by years.

falsifiableTrigger: Google Cloud or CoreWeave rpoBacklog fails to grow sequentially for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Providers sign contracts faster than they can build capacity, so the order book moves before revenue does and shows demand earlier.
rationale: Google Cloud's committed backlog rose to $514 billion from $462 billion in one quarter while revenue was $24.8 billion, CoreWeave's contracted backlog reached $99.4 billion from $66.8 billion a month earlier and it has since added a multi-year expansion, and one smaller provider signed over $2.8 billion of multi-year contracts.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to how much of the backlog converts on time, since only just over half is expected within two years.

falsifiableTrigger: A top hyperscaler returns to positive free cash flow while holding 2027 capex guidance for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Spending has outgrown the cash these businesses generate, so they raise outside money and take on the risk that comes with it.
rationale: Alphabet funded its quarter with $49.6 billion of share issuance and $20.3 billion of notes and reported its first ever negative free cash flow of $5.9 billion, NVIDIA raised $25 billion of bonds to fund a customer financing programme, and Intel launched a $15 billion share sale.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to credit conditions and to share prices, which set the cost of both funding routes.

falsifiableTrigger: A new accelerator generation delivers less than a 1.5x perfPerWatt gain over its predecessor.
mechanism: Each generation does far more work for the same electricity and the same package, so buyers add capability without adding scarce inputs.
rationale: The newest racks are claimed to deliver ten times more work per megawatt than the prior generation, one enterprise system claims ten times the performance per megawatt of what it replaces, the newest flash claims 2.5 times better performance per watt, a wafer-scale system claims ten times the throughput per watt of its predecessor and the new switch claims five times lower power.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether these vendor-claimed gains hold up in real deployments rather than in marketing figures.

falsifiableTrigger: HBM leadTimes shorten and suppliers report unsold capacity for 2 consecutive quarters before end-2027.
mechanism: Each accelerator needs a fixed stack of memory, so a fixed memory pool sets a hard ceiling on how many accelerators can be finished.
rationale: NVIDIA's memory suppliers can meet only 60 to 70 percent of the volume requested for its next generation, Micron says it can supply no more than about half of demand and has no line of sight to balance, memory scarcity has forced NVIDIA to assess four alternative memory specifications, and AMD's next part needs 432 gigabytes per accelerator, a 50 percent increase.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to how much wafer capacity memory makers shift into stacked memory, which displaces standard memory three or four to one.

falsifiableTrigger: Memory supplier grossMargin falls for 2 consecutive quarters as contract prices flatten.
mechanism: Memory is scarce while server assembly is not, so the pricing power and the profit sit with the memory makers rather than the builders.
rationale: Micron's data-centre segment reported $11.5 billion of revenue at an 87 percent gross margin, stacked-memory contract prices are forecast to roughly double into 2027, contracts are locked at high-teen to low-twenties percent increases, and Korean semiconductor exports nearly tripled to $26 billion in twenty days.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to new memory capacity coming online, which would end the pricing power.

falsifiableTrigger: No new sovereign or enterprise cluster above 10,000 GPUs is announced for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Governments and large companies now buy clusters at a scale that used to belong only to the cloud giants, which widens the buyer base.
rationale: A Japanese national project will deploy 27,500 accelerators across 140 megawatts with government involvement, a Korean carrier will build a 2-gigawatt cloud, a pharmaceutical company is deploying a second enterprise cluster, AMD launched a part aimed at sovereign and high-performance customers, and trading firms have become a meaningful neocloud segment.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to public budgets and to whether these buyers can secure power and supply against the cloud giants.

falsifiableTrigger: Intel data-center revenue growth falls below 10% year over year for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Rising server sales and a packaging service that customers now book give Intel a second earning line beside its own chips.
rationale: Intel's data-centre segment grew 59 percent year over year to $6.3 billion, gross margin rose to 40.4 percent from 27.5 percent, foundry revenue rose 31 percent to $5.8 billion with narrowing losses, guidance for the next quarter beat expectations, its bridge packaging has a growing backlog, and it raised $15 billion of equity to fund expansion.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether its newest process and packaging hold their yield and schedule promises.

falsifiableTrigger: New vendor equity-for-compute deals in marginalBuyerFinancing stop appearing for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Vendors put their own money into the firms that buy their chips, so part of reported demand is funded by the seller.
rationale: AMD committed up to $5 billion of equity in Anthropic alongside its accelerator deal, NVIDIA invested an undisclosed amount in Safe Superintelligence alongside a platform commitment, NVIDIA is investing $5 billion in Intel stock, and it is in advanced talks to invest several hundred million dollars in a powered-land developer.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether these customers can raise money elsewhere without vendor participation.

falsifiableTrigger: Standard DRAM S10 spot prices fall for 2 consecutive months as suppliers restore non-AI capacity.
mechanism: Memory makers move wafers to the highest-priced AI parts, so ordinary memory and the products that use it get shorter supply and higher prices.
rationale: AMD raised graphics card bundle prices about 10 percent as one older memory type roughly tripled in spot price since late 2025, older standard memory hit $81.20 above its prior peak while a newer type broke $50 for the first time, makers are cutting standard output to favour AI parts, and consumer drives are being squeezed as enterprise contracts get priority.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to when new fabrication capacity comes online, which reporting puts no earlier than late 2026.

falsifiableTrigger: No new multi-year accelerator-to-memory supply partnership is announced for 2 consecutive quarters through 2027.
mechanism: Buying memory output years ahead turns a scarce input into a reserved one, so vendors trade flexibility for certainty of supply.
rationale: NVIDIA entered a long-term partnership with SK hynix to secure next-generation memory and jointly develop it, all three large memory makers are developing a 16-high next-generation stack specifically for NVIDIA targeting fourth-quarter delivery, and one supplier says it has finalised long-term supply agreements with about ten customers.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to memory scarcity easing, which would remove the reason to lock supply in advance.

falsifiableTrigger: The leading supplier's HBM market-share-pct falls below 50% within 4 quarters as rivals ship volume.
mechanism: A rival supplier reaching comparable production efficiency gives buyers a second place to go, which erodes any single maker's control of access.
rationale: The leading supplier is put at 56.4 to 58 percent of the market, only a little over half, while Samsung has pushed its next-generation yield close to 80 percent about four months ahead of plan and targets raising its share to roughly 38 percent by the end of 2026, so the second source is closing the gap.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the second supplier's parts pass customer qualification in volume, not just on yield charts.

falsifiableTrigger: No new diversion prosecution or whitelist reduction is reported for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Prosecutions and shorter approved-buyer lists raise the cost and risk of reselling restricted hardware, which closes the informal routes.
rationale: Taiwanese prosecutors expanded a criminal smuggling probe, raided a server maker's offices and detained employees over charges tied to some $2.5 billion of servers shipped without a licence, and NVIDIA more than halved the number of Asian customers authorised to buy its chips.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to enforcement effort, since the price gap that motivates diversion remains.

falsifiableTrigger: CoWoS lead times stay above 52 weeks through the end of 2027 while the supply gap fails to narrow below 15%.
mechanism: Packaging capacity is being added faster than memory capacity, so the two constraints are easing at different speeds and reporting on the packaging gap still conflicts.
rationale: The disagreement in the statement persists: one account puts the packaging shortfall at about 10 percent in mid-2026 narrowed from about 20 percent, another still estimates about 20 percent for 2026, lines are reported booked through 2027, while memory suppliers say they can fill only half to two thirds of demand.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to how much packaging work moves to outside assembly partners, which several accounts now report.

falsifiableTrigger: NAND contract prices for server drives fall for 2 consecutive quarters while Rubin deployments keep growing.
mechanism: The new rack design adds a large drive pool to every system, so flash demand jumps by a step rather than a trend and the supply chain has to catch up.
rationale: The newest generation's storage tier is expected to pull flash demand from about 35 million terabytes this year to more than 100 million next year with each unit carrying 576 drives, enterprise contracts are already getting priority over retail, and drive scarcity is named alongside memory as a driver of rack costs rising 2 to 3 percent a week.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to how fast flash makers add capacity against a demand step described as Apple-sized.

falsifiableTrigger: Every major cloud provider publishes list rates for its newest rack-scale systems for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Providers keep their scarcest new systems off the public page and sell them by negotiation, so listed prices describe only older capacity.
