rationale: Lambda's rendered pricing showed no listings for four newer part types on August 5 and still none on August 10 and August 19, with longer terms quoted only as custom pricing, while CoreWeave continues to publish an hourly rate for a prior-generation eight-accelerator node.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to supply loosening, which would push providers back to advertising the newest systems.

falsifiableTrigger: NVIDIA accelerator market-share-pct stabilises or rises for 2 consecutive quarters while rival shipments grow.
mechanism: The whole market is growing faster than NVIDIA's own shipments, so rivals gain share out of new spending rather than by taking existing customers.
rationale: One projection has NVIDIA's accelerator share falling from a 2024 peak of 87 percent to 81 and then 75 percent, another puts it near 70 percent with in-house chips growing 44.6 percent against 16.1 percent for merchant parts, and one account still says as much as 90 percent, all while its data-centre revenue set a record at $75.2 billion.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to how share is measured, since published estimates for the same period range from about 70 to 90 percent.

falsifiableTrigger: A major buyer returns to purchasing loose accelerators rather than vendor racks for a flagship cluster within 2 quarters.
mechanism: Vendors sell the computers, networking and software as one unit, so buyers compare finished systems and cannot mix parts freely.
rationale: AMD's 72-accelerator rack is in production with five named adopters, NVIDIA's 72-accelerator rack entered its production ramp across several clouds, comparisons are now made rack against rack on tokens per dollar, and a wafer-scale entrant sells a rack that plugs into rival racks rather than a loose chip.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to open rack standards, which one buyer is co-developing and which would let systems be mixed again.

falsifiableTrigger: ERCOT data-center additions exceed 5 GW over the next 4 quarters as the pause lifts.
mechanism: Sites cannot open until the grid connects them, so queue length and policy pauses decide the build schedule rather than chip availability.
rationale: The Texas connection queue holds roughly 474 gigawatts with about 90 percent of new requests coming from data centres, yet only about 1.2 gigawatts of additions are forecast over the next year and lost data-centre revenue from the pause is put at up to $8 billion; again no finding this cycle reports transformer lead times.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to state policy on connection pauses, which is what the current forecast reflects.

falsifiableTrigger: Median newest-generation gpuSpotPrice falls while prior-generation rates rise for 2 consecutive months.
mechanism: When new capacity is scarce, buyers bid up whatever is available, so older hardware can gain price rather than lose it.
rationale: The newest publicly listed part held flat at $6.69 per hour while the prior-generation card rose from $3.99 on August 19 to $4.29 on August 21, so the premium moved toward older hardware, and other providers quote the same older card at $3.29 and about $6.16 per hour within a node, showing a wide spread rather than a drift down.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to how quickly the newest systems reach public rental catalogues, since most are not listed at all.

falsifiableTrigger: Alternative packaging upstreamLeadTimes rise above 52 weeks, or no accelerator maker places advanced-packaging volume outside TSMC for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Much shorter waits elsewhere give chip designers a reason to place work outside the market leader, so packaging demand spreads across more suppliers.
rationale: Google has committed to order more than 3 million units of Intel's bridge packaging for a 2028 part, Intel reports very high demand and a growing backlog targeting high-volume production in 2027, alternative routes quote 26 to 39 weeks against 52 to 78 at TSMC, TSMC itself is outsourcing a front-end packaging step to outside assembly partners, and NVIDIA is reported to be weighing a shift of some output.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to yields and qualification at the alternative suppliers, since one route still targets only 50 percent initial substrate yield.

falsifiableTrigger: AMD's share of CoWoS output in pkgCapacityOrderSpread rises above 15% within 2 quarters.
mechanism: One fixed pool of packaging slots serves two product lines, so gaining volume in one costs volume in the other.
rationale: AMD is still put at roughly 11 percent of advanced-packaging output, about 105,000 wafers, against NVIDIA at roughly 60 percent, and must split that allocation between its server processors and its accelerators so each processor packaged displaces an accelerator.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether AMD can qualify an alternative packaging route and escape the shared pool.

falsifiableTrigger: The next flagship ships with its originally planned 288GB memory configuration within 2 quarters of launch.
mechanism: With a fixed memory pool, putting less memory in each accelerator lets the vendor finish more of them, so the product specification absorbs the shortage.
rationale: Several accounts now report the next flagship cut to 192 gigabytes from 288 in a 12-high stack, with tests also at 256 gigabytes and some samples reverting to the prior memory generation, driven by memory scarcity and site power limits, and NVIDIA has been assessing four alternative memory specifications since the third quarter.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether performance holds up at lower memory, since one analyst puts a sharp drop below 500 gigabytes.

falsifiableTrigger: The first Korean AI factory misses its 2027 target or the partnership is not converted from letters of intent into signed contracts within 2 quarters.
mechanism: Tying construction, memory supply and cloud capacity into one country's industrial base creates a second place where the whole chain sits together.
rationale: NVIDIA describes the SK partnership as a $500-billion-plus initiative covering data-centre construction, memory supply and cloud capacity with the first facility targeted for 2027, a Korean carrier will build a 2-gigawatt cloud on that platform, and Korean semiconductor exports nearly tripled to $26 billion in the first twenty days of August.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to conversion, since the headline partnership is still formalised through letters of intent.

falsifiableTrigger: No accelerator or system vendor announces a shipping product using the high-bandwidth flash specification within 4 quarters.
mechanism: A published standard lets system builders add a cheap fast storage layer that does not draw on the scarce stacked-memory pool.
rationale: SK hynix and Sandisk released the first high-bandwidth flash specification through an open consortium covering capacities to 512 gigabytes and speeds from about 0.4 to 3.0 terabytes per second with Google and Tenstorrent joining, the newest flash claims 2.5 times better performance per watt, and the newest rack design already pools 576 drives per unit.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether a shipping product actually adopts the standard rather than the specification sitting unused.

falsifiableTrigger: AMD software releases deliver less than a 1.5x measured inference gain over the prior release for 2 consecutive releases.
mechanism: Software improvements raise the output of hardware customers already own, so competitiveness improves before any new machine ships.
rationale: AMD reports 3.3 times inference and 2.4 times training gains over its prior software release and a 2.10 times end-to-end throughput improvement with a 3.71 times faster first response on a current part, while its rack-scale volume ramp is put at the second quarter of 2027.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to independent confirmation, since these speed-up figures are vendor-reported.

falsifiableTrigger: SpaceX nameplate compute fails to exceed 2 gigawatts by the end of 2026 or its quarterly AI capex falls below $10 billion for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: One buyer outside the traditional cloud group is now committing capital at hyperscale rates, which adds a large single claim on next year's output.
rationale: SpaceX ended the quarter at 1.4 gigawatts of compute from 400 megawatts a year earlier, spent about $15.8 billion on AI infrastructure in the quarter, said it will build exclusively on NVIDIA, expects a very significant share of 2027 output, and now guides past 2 gigawatts by year-end and about 10 gigawatts by end-2027 on AI revenue of $2.6 billion.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether its AI revenue keeps funding the spending as the target rises toward 10 gigawatts.

falsifiableTrigger: Intel's share of 2.5D packaging capacity fails to rise above 20% within 4 quarters, or its bridge packaging misses 2027 mass production.
mechanism: The alternative route depends on one supplier of a key component that is already fully booked, so it cannot scale as fast as its order book suggests.
rationale: Intel's sole silicon capacitor supplier for the bridge route is described as fully booked, the technology is characterised as better suited to custom chips than to high-bandwidth accelerators, Intel holds only about 13.7 percent of this packaging capacity against roughly 70 percent for TSMC, and substrate mass production is not expected before 2027 at about 50 percent initial yield.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether a second supplier of that component qualifies, since one supplier currently gates the route.

falsifiableTrigger: MediaTek market-share-pct of AI accelerators fails to exceed 5% within 4 quarters, or its first chip misses Q4 2026 production.
mechanism: A third design house winning cloud programmes gives buyers another partner for their own chips, which loosens a two-firm market.
rationale: MediaTek confirms its raised 15 to 20 percent share target, expects more than $2 billion of 2026 revenue from this business with its first chip entering production in the fourth quarter of 2026 and a second in 2028, and approved a $5 billion financing, while a Gartner analyst notes its 2024 share was under 1 percent and calls the target very high.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to first-chip execution, given the very low starting share and analyst doubt about the target.

falsifiableTrigger: Used prior-generation server prices fall more than 40% within 2 quarters, or published prior-generation rental rates drop below $2.00 per GPU-hour.
mechanism: The price gap between new and used machines is wide enough that older hardware still pays back at current rental rates.
rationale: A new top-end server is priced at about $500,000 against roughly $150,000 to $180,000 for a used prior-generation eight-accelerator machine, and the same prior-generation card rents from $3.29 to $4.29 an hour across providers with the older one at $2.79, so older hardware still earns its keep.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to rental rates for older cards, which have risen rather than fallen this cycle.

falsifiableTrigger: Wafer suppliers report spare 300mm capacity or falling wafer prices for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Memory makers building new fabs all draw on the same wafer suppliers, so the squeeze moves one step further up the chain.
rationale: GlobalWafers says its lines are effectively at full utilisation with constraints already appearing on some advanced products, spot prices for large wafers are rising with more increases expected, it signed a ten-year agreement with Micron including upfront financial support, and buyers are stretching contracts from about three years to five to eight.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to how many new memory fabs start at once, since supply pressure is expected to peak through the second half of 2027.

falsifiableTrigger: AMD's reported remaining performance obligations stay below $1 billion for 2 consecutive quarters while new gigawatt commitments keep being announced.
mechanism: Announced gigawatt intentions are not contractual obligations, so the reported order book stays small until customers actually place orders.
rationale: AMD reported only $222 million of remaining performance obligations on contracts longer than one year, of which $144 million falls within twelve months, and disclosed no dollar backlog even while describing strong customer pull, against announced commitments of up to 6 gigawatts each from two customers tied to warrants and milestones.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the deployment agreements convert into firm purchase orders as the 2027 ramp approaches.

falsifiableTrigger: No hardwired inference product reaches customer shipment within 4 quarters, or inference workloads stay on general accelerators for 2 consecutive quarters after launch.
mechanism: Fixing a finished model into hardware removes general-purpose overhead, so the cheapest way to serve a settled model may stop being a general accelerator.
rationale: AMD signed a definitive agreement to buy Taalas, a startup whose technology burns model weights into silicon, and plans to pair it with its own accelerators and racks, while NVIDIA's chief executive held early talks with a Korean inference-chip designer about a partnership, investment or acquisition.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to how often models change, since hardwired parts lose their advantage when weights are updated.

falsifiableTrigger: Non-cloud owners stop signing new rental or lease agreements for 2 consecutive quarters, or rented share of their fleets falls below 50%.
mechanism: Owners who bought more capacity than they need sell the surplus, which puts a new layer of resellers between chip vendors and end users.
rationale: SpaceX expects roughly 90 percent of its compute to serve inference or be rented to others with only about 10 percent used for its own training, and it holds multibillion-dollar capacity leases with Google and Anthropic.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to rental prices, since renting out only pays while capacity is scarce.

falsifiableTrigger: Reported HBM4 yields fall back below 70% or contract prices keep rising for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Better yield only helps if wafer capacity is available, and stacked memory consumes three to four times the wafers of standard memory, so higher yields have not translated into more delivered supply.
note: memory-yields-improve-fast-enough-to-promise-relief: applied: corroborated secondary reversal (4 distinct publishers; pending filing checkpoint)
rationale: Yields did reach about 80 percent at both Korean suppliers ahead of plan, but the promised relief has not appeared: NVIDIA's suppliers can still meet only 60 to 70 percent of requested volume, Micron says it can supply no more than about half of demand with no line of sight to balance, supply is projected tight through 2027, and contract prices keep rising with server memory up more than 25 percent quarter over quarter and next-generation prices forecast to roughly double, which is the thesis's own break condition.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to wafer allocation rather than yield, since wafer supply is now the limiting factor.

falsifiableTrigger: No compute-financing platform closes a funded transaction within 2 quarters, or the memorandums lapse without binding agreements.
mechanism: Moving purchase funding onto outside investors shifts the buildout's risk away from chip vendors and cloud balance sheets, but only once money is actually committed.
rationale: NVIDIA signed memorandums with Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs and KKR to set up platforms meant to mobilise more than $500 billion of third-party capital, but the agreements are described as non-binding and no funded transaction is reported yet.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether these non-binding memorandums convert into signed, funded deals.

falsifiableTrigger: Samsung foundry utilisation loosens or it reverses the 10-15% price increase within 2 quarters.
mechanism: Demand overflowing from the market leader fills the second supplier's lines, which lets it raise prices instead of chasing orders.
rationale: Samsung raised contract chipmaking prices 10 to 15 percent on new July orders, says its advanced line runs at full capacity and it cannot meet all orders, and expects AI and high-performance work to exceed 30 percent of foundry revenue this year, up from 15 to 20 percent in late 2025, though it still holds only about 7 percent of the market against more than 70 percent for TSMC.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to leading-edge capacity additions at the market leader, which would pull the overflow back.

falsifiableTrigger: Cerebras fails to report CS-4 customer shipments within 2 quarters, or no named customer expands beyond its initial system within 4 quarters.
mechanism: A whole-wafer machine that plugs into rival racks competes for the fastest serving work without asking buyers to replace their existing systems.
rationale: Cerebras launched a rack-scale system of three whole-wafer processors delivering 750 petaflops with first shipments this quarter, names OpenAI, G42, a university and AWS among customers, claims up to 30 times the per-user speed of accelerator-based systems, and the system is designed to pair with AMD's rack and AWS's own chips, with AMD separately listing that integration.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether named customers move beyond first systems, since the speed claims are vendor-reported.

falsifiableTrigger: No new vendor-guaranteed or vendor-funded data-centre site above 1 gigawatt is announced for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: By guaranteeing leases and funding powered land, the chip vendor makes sure buildings exist for its hardware, and takes on site risk to do it.
rationale: NVIDIA guaranteed leases covering about 4.25 gigawatts of load at an Ohio campus with its payment obligation capped at $105 billion and an option taking the site to 8 gigawatts, is the exclusive compute provider there under a 20-year customer lease, and is in advanced talks to invest several hundred million dollars in a powered-land developer with more than 7 gigawatts sold.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to tenant creditworthiness, since one guarantee only pays out if the customer defaults.

falsifiableTrigger: A hyperscaler raises AI capex guidance and its shares rise on the day for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Investors price a spending increase as an immediate cash cost for the buyer and as future revenue for its suppliers, so the same news moves the two groups in opposite directions.
rationale: ADJUSTED: Shares of companies that raise their own AI spending tend to fall on the day, while suppliers that expect to receive that spending rise, so the market now separates who pays from who gets paid.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to evidence of returns, since proof of payback would remove the penalty on the buyers.

detail.falsifiableTrigger: MLCC lead times for AI server grades fall below 20 weeks for 2 consecutive quarters.
detail.mechanism: A server cannot ship without every part on its bill of materials, so a cheap component with a long wait can hold up an expensive machine.
detail.sensitivity: Most sensitive to how quickly passive component makers add capacity, since these parts normally carry short waits and little spare stock.
detail.statement: Waits for the small high-specification capacitors that every AI server needs are stretching toward 40 weeks, so shortages now reach parts that cost pennies as well as the expensive chips.
detail.title: Passive parts join the AI server shortage list

detail.falsifiableTrigger: No new trading-firm compute commitment above $1 billion is announced for 2 consecutive quarters.
detail.mechanism: Trading firms buy compute to earn returns on their own models rather than to sell cloud services, so their demand does not depend on the AI software market growing.
detail.sensitivity: Most sensitive to trading profits, which fund this spending and swing with market conditions.
detail.statement: Financial trading firms are now signing multi-billion-dollar capacity deals with specialist compute providers, adding a buyer group that sits outside both the cloud giants and the model builders.
detail.title: Trading firms become a new class of accelerator renter

detail.falsifiableTrigger: The next flagship launches in a single memory configuration, or the number of assessed memory specifications falls below 2 within 2 quarters.
detail.mechanism: When memory and site power are both rationed, the vendor builds several versions of one product so each customer takes the version its supply and its building can support.
detail.sensitivity: Most sensitive to memory availability, since a looser memory pool would remove the reason to split the line.
detail.statement: NVIDIA is preparing its next flagship in several memory and power versions at once rather than one configuration, so scarcity is splitting a single product into a family.
detail.title: One flagship becomes several part numbers under scarcity

falsifiableTrigger: B200 rpoBacklog falls below 2 million units for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Buyers order far more accelerators than the parts chain can build, so unfilled orders keep piling up rather than clearing.
rationale: Record data-centre revenue of $75.2 billion and a $91 billion next-quarter guide sit alongside an order book of about 3.6 million top-end units, while memory suppliers can fill only 60 to 70 percent of the volume NVIDIA asks for.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to a large buyer cancelling or deferring orders, which would show up first as a falling order book rather than falling sales.

falsifiableTrigger: HBM leadTimes ease to available-on-demand and CoWoS lead times fall below 26 weeks before the end of 2027.
mechanism: Two separate scarce inputs, stacked memory and advanced packaging, each set a ceiling on how many finished accelerators can leave the factory.
rationale: Packaging lines stay booked into 2027 at 52 to 78 week waits, one house still puts the packaging shortfall near 20 percent, and memory suppliers say they can cover only about half to two thirds of what customers ask for.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to memory output rising faster than packaging, which would move the ceiling to one input instead of two.

falsifiableTrigger: AMD accelerator market-share-pct fails to rise above 7% through 2027.
mechanism: Large named commitments make AMD a real alternative on paper, but its shipped volume only rises when its rack systems reach full production.
rationale: AMD's data-centre revenue came in at $6.7 billion, up 107 percent, exactly as the thesis states, and its racks are in production with named buyers, yet its share is still put at 5 to 7 percent against NVIDIA at 80 to 90 percent and the real volume ramp lands in 2027.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to the 2027 production ramp slipping again, which would keep announced deals from turning into shipped racks.

falsifiableTrigger: ASIC market-share-pct growth falls back below GPU growth for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Every workload a cloud runs on its own chip is a workload it does not buy a merchant accelerator for.
rationale: In-house chips are growing 44.6 percent against 16.1 percent for merchant parts, custom silicon is said to consume about two thirds of all compute, Microsoft is negotiating capacity for over 300,000 of its own chips and Google has added a second outside design partner.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to in-house chip programmes missing their production dates, which would push work back onto bought accelerators.

falsifiableTrigger: gpuSpotPrice for a current-generation part drops more than 20% within a quarter.
mechanism: Scarce supply keeps the price of renting current hardware firm even as second-hand cards come off their scarcity peak.
rationale: Published rental rates for the prior generation hold in a narrow band of $3.29 to $4.29 an hour across three providers, while used cards now ask $21,000 to $28,000 against a $25,000 to $40,000 range earlier and a $50,000 peak.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to a wave of newly delivered racks arriving at once, which would push published hourly rates down quickly.

falsifiableTrigger: exportControlExposure eases so China DC revenue recovers above prior levels within 2 quarters.
mechanism: Government rules on both sides remove a whole class of buyers from the addressable market regardless of how much they want to buy.
rationale: China revenue fell to $4.55 billion from $9.66 billion, NVIDIA assumes no China data-centre revenue at all, the approved-buyer list was more than halved, and Beijing now tells licensed buyers to keep the hardware in Hong Kong.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to a policy change on either side, which can move addressable demand in a single quarter.

falsifiableTrigger: Vendor-financed GPU commitments in rpoBacklog exceed 300,000 units within 2 quarters.
mechanism: The vendor underwrites the buyer's ability to pay, so part of reported demand depends on the vendor's own balance sheet rather than the buyer's.
rationale: The support has landed exactly where the thesis said: the proposed customer guarantee was cut from $250 billion to under $120 billion, a site guarantee was capped at $105 billion, and financing platforms meant to raise over $500 billion from outside investors were signed.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the outside-capital platforms actually fund deals, which would move the exposure off the vendor.

falsifiableTrigger: customerConcentration for the top three direct customers falls below prior shares next fiscal year.
mechanism: A handful of buyers now carry most of the revenue, so one of them slowing down removes a large block of sales at once.
rationale: Three direct customers account for 21, 17 and 16 percent of revenue, the four largest are now more than half, one rocket-company buyer expects a very significant share of next year's output, and a single site guarantee pays out only if one named customer fails.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether new buyer tiers grow fast enough to dilute the top few names.

falsifiableTrigger: NVIDIA DC Ethernet switch market-share-pct slips from #1 within 2 quarters.
mechanism: Selling the switches and the accelerators together makes it harder for a buyer to swap out one part of the system.
rationale: NVIDIA still holds the top revenue spot in data-centre Ethernet switching and its newest switch generation ships with named cloud customers, but again no finding compares networking growth against compute growth, so the sharper claim stays unsupported.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to buyers choosing open networking with rival accelerators, which would break the bundle.

falsifiableTrigger: Cost-per-token gains stall so tokenEconomics improves less than one generation cycle.
mechanism: When running a model gets cheaper, uses that were not worth paying for become worth paying for, so total work grows.
rationale: The newest generation is reported at ten times lower inference cost per token than the one before it, open-source serving costs keep falling sharply each year, and one telecom buyer is already burning about a trillion tokens a month.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to the next generation delivering a small cost improvement, which would stop pulling new work in.

falsifiableTrigger: Prepaid HBM commitments in rpoBacklog shrink or deposits are refunded within a quarter.
mechanism: Buyers who have already paid cash for memory they cannot cancel have every reason to build the accelerators that memory goes into.
rationale: One memory maker holds sixteen non-cancelable five-year agreements backed by more than $22 billion including nearly $18 billion of cash deposits, another has finalised long-term supply deals with about ten customers, and the largest clouds have used cash reserves to lock in supply.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to any renegotiation or refund of those deposits, which would unlock the committed volume.

falsifiableTrigger: exportControlExposure changes lift the sub-50% China cap or clear Blackwell within 2 quarters.
mechanism: Both governments hold a separate veto over the same shipment, so a licence on one side does not produce a delivery.
rationale: The picture is unchanged: case-by-case licences under a sub-50 percent cap and a 25 percent tariff, roughly $10 billion of approved licences producing only trivial shipments and no booked revenue, and Beijing telling approved buyers to keep the hardware in Hong Kong.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to Beijing dropping the keep-it-offshore instruction, which is the binding half right now.

falsifiableTrigger: Memory hbmSupplyCapex expansion pulls DRAM/NVMe prices down within 2 quarters.
mechanism: Memory is a large and rising share of what a server costs, and builders cannot pass all of it on, so it lands on their margins.
rationale: Rack component costs still inflate 2 to 3 percent a week on memory and drive scarcity, one supplier says it can meet only about half of demand, and the biggest contract builder repeats that high memory prices have not slowed customer spending.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to new memory fabs coming online, which would relieve prices before it relieves volumes.

falsifiableTrigger: releaseCadence slips push a major vendor's 2H-2026 ramp into 2027.
mechanism: Each vendor hits full production on its own schedule, so new supply arrives in steps across a year rather than in one wave.
rationale: The staging holds: NVIDIA's newest platform reached full production in July with shipments underway, AMD's rack reached production with third-quarter shipments but its mass ramp is put at 2027, and one hyperscaler's own parts enter production in September.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to further manufacturing delays at the second vendor, which would stretch the wave further out.

falsifiableTrigger: AMD customerConcentration eases as its buyer base broadens over the next 2 quarters.
mechanism: A few very large commitments carry most of the growth, so one partner changing its mind moves the whole line.
rationale: Two named customers each intend to deploy up to 6 gigawatts, a third committed up to 2 gigawatts, and AMD's own filings repeat that a small number of customers will keep accounting for a substantial part of revenue.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether mid-sized buyers appear, which would spread the risk across more names.

falsifiableTrigger: Crescent Island releaseCadence slips its customer sampling past the 2H 2026 quarter.
mechanism: Using ordinary memory lets a chip skip the two most congested steps in the chain, so its output does not depend on them.
rationale: Intel's inference part still uses standard memory instead of stacked memory specifically to avoid packaging and memory contention, and it is still guided to customer sampling in the second half of 2026 with no shipment news.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the part actually samples on time, since nothing has shipped yet.

falsifiableTrigger: TSMC grossMargin declines for 2 consecutive quarters as capacity loosens.
mechanism: When many different chip types compete for the same lines, the foundry can fill every slot and charge more for it.
rationale: TSMC posted a 67.7 percent gross margin, raised full-year growth guidance to above 40 percent and capital spending to $60-64 billion, reported July sales up 44.7 percent year on year, and says packaging tightness is limiting how fast customers can grow.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to a broad slowdown in chip orders, which would show up in margin before it shows up in revenue.

falsifiableTrigger: A hyperscalerCapexRevision cuts 2026 or 2027 AI capex guidance within 2 quarters.
mechanism: Spending is rising much faster than the revenue it is meant to produce, so a disappointing year would force budgets down.
rationale: The four largest buyers plan about $725 billion this year, up 77 percent, one bank projects about $4.1 trillion over three years, one hyperscaler reported its first negative free cash flow, and market commentary in July openly questioned whether the spending is sustainable.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to cloud revenue growth, which is the thing that has to keep up for budgets to hold.

falsifiableTrigger: NVIDIA grossMargin guidance drops below 70% in a coming quarter.
mechanism: Buyers keep paying premium prices because there is no equivalent alternative available in volume.
rationale: Gross margin came in at 75.0 percent with the next quarter guided to the same level, far above AMD at 54 to 56 percent and Intel at about 41 percent.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to rising memory input costs, which squeeze margin from underneath while prices hold.

falsifiableTrigger: Top-buyer customerConcentration in CoWoS output falls below 85% within a year.
mechanism: So few customers hold the bookings that one of them stepping back would leave capacity nobody else has qualified parts to fill.
rationale: The top three buyers again hold more than 85 percent of packaging output with NVIDIA at roughly 60 percent, and NVIDIA is reported to have reserved 800,000 to 850,000 wafers of this year's capacity, over half the total.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to smaller designers qualifying on the same lines, which would broaden the buyer base.

falsifiableTrigger: Aggregate rpoBacklog duration shortens as new commitments turn shorter-dated over 2 quarters.
mechanism: Buyers who fear they cannot get capacity later sign for it now, which pushes the average delivery date further out.
rationale: One cloud backlog rose more than $50 billion in a quarter to $514 billion with only just over half converting inside two years, one purchase commitment runs to 2032, one site lease runs 20 years, and wafer buyers are stretching contracts from about three years to five to eight.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to supply loosening, because buyers stop pre-booking once they trust they can buy on demand.

falsifiableTrigger: A leading model provider reports revenue (apiArr) growth stalling quarter over quarter while compute commitments keep growing.
mechanism: Real and rising sales from the companies that rent the compute pay for the next round of hardware.
rationale: One model provider reached more than $30 billion of annual recurring revenue from $1 billion fifteen months earlier, one compute owner reported AI revenue of $2.6 billion up 247 percent year on year, and one cloud grew 82 percent to $24.8 billion.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to price competition among model providers, which would slow revenue while commitments stay fixed.

falsifiableTrigger: Chinese domestic accelerator designWins for frontier training stall over the next 2 quarters.
mechanism: Domestic parts can now do the work, but they cannot yet be built in the volumes Chinese buyers want.
rationale: The capability case holds with a 1.6-trillion-parameter model trained on more than 50,000 domestic parts, and two domestic vendors now report fast revenue growth with one holding a 57 percent gross margin, yet Chinese firms still ordered over two million restricted parts against about 700,000 units of inventory.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to domestic production volume, not to further proof that the chips work.

falsifiableTrigger: A neocloud's marginalBuyerFinancing debt load or net loss narrows for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Buying fleets faster than contracts pay them back means growth arrives with widening losses.
rationale: The largest example grew revenue about 168 percent from $1.9 billion to $5.1 billion while its net loss widened from $937 million to $1.2 billion, and it raised this year's capital spending to $31-35 billion.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to the pace of new hardware purchases, since slowing them is what would close the loss.

falsifiableTrigger: A top hyperscaler cuts its 2027 gigawatt power target below its 2026 level.
mechanism: A site can only run as many accelerators as its electricity supply allows, so power decides deployment once chips are available.
rationale: Buyers now state plans in gigawatts rather than chips, one is at 1.4 gigawatts heading past 2 by year end and about 10 by end-2027, power shortages are cited as a reason to lower the next flagship's power rating, and a Texas connection queue of about 474 gigawatts is expected to deliver only about 1.2 gigawatts in a year.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to grid connection approvals, which decide how fast announced gigawatts become live ones.

falsifiableTrigger: Broadcom-plus-Marvell market-share-pct of custom ASIC co-design falls below 90% within a year.
mechanism: New design houses and in-house teams give buyers routes to custom silicon that do not pass through the incumbent two.
rationale: The two firms are still put at about 95 percent of custom design work, but a third designer has raised its share target to 15 to 20 percent with a first chip entering production this quarter, one of the two appears to be taking work from the other rather than adding new spend, and one model builder has hired a chip leader and opened talks with a foundry to design its own part.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the newcomer's first chip actually reaches production on its stated quarter.

falsifiableTrigger: Wistron odmMonthlyAiRevenue falls year-over-year for 2 consecutive months.
mechanism: Contract builders only book revenue when finished systems leave the plant, so their monthly sales track real shipments.
rationale: One contract maker posted record June revenue up 53.9 percent year on year, another cleared NT$900 billion for the first time in July at up 54.2 percent, and the leading foundry's July sales rose 44.7 percent.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to component shortages holding back assembly, which would show as flat monthly sales despite full order books.

falsifiableTrigger: A neocloud's marginalBuyerFinancing debt-to-equity rises above 6:1 within 2 quarters.
mechanism: Fleets bought with borrowed money leave little equity to absorb a fall in rental rates.
rationale: The largest example has raised $18.81 billion of debt against $3.5 billion of equity, a 5.4 to 1 ratio, with total debt of $24.86 billion up 16.1 percent in a single quarter.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to borrowing costs and to rental rates, either of which can turn a thin cushion negative.

falsifiableTrigger: Co-packaged optics adoption stalls below 5% of AI optical modules through 2027.
mechanism: Putting the optics inside the switch package cuts power and parts count but ties cluster wiring to a new and thinly supplied component chain.
rationale: Order books for the new switch platform are reported full through 2027 with supply tight into 2028, adoption is projected to climb from about 0.5 percent of modules this year toward about 35 percent by 2030, and one vendor is funding a tenfold expansion of US optical connectivity capacity.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to optical engine yields, which the reporting names as the limit on expansion.

falsifiableTrigger: A named US fab or packaging project slips its build milestone past 2027.
mechanism: Building fabrication, packaging and assembly inside the United States adds capacity that does not depend on Taiwan.
rationale: One vendor plans up to $500 billion of US-built AI infrastructure with named partners, a memory maker committed $250 billion through 2035 and broke ground in New York, the leading foundry added an incremental $100 billion, and new plants opened in Texas and are planned in North Carolina.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to construction and staffing timelines, since announced dollars take years to become output.

falsifiableTrigger: Google Cloud or CoreWeave rpoBacklog fails to grow sequentially for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Contracts are signed faster than capacity can be built, so the order book grows even while quarterly sales are capped by delivery.
rationale: One cloud's backlog rose more than $50 billion in a quarter to $514 billion against $24.8 billion of quarterly revenue, another holds $99.4 billion of contracted backlog, and a smaller provider added over $2.8 billion of multi-year contracts.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to conversion pace, because a backlog that stops turning into revenue stops being proof of demand.

falsifiableTrigger: A top hyperscaler returns to positive free cash flow while holding 2027 capex guidance for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Spending now exceeds what the businesses generate in cash, so the gap is filled by issuing debt and shares.
rationale: One hyperscaler funded its quarter with $49.6 billion of equity issuance and $20.3 billion of notes and reported its first-ever negative free cash flow of $5.9 billion, while a chipmaker raised $15 billion of stock and a designer approved $5 billion of financing.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to credit market conditions, which decide how long borrowed funding stays cheap.

falsifiableTrigger: A new accelerator generation delivers less than a 1.5x perfPerWatt gain over its predecessor.
mechanism: More work per megawatt lets a buyer raise output inside a fixed power and packaging allowance.
rationale: The newest rack is claimed to deliver ten times the throughput per megawatt of the one before it, an enterprise system claims up to ten times the performance per megawatt of what it replaces, and a wafer-scale rival claims ten times the throughput per watt of its own last generation.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to vendor claims being measured on comparable workloads rather than best-case ones.

falsifiableTrigger: HBM leadTimes shorten and suppliers report unsold capacity for 2 consecutive quarters before end-2027.
mechanism: Every accelerator needs its stack of memory, so the memory a vendor can buy sets the number of units it can finish.
rationale: Memory suppliers can meet only 60 to 70 percent of the volume asked for the next flagship generation, one supplier says it can cover no more than about half of demand and calls memory the number one customer constraint, and the flagship's memory specification is being cut because of it.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to how fast new memory yields and fabs convert into shipped bits.

falsifiableTrigger: Memory supplier grossMargin falls for 2 consecutive quarters as contract prices flatten.
mechanism: Memory is scarce and its makers set the price, so more of each server's value ends up with them rather than with the builder.
rationale: One memory maker's data-centre segment posted $11.5 billion at an 87 percent gross margin, suppliers are locking contracts at high-teen to low-twenties percent price increases with one seeking up to 20 percent more, and Korean chip exports nearly tripled year on year in August.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to new memory capacity arriving, which is what would end the pricing power.

falsifiableTrigger: No new sovereign or enterprise cluster above 10,000 GPUs is announced for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Governments and large companies now buy clusters big enough to sit alongside cloud orders in the same supply queue.
rationale: A national project in Japan will deploy 27,500 accelerators across 140 megawatts with government involvement, a Korean carrier is building a 2-gigawatt AI cloud, a drug maker deployed a second enterprise cluster, and a wafer-scale vendor names a sovereign fund and a national university among its customers.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to public funding cycles, which can pause national projects faster than company budgets.

falsifiableTrigger: Intel data-center revenue growth falls below 10% year over year for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Growing revenue with improving margins gives buyers a third supplier for processors, packaging and foundry work.
rationale: Its data-centre segment grew 59 percent to $6.3 billion, foundry revenue rose 31 percent to $5.8 billion, gross margin improved to 40.4 percent from 27.5 percent, next-quarter guidance came in above expectations, and it raised $15 billion of new stock to fund capacity.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether its new packaging reaches high-volume production on its 2027 target.

falsifiableTrigger: New vendor equity-for-compute deals in marginalBuyerFinancing stop appearing for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: When the seller owns part of the buyer, reported demand partly reflects the seller's own money coming back.
rationale: AMD committed up to $5 billion of equity in a model builder alongside a compute deal, NVIDIA invested in a research lab alongside a platform commitment, took about 20 percent of a power developer for an initial $2 billion, and is in talks to invest in a powered-land developer.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to accounting and disclosure scrutiny, which would change how these deals are structured.

falsifiableTrigger: Standard DRAM S10 spot prices fall for 2 consecutive months as suppliers restore non-AI capacity.
mechanism: Memory makers move capacity to the highest-priced AI parts, so everything else gets less supply and pays more.
rationale: One vendor raised graphics card bundle prices about 10 percent citing tight memory and tripled graphics memory spot prices, older standard memory spot prices rose 17.5 percent in a month above their prior peak, and enterprise contracts are getting priority over retail drives.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to suppliers restoring standard memory lines, which only happens once AI prices stop rising.

falsifiableTrigger: No new multi-year accelerator-to-memory supply partnership is announced for 2 consecutive quarters through 2027.
mechanism: Buying and co-developing memory directly reserves output that would otherwise be sold to whoever bids most.
rationale: NVIDIA entered a long-term partnership with a Korean memory maker to secure next-generation supply and jointly develop it, the same partnership sits inside a $500-billion-plus initiative covering memory supply, and three memory makers are jointly developing a 16-high stack for NVIDIA with delivery targeted this year.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to memory scarcity easing, which would remove the reason to sign these deals.

falsifiableTrigger: The leading supplier's HBM market-share-pct falls below 50% within 4 quarters as rivals ship volume.
mechanism: A second supplier reaching comparable yields gives buyers a real alternative source, so one company no longer decides who can build.
rationale: The leader is still put at 56 to 58 percent of the market and about 62 percent of the next generation, but its main rival's yields have reached close to 80 percent about four months early, matching the leader's efficiency, and that rival targets roughly 38 percent share by year end.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the rival's yield gain converts into qualified shipped volume rather than announced capacity.

falsifiableTrigger: No new diversion prosecution or whitelist reduction is reported for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Prosecutions and shorter buyer lists raise the personal and corporate cost of moving restricted parts, so the informal channel narrows.
rationale: The approved-buyer list was more than halved, Taiwanese prosecutors raided a server maker's offices and detained staff over an alleged $2.5 billion of diverted servers, and that maker's own board probe led to terminations and an expanded compliance programme.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to enforcement attention persisting, since the routes reopen when scrutiny fades.

falsifiableTrigger: CoWoS lead times stay above 52 weeks through the end of 2027 while the supply gap fails to narrow below 15%.
mechanism: Packaging capacity is being added faster than memory capacity, but the reported size of the remaining packaging gap still differs by a factor of two.
rationale: The disagreement is unchanged: one source puts the packaging shortfall at about 10 percent in mid-2026, narrowed from about 20 percent, while another still puts it at about 20 percent this year, lines remain booked through 2027, and memory shows no easing at all.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to which capacity number is correct, since the two estimates imply different constraints.

falsifiableTrigger: NAND contract prices for server drives fall for 2 consecutive quarters while Rubin deployments keep growing.
mechanism: Each new rack now ships with a large drive pool, so accelerator volume pulls flash demand up with it.
rationale: The newest generation's storage tier is expected to lift flash demand from about 35 million terabytes this year to more than 100 million next year with 576 drives per unit, enterprise contracts are already taking priority over retail, and the industry has published a first standard for a high-bandwidth flash tier.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to how many of the new racks actually ship, since the storage demand rides on rack volume.

falsifiableTrigger: Every major cloud provider publishes list rates for its newest rack-scale systems for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Providers keep their scarcest, newest capacity off the public page and sell it through negotiation instead.
rationale: One provider's public pages still show no listing for the newest rack systems, leaving its most recent publicly rentable part a generation behind, while another still publishes an hourly rate for a prior-generation eight-accelerator node.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to newest-generation supply loosening, since providers publish rates once capacity is plentiful.

falsifiableTrigger: NVIDIA accelerator market-share-pct stabilises or rises for 2 consecutive quarters while rival shipments grow.
mechanism: The market is growing faster than one vendor can supply it, so rivals absorb the extra growth without taking existing business.
rationale: Revenue set another record at $75.2 billion, up 92 percent, while share estimates this cycle range widely from a projected 75 percent, to about 70 percent, to as much as 90 percent, so the direction is down but the level is not agreed.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to how share is measured, since the estimates in circulation differ by twenty points.

falsifiableTrigger: A major buyer returns to purchasing loose accelerators rather than vendor racks for a flagship cluster within 2 quarters.
mechanism: Vendors now sell the whole cabinet with its own networking and software, so buyers compare finished systems rather than individual chips.
rationale: AMD put a 72-accelerator rack into production against NVIDIA's 72-accelerator rack, NVIDIA is scaling to an eight-rack, 576-accelerator configuration, and even a wafer-scale challenger now sells a rack-level system that pairs with rival racks.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to open rack standards gaining ground, which would let buyers mix parts again.

falsifiableTrigger: ERCOT data-center additions exceed 5 GW over the next 4 quarters as the pause lifts.
mechanism: Sites wait in a connection queue that clears far more slowly than the requests arrive, so approvals rather than chips set the pace.
rationale: The Texas connection queue holds about 474 gigawatts with roughly 90 percent of requests from data centres, yet only about 1.2 gigawatts of additions are forecast over the next year, and up to $8 billion of lost revenue is attributed to the pause; again no finding reports transformer lead times.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to state-level policy on the connection pause, which controls the whole queue.

falsifiableTrigger: Median newest-generation gpuSpotPrice falls while prior-generation rates rise for 2 consecutive months.
mechanism: Newer hardware does command a higher hourly rate, but the newest systems are not publicly priced at all, so no premium trend can be observed.
rationale: There is still no time series showing newest-generation rates rising: the newest publicly listed part is a generation behind at $6.69 to $6.99 an hour, the prior generation sits in a tight $3.29 to $4.29 band across three providers, and the generation before that is quoted at $2.79.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to providers publishing rates for their newest systems, without which the claim cannot be checked.

falsifiableTrigger: Alternative packaging upstreamLeadTimes rise above 52 weeks, or no accelerator maker places advanced-packaging volume outside TSMC for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Much shorter quoted waits elsewhere give chip designers a reason to place work outside the leading packaging supplier.
rationale: One cloud has committed to more than 3 million units of Intel's bridge packaging for a 2028 part, Intel reports high demand and a growing backlog for it, the leading foundry is itself outsourcing a front-end packaging step to subcontractors, and alternative routes still quote 26 to 39 weeks against 52 to 78.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to alternative suppliers proving yield at volume, since short quotes mean little without output.

falsifiableTrigger: AMD's share of CoWoS output in pkgCapacityOrderSpread rises above 15% within 2 quarters.
mechanism: One fixed packaging allocation has to cover two product lines, so every processor packaged displaces an accelerator.
rationale: AMD is still put at about 11 percent of the leading foundry's packaging output, roughly 105,000 wafers, and must split that allocation between its server processors and its accelerators, and its new accelerator carries 50 percent more stacked memory than the last one.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to AMD winning capacity at alternative packaging suppliers, which would end the trade-off.

falsifiableTrigger: The next flagship ships with its originally planned 288GB memory configuration within 2 quarters of launch.
mechanism: Giving each accelerator less memory lets the vendor build more of them from the same limited memory pool.
rationale: ADJUSTED: NVIDIA is cutting the memory in its next top-end accelerator to 192 gigabytes, far below the one terabyte it previewed and below the 288 gigabytes of the current generation, because it cannot secure enough stacked memory and because sites cannot supply enough power.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to memory supply recovering before the part is finalised, which would restore the higher configuration.

falsifiableTrigger: The first Korean AI factory misses its 2027 target or the partnership is not converted from letters of intent into signed contracts within 2 quarters.
mechanism: Tying construction, memory supply and cloud capacity together in one country makes it a second base for the buildout rather than only a parts supplier.
rationale: The partnership is now described by NVIDIA itself as a $500-billion-plus initiative covering factory construction, memory supply and cloud, with a 2-gigawatt national AI cloud named and the first factory targeted for 2027, while Korean chip exports nearly tripled year on year in August.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to the letters of intent becoming binding contracts, which has not yet been reported.

falsifiableTrigger: No accelerator or system vendor announces a shipping product using the high-bandwidth flash specification within 4 quarters.
mechanism: A cheaper flash tier holds data that would otherwise need scarce stacked memory, so it adds capacity without competing for the same supply.
rationale: The first high-bandwidth flash specification has now been published through an industry body, covering up to 512 gigabytes per stack and three performance grades, with two more large names joining the consortium, and the newest rack generation is already designed around large drive pools.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to a shipping product appearing, since a published standard alone changes nothing.

falsifiableTrigger: AMD software releases deliver less than a 1.5x measured inference gain over the prior release for 2 consecutive releases.
mechanism: Software improvements raise what existing hardware can do immediately, while new hardware volume waits on manufacturing.
rationale: AMD reports software gains of 3.3 times on inference and 2.4 times on training over its prior release plus a 2.10 times end-to-end throughput gain on a specific model, while its rack systems only reach mass production in 2027.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to independent testing, since the gains so far are vendor-reported.

falsifiableTrigger: SpaceX nameplate compute fails to exceed 2 gigawatts by the end of 2026 or its quarterly AI capex falls below $10 billion for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: A single non-cloud buyer is now scaling fast enough to take a large slice of one vendor's output.
rationale: The fleet went from 400 megawatts to 1.4 gigawatts in a year with guidance above 2 gigawatts by year end and about 10 by end-2027, quarterly AI infrastructure spending reached $15.8 billion, AI revenue hit $2.6 billion up 247 percent, and it says it will build exclusively on one vendor while expecting a very significant share of next year's output.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to its ability to keep funding this spending, since the capex runs well ahead of the revenue.

falsifiableTrigger: Intel's share of 2.5D packaging capacity fails to rise above 20% within 4 quarters, or its bridge packaging misses 2027 mass production.
mechanism: The alternative route depends on a component with one booked-out supplier, so it cannot scale faster than that supplier can.
rationale: Intel's bridge packaging has real backlog and a large committed order, but a single silicon capacitor supplier is described as fully booked, the substrate is expected in mass production only in 2027 at about 50 percent initial yields, and the technology is again called a better fit for custom chips than for high-bandwidth accelerators.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to a second capacitor supplier qualifying, which would remove the single point of failure.

falsifiableTrigger: MediaTek market-share-pct of AI accelerators fails to exceed 5% within 4 quarters, or its first chip misses Q4 2026 production.
mechanism: A third design house gives cloud buyers another route to a custom chip that does not run through the incumbent two.
rationale: MediaTek confirmed its raised 15 to 20 percent share target and its first chip entering production in the fourth quarter of 2026, with more than $2 billion of expected data-centre revenue this year, but an outside analyst notes its 2024 share was under 1 percent and calls the target very high.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to the first chip actually entering production this quarter, since the share target rests on it.

falsifiableTrigger: Used prior-generation server prices fall more than 40% within 2 quarters, or published prior-generation rental rates drop below $2.00 per GPU-hour.
mechanism: Older hardware costs a fraction of new hardware and still earns rent, so buyers keep it in service instead of retiring it.
rationale: A new top-end server is still about $500,000 against roughly $150,000 to $180,000 for a used prior-generation one, used cards ask $21,000 to $28,000, and published hourly rates for prior-generation parts run $2.79 to $4.29.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to a flood of new capacity, which would push older hardware's rental rates below its running costs.

falsifiableTrigger: Wafer suppliers report spare 300mm capacity or falling wafer prices for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Memory makers building new fabs all draw on the same wafer supply, so the squeeze moves one step further back in the chain.
rationale: The largest wafer maker says its 300mm, 200mm and 150mm lines are effectively at full utilisation with shortages already appearing on some advanced products, spot prices are rising with more increases expected, and buyers are lengthening contracts from about three years to five to eight, including a ten-year deal with upfront financial support.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to new wafer capacity, which takes years to build and is not yet announced at scale.

falsifiableTrigger: AMD's reported remaining performance obligations stay below $1 billion for 2 consecutive quarters while new gigawatt commitments keep being announced.
mechanism: Gigawatt announcements are statements of intent, and only contracted obligations show what a customer is actually bound to buy.
rationale: AMD reported only $222 million of contracted obligations beyond one year, of which $144 million falls inside twelve months, and disclosed no dollar backlog figure at all, while announcing up to 6 gigawatts each with two named customers.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to the first large firm order converting, which would turn intent into a booked number.

falsifiableTrigger: No hardwired inference product reaches customer shipment within 4 quarters, or inference workloads stay on general accelerators for 2 consecutive quarters after launch.
mechanism: Burning a finished model into fixed silicon runs it far more cheaply, so cost-sensitive inference work can leave general-purpose accelerators.
rationale: AMD signed a definitive agreement to buy a startup that hardwires model weights into silicon and will pair it with its own accelerators, NVIDIA opened talks with a Korean inference-chip designer about a partnership or acquisition, and one model builder has placed about $250 million of initial orders with another such startup.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to how fast models change, since fixed silicon only pays back if the model stays put.

falsifiableTrigger: Non-cloud owners stop signing new rental or lease agreements for 2 consecutive quarters, or rented share of their fleets falls below 50%.
mechanism: Owners who bought more compute than they need rent the surplus out, adding a supply layer between the chip vendors and end users.
rationale: One non-cloud owner expects about 90 percent of its compute to serve inference or be rented out with only about 10 percent used for its own training, and it holds multibillion-dollar capacity leases with two named AI buyers, while one model builder has signed capacity agreements with two more non-cloud operators.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to these owners' own workloads growing, which would absorb the capacity they currently rent out.

falsifiableTrigger: No compute-financing platform closes a funded transaction within 2 quarters, or the memorandums lapse without binding agreements.
mechanism: Third-party capital would move part of the buildout's funding off the chip vendor's and the clouds' balance sheets.
rationale: NVIDIA signed memorandums with six large asset managers and banks to set up financing platforms meant to mobilise over $500 billion, but the agreements are described as non-binding and no funded transaction has been reported.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to the first closed deal, since everything so far is a letter of intent.

falsifiableTrigger: Samsung foundry utilisation loosens or it reverses the 10-15% price increase within 2 quarters.
mechanism: Once the second-place supplier is also full, buyers have nowhere cheap to overflow to and prices rise across the market.
rationale: Samsung raised contract chipmaking prices 10 to 15 percent on new orders in July, says it cannot meet all orders with one advanced line at full capacity, and expects AI and high-performance work to exceed 30 percent of foundry revenue this year against 15 to 20 percent in late 2025.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to how much of the fill is AI work, since the rest of the business could soften independently.

falsifiableTrigger: Cerebras fails to report CS-4 customer shipments within 2 quarters, or no named customer expands beyond its initial system within 4 quarters.
mechanism: A wafer-scale system that plugs into existing racks competes for specific fast-inference work without asking buyers to replace their infrastructure.
rationale: Cerebras launched a rack-scale system built from three whole wafers delivering 750 petaflops with first shipments this quarter, names four customers including a large cloud and a sovereign group, and says it pairs with rival racks rather than replacing them.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to shipments starting on schedule, since the named customers are announcements so far.

falsifiableTrigger: No new vendor-guaranteed or vendor-funded data-centre site above 1 gigawatt is announced for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Guaranteeing leases and buying powered land makes sure sites exist for the vendor's own hardware to fill.
rationale: NVIDIA guaranteed leases covering about 4.25 gigawatts at an Ohio campus with the obligation capped at $105 billion and an option for 8 gigawatts total, will invest up to $3 billion for about 20 percent of a power developer, and is in advanced talks to invest in a powered-land developer with over 7 gigawatts sold.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to the vendor's willingness to carry lease risk, which it has already trimmed once.

falsifiableTrigger: A hyperscaler raises AI capex guidance and its shares rise on the day for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Investors now price a spending increase as money leaving the payer and arriving at the supplier, so the two move in opposite directions.
rationale: One hyperscaler's shares fell about 6 percent on the day it raised its spending forecast and one chipmaker's fell more than 8 percent on a capital spending overshoot, while a memory supplier's shares rose 4.86 percent on the same spending news and another chipmaker rose 8.64 percent on customer wins.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to visible returns on the spending, which would let payers be rewarded for spending more.

falsifiableTrigger: MLCC lead times for AI server grades fall below 20 weeks for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Every server needs thousands of these small parts, so a shortage of them holds up assembly regardless of chip supply.
rationale: Waits for the high-specification capacitors used in AI servers are still reported as stretching toward 40 weeks on AI server demand, with no new evidence either way.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to suppliers adding capacity, which is quick for simple parts once they commit.

falsifiableTrigger: No new trading-firm compute commitment above $1 billion is announced for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Trading firms need large bursts of compute without owning data centres, so they rent capacity from specialist providers.
rationale: One specialist provider signed a multiyear, multibillion-dollar expansion with a trading firm on top of a $6 billion commitment from another and a separate expansion with a third, and describes trading firms as a meaningful customer segment.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to trading profits, which fund this spending and can fall quickly.

falsifiableTrigger: The next flagship launches in a single memory configuration, or the number of assessed memory specifications falls below 2 within 2 quarters.
mechanism: When memory and power are both short, the vendor builds several smaller versions of one product so it can ship whatever parts it can actually get.
rationale: NVIDIA is reported to be assessing four alternative memory specifications for its next top-end part since the third quarter, testing both 192 and 256 gigabyte configurations with some samples reverting to the older memory type, and offering power variants at roughly 1,200, 1,800 and 2,600 to 2,800 watts.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to memory supply recovering, which would let the vendor collapse the family back to one part.

detail.falsifiableTrigger: A major vendor's next flagship arrives more than 24 months after its predecessor, or a named 2027 or 2028 roadmap part slips by 2 quarters.
detail.mechanism: Shorter gaps between generations force buyers to decide sooner and give the vendor with the fastest cadence a fresh performance claim more often.
detail.sensitivity: Most sensitive to manufacturing and memory readiness, since a shorter design cycle still has to survive the supply chain.
detail.statement: Accelerator vendors are compressing the gap between generations, so buyers face a new top-end system roughly every year instead of every two to three.
detail.title: Product cycles get shorter

detail.falsifiableTrigger: No model builder taped out a custom accelerator within 4 quarters, or the announced design effort is abandoned within 2 quarters.
detail.mechanism: A model builder that designs its own chip can tune it to its own model and stop paying a merchant vendor's margin on the largest part of its cost base.
detail.sensitivity: Most sensitive to how long a first custom chip takes, since these programmes usually run several years before first silicon.
detail.statement: The companies that build the largest models are moving from buying chips to designing them, adding a new source of custom silicon beyond the cloud giants.
detail.title: Model builders start designing their own chips

falsifiableTrigger: B200 rpoBacklog falls below 2 million units for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Buyers keep ordering more accelerators than the memory and packaging chain can build, so unfilled orders pile up faster than shipments clear them.
rationale: Record data-centre sales of $75.2 billion (up 92% year over year) with next-quarter guidance of $91 billion, a B200 order book near 3.6 million units, and more than $750 billion of infrastructure agreements under negotiation, all while memory suppliers can fill only 60-70% of the requested volume for the next generation.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to hyperscaler capital budgets and to how quickly memory suppliers add output.

falsifiableTrigger: HBM leadTimes ease to available-on-demand and CoWoS lead times fall below 26 weeks before the end of 2027.
mechanism: Every accelerator needs both stacked memory and advanced packaging, so whichever is scarcer sets the ceiling on how many units vendors can ship.
rationale: Packaging waits stay at 52 to 78 weeks with lines booked into 2027 and the supply gap still put near 20% by one house against 10% by another, while memory suppliers say they can meet only about half of demand and can fill just 60-70% of next-generation requests.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to the pace of new packaging and memory capacity coming online in 2027.

falsifiableTrigger: AMD accelerator market-share-pct fails to rise above 7% through 2027.
mechanism: A second vendor only becomes a real alternative once its whole-rack product ships in volume, and its named anchor customers arrive a year before that volume does.
rationale: Second-quarter data-centre revenue of $6.7 billion more than doubled year over year and the 72-accelerator rack reached production with Anthropic, OpenAI, Meta and Microsoft named, yet share is still put at 5-7% against a rival near 90% and the real volume ramp lands in 2027.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the rack ramp holds its 2027 schedule and to packaging slots the vendor can secure.

falsifiableTrigger: ASIC market-share-pct growth falls back below GPU growth for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Cloud buyers move their steady inference work onto chips they design themselves, which takes growth that would otherwise go to merchant vendors.
rationale: Custom chips are projected to grow 44.6% in 2026 against 16.1% for merchant accelerators and to reach 27.8% of servers, one cloud is negotiating capacity for more than 300,000 in-house parts for 2027, another added a second design partner for inference silicon, and a third puts four new in-house accelerators into production in September.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether in-house parts reach volume production on schedule and to packaging capacity for them.

falsifiableTrigger: gpuSpotPrice for a current-generation part drops more than 20% within a quarter.
mechanism: Scarce new hardware keeps rental rates firm, while the second-hand market clears at lower prices because buyers prefer newer parts.
rationale: Published hourly rates for current and prior-generation parts hold across providers at $3.29 to $6.69 with the newest part unchanged at $6.69, the system vendor is raising system prices more than 15%, while used cards ask roughly $21,000 to $28,000 against a $25,000 to $40,000 range earlier.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to how fast new rack capacity reaches rental fleets.

falsifiableTrigger: exportControlExposure eases so China DC revenue recovers above prior levels within 2 quarters.
mechanism: Licence rules and tariffs remove a large block of buyers from the addressable market regardless of how much they want to order.
rationale: China data-centre revenue fell to $4.55 billion from $9.66 billion and the vendor books no China compute revenue in its outlook, licensed shipments remain trivial with a 25% tariff, and the approved buyer list for Asia was more than halved.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to policy changes in Washington and Beijing rather than to any company action.

falsifiableTrigger: Vendor-financed GPU commitments in rpoBacklog exceed 300,000 units within 2 quarters.
mechanism: The seller stands behind its own buyers' purchases, so part of reported demand depends on the seller's own balance sheet rather than on independent buying power.
rationale: The vendor cut one proposed customer guarantee from $250 billion to under $120 billion while capping a new site guarantee at $105 billion, signed platforms meant to raise over $500 billion from outside investors, and backstops about 210,000 accelerators at smaller clouds.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether outside capital replaces vendor guarantees and to the credit standing of the backed buyers.

falsifiableTrigger: customerConcentration for the top three direct customers falls below prior shares next fiscal year.
mechanism: A handful of buyers take most of the output, so one of them slowing orders would leave a hole no smaller customer can fill.
rationale: Three direct customers were 21%, 17% and 16% of revenue in the latest quarter after one reached 22% and another 14% for the year, one rocket company expects a very significant share of 2027 output, and a new 8-gigawatt campus is dedicated to a single tenant under a 20-year lease.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether sovereign and enterprise buyers grow fast enough to dilute the top few.

falsifiableTrigger: NVIDIA DC Ethernet switch market-share-pct slips from #1 within 2 quarters.
mechanism: Selling switches and accelerators as one system makes it harder for a buyer to swap out either part on its own.
rationale: The vendor took the top revenue spot in data-centre Ethernet switching, its newest switch line names five launch customers, and a large trading-firm cluster is being built on the same switching fabric, but no finding compares networking growth against compute growth.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether large buyers insist on open switching standards in new clusters.

falsifiableTrigger: Cost-per-token gains stall so tokenEconomics improves less than one generation cycle.
mechanism: Each cut in the cost of serving a request makes more uses affordable, so total work grows faster than the price falls.
rationale: The newest platform is quoted at one-tenth the cost per million tokens of the prior generation, open-model serving costs have fallen 30-50% a year, and one carrier now burns roughly a trillion tokens a month.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the next generation delivers a similar cost step down.

falsifiableTrigger: Prepaid HBM commitments in rpoBacklog shrink or deposits are refunded within a quarter.
mechanism: Buyers who put cash down years ahead for memory have already committed to build the accelerators that memory goes into.
rationale: Sixteen non-cancelable five-year memory agreements are backed by more than $22 billion of cash and related commitments including nearly $18 billion of deposits, with 2026 memory output fully pre-sold under non-cancellable contracts.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether any large depositor seeks to renegotiate or walk away.

falsifiableTrigger: exportControlExposure changes lift the sub-50% China cap or clear Blackwell within 2 quarters.
mechanism: Both governments now limit the trade from their own side, so a licence on paper does not turn into shipped hardware or booked revenue.
rationale: Licences remain case-by-case under a sub-50 percent cap and a 25 percent tariff, shipments are still described as trivial with no revenue booked, and Chinese regulators told approved buyers to keep the licensed hardware in Hong Kong.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to Beijing's stance on domestic chipmakers as much as to Washington's licences.

falsifiableTrigger: Memory hbmSupplyCapex expansion pulls DRAM/NVMe prices down within 2 quarters.
mechanism: Memory is a large part of an AI server bill, so its price rises land first on builders' margins and then on the price buyers pay.
rationale: Memory contract prices are up roughly 50% cumulatively this year on top of a 90% rise since late 2025 with 32 to 40 week waits, rack component costs inflate 2 to 3 percent a week, the largest contract builder says high prices have not slowed customer spending, and the chip vendor is now raising system prices more than 15%.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to when new memory fabs come online and to buyers' willingness to absorb higher system prices.

falsifiableTrigger: releaseCadence slips push a major vendor's 2H-2026 ramp into 2027.
mechanism: Each vendor's ramp depends on its own packaging and memory allocations, so their production dates spread out instead of lining up.
rationale: The leader's newest platform reached full production on 21 July with shipments underway, the challenger's rack reached production with third-quarter shipments but its real volume ramp is put at the second quarter of 2027, and one cloud's in-house parts enter production in September, so the wave still lands in stages.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to manufacturing delays at the trailing vendors.

falsifiableTrigger: AMD customerConcentration eases as its buyer base broadens over the next 2 quarters.
mechanism: A handful of very large commitments carries the growth, so one partner changing plans moves the whole forecast.
rationale: The quarterly filing names two customers each intending up to 6 gigawatts under multi-year agreements with warrant incentives, a third takes up to 2 gigawatts, and the risk factors say a small number of customers will keep making up a substantial part of revenue.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the named gigawatt partners convert intent into firm orders.

falsifiableTrigger: Crescent Island releaseCadence slips its customer sampling past the 2H 2026 quarter.
mechanism: Using standard memory instead of stacked memory lets a chip skip the two supply steps that gate everyone else.
rationale: The inference part using standard memory of up to 480 gigabytes instead of stacked memory is still guided to customer sampling in the second half of 2026, with the stated aim of avoiding packaging and memory contention.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the sampling date holds and to whether standard memory itself stays available.

falsifiableTrigger: TSMC grossMargin declines for 2 consecutive quarters as capacity loosens.
mechanism: When accelerators, custom chips, networking and power parts all compete for the same lines, the foundry can fill every slot and charge more for it.
rationale: Quarterly gross margin reached 67.7% with revenue up 36% and full-year growth guidance raised above 40%, July revenue rose 44.7% year over year, capital spending was lifted to $60-64 billion, and packaging capacity is described as so tight it limits customer growth through 2029-2030.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to a broad pullback in AI orders rather than to any single customer.

falsifiableTrigger: A hyperscalerCapexRevision cuts 2026 or 2027 AI capex guidance within 2 quarters.
mechanism: Spending is rising faster than the cash these buyers generate, so a disappointing return would force them to cut orders.
