rationale: The four largest buyers plan about $725 billion of 2026 spending, up 77%, one bank projects about $4.1 trillion over 2026 to 2028, one buyer posted its first negative free cash flow of $5.9 billion, and analysts warned in July that the jump may be unsustainable while shares fell on the news.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to reported cloud revenue growth and to how investors price the spending.

falsifiableTrigger: NVIDIA grossMargin guidance drops below 70% in a coming quarter.
mechanism: Buyers keep paying premium prices for the leading system, so rising component costs have not yet cut into the margin.
rationale: Gross margin was 75.0% in the latest quarter with the next quarter guided to the same level, far above the challenger's 54% and the foundry's 67.7%.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to memory prices and to the cost of ramping the newest platform.

falsifiableTrigger: Top-buyer customerConcentration in CoWoS output falls below 85% within a year.
mechanism: Because so few customers book almost all the packaging line, one of them cancelling would leave capacity with no ready replacement buyer.
rationale: The top three buyers hold more than 85 percent of packaging output for 2026 and 2027 with the leader at roughly 60 percent, and the leader is reported to have reserved 800,000 to 850,000 wafers of 2026 capacity, over half the year's total.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether smaller custom-chip programmes take a bigger slice of new capacity.

falsifiableTrigger: Aggregate rpoBacklog duration shortens as new commitments turn shorter-dated over 2 quarters.
mechanism: Buyers who fear shortage sign longer contracts, which pushes the average life of the order book further into the future.
rationale: One cloud's backlog rose more than $50 billion sequentially to $514 billion with only just over half converting inside 24 months, one campus is committed under a 20-year lease, memory buyers signed five-year take-or-pay deals, and wafer contracts are stretching from about three years to five to eight.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to any easing of shortage, which would remove the reason to book so far ahead.

falsifiableTrigger: A leading model provider reports revenue (apiArr) growth stalling quarter over quarter while compute commitments keep growing.
mechanism: Rising paid sales give model builders real cash to justify the compute they are contracting for.
rationale: One model provider's recurring revenue reached over $30 billion by April from $1 billion in January 2025, another reported quarterly AI revenue of $2.6 billion up 247% year over year, and a compute chief ties frontier work directly to meeting paying customer demand.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether revenue growth keeps pace with the size of new compute commitments.

falsifiableTrigger: Chinese domestic accelerator designWins for frontier training stall over the next 2 quarters.
mechanism: Domestic parts now prove they can train frontier models, but they cannot yet be built in the volumes Chinese buyers want.
rationale: A 1.6-trillion-parameter model was pretrained on more than 50,000 domestic parts across over 35 trillion tokens, two domestic vendors guided to first-half growth of 135-149% and 56-70% with one holding 56.95% gross margin and cutting its loss by 95.7%, yet Chinese firms still ordered over two million restricted parts against roughly 700,000 units of inventory.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to domestic memory and packaging capacity rather than to chip design.

falsifiableTrigger: A neocloud's marginalBuyerFinancing debt load or net loss narrows for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Buying fleets on credit means interest and depreciation grow alongside revenue, so faster growth deepens the loss.
rationale: One operator grew revenue about 168% from $1.9 billion to $5.1 billion while its net loss widened from $937 million to $1.2 billion, with total debt up 16.1% in a single quarter to $24.86 billion.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to rental rates and to the cost of new borrowing.

falsifiableTrigger: A top hyperscaler cuts its 2027 gigawatt power target below its 2026 level.
mechanism: Buyers now plan in gigawatts because a site without power cannot host accelerators no matter how many they can buy.
rationale: One buyer plans 7 gigawatts in 2026 and roughly double that in 2027, another went from 400 megawatts to 1.4 gigawatts in a year and guides above 2 gigawatts, the chip vendor is lowering product power ratings because of site power limits, and a new campus comes with a $4.2 billion grid investment tied to at least 10 gigawatts of new generation.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to grid connection queues and to how fast new generation is built.

falsifiableTrigger: Broadcom-plus-Marvell market-share-pct of custom ASIC co-design falls below 90% within a year.
mechanism: New design partners entering the market spread custom-chip work across more suppliers than the original two.
rationale: The two firms are still put at about 95% of custom design work, but a third designer raised its share target to 15-20% with over $2 billion of 2026 revenue and a first chip in production in the fourth quarter, one cloud shifted part of its programme to the smaller of the two incumbents, and a model builder hired a chip leader and is talking to a memory maker about its own part.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the newest entrant's first chip actually reaches volume production.

falsifiableTrigger: Wistron odmMonthlyAiRevenue falls year-over-year for 2 consecutive months.
mechanism: Contract builders only book revenue when finished systems leave the factory, so their monthly sales show real shipments rather than orders.
rationale: One contract maker posted record June revenue of NT$321.82 billion up 53.9% year over year, the largest posted July revenue of NT$946.51 billion up 54.19% and its first month above NT$900 billion, the foundry's July revenue rose 44.7%, and one builder says AI servers are now 95% of its server business.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to component shortages that can hold finished racks in the factory.

falsifiableTrigger: A neocloud's marginalBuyerFinancing debt-to-equity rises above 6:1 within 2 quarters.
mechanism: Fleets are financed with borrowed money against hardware that loses value, which leaves a thin cushion if rental rates slip.
rationale: One operator carries $18.81 billion of debt against $3.5 billion of equity, a 5.4:1 ratio, with total debt up 16.1% in a quarter, while raising 2026 capital spending to $31-35 billion from $14.9 billion.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to credit availability and to the resale value of prior-generation hardware.

falsifiableTrigger: Co-packaged optics adoption stalls below 5% of AI optical modules through 2027.
mechanism: Moving the optics into the switch package cuts power and parts, which ties cluster wiring to how fast that new optics supply chain can scale.
rationale: Co-packaged designs are projected to go from about 0.5% of AI optical modules in 2026 to about 35% by 2030, a switch platform claims 4x fewer lasers and 5x lower power, order books are reported full through 2027 with supply tight into 2028, and the vendor signed a long-term deal to expand US optical manufacturing tenfold.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to optical engine yields and to packaging capacity for them.

falsifiableTrigger: A named US fab or packaging project slips its build milestone past 2027.
mechanism: Building fabs, packaging and component plants in the United States adds capacity that does not depend on one island's factories.
rationale: The vendor plans up to $500 billion of US AI infrastructure with named partners, a contract maker opened a 324,000-square-foot Texas plant, the foundry added an incremental $100 billion US investment, a memory maker committed $250 billion through 2035 targeting 40% domestic output, and an optics partner is adding three plants and over 3,000 jobs.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to construction schedules, power hookups and trained staff rather than to demand.

falsifiableTrigger: Google Cloud or CoreWeave rpoBacklog fails to grow sequentially for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Contracts are signed faster than capacity can be built, so the order book grows even when quarterly sales are capped by delivery.
rationale: One cloud's backlog rose more than $50 billion sequentially to $514 billion with just over half converting inside 24 months while its revenue grew 82% year over year, and a specialist's contracted backlog reached $99.4 billion from $66.8 billion a month earlier.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to how quickly new sites and hardware come online to convert the backlog.

falsifiableTrigger: A top hyperscaler returns to positive free cash flow while holding 2027 capex guidance for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Spending has outgrown the cash these businesses throw off, so they raise debt and shares to keep building.
rationale: One buyer funded its quarter with $49.6 billion of equity issuance and $20.3 billion of notes and reported its first-ever negative free cash flow of $5.9 billion, another roughly doubled 2026 spending to $31-35 billion, and combined spending is guided about 77% higher to roughly $725 billion.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to borrowing costs and to investor appetite for funding the buildout.

falsifiableTrigger: A new accelerator generation delivers less than a 1.5x perfPerWatt gain over its predecessor.
mechanism: More work per megawatt lets a buyer add capability inside a fixed power and packaging budget.
rationale: The newest rack is claimed at 10x the work per megawatt of the prior one, an enterprise system at up to 10x the performance per megawatt of what it replaces, the last generation step measured about 1.6x, a photonics switch claims 5x better power efficiency, and a wafer-scale rival claims 10x throughput per watt over its own prior system.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether vendor claims hold up in real deployments rather than in marketing figures.

falsifiableTrigger: HBM leadTimes shorten and suppliers report unsold capacity for 2 consecutive quarters before end-2027.
mechanism: Stacked memory is now scarcer than the chips or the packaging, so it sets how many finished accelerators can be built.
rationale: Suppliers can fill only 60-70% of requested volume for the next generation, one maker says it can supply no more than about half of demand and calls memory the top constraint with no line of sight to balance, customers ask for about 50% more than can be committed, and the vendor is assessing four alternative memory specifications as a result.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to yields on the newest stacked memory and to how much wafer capacity is diverted to it.

falsifiableTrigger: Memory supplier grossMargin falls for 2 consecutive quarters as contract prices flatten.
mechanism: Scarcity lets memory suppliers set prices, so more of the money paid for an AI server ends up with them instead of the builder.
rationale: One maker's data-centre segment posted $11.5 billion of revenue up 103% sequentially at an 87% gross margin, next-generation contract prices are forecast to roughly double into 2027, another seeks up to a 20% quarterly contract price rise with quotes valid for only 72 hours, and contracts are locked at high-teen to low-twenties percent increases.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to new memory capacity arriving and to buyers designing around less memory.

falsifiableTrigger: No new sovereign or enterprise cluster above 10,000 GPUs is announced for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Governments and large companies are now buying clusters at a size that used to belong only to cloud giants, adding a separate pool of orders.
rationale: A Japanese national project takes 27,500 accelerators across 140 megawatts, a Korean carrier is building a 2-gigawatt cloud, a pharmaceutical company deployed eight of the newest systems, a wafer-scale vendor names a sovereign fund and a national university among customers, and the challenger launched a part aimed specifically at sovereign work.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to public budgets and to whether these buyers can secure power and staff.

falsifiableTrigger: Intel data-center revenue growth falls below 10% year over year for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Growing server sales and a foundry with better yields give buyers a third supplier for parts of the AI stack.
rationale: Data-centre revenue reached $6.3 billion up 59% year over year, foundry revenue $5.8 billion up 31% with losses narrowing, gross margin rose to 40.4% from 27.5% with the next quarter guided near 41%, and the company raised $15 billion in a stock offering to fund more capacity.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to yields on its newest process and to winning external foundry customers.

falsifiableTrigger: New vendor equity-for-compute deals in marginalBuyerFinancing stop appearing for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: When the seller owns part of the buyer, some reported demand rests on money the seller put in rather than on independent budgets.
rationale: The challenger committed up to $5 billion of equity in a model builder alongside a gigawatt compute deal, the leader invested in a research lab it also supplies, put $1.5 billion into a site developer and up to $3 billion into a power developer for about 20% ownership, and earlier bought $5 billion of a rival's stock.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the funded customers can later raise money on their own.

falsifiableTrigger: Standard DRAM S10 spot prices fall for 2 consecutive months as suppliers restore non-AI capacity.
mechanism: Memory makers move wafers to the highest-priced AI parts, which leaves less for consumer and general-purpose products and lifts their prices.
rationale: A graphics vendor raised bundle prices about 10% citing memory costs with one memory type's spot price roughly tripled since late 2025, older standard memory hit $81.20 up 17.5% in a month and above its prior peak, suppliers are cutting standard output to favour AI grades, and enterprise contracts get priority on flash over retail.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to when new memory capacity arrives late in 2026 and beyond.

falsifiableTrigger: No new multi-year accelerator-to-memory supply partnership is announced for 2 consecutive quarters through 2027.
mechanism: Chip vendors sign straight to the memory makers because reserving future output is the only way to protect their own build plans.
rationale: The leader entered a long-term partnership with a memory maker to secure next-generation supply and jointly develop it, three suppliers began full-scale development of a 16-high part specifically for that vendor targeting fourth-quarter delivery, the partnership sits inside a $500-billion-plus Korean initiative, and one supplier has finalised long-term agreements with about ten customers.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether memory stays scarce enough to justify locking supply years ahead.

falsifiableTrigger: The leading supplier's HBM market-share-pct falls below 50% within 4 quarters as rivals ship volume.
mechanism: A second supplier reaching similar production yields gives buyers a real alternative source for stacked memory.
rationale: The leader still holds about 56-58% of the market and roughly 62% of the newest generation, but its nearest rival reached close to 80% yield about four months ahead of expectations and targets roughly 38% share by year-end while the leader itself sits at similar yield, so the single-source grip is loosening.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the second supplier's parts pass customer qualification in volume.

falsifiableTrigger: No new diversion prosecution or whitelist reduction is reported for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Criminal charges and shorter buyer whitelists raise the personal and commercial cost of moving restricted hardware through informal channels.
rationale: Prosecutors indicted nine people including employees of a chip vendor and a server maker over exporting controlled parts, an earlier probe raided offices and detained staff over about $2.5 billion of diverted servers, the server maker's own board review led to terminations and a wider compliance programme, and the chip vendor more than halved its approved Asian buyer list.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to prosecutors' follow-through and to how far whitelists are tightened.

falsifiableTrigger: CoWoS lead times stay above 52 weeks through the end of 2027 while the supply gap fails to narrow below 15%.
mechanism: Packaging capacity is being added faster than memory capacity, so the two constraints are now moving in different directions.
rationale: One account puts the packaging shortfall at about 10 percent in mid-2026, narrowed from about 20 percent, while another still estimates about 20 percent for 2026 with lines booked through 2027, and the memory side shows no easing at all with one supplier meeting about half of demand.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to which packaging estimate proves right, since the two published figures still differ by half.

falsifiableTrigger: NAND contract prices for server drives fall for 2 consecutive quarters while Rubin deployments keep growing.
mechanism: Adding a large drive pool to every rack creates a new source of demand big enough to strain flash supply.
rationale: The newest generation's storage tier is expected to lift flash demand from about 35 million terabytes this year to more than 100 million next year with each unit carrying 576 drives, enterprise contracts already get priority allocation over retail, and rack component costs are inflating 2 to 3 percent a week partly on drive scarcity.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to how quickly flash makers add capacity against this new tier.

falsifiableTrigger: Every major cloud provider publishes list rates for its newest rack-scale systems for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Providers with scarce new capacity sell it through negotiated contracts, so their public pages show only the older parts they can offer to anyone.
rationale: One provider publishes an hourly rate for the newest rack class while another's public catalogue as of 24 August still lists nothing newer than the prior flagship and no rates for two other current parts, exactly the split the thesis describes.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to how quickly the newest racks reach general availability at each provider.

falsifiableTrigger: NVIDIA accelerator market-share-pct stabilises or rises for 2 consecutive quarters while rival shipments grow.
mechanism: The whole market is growing faster than the leader's own shipments, so rivals gain share without taking existing business away.
rationale: Share estimates keep falling in one series from 87% in 2024 to 81% and 75%, other counts put it at 70-80% and one at as much as 90%, while the same period brought record data-centre revenue of $75.2 billion up 92% year over year, so the direction is clear but the level is disputed.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to how custom chips are counted, since published share figures differ by twenty points.

falsifiableTrigger: A major buyer returns to purchasing loose accelerators rather than vendor racks for a flagship cluster within 2 quarters.
mechanism: Vendors now sell complete racks with their own networking and software, so buyers compare finished systems rather than individual chips.
rationale: The challenger's 72-accelerator rack with its own memory, processors and software reached production with five named adopters, the leader's 72-accelerator rack ramped across five clouds, a wafer-scale rival launched a rack-scale system, and pricing is now quoted per rack at $2.8-3.4 million rising to $5-7 million for the newest.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to open rack standards that would let buyers mix parts again.

falsifiableTrigger: ERCOT data-center additions exceed 5 GW over the next 4 quarters as the pause lifts.
mechanism: A site cannot take delivery of accelerators until it is connected to the grid, so the queue rather than chip supply sets the pace.
rationale: The Texas connection queue holds roughly 474 gigawatts with about 90 percent of requests from data centres, yet only about 1.2 gigawatts of additions are forecast over the next year and up to $8 billion of lost revenue is attributed to the pause, while the chip vendor is buying into powered land and grid projects to get around it; no finding this cycle reports transformer lead times.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to state-level policy on connection queues and to private grid investment.

falsifiableTrigger: Median newest-generation gpuSpotPrice falls while prior-generation rates rise for 2 consecutive months.
mechanism: A premium only concentrates in new hardware if its published rate rises while older rates fall, and the newest published rate has held flat.
rationale: The newest publicly rented part is still quoted at $6.69 an hour, unchanged across three captures in August, while prior-generation quotes spread widely from $3.29 to about $6.16 an hour across providers, so the premium is not visibly concentrating in the newest hardware.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to the fact that the newest racks are largely absent from public price pages.

falsifiableTrigger: Alternative packaging upstreamLeadTimes rise above 52 weeks, or no accelerator maker places advanced-packaging volume outside TSMC for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Buyers facing year-long waits at the leading packager place work wherever the queue is shorter.
rationale: Alternative routes quote 26-39 week waits against 52-78 weeks at the leader, one cloud committed to more than 3 million units of a rival's bridge packaging for 2028, that rival reports high demand and a growing backlog targeting 2027 volume, the leader itself is outsourcing a front-end step to subcontractors, and two more subcontractors are adding capacity.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether alternative routes hold their yields at volume.

falsifiableTrigger: AMD's share of CoWoS output in pkgCapacityOrderSpread rises above 15% within 2 quarters.
mechanism: One packaging line serves both product families, so every processor packaged uses a slot an accelerator cannot have.
rationale: The challenger holds about 11% of the leading packager's output, roughly 105,000 wafers, and must split it between its server processors and its accelerators, while its new accelerator carries 432 gigabytes of stacked memory, half again more than the previous part, which raises the cost of each slot.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the challenger secures capacity outside the leading packager.

falsifiableTrigger: The next flagship ships with its originally planned 288GB memory configuration within 2 quarters of launch.
mechanism: With a fixed pool of stacked memory, putting less in each unit is the only way to build more units.
rationale: Multiple accounts now put the next top-end part at 192 gigabytes in an 8-high stack, down from a previewed 1 terabyte and below the current 288 gigabytes, with constrained memory named as the driver, some samples reverting to the older memory type, power shortages cited for lower power ratings, and the vendor assessing four alternative memory specifications.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to yields on the newest 12-high and 16-high memory stacks.

falsifiableTrigger: The first Korean AI factory misses its 2027 target or the partnership is not converted from letters of intent into signed contracts within 2 quarters.
mechanism: Tying construction, memory supply and cloud capacity into one national programme concentrates a second cluster of the buildout in Korea.
rationale: The partnership was formalised through letters of intent as a $500-billion-plus initiative with a first AI factory targeted for 2027, a Korean carrier will build a 2-gigawatt cloud on the newest platform and local memory, a memory maker approved a 7.09 trillion won packaging plant, and Korean chip exports nearly tripled to $26 billion in the first 20 days of August.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the letters of intent become binding contracts.

falsifiableTrigger: No accelerator or system vendor announces a shipping product using the high-bandwidth flash specification within 4 quarters.
mechanism: A standard flash tier gives system builders a cheaper memory layer that does not draw on the scarce stacked-memory pool.
rationale: Two suppliers published the first high-bandwidth flash specification through an industry consortium covering up to 512 gigabytes per stack and three speed grades, with two more firms joining, while the newest racks are being designed around large drive pools of 576 drives per unit and a new flash generation claims 2.5 times better performance per watt.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether a shipping product actually adopts the new specification.

falsifiableTrigger: AMD software releases deliver less than a 1.5x measured inference gain over the prior release for 2 consecutive releases.
mechanism: Software tuning raises the useful output of hardware already installed, so competitiveness improves before new hardware ships.
rationale: The vendor reports 3.3x inference and 2.4x training gains over its prior software release and a 2.10x end-to-end throughput gain with a 3.71x faster first response on a current part, and claims 30% more tokens per dollar than the rival's newest system, while its own rack volume ramp is put at the second quarter of 2027.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to independent benchmarks confirming vendor-reported gains.

falsifiableTrigger: SpaceX nameplate compute fails to exceed 2 gigawatts by the end of 2026 or its quarterly AI capex falls below $10 billion for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: A single non-cloud buyer spending at this rate takes a large slice of a supply that is already short.
rationale: The company ended the quarter at 1.4 gigawatts of compute from 400 megawatts a year earlier and guides above 2 gigawatts by year-end and about 10 gigawatts by end-2027, spent roughly $15.8 billion on AI infrastructure in the quarter, says it will build exclusively on one vendor, and expects a very significant share of that vendor's 2027 output.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether its AI revenue keeps funding spending at this pace.

falsifiableTrigger: Intel's share of 2.5D packaging capacity fails to rise above 20% within 4 quarters, or its bridge packaging misses 2027 mass production.
mechanism: The alternative route depends on a single small-component supplier and unproven substrate output, so it inherits a bottleneck of its own.
rationale: The bridge route is winning volume with a cloud ordering more than 3 million units and yields reported above 90%, but its sole silicon-capacitor supplier is already fully booked, substrate mass production is only expected in 2027 at 50% initial yields with one supplier doubting full volume before then, and the technology is described as better suited to custom chips than to high-bandwidth accelerators.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to substrate yields and to a second source for the silicon capacitors.

falsifiableTrigger: MediaTek market-share-pct of AI accelerators fails to exceed 5% within 4 quarters, or its first chip misses Q4 2026 production.
mechanism: A third design house with funded programmes and a named cloud customer gives buyers an alternative to the two incumbent designers.
rationale: The entrant raised its share target to 15-20% from 10-15%, expects over $2 billion of 2026 revenue with a first chip in production in the fourth quarter and a second in 2028, and approved $5 billion of financing, but one analyst notes its 2024 share was under 1 percent and calls the target very high.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the first chip reaches production on time, given the gap between target and current share.

falsifiableTrigger: Used prior-generation server prices fall more than 40% within 2 quarters, or published prior-generation rental rates drop below $2.00 per GPU-hour.
mechanism: Older systems cost a fraction of new ones and still rent at workable rates, so buyers keep running them instead of retiring them.
rationale: A new top-end server is priced near $500,000 against roughly $150,000 to $180,000 for a used prior-generation one, used cards ask about $21,000 to $28,000 against a $25,000 to $40,000 range earlier, and prior-generation rental quotes still run from $2.79 to about $6.16 an hour across providers.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to how fast new capacity arrives and to power costs of running older gear.

falsifiableTrigger: Wafer suppliers report spare 300mm capacity or falling wafer prices for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Every extra memory and packaging wafer starts as a blank silicon wafer, so the shortage moves one step further back up the chain.
rationale: One maker says its 300mm, 200mm and 150mm lines are effectively at full use with constraints already appearing on some advanced products, spot prices for 300mm wafers are rising with more increases expected, buyers are lengthening contracts from about three years to five to eight, and a memory maker signed a 10-year agreement with $500 million of upfront support.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to new memory fabs starting up and competing for the same wafer supply through 2027.

falsifiableTrigger: AMD's reported remaining performance obligations stay below $1 billion for 2 consecutive quarters while new gigawatt commitments keep being announced.
mechanism: Announced gigawatt intentions do not appear as contracted obligations until customers sign firm, dated purchase commitments.
rationale: The quarterly filing reports only $222 million of remaining performance obligations on contracts longer than a year, of which $144 million falls within twelve months, and the company disclosed no dollar backlog while describing customer pull as ahead of forecast, even as two customers each state intent for up to 6 gigawatts.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the announced deployments convert into disclosed contract obligations.

falsifiableTrigger: No hardwired inference product reaches customer shipment within 4 quarters, or inference workloads stay on general accelerators for 2 consecutive quarters after launch.
mechanism: Fixing a finished model into hardware removes general-purpose overhead, which makes running that model cheaper than on a flexible accelerator.
rationale: The challenger signed a definitive agreement to buy a startup that burns model weights into silicon and plans to pair it with its own systems, the leader held early talks with a Korean inference-chip designer about partnership or acquisition, and a model builder placed about $250 million of initial orders with another inference-chip startup.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to how often models change, since hardwired parts lose value when the model does.

falsifiableTrigger: Non-cloud owners stop signing new rental or lease agreements for 2 consecutive quarters, or rented share of their fleets falls below 50%.
mechanism: Owners who bought more capacity than they use rent the surplus, which puts a new layer of supply between chip vendors and end users.
rationale: One non-cloud owner expects roughly 90% of its compute to serve inference or be rented out with only about 10% used for its own training, and holds multibillion-dollar capacity leases with two large AI buyers, while cloud-designed custom chips remain captive and unavailable to rent.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether their own workloads grow enough to absorb the capacity.

falsifiableTrigger: No compute-financing platform closes a funded transaction within 2 quarters, or the memorandums lapse without binding agreements.
mechanism: Third-party capital can carry purchases the vendor now underwrites itself, but only once the platforms sign binding deals.
rationale: The vendor signed memorandums with six large asset managers and banks to set up financing platforms meant to mobilise over $500 billion of third-party capital, but the memorandums are described as non-binding, and its own backstop programme still carries about 210,000 accelerators.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the non-binding memorandums turn into funded transactions.

falsifiableTrigger: Samsung foundry utilisation loosens or it reverses the 10-15% price increase within 2 quarters.
mechanism: AI orders overflowing from the market leader fill the second supplier's lines, which lets it raise prices too.
rationale: The second-largest contract chipmaker raised prices 10-15% on new orders in July, says it cannot meet all orders with its main advanced line at full capacity, and expects AI and high-performance work to exceed 30% of foundry revenue this year against 15-20% in late 2025, though it still holds only 7% of global foundry revenue.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the market leader's capacity expansion pulls those overflow orders back.

falsifiableTrigger: Cerebras fails to report CS-4 customer shipments within 2 quarters, or no named customer expands beyond its initial system within 4 quarters.
mechanism: Building the system from whole wafers avoids the packaging and stacked-memory queue that limits accelerator racks.
rationale: The vendor launched a rack-scale system of three whole wafers delivering 750 petaflops with first shipments this quarter, claims up to 30 times the per-user speed of accelerator systems and 10 times the throughput per watt of its own prior generation, and names a model builder, a sovereign group, a university and a large cloud among customers while supporting pairing with rival racks.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether named customers expand beyond first systems.

falsifiableTrigger: No new vendor-guaranteed or vendor-funded data-centre site above 1 gigawatt is announced for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: The chip vendor pays for sites and power so that buildings exist to hold the hardware it wants to sell.
rationale: The vendor guaranteed leases for about 4.25 gigawatts at an Ohio campus with its payment obligation capped at $105 billion and an option taking the site to 8 gigawatts, invested $1.5 billion in the site developer alongside a $4.2 billion regional grid investment, is putting up to $3 billion into a power developer for about 20% ownership, and is in advanced talks to fund a powered-land developer with over 7 gigawatts sold.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to the credit of the tenants whose leases are being guaranteed.

falsifiableTrigger: A hyperscaler raises AI capex guidance and its shares rise on the day for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Investors now read a bigger AI budget as money leaving the payer and arriving at the supplier, so the two move in opposite directions on the day.
rationale: One buyer's shares fell about 6% on the day it raised its spending forecast, with other spending names falling too, while a memory supplier rose 4.86% in one session attributed to that same forecast, and the challenger's shares fell more than 8% on a capital-spending overshoot.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether reported returns on the spending start to show up in results.

falsifiableTrigger: MLCC lead times for AI server grades fall below 20 weeks for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Every server needs thousands of these tiny parts, so a wait on them holds up a finished rack just as a missing chip would.
rationale: Waits for the high-capacitance, high-specification small capacitors used in AI servers are stretching toward 40 weeks on AI server demand.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to capacitor makers adding lines, and this cycle rests on a single report.

falsifiableTrigger: No new trading-firm compute commitment above $1 billion is announced for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Trading firms need large bursts of compute without owning data centres, so they sign capacity contracts alongside the clouds and model builders.
rationale: One specialist cloud signed a multiyear, multibillion-dollar expansion with a trading firm covering the newest racks, stacking on another firm's $6 billion capacity commitment and a third firm's expansion, and describes quant traders as a meaningful customer segment.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to trading profits, which fund these commitments.

falsifiableTrigger: The next flagship launches in a single memory configuration, or the number of assessed memory specifications falls below 2 within 2 quarters.
mechanism: When memory and power supply are both uncertain, the vendor prepares several versions so it can build whichever parts it can source.
rationale: The vendor has been assessing four alternative memory specifications for its next top-end part since the third quarter, is testing both 192 and 256 gigabyte versions with some samples on the older memory type, and reported power versions span roughly 1,800 watts, 2,600 to 2,800 watts and a 1,200 watt option for lighter work.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to memory qualification results, which decide how many versions survive to launch.

falsifiableTrigger: A major vendor's next flagship arrives more than 24 months after its predecessor, or a named 2027 or 2028 roadmap part slips by 2 quarters.
mechanism: Vendors shorten the gap between generations to hold buyers' attention, so a new top-end system now appears about every year.
rationale: The newest platform reached full production on 21 July with shipments underway, described as compressing the usual 24-to-30-month cycle into 18 months, while the challenger laid out yearly steps with new accelerator families in 2027 and 2028 and its current parts already generally available.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to memory and packaging supply, which has already forced changes to the next top-end part.

falsifiableTrigger: No model builder taped out a custom accelerator within 4 quarters, or the announced design effort is abandoned within 2 quarters.
mechanism: Model builders large enough to fill a chip line design their own parts to cut cost and secure supply.
rationale: One model builder hired the founder of a cloud's custom chip programme to lead its own silicon effort while still buying from three suppliers, is in early talks with a memory maker about building a custom part on a 2nm process, and placed about $250 million of initial orders with an inference-chip startup, while Chinese labs pursue their own designs judged more than two years out.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to how long a first design takes, with in-house parts judged years away.

detail.falsifiableTrigger: The announced system price increase above 15% is withdrawn or rack quotes fall for 2 consecutive quarters.
detail.mechanism: Memory is a large share of a rack's parts cost, so when memory prices rise the system vendor raises its own price rather than lose margin.
detail.sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether buyers accept higher prices or shift budgets to older systems.
detail.statement: The leading vendor is raising prices on AI server systems by more than 15% for shipments from early next year as memory costs climb.
detail.title: Chip vendors pass memory costs into system prices

detail.falsifiableTrigger: Mid-size cloud AI contract signings fall or capex drops below 20% of revenue for 2 consecutive quarters.
detail.mechanism: Buyers shut out of scarce capacity at the largest clouds sign long contracts with smaller providers, which then spend heavily to build for them.
detail.sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether these providers can secure hardware allocations to serve what they have sold.
detail.statement: Smaller cloud providers are signing multi-year compute contracts worth hundreds of millions and spending a third of their revenue on capacity to serve them.
detail.title: Mid-size clouds win multi-year AI contracts

falsifiableTrigger: B200 rpoBacklog falls below 2 million units for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Buyers commit to multi-year capacity faster than the vendor can build and ship it, so unfilled orders keep stacking up ahead of deliveries.
rationale: Record data-center revenue of $75.2 billion, up 92% year over year, with the next quarter guided to $91.0 billion, sit alongside a roughly 3.6 million unit order backlog, more than $750 billion of infrastructure agreements under negotiation, and an 8 gigawatt Ohio campus reserved for a single customer through 2028. Orders keep being booked years ahead of what can be built.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to the cloud giants' capital budgets, because a coordinated spending cut would drain the order book faster than any supply change.

falsifiableTrigger: HBM leadTimes ease to available-on-demand and CoWoS lead times fall below 26 weeks before the end of 2027.
mechanism: Each accelerator needs both a packaging slot and a stack of fast memory, so whichever of the two runs out first sets the ceiling on how many finished units the vendors can deliver.
rationale: Advanced packaging is still sold out with 52 to 78 week waits and bookings into 2027 even as monthly capacity climbs toward 130,000 wafers, while memory suppliers can meet only 60 to 70 percent of the volume requested for the next flagship generation and one supplier says it can cover no more than about half of customer demand.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to how fast memory makers convert new fabs into shipping output, since packaging capacity is already expanding faster than memory.

falsifiableTrigger: AMD accelerator market-share-pct fails to rise above 7% through 2027.
mechanism: AMD now offers a complete rack that named large buyers will take, but its packaging and memory allocation limits how many it can build before 2027, so credibility rises ahead of share.
rationale: Every clause holds: data-center revenue reached $6.7 billion in the second quarter, up 107% year over year, the 72-accelerator rack reached full production with Anthropic, OpenAI, Meta, Microsoft and Oracle named, and share estimates still put AMD near 5 to 7 percent against a rival at roughly 90 percent, with volume ramp running into the second half of 2027.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the 2027 volume ramp holds its schedule, because the named commitments only convert into share once racks ship.

falsifiableTrigger: ASIC market-share-pct growth falls back below GPU growth for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Large cloud buyers design their own inference parts to cut cost per unit of work, and every workload they move in-house is a workload they no longer buy a merchant accelerator for.
rationale: Custom silicon is projected to grow 44.6% in 2026 against 16.1% for merchant accelerators and to reach 27.8% of AI servers, Google added a second outside design partner under an agreement implying a roughly $120 billion ceiling, Microsoft is negotiating capacity for upward of 300,000 in-house parts for 2027, and Meta's own accelerators enter production in September.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether in-house parts handle training as well as inference, since so far they mainly take the cheaper inference work.

falsifiableTrigger: gpuSpotPrice for a current-generation part drops more than 20% within a quarter.
mechanism: Renters pay for guaranteed access to working capacity while second-hand buyers pay only for the hardware, so rental quotes stay firm even as resale asking prices ease.
rationale: Published hourly rates for current and prior-generation parts hold in a firm band across several providers, from $3.29 to $4.29 for one prior-generation card and $6.69 to $6.99 for the current one, while second-hand card asking prices of roughly $21,000 to $28,000 sit below the $25,000 to $40,000 range and $50,000 peak seen earlier.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to how quickly new capacity comes online, since a wave of freshly installed racks would show up in published hourly rates first.

falsifiableTrigger: exportControlExposure eases so China DC revenue recovers above prior levels within 2 quarters.
mechanism: Government rules decide which parts may be sold to which buyers, so policy sets the size of the market before any commercial factor does.
rationale: China revenue fell to $4.55 billion from $9.66 billion a year earlier with no Hopper data-center shipments in the quarter, the vendor assumes no China data-center revenue at all in its outlook, licensed shipments remain trivial, Beijing has told approved buyers to keep the hardware in Hong Kong, and AMD carries its own restrictions and inventory charges.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to policy on both sides at once, because Washington's cap and Beijing's discouragement each independently keep volumes near zero.

falsifiableTrigger: Vendor-financed GPU commitments in rpoBacklog exceed 300,000 units within 2 quarters.
mechanism: The vendor underwrites the leases, guarantees and financing that let its customers buy, so part of the demand it reports rests on promises it made itself.
rationale: The pattern the statement describes is confirmed point for point: the proposed customer guarantee was cut from $250 billion to under $120 billion, a site residual-value guarantee is capped at $105 billion, financing platforms with six large asset managers aim to mobilise more than $500 billion of outside capital, and the vendor keeps backstopping smaller clouds covering roughly 210,000 accelerators.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the outside-capital platforms actually close funded deals, since that would move the risk off the vendor's own balance sheet.

falsifiableTrigger: customerConcentration for the top three direct customers falls below prior shares next fiscal year.
mechanism: A handful of buyers place nearly all the large orders, so one of them slowing or switching to its own silicon removes a slice of revenue no other buyer can replace quickly.
rationale: Three direct customers accounted for 21%, 17% and 16% of revenue in the latest quarter, the four largest are now more than half, one rocket-company buyer says it expects a very significant share of 2027 output, and the largest single tranche of guaranteed demand rests on one unprofitable customer under a 20-year lease.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to the financial health of the single largest committed buyer, whose lease obligations sit behind the biggest guaranteed block of demand.

falsifiableTrigger: NVIDIA DC Ethernet switch market-share-pct slips from #1 within 2 quarters.
mechanism: Selling the switches and cabling with the accelerators makes the whole cluster one purchase, which raises the cost of mixing in another vendor's parts.
rationale: The vendor took the top revenue spot in data-center Ethernet switching for the first time, named first customers for its next switch generation, and its networking rides along in new cloud deals and a long-term optical manufacturing partnership; still no finding compares networking growth with compute growth, so the sharper claim remains unsupported.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether large buyers keep accepting bundled networking rather than insisting on standard switching from other suppliers.

falsifiableTrigger: Cost-per-token gains stall so tokenEconomics improves less than one generation cycle.
mechanism: When the cost of answering a request falls, uses that were too expensive become worth running, so cheaper serving brings in more work rather than less spending.
rationale: The newest platform is claimed to cut inference cost per token roughly tenfold against the prior generation, open-model serving costs have fallen 30 to 50 percent a year, one telecom buyer now burns about a trillion tokens a month, and a large new buyer expects about 90 percent of its fleet to serve inference.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether cheaper serving keeps arriving on merchant accelerators rather than on purpose-built inference parts.

falsifiableTrigger: Prepaid HBM commitments in rpoBacklog shrink or deposits are refunded within a quarter.
mechanism: Buyers who put cash down years ahead for memory they cannot cancel have already decided to build the accelerators that memory goes into.
rationale: The same commitments stand: 16 non-cancelable five-year take-or-pay agreements backed by more than $22 billion of cash deposits and related commitments, with 2026 memory output sold out under non-cancellable contracts and order books running into 2028.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether any large depositor walks away and forfeits, which would be the first real test of the commitments.

falsifiableTrigger: exportControlExposure changes lift the sub-50% China cap or clear Blackwell within 2 quarters.
mechanism: One government caps how much may be sold and the other discourages taking delivery, so approvals on paper do not turn into shipments.
rationale: Both sides of the block remain in place: case-by-case licensing under a cap of no more than 50 percent of US-shipped volumes plus a roughly 25 percent tariff, roughly ten approved buyers with about $10 billion of licences but shipments still described as trivial, Beijing telling those buyers to hold the hardware in Hong Kong, and no revenue booked.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to Beijing's stance, since licences already exist and it is the buyer side that is currently holding volumes down.

falsifiableTrigger: Memory hbmSupplyCapex expansion pulls DRAM/NVMe prices down within 2 quarters.
mechanism: Memory is a large and rising part of the bill for every AI server, and the vendor has now started charging buyers for that increase instead of absorbing it.
rationale: ADJUSTED: Memory and flash prices keep raising what every AI server costs, with component waits of 32 to 40 weeks, memory prices up about 90 percent since late 2025 and contract prices up roughly 50 percent this year, and the leading vendor is now passing more than 15 percent of that increase into system prices from early next year rather than leaving it all on system builders' margins, while the largest contract builder still reports that high memory prices have not slowed customer spending.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether buyers accept the higher system prices without trimming order volumes.

falsifiableTrigger: releaseCadence slips push a major vendor's 2H-2026 ramp into 2027.
mechanism: Each vendor's ramp depends on its own packaging and memory allocation, so the new parts arrive in sequence rather than together.
rationale: The staged picture holds: the leading vendor's new platform reached full production on July 21, 2026 with shipments underway, AMD's rack reached production with third-quarter shipment start but ramps into the second half of 2027 and one account puts first production output at the second quarter of 2027, and Meta's in-house parts enter production in September.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to AMD's manufacturing schedule, since its ramp is the one already reported to have moved.

falsifiableTrigger: AMD customerConcentration eases as its buyer base broadens over the next 2 quarters.
mechanism: A handful of very large commitments carry almost all of AMD's accelerator growth, so the fate of each partner moves the whole line.
rationale: Regulatory filings now name two customers each intending to deploy up to 6 gigawatts under multi-year agreements with warrant incentives tied to purchase milestones, plus a third at up to 2 gigawatts and a Microsoft expansion, while the company's own risk factors state a small number of customers will keep accounting for a substantial part of revenue.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the announced gigawatt commitments convert into firm orders, since they are currently intent rather than booked.

falsifiableTrigger: Crescent Island releaseCadence slips its customer sampling past the 2H 2026 quarter.
mechanism: Using ordinary memory on a simpler package lets a chip be built without a slot in the queue for stacked memory or advanced packaging.
rationale: Intel's inference part still uses standard low-power memory of up to 480GB rather than stacked memory specifically to avoid contention for advanced packaging and stacked memory, and it remains guided to customer sampling in the second half of 2026 with no slip and no volume reported.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the slower memory is good enough for real inference work, since the route only matters if customers accept the trade.

falsifiableTrigger: TSMC grossMargin declines for 2 consecutive quarters as capacity loosens.
mechanism: AI work now fills capacity across many product types at once, so the foundry can choose the best-paying orders and raise prices.
rationale: Gross margin reached 67.7%, up 9.1 points year over year, full-year revenue growth guidance was raised to slightly above 40 percent, July revenue rose 44.7% year over year, capital spending was lifted to $60-64 billion, and the company says packaging tightness is limiting customer growth with the gap staying very big through 2029-2030.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to how much capacity rivals add, since a credible second source would cap what the leader can charge.

falsifiableTrigger: A hyperscalerCapexRevision cuts 2026 or 2027 AI capex guidance within 2 quarters.
mechanism: Spending is being pulled years forward against revenue that has not arrived yet, so a disappointing return would force budgets down and orders with them.
rationale: Projected spending of about $4.1 trillion over 2026 to 2028 roughly triples the prior six years, one buyer posted its first-ever negative free cash flow of $5.9 billion and fell about 6% on the day it raised guidance, analysts warn the jump may be unsustainable, and large cloud server procurement is forecast to decelerate from 11.6% to 1.7% sequentially.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to reported cloud revenue growth, because that is the number investors use to judge whether the spending is paying back.

falsifiableTrigger: NVIDIA grossMargin guidance drops below 70% in a coming quarter.
mechanism: Buyers pay a premium for the complete system rather than shopping on price, which lets the vendor hold a wide margin even while introducing new products.
rationale: Gross margin came in at 75.0% on a non-GAAP basis with the following quarter guided to the same level, far above AMD at 56% and Intel at 41.8% in the same period.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to memory input costs, which are rising fast and land directly in the cost of each system.

falsifiableTrigger: Top-buyer customerConcentration in CoWoS output falls below 85% within a year.
mechanism: Three buyers hold nearly all the booked packaging slots, so if one cancels there is no queue of other customers able to absorb that volume.
rationale: Advanced packaging is pre-booked at more than 85 percent for 2026 and 2027, the top three customers hold more than 85 percent of output with the leader at roughly 60 percent, and that leader has reserved about 800,000 to 850,000 wafers of 2026 capacity, over half the year's total.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether packaging work spreads to other suppliers, which would dilute how much any single booking matters.

falsifiableTrigger: Aggregate rpoBacklog duration shortens as new commitments turn shorter-dated over 2 quarters.
mechanism: Buyers who fear being shut out sign longer contracts to reserve their place, which pushes the average life of the order book further out.
rationale: One cloud backlog rose more than $50 billion sequentially to $514 billion with only just over half converting within 24 months, a specialist cloud holds a purchase commitment running to 2032, a data-centre lease runs 20 years phasing from 2028, a wafer supplier signed a 10-year agreement, and wafer buyers are stretching contracts from about three years to five to eight.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to how much supply frees up, since buyers only lock in years ahead while they expect scarcity.

falsifiableTrigger: A leading model provider reports revenue (apiArr) growth stalling quarter over quarter while compute commitments keep growing.
mechanism: Model providers pay for compute out of subscription and interface sales, so their revenue growth is what turns compute commitments into something other than a bet.
rationale: One leading provider reached more than $30 billion of annualised revenue from $1 billion 15 months earlier and another posted AI revenue of $2.6 billion, up 247% year over year, but the largest committed buyer is described as unprofitable and seeking more than $500 billion of outside capital, so rising sales and unproven economics sit side by side.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to the profitability, not just the growth, of the biggest committed buyers.

falsifiableTrigger: Chinese domestic accelerator designWins for frontier training stall over the next 2 quarters.
mechanism: Chinese buyers cut off from foreign parts fund local alternatives, but local output is far smaller than the demand those buyers still express for foreign hardware.
rationale: Capability is confirmed again, with a 1.6-trillion-parameter model pretrained on more than 50,000 domestic parts across more than 35 trillion tokens and two Chinese suppliers guiding to first-half growth of 55% to 149%, but volume displacement is not, since buyers ordered more than 2 million restricted foreign parts against roughly 700,000 units of inventory, home-grown lab silicon is judged more than two years out, and one Chinese lab still trained on foreign chips rented offshore.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to how much local manufacturing capacity comes online, since capability without volume changes nothing for merchant demand.

falsifiableTrigger: A neocloud's marginalBuyerFinancing debt load or net loss narrows for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: These operators borrow to buy hardware and depreciate it fast, so revenue growth arrives before profit does.
rationale: The pattern repeats: full-year revenue grew about 168% from $1.9 billion to $5.1 billion while net loss widened from $937 million to $1.2 billion, against total debt of $24.86 billion, up 16.1% in one quarter.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to borrowing costs, since interest on the fleet is what turns growing revenue into widening losses.

falsifiableTrigger: A top hyperscaler cuts its 2027 gigawatt power target below its 2026 level.
mechanism: A site can only run as many racks as its electricity supply allows, so available power sets the deployable number regardless of how many accelerators are bought.
rationale: Buildouts are now stated in gigawatts rather than units, with one campus planned at 8 gigawatts, one buyer at 7 gigawatts in 2026 and roughly double in 2027, another moving from 1.4 to more than 2 gigawatts by year end and about 10 by end-2027, and power shortages are cited as a reason the next flagship's power specification was lowered.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to grid connection timelines, which determine when contracted power actually becomes usable.

falsifiableTrigger: Broadcom-plus-Marvell market-share-pct of custom ASIC co-design falls below 90% within a year.
mechanism: Custom chips need an outside design partner, so the number of firms able to do that work sets how concentrated the alternative to merchant parts really is.
rationale: The two incumbents are still estimated at about 95 percent of custom design work, but a third designer has raised its share target to 15 to 20 percent with its first part entering production in the fourth quarter of 2026 and more than $2 billion of 2026 revenue expected, one incumbent appears to be taking work from the other at the same buyer, and a model builder has hired a custom-chip leader and opened talks with a Korean manufacturer.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the newest entrant ships on schedule, since an analyst has already called its share target very high against a sub-1 percent starting point.

falsifiableTrigger: Wistron odmMonthlyAiRevenue falls year-over-year for 2 consecutive months.
mechanism: Contract builders only book revenue when finished systems leave the factory, so their monthly sales show shipments rather than promises.
rationale: One contract builder posted record June revenue of NT$321.82 billion, up 53.9% year over year, another crossed NT$900 billion for the first time in July at NT$946.51 billion, up 54.19%, the leading foundry reported July revenue up 44.7%, and one builder says AI servers are now 95% of its server business.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to component supply, since memory and substrate shortages are already named as the brake on server shipment growth.

falsifiableTrigger: A neocloud's marginalBuyerFinancing debt-to-equity rises above 6:1 within 2 quarters.
mechanism: Accelerator fleets are bought with borrowed money secured on the hardware, which leaves a thin equity cushion if rental rates fall.
rationale: One operator carries $18.81 billion of debt against $3.5 billion of equity, a 5.4-to-1 ratio, with total debt of $24.86 billion up 16.1% in a single quarter.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to the resale value of the installed fleet, since that is the collateral behind the borrowing.

falsifiableTrigger: Co-packaged optics adoption stalls below 5% of AI optical modules through 2027.
mechanism: Building the optics into the switch package cuts power and parts count, which ties cluster wiring to a new manufacturing chain with its own limits.
rationale: Adoption is projected to rise from about 0.5 percent of AI optical modules in 2026 to about 35 percent by 2030, the new switch platform claims four times fewer lasers and five times lower power at up to 409.6 terabits per second, order books are reported full through 2027 with supply tight into 2028, and packaging houses are newly competing for this work.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to optical engine yields and packaging capacity, both named as the limits on expansion.

falsifiableTrigger: A named US fab or packaging project slips its build milestone past 2027.
mechanism: Buyers and policy both push manufacturing onto US soil, which adds a second place where the same parts can be made.
rationale: Commitments keep landing: up to $500 billion of US-built AI infrastructure with named partners, a new Texas plant for AI systems, $250 billion of US memory investment targeting 40 percent domestic output with a new fab groundbreaking, an incremental $100 billion foundry investment, a US optical manufacturing expansion with three new plants, and a $15 billion equity raise earmarked partly for capacity.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to build schedules, since announced money only broadens supply once the plants actually run.

falsifiableTrigger: Google Cloud or CoreWeave rpoBacklog fails to grow sequentially for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Providers sign contracts they cannot yet serve, so the signed but undelivered pile shows demand earlier than quarterly sales do.
rationale: One cloud backlog rose more than $50 billion sequentially to $514 billion while its revenue grew 82% year over year to $24.8 billion, a specialist cloud's contracted backlog reached $99.4 billion from $66.8 billion a month earlier, and a mid-size provider disclosed more than $2.8 billion of multi-year contracts, so bookings keep running well ahead of delivered sales.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether signed contracts convert on time, since a stalling conversion rate would turn the backlog into a warning instead of a proof.

falsifiableTrigger: A top hyperscaler returns to positive free cash flow while holding 2027 capex guidance for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Spending has outgrown the cash the businesses generate, so the shortfall is now covered by borrowing and share sales.
rationale: One buyer funded its quarter with $49.6 billion of equity issuance and $20.3 billion of notes and reported its first-ever negative free cash flow of $5.9 billion, a chipmaker raised $25 billion of bonds to fund a customer-financing programme and signed platforms aiming at more than $500 billion of outside capital, and a foundry launched a $15 billion share sale.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to credit conditions, because the buildout's pace now depends on how cheaply this debt can be raised.

falsifiableTrigger: A new accelerator generation delivers less than a 1.5x perfPerWatt gain over its predecessor.
mechanism: Each generation does more work for the same electricity, so a site with fixed power can keep adding capability without adding megawatts.
rationale: The newest rack is claimed to deliver ten times the throughput per megawatt of the prior generation and ten times the performance per megawatt of the infrastructure it replaces, a wafer-scale rival claims ten times the throughput per watt of its own prior system, a photonic switch claims five times lower power, and a new flash generation claims 2.5 times better performance per watt.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether vendor efficiency claims hold up in real deployments rather than in launch material.

falsifiableTrigger: HBM leadTimes shorten and suppliers report unsold capacity for 2 consecutive quarters before end-2027.
mechanism: Every accelerator needs its stack of fast memory, and memory production displaces ordinary memory at three to four times the wafer cost, so memory output now sets the shipping number.
rationale: One supplier says it can cover no more than about half of customer demand, calls memory the single biggest constraint its largest customers face and has no line of sight to balance, another says customers ask for about 50 percent more than it can commit, suppliers can meet only 60 to 70 percent of the volume requested for the next flagship, and tight memory is named as the primary brake on server shipment growth.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to yields at the two Korean suppliers, since better yields turn the same wafers into more usable stacks.

falsifiableTrigger: Memory supplier grossMargin falls for 2 consecutive quarters as contract prices flatten.
mechanism: Memory is scarce while server assembly is not, so the suppliers of the scarce part set the price and keep the profit.
rationale: One supplier's data-centre segment posted $11.5 billion of revenue at an 87% gross margin, up 103% sequentially, stacked-memory contract prices are forecast to roughly double into 2027, all 2026 output is pre-allocated at high-teen to low-twenties percent price increases, one supplier seeks up to a 20% quarterly increase with quote validity cut to 72 hours, and contract prices are already up roughly 50 percent this year.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to when new memory fabs come online, since added supply is what would end the pricing power.

falsifiableTrigger: No new sovereign or enterprise cluster above 10,000 GPUs is announced for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Governments and large companies now buy their own clusters rather than renting, which adds a set of buyers that did not previously order at this size.
rationale: A national AI facility will deploy 27,500 accelerators across 140 megawatts, a Korean carrier will build a 2-gigawatt AI cloud, a pharmaceutical company is installing a second eight-system cluster, a new accelerator variant is aimed specifically at sovereign and scientific buyers, and a wafer-scale vendor names a state-backed group and a national university among customers.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to public budgets, since national projects are funded on political rather than commercial timetables.

falsifiableTrigger: Intel data-center revenue growth falls below 10% year over year for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Better factory yields and improving margins let the company sell processors and manufacturing services again, which adds a third supplier alongside the two accelerator vendors.
rationale: Data-centre revenue reached $6.3 billion, up 59% year over year with $2.5 billion of operating income, foundry revenue rose 31% to $5.8 billion, gross margin improved to 40.4% from 27.5% a year earlier with the next quarter guided above expectations, a first external foundry customer was named, and a $15 billion share sale funds further capacity.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the newest process holds its yield ramp, since the foundry recovery rests on it.

falsifiableTrigger: New vendor equity-for-compute deals in marginalBuyerFinancing stop appearing for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Vendors put their own money into the firms that will buy or host their chips, so part of the reported demand is funded by the seller.
rationale: One vendor committed up to $5 billion of equity in a model builder alongside a 2-gigawatt deployment deal, the other invested an undisclosed amount in a research lab, $1.5 billion in a data-centre developer, up to $3 billion for about 20 percent of a power developer, and is in advanced talks to invest several hundred million more in a powered-land developer.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether outside investors take over this funding role, which would break the loop between seller and buyer.

falsifiableTrigger: Standard DRAM S10 spot prices fall for 2 consecutive months as suppliers restore non-AI capacity.
mechanism: Memory makers move wafers to the highest-paying AI grades, which leaves less output for ordinary memory and pushes those prices up too.
rationale: Older standard memory spot prices hit $81.20, up 17.5% in a month and above the prior peak, newer standard memory broke $50 for the first time, one vendor raised consumer graphics bundle prices about 10 percent citing tripled memory spot prices, suppliers are cutting standard output to favour server grades, and enterprise contracts now take priority over retail for flash.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to when new fabs start, since suppliers will not return capacity to cheaper grades while AI grades pay more.

falsifiableTrigger: No new multi-year accelerator-to-memory supply partnership is announced for 2 consecutive quarters through 2027.
mechanism: Buying memory output directly from the makers reserves the scarce part before it reaches the open market.
rationale: The pattern holds without new escalation this cycle: one vendor entered a long-term partnership with a Korean supplier to secure next-generation memory and jointly develop it, three suppliers began full-scale development of a taller stack specifically for that vendor targeting fourth-quarter delivery, and the largest cloud buyers have used their own cash to lock long-term memory contracts.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to memory scarcity itself, since direct deals stop being worth signing once supply loosens.

falsifiableTrigger: The leading supplier's HBM market-share-pct falls below 50% within 4 quarters as rivals ship volume.
mechanism: One supplier's yield advantage is what gave it most of the stacked-memory market, and a rival matching that yield removes the reason the concentration persists.
rationale: The leader still holds 56% to 62% of stacked memory and about two-thirds of the top vendor's next-generation supply with long-term deals across roughly ten customers, but the second supplier's yield has reached close to 80% from below 60% in February, about four months ahead of schedule and level with the leader, and it aims to lift its share to roughly 38% by year end.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the rival's improved yield turns into qualified shipments at the largest accelerator vendor.

falsifiableTrigger: No new diversion prosecution or whitelist reduction is reported for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Criminal charges and shorter approved-buyer lists raise the personal and commercial cost of moving restricted hardware, which closes the informal routes.
rationale: Prosecutors indicted nine people including employees of a chip vendor and a server maker over exporting controlled parts, that server maker's own board probe led to terminations and an expanded compliance programme, and the authorised Asian buyer list was more than halved; a new leak is appearing though, with one Chinese lab reported to have trained on restricted chips rented offshore and Commerce now investigating.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to renting rather than shipping, since offshore rental gives access without moving any hardware across a border.

falsifiableTrigger: CoWoS lead times stay above 52 weeks through the end of 2027 while the supply gap fails to narrow below 15%.
mechanism: Packaging capacity can be added in about a year while memory needs new fabs, so the two constraints ease on different timetables.
rationale: The disagreement the statement records is unchanged: one account puts the packaging shortfall at about 10 percent in mid-2026 narrowed from about 20 percent, another still puts it at about 20 percent for 2026, lines are booked through 2027, and memory shows no easing with one supplier saying it can cover only about half of demand and seeing no line of sight to balance.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to which shortfall estimate proves right, since the two published figures differ by a factor of two.

falsifiableTrigger: NAND contract prices for server drives fall for 2 consecutive quarters while Rubin deployments keep growing.
mechanism: The newest rack design adds a large bank of drives beside the accelerators, so every rack shipped now pulls far more flash than the last generation did.
rationale: The new context-memory tier is still projected to lift flash demand from about 35 million terabytes this year to more than 100 million next, with each unit carrying 576 drives for 9,600 terabytes, enterprise contracts already taking priority over retail, and rack component costs inflating 2 to 3 percent a week partly on drive scarcity.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to how quickly this rack design is actually deployed, since the demand jump only lands as those units ship.

falsifiableTrigger: Every major cloud provider publishes list rates for its newest rack-scale systems for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Providers keep their scarcest new systems off the price page and sell them through negotiation, so published rates cover only the older parts.
rationale: Repeated captures across August show one provider's newest publicly rentable part is still the prior flagship, with no listing for three newer parts and longer terms quoted only as custom pricing, while another provider does publish an hourly rate for the newest rack system, so public pages show only part of what leading-edge capacity costs.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to how scarce the newest systems are, since providers publish rates once they have spare capacity to fill.

falsifiableTrigger: NVIDIA accelerator market-share-pct stabilises or rises for 2 consecutive quarters while rival shipments grow.
mechanism: The market is growing faster than one vendor can supply it, so rivals fill the extra growth without taking existing business away.
rationale: Record revenue of $75.2 billion, up 92% year over year, sits alongside share estimates that both slip and disagree sharply, from a projected fall from 87% in 2024 to 75% in 2026, to about 70%, to 70-80%, to roughly 80%, to as much as 90% in a given quarter, so the direction is repeated but the level is unsettled.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to how share is measured, since published estimates for the same period range from 70 to 90 percent.

falsifiableTrigger: A major buyer returns to purchasing loose accelerators rather than vendor racks for a flagship cluster within 2 quarters.
mechanism: Vendors sell the whole cabinet with its wiring and software, so buyers compare finished systems rather than individual chips.
rationale: Both merchant vendors now sell 72-accelerator racks with their own networking and software, a wafer-scale entrant launched a rack-scale system of three whole-wafer processors and pairs with rivals' racks, and pricing is now quoted per rack at $2.8 to $3.4 million for the current generation and $5 to $7 million for the next.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to open rack standards, since a common design would let buyers mix parts again.

falsifiableTrigger: ERCOT data-center additions exceed 5 GW over the next 4 quarters as the pause lifts.
mechanism: A site cannot open until the grid connects it, so the queue and the local pause set the build date rather than chip availability.
rationale: The Texas connection queue still holds roughly 474 gigawatts with about 90 percent of new requests coming from data centres, only about 1.2 gigawatts of additions are forecast over the next year, and lost data-centre revenue from the pause is put at up to $8 billion; connection and generation, not transformers, remain what is reported, with one campus tied to a $4.2 billion grid investment.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to state-level policy, since a single pause decision moves gigawatts of planned capacity.

falsifiableTrigger: Median newest-generation gpuSpotPrice falls while prior-generation rates rise for 2 consecutive months.
mechanism: Buyers pay up for whatever just launched because it does the most work per rack, while older parts compete on price against each other.
rationale: The newest publicly listed part still carries a clear premium at $6.69 to $6.99 an hour against $3.29 to $4.29 for the prior generation and $2.79 for the one before, and prior-generation quotes do spread widely across providers, but no finding this cycle shows a prior-generation rate actually falling over time, so the drift-lower half of the claim is unsupported.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether providers publish rates for the newest systems at all, since the premium cannot be measured on parts kept off the price page.

falsifiableTrigger: Alternative packaging upstreamLeadTimes rise above 52 weeks, or no accelerator maker places advanced-packaging volume outside TSMC for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: When the leading packager quotes waits of more than a year, buyers place work with suppliers that can start sooner.
rationale: Alternative routes quote 26 to 39 week waits against 52 to 78 at the leader, one cloud buyer has committed to more than 3 million units of a rival's bridge packaging for 2028 delivery, that rival reports very high demand and a growing backlog targeting 2027 volume, a designer confirmed it uses the same route, the leading accelerator vendor is reported to be weighing a shift of some output, and the leader itself is now outsourcing a front-end packaging step.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to yields on the alternative routes, since initial substrate yields are targeted at only about 50 percent.

falsifiableTrigger: AMD's share of CoWoS output in pkgCapacityOrderSpread rises above 15% within 2 quarters.
mechanism: One fixed pool of packaging slots has to cover two product lines, so building more of one means building fewer of the other.
rationale: AMD still holds roughly 11 percent of the leading packager's output, about 105,000 wafers, against the top customer's roughly 60 percent, and must split that allocation between its server processors and its accelerators so each processor slot used cannot go to an accelerator.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether AMD moves some packaging to alternative suppliers, which would loosen the trade-off.

falsifiableTrigger: The next flagship ships with its originally planned 288GB memory configuration within 2 quarters of launch.
mechanism: With a fixed pool of memory, putting less in each accelerator lets the vendor build more of them, so scarcity changes the product rather than only the count.
rationale: Multiple accounts now confirm the cut to 192GB in an eight-high stack, down from the 1TB design previewed and below the current generation's 288GB, with testing also at 256GB and some samples reverting to the prior memory generation, four alternative specifications under assessment, and memory supply plus site power named as the reasons.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether buyers accept the smaller memory, since one bank's research says performance drops sharply below 500GB.
