falsifiableTrigger: The first Korean AI factory misses its 2027 target or the partnership is not converted from letters of intent into signed contracts within 2 quarters.
mechanism: Tying memory supply, construction and cloud capacity to one country's industrial group concentrates a second cluster of the buildout there.
rationale: The partnership was formalised through letters of intent covering AI factory construction, next-generation memory supply and cloud deployment across the region with the first facility targeted for 2027, a Korean carrier will build a 2-gigawatt AI cloud on the platform, a memory supplier approved a $4.83 billion packaging plant, and Korean semiconductor exports nearly tripled year over year to $26 billion in twenty days of August.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the letters of intent become binding contracts, since the headline figure rests on intentions.

falsifiableTrigger: No accelerator or system vendor announces a shipping product using the high-bandwidth flash specification within 4 quarters.
mechanism: A flash tier built to a common specification gives system designers a cheaper memory layer that does not draw on the scarce stacked-memory pool.
rationale: The first specification for a high-bandwidth flash tier is published through an industry body, covering capacities to 512GB in eight- and sixteen-high stacks and three performance grades from about 0.4 to 3.0 terabytes a second, with two more members joining, and the newest rack already builds around large drive pools of 576 drives per unit; no shipping product yet uses the specification.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether accelerator vendors adopt the specification, since a standard with no products changes nothing.

falsifiableTrigger: AMD software releases deliver less than a 1.5x measured inference gain over the prior release for 2 consecutive releases.
mechanism: Software improvements reach hardware customers already own, so they raise competitiveness immediately while new silicon waits on manufacturing.
rationale: Software work lifted end-to-end throughput 2.10 times and cut time-to-first-token 3.71 times on the current accelerator, and the newest software release claims 3.3 times inference and 2.4 times training gains, while the rack that carries the new parts only ships from the third quarter of 2026 and ramps into the second half of 2027, with one account putting first production output at the second quarter of 2027.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether these gains are measured by customers rather than claimed by the vendor.

falsifiableTrigger: SpaceX nameplate compute fails to exceed 2 gigawatts by the end of 2026 or its quarterly AI capex falls below $10 billion for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: A buyer outside the usual cloud group is spending at cloud-giant scale each quarter, which adds a large new claim on the same limited output.
rationale: Every element is confirmed and extended: nameplate compute rose from 400 megawatts a year earlier to 1.4 gigawatts with guidance above 2 by year end and about 10 by end-2027, roughly $15.8 billion of a $18.4 billion quarter went to AI compute, the buyer says it will build exclusively on one vendor and expects a very significant share of that vendor's 2027 output, and it has now committed to the next processor generation as well.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to this buyer's own funding, since the spending far exceeds the $2.6 billion of AI revenue it currently reports.

falsifiableTrigger: Intel's share of 2.5D packaging capacity fails to rise above 20% within 4 quarters, or its bridge packaging misses 2027 mass production.
mechanism: The alternative route depends on one supplier for a needed component and suits a narrower set of chips, so it cannot simply absorb overflow from the leader.
rationale: The single silicon-capacitor supplier is still described as fully booked, the technology is still characterised as better suited to custom chips than to high-bandwidth accelerators because of limited bridge area, and although yield is reported above 90 percent, substrate mass production is only expected in 2027 with initial yields near 50 percent and one supplier doubting full-scale volume before then.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether a second supplier of the scarce component appears before the 2027 volume ramp.

falsifiableTrigger: MediaTek market-share-pct of AI accelerators fails to exceed 5% within 4 quarters, or its first chip misses Q4 2026 production.
mechanism: A third design house with cloud customers and its own funding gives buyers an alternative to the two firms that previously shared this work.
rationale: The share target of 15 to 20 percent is confirmed with a 2027 market sized at $80 billion, the first part is still on track for fourth-quarter 2026 production with more than $2 billion of 2026 revenue expected and a $5 billion financing approved, and a second part targets 2028; an analyst notes the 2024 starting share was under 1 percent and calls the target very high.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to the first part reaching production on time, since everything else rests on that milestone.

falsifiableTrigger: Used prior-generation server prices fall more than 40% within 2 quarters, or published prior-generation rental rates drop below $2.00 per GPU-hour.
mechanism: Older systems cost a fraction of new ones to buy but still rent for a workable hourly rate, so they stay in service instead of being retired.
rationale: A new current-generation server is priced at about $500,000 against roughly $150,000 to $180,000 for a used eight-accelerator prior-generation one, second-hand cards ask $21,000 to $28,000, and published hourly rates for those older parts still span $2.79 to $4.29 with interruptible capacity at $1.99, so the older hardware keeps earning.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to how much new capacity arrives, since a flood of new racks would pull older rental rates down.

falsifiableTrigger: Wafer suppliers report spare 300mm capacity or falling wafer prices for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Every chip and every memory stack starts as a blank wafer, so the memory expansion pulls the squeeze one step further back up the chain.
rationale: One major wafer maker says its 300mm, 200mm and 150mm lines are effectively at maximum utilisation with constraints already appearing on some advanced products, spot prices for 300mm wafers are rising with more increases expected, buyers are lengthening contracts from about three years to five to eight and rebuilding safety stock, and a ten-year supply agreement with upfront financial support was signed.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to how many new memory fabs start at once, since they compete for the same wafer supply.

falsifiableTrigger: AMD's reported remaining performance obligations stay below $1 billion for 2 consecutive quarters while new gigawatt commitments keep being announced.
mechanism: Announced gigawatt intentions do not appear in contracted obligations, so the gap between the two shows how much of the pipeline is still non-binding.
rationale: The company reported only $222 million of remaining performance obligations on contracts longer than a year, of which $144 million falls within twelve months, and disclosed no dollar backlog at all while describing customer pull as ahead of forecast, even as filings name two customers each intending up to 6 gigawatts and a third at up to 2.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the first named deployments convert into firm purchase orders during 2027.

falsifiableTrigger: No hardwired inference product reaches customer shipment within 4 quarters, or inference workloads stay on general accelerators for 2 consecutive quarters after launch.
mechanism: Burning a finished model directly into silicon removes the flexibility a general accelerator provides and with it much of the cost, which suits high-volume serving of a settled model.
rationale: One merchant vendor signed a definitive agreement to acquire a startup that hardwires model weights into silicon and will pair it with its own accelerators and racks, the other held preliminary talks with a Korean inference-chip startup about partnership, investment or acquisition, and a model builder placed about $250 million of initial orders with another inference-chip startup.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to how fast models change, since a hardwired chip loses its value the moment its model is replaced.

falsifiableTrigger: Non-cloud owners stop signing new rental or lease agreements for 2 consecutive quarters, or rented share of their fleets falls below 50%.
mechanism: Owners who bought more capacity than their own work needs rent the surplus out, which puts a new layer of sellers between the chip vendors and end users.
rationale: One large non-cloud owner now expects roughly 90 percent of its compute to serve inference or be rented to others with only about 10 percent used for its own training, and it holds multibillion-dollar capacity leases with two named counterparties, while its fleet grows from 1.4 toward more than 2 gigawatts.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the owner's own workloads grow enough to reclaim the rented capacity.

falsifiableTrigger: No compute-financing platform closes a funded transaction within 2 quarters, or the memorandums lapse without binding agreements.
mechanism: Bringing in asset managers moves the cost of buying accelerators off the chip vendor's and cloud buyer's balance sheets and onto outside capital.
rationale: The six asset managers and banks are named again for platforms intended to mobilise more than $500 billion, but the agreements are explicitly non-binding memorandums with no funded transaction reported, and the largest committed customer is separately described as seeking over $500 billion of third-party capital while unprofitable.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether any of these memorandums becomes a signed, funded deal.

falsifiableTrigger: Samsung foundry utilisation loosens or it reverses the 10-15% price increase within 2 quarters.
mechanism: AI orders have filled the number two foundry as well as the leader, so tightness now reaches beyond a single supplier.
rationale: The 10 to 15 percent increase on new orders stands, the main advanced line runs at full capacity and the company says it cannot meet all orders, AI and high-performance work is expected to exceed 30 percent of foundry revenue this year against 15 to 20 percent in late 2025, though its 7 percent global share against more than 70 percent for the leader keeps the effect small.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether this fullness reflects AI demand or its own memory base-die needs competing for the same line.

falsifiableTrigger: Cerebras fails to report CS-4 customer shipments within 2 quarters, or no named customer expands beyond its initial system within 4 quarters.
mechanism: A whole-wafer processor keeps a model on one piece of silicon, which suits fast single-user serving and slots in beside existing racks rather than competing for the same job.
rationale: The rack-scale system of three whole-wafer processors is launched at 750 petaflops with first shipments beginning this quarter, claims more than 4,400 tokens per second per user and up to ten times the throughput per watt of its predecessor, names four customers including a leading model builder and a large cloud, and supports pairing with a rival vendor's rack and another's custom silicon rather than replacing them.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether named customers order repeat systems, since first shipments alone prove little.

falsifiableTrigger: No new vendor-guaranteed or vendor-funded data-centre site above 1 gigawatt is announced for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: With power and land now the limit, the chip vendor pays to create the sites so there is somewhere for its own hardware to be installed.
rationale: The vendor entered residual value guaranties covering roughly 4.25 gigawatts of load capped at $105 billion, invested $1.5 billion in the site developer alongside a cited $4.2 billion regional grid investment, will take about 20 percent of a power developer for an initial $2 billion of a commitment up to $3 billion, and is in advanced talks to invest several hundred million more in a developer holding more than 7 gigawatts of sold powered land.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the guarantees are ever called, since they only cost the vendor money if a hosted customer fails.

falsifiableTrigger: A hyperscaler raises AI capex guidance and its shares rise on the day for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Investors now read a bigger AI budget as money leaving the buyer and arriving at the supplier, so the two sets of shares move in opposite directions on the same news.
rationale: One buyer's shares fell about 6% on the day it raised its spending forecast, with other spending names falling too, while a memory supplier rose 4.86% in the same session attributed to that raised forecast; a chipmaker fell more than 8% on a capital spending overshoot, and a foundry rose 8.64% on customer and collaboration news.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to evidence that the spending is paying back, which would let buyers' shares rise on higher budgets again.

falsifiableTrigger: MLCC lead times for AI server grades fall below 20 weeks for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: An AI server cannot ship without its thousands of cheap capacitors, so a shortage of a penny part stops a million-dollar rack just as effectively as a chip shortage.
rationale: Waits for the high-capacitance, high-specification capacitors used in AI servers are still stretching toward 40 weeks on AI server demand, the same picture as before with no new easing or worsening reported.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to how fast capacitor makers add lines, since this is the easiest of the shortages to fix with capacity.

falsifiableTrigger: No new trading-firm compute commitment above $1 billion is announced for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Trading firms need large bursts of compute without owning data centres, so they sign capacity deals that behave like a new buyer group alongside the clouds and model builders.
rationale: A specialist cloud signed a multiyear, multibillion-dollar expansion with one trading firm covering the newest racks, and describes quantitative trading firms as a meaningful customer segment with that deal stacking on another firm's $6 billion commitment and a third firm's expansion.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to trading-firm profitability, since these commitments are discretionary in a way cloud contracts are not.

falsifiableTrigger: The next flagship launches in a single memory configuration, or the number of assessed memory specifications falls below 2 within 2 quarters.
mechanism: When memory and power both run short, the vendor builds several versions of one product so each site can take whichever version it can actually supply.
rationale: Four alternative memory specifications are under assessment for the next flagship since the third quarter, testing spans 192GB and 256GB with some samples reverting to the prior memory generation, and reported power variants span roughly 1,200W, 1,800W and 2,600W to 2,800W for different workloads within the same system family.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to memory qualification, since a settled specification would collapse the family back to one part.

falsifiableTrigger: A major vendor's next flagship arrives more than 24 months after its predecessor, or a named 2027 or 2028 roadmap part slips by 2 quarters.
mechanism: Vendors shorten the gap between generations to stay ahead of rivals, so buyers face a new top-end system roughly every year.
rationale: The newest platform reached full production on July 21, 2026 with the usual 24 to 30 month cycle compressed into 18 months and shipments underway to six named buyers, while the rival has published a yearly cadence with its next accelerator family in 2027 and another in 2028.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to memory and packaging schedules, which have already forced changes to the next flagship's specification.

falsifiableTrigger: No model builder taped out a custom accelerator within 4 quarters, or the announced design effort is abandoned within 2 quarters.
mechanism: Model builders that know their own workloads best now design silicon around them, which adds a source of custom parts beyond the cloud giants.
rationale: One model builder hired the founder of a large cloud's custom chip programme to lead its own silicon development while continuing to buy from three suppliers, is in early talks with a Korean manufacturer about a custom part on a 2-nanometre process, and placed about $250 million of initial orders with an inference-chip startup, while two Chinese labs are pursuing their own inference parts.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to how long these efforts take, since one Chinese assessment puts viable in-house silicon more than two years out.

falsifiableTrigger: The announced system price increase above 15% is withdrawn or rack quotes fall for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Memory has become a large enough share of what a system costs that the vendor charges buyers for the increase rather than absorbing it in its own margin.
rationale: The leading vendor is reported to be raising AI server system prices by more than 15 percent in many cases for systems shipping from early next year, against memory contract prices up roughly 50 percent cumulatively this year, with rack quotes moving from $2.8 to $3.4 million for the current generation to $5 to $7 million for the next; a second vendor separately raised consumer graphics bundle prices about 10 percent on the same cause.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to buyer tolerance, since the pass-through only holds while orders keep coming at the higher price.

falsifiableTrigger: Mid-size cloud AI contract signings fall or capex drops below 20% of revenue for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Buyers shut out of the largest clouds' scarce capacity sign with smaller providers, who then spend a third of their revenue building capacity to serve them.
rationale: One mid-size provider disclosed year-to-date multi-year cloud infrastructure contracts collectively worth more than $2.8 billion including a single customer above $600 million over four years, with the related revenue up 39% year over year, while spending $346.5 million in the quarter, equal to 32% of total company revenue.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether these providers can fund the capacity, since the spending arrives well before the contract revenue does.

detail.falsifiableTrigger: Large US cloud server procurement growth returns above 5% quarter over quarter with accelerator-led servers taking a rising share for 2 consecutive quarters.
detail.mechanism: Agent-style work spends more of its time on ordinary processing and data handling than on model maths, so each new deployment needs proportionally fewer accelerators.
detail.sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the slowdown reflects a real mix shift or only the memory and substrate shortage that is separately named as the brake.
detail.statement: Cloud providers are shifting part of their new server buying away from accelerator-heavy machines toward ordinary processors and storage as agent-style work spreads.
detail.title: Agent-style workloads tilt cloud buying toward general-purpose servers

detail.falsifiableTrigger: Next-generation rack quotes settle below $4 million per unit, or quoted rack prices fall for 2 consecutive quarters.
detail.mechanism: Each new rack carries more memory, more storage and more power delivery at a time when all three are scarce, so the price of the whole cabinet climbs faster than the chip count inside it.
detail.sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the higher price buys proportionally more work, since buyers judge cost per unit of output rather than cost per rack.
detail.statement: Buyers are being quoted about twice as much for the next generation of AI racks as for the current one, so the price of a unit of leading-edge capacity is rising sharply between generations.
detail.title: Each new rack generation lands at roughly twice the price of the last

falsifiableTrigger: B200 rpoBacklog falls below 2 million units for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Buyers keep ordering more accelerators than the company can build, so unfilled orders pile up while sales still set records.
rationale: Record data-center sales of $75.2 billion (up 92 percent) with next-quarter guidance of $91 billion, an order book of about 3.6 million units for the current part, and purchase orders in hand from almost all major customers ahead of the new rack ramp all point the same way. Demand keeps arriving faster than the company can build.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to a cut in the big cloud buyers' capital spending plans, which would drain the order book before sales fall.

falsifiableTrigger: HBM leadTimes ease to available-on-demand and CoWoS lead times fall below 26 weeks before the end of 2027.
mechanism: Stacked memory and advanced packaging each run out before chip supply does, so whichever is scarcer sets the ceiling on how many systems can ship.
rationale: Packaging waits stay at 52 to 78 weeks with lines booked into 2027, and memory suppliers say they can cover only 60 to 70 percent of what the leading vendor asked for the next generation while one maker says it can supply about half of total demand. One report still puts the packaging shortfall near 20 percent for 2026.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to how fast new packaging lines and memory fabs come online in the next 4 quarters.

falsifiableTrigger: AMD accelerator market-share-pct fails to rise above 7% through 2027.
mechanism: A second vendor with a working rack and named anchor customers gives buyers an alternative, but its share only moves once volume production starts.
rationale: AMD's data-center revenue more than doubled to $6.7 billion and its rack system is in production with Anthropic, OpenAI, Meta, Microsoft and Oracle named, yet one account still puts NVIDIA near 90 percent and AMD at 5 to 7 percent, and another puts AMD's real volume ramp at the second quarter of 2027. The picture is unchanged: credible, but not yet a share shift.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the volume ramp holds its 2027 date or slips another 2 quarters.

falsifiableTrigger: ASIC market-share-pct growth falls back below GPU growth for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Every in-house chip a large buyer puts into production is compute it no longer buys from the merchant vendors.
rationale: Custom chips are forecast to grow 44.6 percent against 16.1 percent for merchant parts and to reach 27.8 percent of AI servers in 2026, Google added a second design partner under an agreement implying roughly $120 billion, Microsoft is negotiating capacity for upward of 300,000 in-house parts for 2027, OpenAI unveiled its own inference chip, and Meta's four in-house parts enter production in September.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the in-house parts actually reach volume production on their stated dates rather than staying on slides.

falsifiableTrigger: gpuSpotPrice for a current-generation part drops more than 20% within a quarter.
mechanism: Rental capacity stays scarce enough that providers hold their published hourly rates, while the second-hand card market clears at softer prices.
rationale: Published rental rates hold across providers: prior-generation cards at $3.29 to $4.29 an hour, the current generation flat at $6.69, and a mid-tier part at $3.99 to $4.50. Used card asking prices of roughly $21,000 to $28,000 sit below the $25,000 to $40,000 range of the prior two years.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to new rental capacity landing faster than rental demand grows.

falsifiableTrigger: exportControlExposure eases so China DC revenue recovers above prior levels within 2 quarters.
mechanism: Rules on both sides of the Pacific keep restricted parts from reaching Chinese buyers, so a large block of willing demand never turns into revenue.
rationale: China data-center compute revenue is gone, licensed shipments are described as trivial despite about $10 billion of approved licences, the authorised Asian buyer list was more than halved, Chinese regulators told approved buyers to keep the hardware in Hong Kong, and the second vendor still carries export-related inventory charges and licence requirements.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to a policy change in either capital rather than to anything the vendors do.

falsifiableTrigger: Vendor-financed GPU commitments in rpoBacklog exceed 300,000 units within 2 quarters.
mechanism: The seller guarantees or funds part of what its customers buy, so some reported demand rests on the seller's own balance sheet rather than on independent buying power.
rationale: The pattern holds exactly as stated: the proposed customer guarantee was cut from $250 billion to under $120 billion, the site guarantee is capped at $105 billion and pays only if the tenant defaults, financing platforms with six large investors aim to raise over $500 billion of outside money, and the backstop programme still covers about 210,000 chips at smaller clouds.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the outside financing platforms convert from memorandums into funded deals.

falsifiableTrigger: customerConcentration for the top three direct customers falls below prior shares next fiscal year.
mechanism: A handful of buyers account for most of the sales, so one of them slowing down or switching to its own chips removes a large slice of revenue at once.
rationale: Three direct customers were 21, 17 and 16 percent of revenue in the latest quarter, up from 12, 11 and 11 percent two years earlier, and new commitments deepen it further: one rocket company expects a very significant share of 2027 output, and the largest guaranteed site rests on a single unprofitable tenant under a 20-year lease.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the sovereign, enterprise and rental buyers grow fast enough to dilute the top three.

falsifiableTrigger: NVIDIA DC Ethernet switch market-share-pct slips from #1 within 2 quarters.
mechanism: Selling the switching and the accelerators as one system makes it costly for a buyer to swap out just the chips.
rationale: The vendor took the top revenue spot in data-center Ethernet switching, its new switch generation names CoreWeave, Microsoft, Nebius, SpaceXAI and Tesla as first customers, and a new multi-year deal with a trading firm ships racks and the vendor's own switching together. Still no finding compares networking growth against compute growth, so the sharper claim stays unsupported.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to open switching standards gaining ground inside large clusters.

falsifiableTrigger: Cost-per-token gains stall so tokenEconomics improves less than one generation cycle.
mechanism: When serving a model gets cheaper, uses that were not worth paying for become worth paying for, so total compute bought goes up rather than down.
rationale: The new generation is cited at ten times lower cost per token than the prior one and a tenth the cost per million tokens of the generation before, open-model serving costs have fallen 30 to 50 percent a year, one telecoms buyer now burns about a trillion tokens a month, and one large owner expects about 90 percent of its fleet to serve inference.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to purpose-built inference silicon capturing the cheap-serving work instead.

falsifiableTrigger: Prepaid HBM commitments in rpoBacklog shrink or deposits are refunded within a quarter.
mechanism: Customers who have already paid cash they cannot get back have every reason to take the parts and build the systems around them.
rationale: One memory maker has 16 non-cancellable five-year take-or-pay agreements backed by more than $22 billion of cash and related commitments including nearly $18 billion of deposits, and reconfirmed that $22 billion figure in August; all three makers have 2026 output pre-allocated under non-cancellable contracts.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to any renegotiation or refund of those deposits, which would signal buyers backing away.

falsifiableTrigger: exportControlExposure changes lift the sub-50% China cap or clear Blackwell within 2 quarters.
mechanism: Both governments place conditions on the same shipments, so licences exist on paper while almost no hardware actually crosses the border.
rationale: The rule stays case-by-case with a sub-50 percent cap and a 25 percent tariff, shipments are still described as trivial against orders of more than two million parts, licences granted since February have generated no revenue, and Chinese regulators now tell approved buyers to keep the hardware in Hong Kong. Nothing in the statement needs changing.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to Beijing relaxing its own restriction, since Washington has already opened its side partway.

falsifiableTrigger: Memory hbmSupplyCapex expansion pulls DRAM/NVMe prices down within 2 quarters.
mechanism: Memory and flash are a rising share of what a server costs, so their price increases either land in the builder's margin or get passed to the buyer.
rationale: Component waits of 32 to 40 weeks and prices up about 90 percent since late 2025 still stand, contract prices are up roughly 50 percent this year with more expected, the leading vendor is raising system prices by more than 15 percent from early next year, and the largest contract builder still reports high memory prices have not slowed customer spending.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether buyers keep paying the higher prices without cutting order volumes.

falsifiableTrigger: releaseCadence slips push a major vendor's 2H-2026 ramp into 2027.
mechanism: The rival platforms reach production months apart, so extra supply arrives in steps instead of all at once.
rationale: The staged picture holds: the leading vendor's new rack reached full production in July with shipments underway, the second vendor's rack reached production with third-quarter shipment start but one account still puts its real volume at the second quarter of 2027, and one hyperscaler's in-house parts enter production in September.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to manufacturing delays at the second vendor, which decides whether the wave is one step or two.

falsifiableTrigger: AMD customerConcentration eases as its buyer base broadens over the next 2 quarters.
mechanism: A handful of very large commitments carry nearly all the growth, so one of them shrinking or slipping swings the whole result.
rationale: The quarterly filing now names two customers each intending to deploy up to 6 gigawatts under multi-year agreements, with a third at up to 2 gigawatts and a fourth expansion in July, and the risk factors repeat that a small number of customers will keep accounting for a substantial part of revenue.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether smaller and sovereign buyers place orders large enough to spread the base.

falsifiableTrigger: Crescent Island releaseCadence slips its customer sampling past the 2H 2026 quarter.
mechanism: Using ordinary memory instead of the stacked kind lets a chip skip the two queues that limit everyone else.
rationale: The part was detailed again at a chip conference in August and remains guided to customer sampling in the second half of 2026 using standard low-power memory of up to 480 gigabytes instead of stacked memory, exactly as before. Still no customer, volume or revenue figure.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the lower memory bandwidth is good enough for real serving work.

falsifiableTrigger: TSMC grossMargin declines for 2 consecutive quarters as capacity loosens.
mechanism: Demand from several kinds of AI chip at once fills the same factories, and full factories let the maker charge more.
rationale: Gross margin reached 67.7 percent, up 9.1 points year on year, with revenue up 36 percent and full-year growth guidance raised from over 30 percent to above 40 percent; July revenue was up 44.7 percent year on year and capital spending was raised to $60 to $64 billion. The company says the demand-supply gap stays very big through 2029 to 2030.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to rival packaging and foundry capacity absorbing part of the overflow.

falsifiableTrigger: A hyperscalerCapexRevision cuts 2026 or 2027 AI capex guidance within 2 quarters.
mechanism: Spending is rising much faster than the revenue it is meant to produce, so a disappointing return would force buyers to cut orders.
rationale: One bank projects about $4.1 trillion of spending over 2026 to 2028, roughly triple the prior six years, one buyer posted its first ever negative free cash flow of $5.9 billion and its shares fell about 6 percent on the day, analysts warned the 67 percent jump in spending may be unsustainable, and large cloud server buying is forecast to slow from 11.6 percent to 1.7 percent growth in the third quarter.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether AI revenue at the buyers grows fast enough to justify the next budget round.

falsifiableTrigger: NVIDIA grossMargin guidance drops below 70% in a coming quarter.
mechanism: Buyers pay premium prices even as new products ramp, so the profit per unit stays far above what rivals earn.
rationale: Gross margin was 75.0 percent with the next quarter guided to the same level, against 54 to 56 percent at the second vendor and about 40 to 42 percent at the third. Nothing changed this cycle.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to memory and packaging cost increases that the vendor cannot pass on.

falsifiableTrigger: Top-buyer customerConcentration in CoWoS output falls below 85% within a year.
mechanism: So few buyers hold the packaging slots that if one walks away there is no queue of others able to take the space.
rationale: Two independent counts still put the top three buyers above 85 percent of advanced-packaging output with the largest at roughly 60 percent, and a third report says that one buyer has reserved 800,000 to 850,000 wafers of 2026 capacity, more than half the year's total. Capacity is pre-booked above 85 percent for both 2026 and 2027.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to smaller custom-chip programmes booking capacity and broadening the customer list.

falsifiableTrigger: Aggregate rpoBacklog duration shortens as new commitments turn shorter-dated over 2 quarters.
mechanism: Buyers who fear being short of capacity sign longer contracts, so the average commitment stretches further into the future each cycle.
rationale: One cloud backlog rose more than $50 billion in a quarter to $514 billion with just over half converting within 24 months, one purchase commitment runs to 2032, a new campus is committed under a 20-year lease phasing online from 2028, a mid-size provider signed $2.8 billion of multi-year contracts, and a wafer supply deal now runs ten years.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to any easing of scarcity, which would remove the reason to book years ahead.

falsifiableTrigger: A leading model provider reports revenue (apiArr) growth stalling quarter over quarter while compute commitments keep growing.
mechanism: Real and fast-growing sales at the model providers are what turns their compute commitments into payments the suppliers can count on.
rationale: One model provider reached more than $30 billion of annual recurring revenue, up from $1 billion fifteen months earlier, and one compute owner reported AI revenue of $2.6 billion, up 247 percent year on year. Against that, the largest single tranche of guaranteed demand rests on a provider that is still unprofitable and seeking over $500 billion of outside capital.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to the gap between revenue growth and cash burn at the largest unprofitable provider.

falsifiableTrigger: Chinese domestic accelerator designWins for frontier training stall over the next 2 quarters.
mechanism: Chinese buyers cut off from imported parts fund home-grown suppliers, whose revenue and capability rise even though their volume stays small.
rationale: Two findings confirm a 1.6-trillion-parameter model pretrained on more than 50,000 domestic parts across over 35 trillion tokens, and two Chinese suppliers now guide to first-half revenue growth of 135 to 149 percent and 56 to 70 percent, with one holding gross margin near 57 percent and cutting its net loss by 96 percent. Volume still falls far short of the more than two million restricted parts ordered.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to domestic memory supply, which is the stated limit on scaling those systems.

falsifiableTrigger: A neocloud's marginalBuyerFinancing debt load or net loss narrows for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: These buyers grow by adding rented-out hardware bought with borrowed money, so revenue and interest costs rise together.
rationale: The one direct data point this cycle repeats the pattern: revenue up about 168 percent from $1.9 billion to $5.1 billion while net loss widened from $937 million to $1.2 billion.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to borrowing costs and to how quickly new hardware fills with paying customers.

falsifiableTrigger: A top hyperscaler cuts its 2027 gigawatt power target below its 2026 level.
mechanism: Sites can only power so many racks, so available electricity, not chip supply, sets how much gets installed.
rationale: Power shortages are now cited as a reason the leading vendor is lowering the power rating of its next flagship and cutting its memory, buyers state targets in gigawatts rather than units, one buyer went from 400 megawatts to 1.4 gigawatts in a year and another plans 7 gigawatts in 2026, and one grid queue holds about 474 gigawatts of requests against about 1.2 gigawatts of forecast additions.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to how fast new generation and grid connections are approved.

falsifiableTrigger: Broadcom-plus-Marvell market-share-pct of custom ASIC co-design falls below 90% within a year.
mechanism: If only two firms can co-design custom chips, the alternative to merchant parts carries the same narrow-supplier risk it was meant to avoid.
rationale: The two firms are still put at about 95 percent of custom design work, but a third designer raised its share target to 15 to 20 percent, expects more than $2 billion of revenue in 2026 with a first chip in production in the fourth quarter, and one buyer's new award may simply move work between the two incumbents rather than add new spend. One analyst calls the third designer's target very high.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the third designer's first chip actually reaches production on its stated date.

falsifiableTrigger: Wistron odmMonthlyAiRevenue falls year-over-year for 2 consecutive months.
mechanism: Contract builders only book revenue when finished systems leave the factory, so their monthly sales are the closest thing to a shipment count.
rationale: One contract builder posted July revenue of NT$946.51 billion, up 54 percent year on year and its first month above NT$900 billion, another posted record June revenue up 53.9 percent, the leading foundry posted July revenue up 44.7 percent, and one builder says AI servers are now 95 percent of its server business.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to component shortages that stall assembly even when orders are firm.

falsifiableTrigger: A neocloud's marginalBuyerFinancing debt-to-equity rises above 6:1 within 2 quarters.
mechanism: Hardware bought with borrowed money must earn its interest every month, leaving little room if rental prices or usage fall.
rationale: One operator carries $18.81 billion of debt against $3.5 billion of equity, a 5.4 to 1 ratio, with total debt up 16.1 percent in a quarter. Another borrowed $917 million for chips and is now in talks for a pre-listing round of up to $3 billion, which would thicken its equity cushion if it closes.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether equity raises land before the next round of hardware borrowing.

falsifiableTrigger: Co-packaged optics adoption stalls below 5% of AI optical modules through 2027.
mechanism: Putting the optics inside the switch package cuts power and parts count but ties cluster wiring to one fast-moving supply chain.
rationale: A shipping switch platform now claims four times fewer lasers, five times lower power and up to 409.6 terabits per second, order books for these switches are reported full through 2027 with supply tight into 2028, adoption is forecast to rise from about 0.5 percent of AI optical modules in 2026 to about 35 percent by 2030, and one vendor is funding a tenfold expansion of domestic optical manufacturing.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to optical engine yield and packaging capacity, both named as the limits on expansion.

falsifiableTrigger: A named US fab or packaging project slips its build milestone past 2027.
mechanism: New domestic plants add a second place where the same parts can be made, which lowers the risk of relying on one region.
rationale: Commitments keep landing: up to $500 billion of domestic AI hardware production with named partners, three new optical plants and a tenfold capacity increase, $250 billion of domestic memory investment targeting 40 percent of output with $500 million into a domestic wafer plant, an added $100 billion foundry investment, and a $15 billion share sale to fund capacity.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to construction and staffing timelines, since none of this capacity produces yet.

falsifiableTrigger: Google Cloud or CoreWeave rpoBacklog fails to grow sequentially for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Contracts are signed faster than capacity can be built, so the order book grows even when quarterly sales are capped by what is installed.
rationale: One cloud backlog rose more than $50 billion in a quarter to $514 billion while its revenue grew 82 percent, a specialist provider's contracted backlog reached $99.4 billion from $66.8 billion a month earlier, a mid-size provider added $2.8 billion of multi-year contracts, and a new multi-year trading-firm expansion was signed in August.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether booked contracts actually convert to revenue on schedule.

falsifiableTrigger: A top hyperscaler returns to positive free cash flow while holding 2027 capex guidance for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Spending has outgrown the cash these businesses generate, so the shortfall is covered by new debt and new shares.
rationale: One buyer funded its quarter with $49.6 billion of share issuance and $20.3 billion of notes and reported its first ever negative free cash flow of $5.9 billion; the four largest are on track for about $725 billion of 2026 spending, up about 77 percent, and one specialist roughly doubled its own budget to $31 to $35 billion. Investors marked the shares down about 6 percent on the day.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to borrowing costs and to how patient shareholders stay with negative cash flow.

falsifiableTrigger: A new accelerator generation delivers less than a 1.5x perfPerWatt gain over its predecessor.
mechanism: If each new rack does more work per megawatt, a buyer with a fixed power budget can still add capacity every year.
rationale: Vendor claims of ten times the work per megawatt over the prior rack generation repeat this cycle, a wafer-scale rival claims ten times the throughput per watt over its own prior system, and a memory maker claims 2.5 times better performance per watt. An independent measure of the current generation over its predecessor is a more modest 1.6 times, so the size of the gain is still vendor-stated.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to independent measurements, since almost every figure here comes from the seller.

falsifiableTrigger: HBM leadTimes shorten and suppliers report unsold capacity for 2 consecutive quarters before end-2027.
mechanism: Every accelerator needs its stack of memory, so when memory runs short the number of finished accelerators falls with it.
rationale: Suppliers can meet only 60 to 70 percent of what the leading vendor asked for its next generation, one maker says it can supply about half of customer demand and calls memory the number one constraint its largest customers face with no line of sight to balance, another says customers want about 50 percent more than it can commit, and the shortage has already forced memory cuts in the next flagship.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to how much standard memory capacity makers convert to the stacked kind over the next 4 quarters.

falsifiableTrigger: Memory supplier grossMargin falls for 2 consecutive quarters as contract prices flatten.
mechanism: Scarce memory lets its makers set the price, so more of the money a buyer pays for a server ends up with them instead of the assembler.
rationale: One maker's data-center segment posted $11.5 billion of revenue, up 103 percent in a quarter, at an 87 percent gross margin; contract prices are up roughly 50 percent this year, another maker is seeking up to a 20 percent contract increase with quote validity cut to 72 hours, and all three have 2026 output locked in at high-teen to low-twenties percent increases.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to new memory fabs coming online and ending the shortage pricing.

falsifiableTrigger: No new sovereign or enterprise cluster above 10,000 GPUs is announced for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Governments and large companies now place orders big enough to sit beside the cloud giants in the same allocation queue.
rationale: A binding order for 9,000 systems within an $8 billion, one-gigawatt plan in India, a Japanese national project of 27,500 accelerators across 140 megawatts, a 2-gigawatt Korean cloud build, a pharmaceutical company deploying a second cluster, and a second vendor shipping a part aimed specifically at sovereign work all land in one cycle.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to public funding decisions, which can be reversed faster than corporate budgets.

falsifiableTrigger: Intel data-center revenue growth falls below 10% year over year for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: A third supplier with improving factories and margins gives buyers another place to source processors, packaging and inference parts.
rationale: Data-center revenue reached $6.3 billion, up 59 percent, gross margin rose to 40.4 percent from 27.5 percent a year earlier, contract manufacturing revenue rose 31 percent to $5.8 billion with narrowing losses, the next quarter is guided above expectations, and a $15 billion share sale funds further capacity while its packaging backlog grows.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether its new packaging reaches high-volume production in 2027 as promised.

falsifiableTrigger: New vendor equity-for-compute deals in marginalBuyerFinancing stop appearing for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: When a seller owns part of its buyer, some of the money used to buy the chips came from the seller in the first place.
rationale: The second vendor committed up to $5 billion of equity in a model provider alongside a two-gigawatt deployment deal, the leading vendor invested an undisclosed amount in another model provider as part of a platform commitment, and it also holds a $5 billion stake in a rival chipmaker that is building processors for its own systems.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the funded customers can raise money independently.

falsifiableTrigger: Standard DRAM S10 spot prices fall for 2 consecutive months as suppliers restore non-AI capacity.
mechanism: Making the stacked memory that AI servers need consumes several times the factory space of ordinary memory, so ordinary memory gets scarce and dear.
rationale: A graphics vendor raised bundle prices about 10 percent citing tripled graphics memory spot prices, older standard memory spot prices reached $81.20, up 17.5 percent in a month and above the prior peak, makers are cutting older and embedded output to favour AI parts, consumer drives are losing allocation to enterprise contracts, and stacked memory displaces standard memory at three to one, worsening to four to one.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to new fabs opening, which is the only way both kinds of memory can be made at once.

falsifiableTrigger: No new multi-year accelerator-to-memory supply partnership is announced for 2 consecutive quarters through 2027.
mechanism: Buying memory capacity years ahead is the only way an accelerator maker can be sure it will have the parts to finish its own products.
rationale: The leading vendor signed a long-term partnership with a Korean maker to secure next-generation memory and jointly develop it, all three makers are developing a taller stack specifically for that vendor, a Korean cloud build pairs the vendor's platform with that maker's memory, and three hyperscalers have used their own cash to lock long-term supply.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether memory stays scarce enough to justify locking supply this far out.

falsifiableTrigger: The leading supplier's HBM market-share-pct falls below 50% within 4 quarters as rivals ship volume.
mechanism: One maker holding most of the supply would decide who can build AI servers, but a rival reaching the same production efficiency removes that single point of control.
rationale: The leader is still put at 56 to 58 percent of the market and about 62 percent of the next-generation supply, but the second maker's yield reached close to 80 percent, up from below 60 percent in February and about four months ahead of schedule, matching the leader's yield, and it aims to lift its share to about 38 percent by year end.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the second maker's improved yield converts into qualified volume at the large accelerator buyers.

falsifiableTrigger: No new diversion prosecution or whitelist reduction is reported for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Prosecutions and shorter approved-buyer lists raise the cost of physically moving restricted hardware, but renting it abroad moves the work instead of the chips and sidesteps that enforcement.
rationale: ADJUSTED: Prosecutions and shorter approved-buyer lists are closing the smuggling route into China, but renting banned hardware offshore remains an open channel that regulators have only just begun to investigate.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the new investigation into offshore rental produces enforceable rules.

falsifiableTrigger: CoWoS lead times stay above 52 weeks through the end of 2027 while the supply gap fails to narrow below 15%.
mechanism: New packaging lines can be added within a year or two while new memory fabs take longer, so the two shortages ease on different clocks.
rationale: The disagreement in the statement persists: one report puts the packaging shortfall at about 10 percent in mid-2026, narrowed from about 20 percent, while another still puts it at about 20 percent for 2026, and lines are described as booked through 2027. Memory shows no easing, with one maker saying it can supply about half of demand and no line of sight to balance.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to which of the two conflicting shortfall estimates the next quarter's data supports.

falsifiableTrigger: NAND contract prices for server drives fall for 2 consecutive quarters while Rubin deployments keep growing.
mechanism: Adding a large drive pool to every new rack creates a step change in flash demand that the existing supply base was not sized for.
rationale: The new generation's storage tier is still expected to pull flash demand from about 35 million terabytes this year to more than 100 million next year, with each unit carrying 576 drives for 9,600 terabytes, enterprise contracts are getting priority over retail, and rack component costs are inflating 2 to 3 percent a week on memory and drive scarcity.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to how many of the new racks actually ship with the full storage tier.

falsifiableTrigger: Every major cloud provider publishes list rates for its newest rack-scale systems for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: When the newest systems are scarce, some providers move them off the public price page and sell them through negotiation instead.
rationale: Four separate captures across August show one provider listing nothing newer than the prior flagship, with no mid-tier or current rack parts and no spot instances, while another publishes an hourly rate for a current rack system and a third publishes a mid-tier rate. Longer terms at the first provider are quoted only as custom pricing.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to supply loosening, which would bring the newest parts back onto public price pages.

falsifiableTrigger: NVIDIA accelerator market-share-pct stabilises or rises for 2 consecutive quarters while rival shipments grow.
mechanism: The overall market is growing faster than the leader can supply, so rivals absorb the growth while the leader's own sales still rise.
rationale: One projection has the share falling from a 2024 peak of 87 percent to 75 percent in 2026 and another puts it near 70 percent, but two other sources this cycle put it at 70 to 80 percent and as much as 90 percent, so the level is disputed even as record revenue of $75.2 billion is not.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to how each source counts custom in-house chips, which drives most of the disagreement.

falsifiableTrigger: A major buyer returns to purchasing loose accelerators rather than vendor racks for a flagship cluster within 2 quarters.
mechanism: Vendors now sell whole cabinets with their own wiring and software, so buyers compare finished systems rather than individual chips.
rationale: The second vendor's 72-accelerator rack reached full production with named adopters and is pitched directly against the leader's 72-accelerator rack, the leader's rack reached full production in July with fourteen server partners, a wafer-scale rival now sells a rack-scale system too, and buyers are quoted rack prices of $2.8 to $3.4 million and $5 to $7 million rather than chip prices.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to open rack standards letting buyers mix parts from different vendors again.

falsifiableTrigger: ERCOT data-center additions exceed 5 GW over the next 4 quarters as the pause lifts.
mechanism: A site cannot open until it is connected to the grid, so the connection queue rather than chip supply sets the opening date.
rationale: The Texas connection queue still holds roughly 474 gigawatts with about 90 percent of requests from data centres against only about 1.2 gigawatts of forecast additions, and lost revenue from the pause is put at up to $8 billion by early 2027. One new campus comes with a cited $4.2 billion regional grid investment. Still no finding reports transformer lead times.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to state-level policy on new connections, which is what created the pause.

falsifiableTrigger: Median newest-generation gpuSpotPrice falls while prior-generation rates rise for 2 consecutive months.
mechanism: Scarcity of the newest hardware should lift its rental price relative to older parts, but that only shows up if providers publish rates for it.
rationale: Across six captures this month the current-generation rate sits flat at $6.69 while prior-generation quotes range from $3.29 to $4.29 and a mid-tier part is quoted at $3.99 to $4.50, so the premium is not visibly widening. The truly newest rack systems are largely absent from public price pages, so there is no published rate in which a premium could show up.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to providers publishing rates for the newest rack systems at all.

falsifiableTrigger: Alternative packaging upstreamLeadTimes rise above 52 weeks, or no accelerator maker places advanced-packaging volume outside TSMC for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: When one packager's queue runs past a year, buyers place work wherever the wait is shorter.
rationale: One hyperscaler has committed to order more than 3 million units of a rival's bridge packaging for delivery in 2028, that rival reports very high demand and a growing backlog targeting high-volume production in 2027, alternative routes are quoted at 26 to 39 weeks against 52 to 78 at the leader, two Asian packaging firms are adding capacity, and the leader is now outsourcing a front-end step to outside packagers.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the alternative routes reach the yield and bandwidth that high-end accelerators need.

falsifiableTrigger: AMD's share of CoWoS output in pkgCapacityOrderSpread rises above 15% within 2 quarters.
mechanism: One fixed pool of packaging slots must cover two product lines, so building more of one means building fewer of the other.
rationale: The second vendor is still put at about 11 percent of advanced-packaging output, roughly 105,000 wafers, against about 60 percent for the leader, and must split that allocation between its server processors and its accelerators, so each processor packaged displaces an accelerator.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the vendor secures capacity at an alternative packager and relieves the split.

falsifiableTrigger: The next flagship ships with its originally planned 288GB memory configuration within 2 quarters of launch.
mechanism: Putting less memory on each accelerator lets a fixed pool of memory cover more accelerators, so the product shrinks to keep the unit count up.
rationale: Five independent reports now describe the next top-end part being cut to 192 gigabytes from a previewed one terabyte and below the current 288, driven by memory supply and power limits, with test configurations at 192 and 256 gigabytes and some samples reverting to the prior memory generation. Memory makers are simultaneously shifting to shorter stacks and cutting taller-stack output.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether cutting memory hurts performance enough to lose sales, since one bank says performance drops sharply below 500 gigabytes.

falsifiableTrigger: The first Korean AI factory misses its 2027 target or the partnership is not converted from letters of intent into signed contracts within 2 quarters.
mechanism: Tying construction, memory supply and cloud capacity into one national partnership concentrates a second cluster of the buildout in Korea.
rationale: The partnership is described by the vendor itself as a more than $500 billion initiative covering data-centre construction, next-generation memory supply and cloud capacity across the region, with the first plant targeted for 2027 and a 2-gigawatt cloud build named; one memory maker approved a $4.83 billion packaging plant, and Korean chip exports nearly tripled to $26 billion in twenty days.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to the letters of intent turning into signed contracts, since that is how the deal was formalised.

falsifiableTrigger: No accelerator or system vendor announces a shipping product using the high-bandwidth flash specification within 4 quarters.
mechanism: A fast flash tier holds data that would otherwise need scarce stacked memory, so it adds capacity without competing for the same supply.
rationale: The first specification is now published through an open industry body, covering up to 512 gigabytes in eight and sixteen-high stacks and three speed grades from about 0.4 to 3.0 terabytes a second, with two more companies joining the consortium, and the newest rack generation already builds a large drive pool with 576 drives per unit.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether an accelerator vendor actually designs a shipping product around the new specification.

falsifiableTrigger: AMD software releases deliver less than a 1.5x measured inference gain over the prior release for 2 consecutive releases.
mechanism: Software tuning lifts what today's hardware can do without waiting for the next hardware generation to ship.
rationale: A tuned kernel improved end-to-end throughput 2.10 times and cut first-token latency 3.71 times on the current part, and the new software release claims 3.3 times inference and 2.4 times training gains over the prior one, while one account still puts mass production and first production output at the second quarter of 2027.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to independent benchmarks, since these gains are all vendor-reported.

falsifiableTrigger: SpaceX nameplate compute fails to exceed 2 gigawatts by the end of 2026 or its quarterly AI capex falls below $10 billion for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: A buyer spending nearly $16 billion a quarter on compute takes a slice of output large enough to change who else can get parts.
rationale: Nameplate compute reached 1.4 gigawatts from 1.0 a quarter earlier and 400 megawatts a year earlier, with guidance above 2 gigawatts by year end and about 10 gigawatts by end-2027; quarterly capital spending was about $18.4 billion of which roughly $15.8 billion went to AI compute, and it says it will build exclusively on one vendor and expects a very significant share of that vendor's 2027 output.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether its AI revenue, at $2.6 billion a quarter, keeps funding spending of that size.

falsifiableTrigger: Intel's share of 2.5D packaging capacity fails to rise above 20% within 4 quarters, or its bridge packaging misses 2027 mass production.
mechanism: A route around one shortage runs into its own single supplier and its own yield problem, so relief is smaller than the headline orders suggest.
rationale: The sole supplier of the silicon capacitors for this route is still described as fully booked, the technique is still called a better fit for custom chips than for high-bandwidth accelerators, substrate mass production is expected only in 2027 at an initial 50 percent yield, and the vendor holds about 13.7 percent of global capacity for this class of packaging against about 70 percent for the leader.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to a second silicon capacitor supplier appearing, which would remove the named choke point.

falsifiableTrigger: MediaTek market-share-pct of AI accelerators fails to exceed 5% within 4 quarters, or its first chip misses Q4 2026 production.
mechanism: A third firm able to co-design custom chips gives buyers another option and reduces the pricing power of the two incumbents.
rationale: The share target was raised to 15 to 20 percent from 10 to 15 percent, the first chip still enters production in the fourth quarter of 2026 with more than $2 billion of 2026 revenue expected and a second part in 2028, and a $5 billion financing was board approved. One analyst notes its 2024 share was under 1 percent and calls the target very high, so entry is confirmed but scale is not.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the first chip reaches production in the fourth quarter as scheduled.

falsifiableTrigger: Used prior-generation server prices fall more than 40% within 2 quarters, or published prior-generation rental rates drop below $2.00 per GPU-hour.
mechanism: Older systems cost a fraction of new ones to buy while still renting for more than half the price, so they stay economic to run.
rationale: A new top-end server is still about $500,000 against roughly $150,000 to $180,000 for a used prior-generation one, used cards list at about $21,000 to $28,000, and prior-generation rental rates run $3.29 to $4.29 an hour against $6.69 for the current generation, so the older hardware still earns its keep.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to power costs, which hit older and less efficient hardware hardest.

falsifiableTrigger: Wafer suppliers report spare 300mm capacity or falling wafer prices for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: New memory fabs and AI chips all draw on the same blank silicon, so the squeeze moves one step further back up the chain.
rationale: One maker says its 300mm, 200mm and 150mm lines are effectively at maximum use with constraints already appearing on some advanced 300mm products, spot prices are rising with more increases expected, buyers are lengthening contracts from about three years to five to eight, and one ten-year supply deal starting in 2027 comes with $500 million of upfront support from the customer.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to how many new memory fabs come online in 2027, since they compete for the same wafers.

falsifiableTrigger: AMD's reported remaining performance obligations stay below $1 billion for 2 consecutive quarters while new gigawatt commitments keep being announced.
mechanism: Announced gigawatt intentions are not firm orders until they appear as contracted obligations in the accounts.
rationale: The quarterly filing still reports only $222 million of obligations on contracts longer than a year, of which $144 million falls within twelve months, while the same filing names two customers each intending up to 6 gigawatts under agreements whose incentives are tied to purchase milestones and share-price targets. The company reports strong pull but disclosed no dollar backlog.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to the next quarterly filing, which is where any conversion to firm orders would first show.

falsifiableTrigger: No hardwired inference product reaches customer shipment within 4 quarters, or inference workloads stay on general accelerators for 2 consecutive quarters after launch.
mechanism: Burning a finished model into fixed silicon makes serving it much cheaper, which takes the highest-volume work away from general-purpose parts.
rationale: The second vendor signed a definitive agreement to buy a startup that hardwires model weights into silicon and will pair it with its own accelerators and racks, describing purpose-built inference parts as able to erode merchant demand in cost-sensitive serving; the leading vendor is in early talks with a Korean inference-chip startup, and one model provider placed about $250 million of initial orders with another such startup.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to how often models change, since fixed silicon only pays off for models that stay put.

falsifiableTrigger: Non-cloud owners stop signing new rental or lease agreements for 2 consecutive quarters, or rented share of their fleets falls below 50%.
mechanism: Owners who bought more compute than they need for themselves rent the surplus out, creating a supply layer between the chip vendors and end users.
rationale: One owner says roughly 90 percent of its compute will serve inference or be rented to others with only about 10 percent used for its own training, and it holds multibillion-dollar capacity leases with two named counterparties; a model provider has separately signed capacity agreements with a bitcoin miner and an infrastructure holder.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to their own workloads growing enough to absorb the capacity they are currently renting out.

falsifiableTrigger: No compute-financing platform closes a funded transaction within 2 quarters, or the memorandums lapse without binding agreements.
mechanism: Bringing asset managers and banks into the buildout moves funding off the chip vendors' and clouds' own balance sheets, but only once the money is actually committed.
rationale: Six large investors have signed up to compute-financing platforms meant to mobilise over $500 billion, but the agreements are described as non-binding memorandums with no funded transaction reported, and the largest tenant is separately seeking over $500 billion of third-party capital. One smaller operator is in talks for a pre-listing round of up to $3 billion.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to the first funded deal, since everything so far is non-binding.

falsifiableTrigger: Samsung foundry utilisation loosens or it reverses the 10-15% price increase within 2 quarters.
mechanism: When the largest chipmaker is full, overflow work fills the second one too, and a full factory can raise its prices.
rationale: The maker raised advanced contract prices 10 to 15 percent on new orders in July, its main advanced line runs at full capacity making logic chips for outside customers and base parts for its own memory, and it says it cannot meet all orders. It expects AI and high-performance work to exceed 30 percent of its contract revenue this year, up from 15 to 20 percent in late 2025, though it still holds only about 7 percent of global contract chipmaking. All four points come from one publisher.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to corroboration from a second publisher, since every figure here comes from one.

falsifiableTrigger: Cerebras fails to report CS-4 customer shipments within 2 quarters, or no named customer expands beyond its initial system within 4 quarters.
mechanism: A whole-wafer machine that slots alongside existing racks competes for the fastest serving work without asking buyers to replace what they have.
rationale: The rack-scale system built from three whole-wafer processors launched with 750 petaflops and first shipments this quarter, claims of more than 4,400 tokens a second per user and up to 30 times the per-user speed of accelerator systems, named customers including a model provider, a sovereign group, a university and one large cloud, and native support for pairing with a rival's racks rather than replacing them.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether named customers order a second system, since all performance figures are vendor-stated.

falsifiableTrigger: No new vendor-guaranteed or vendor-funded data-centre site above 1 gigawatt is announced for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: If no powered site exists, the hardware cannot be installed, so the vendor pays to make sure sites exist for its own products to fill.
rationale: The leading vendor will invest up to $3 billion for about 20 percent of a power-infrastructure developer, is in advanced talks to put several hundred million into a developer of powered land with more than 7 gigawatts sold, guaranteed leases for about 4.25 gigawatts capped at $105 billion, and is investing $1.5 billion in the site's builder alongside a cited $4.2 billion regional grid investment.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to how much of the vendor's balance sheet these guarantees tie up if a tenant fails.

falsifiableTrigger: A hyperscaler raises AI capex guidance and its shares rise on the day for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Investors now price a bigger AI budget as money leaving the payer and arriving at the supplier, so the two move in opposite directions on the day.
rationale: One buyer's shares fell about 6 percent on the day it raised its budget, with other AI-spending names falling alongside; a chipmaker's shares fell more than 8 percent specifically because its own capital spending overshot; and a memory supplier's shares rose 4.86 percent in one session attributed to that same raised budget.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to evidence that the spending is producing returns, which would flip the reaction.

falsifiableTrigger: MLCC lead times for AI server grades fall below 20 weeks for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: A server cannot ship without every part on its list, so a shortage of a cheap component stalls an expensive machine.
rationale: Waits for the high-specification capacitors used in AI servers are still stretching toward 40 weeks, and tight supply of memory, processors and circuit substrate is named as the main brake on server shipment growth through the third quarter.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to component makers adding capacity, which is faster for these parts than for chips.

falsifiableTrigger: No new trading-firm compute commitment above $1 billion is announced for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Trading firms need large bursts of compute without owning data centres, so they rent at a scale that shows up as a distinct buyer group.
rationale: A multiyear, multibillion-dollar expansion with one trading firm will deliver current and prior-generation systems, and it stacks on another firm's $6 billion capacity commitment plus a separate expansion by a third, so the provider now describes trading firms as a meaningful customer segment.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to trading profits, which fund this spending and can turn quickly.

falsifiableTrigger: The next flagship launches in a single memory configuration, or the number of assessed memory specifications falls below 2 within 2 quarters.
mechanism: When parts and power are both rationed, the vendor builds several versions of one product so each site can take whatever it can actually supply.
rationale: The vendor has been assessing four alternative memory specifications for its next flagship since the third quarter, is testing 192 and 256 gigabyte versions with some samples using the prior memory generation, and reported power variants span about 1,200, 1,800 and 2,600 to 2,800 watts. Memory makers are simultaneously shifting the main configuration to shorter stacks.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to memory supply loosening, which would let the vendor settle on one configuration.

falsifiableTrigger: A major vendor's next flagship arrives more than 24 months after its predecessor, or a named 2027 or 2028 roadmap part slips by 2 quarters.
mechanism: Vendors shorten the gap between generations to stay ahead of rivals, so buyers face a new top-end system roughly every year.
rationale: The leading vendor's new platform reached full production in July with shipments underway, described as compressing the usual 24 to 30 month cycle into 18 months, and the second vendor laid out yearly steps with new accelerators in 2027 and 2028. Against that, one account puts the second vendor's real volume ramp at the second quarter of 2027, so the compressed cadence is clearer at the leader than across the field.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to manufacturing delays, which have already pushed one vendor's volume ramp out.

falsifiableTrigger: No model builder taped out a custom accelerator within 4 quarters, or the announced design effort is abandoned within 2 quarters.
mechanism: Model builders that know exactly what their own models need can design cheaper silicon for that one job instead of buying general-purpose parts.
rationale: One model provider unveiled its first custom inference chip built on a 3nm process with an outside design partner and six memory stacks per package, another hired the founder of a hyperscaler's custom chip programme to lead its own effort and is in early talks with a memory maker to build a 2nm part, and two Chinese labs are pursuing their own inference parts.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether these designs reach production, since one estimate puts viable in-house silicon more than two years out.

falsifiableTrigger: The announced system price increase above 15% is withdrawn or rack quotes fall for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Rather than absorb rising memory bills, the system vendor raises its own prices and moves the cost onto the buyer.
rationale: The leading vendor is reported to be raising AI system prices by more than 15 percent in many cases from early next year as contract memory prices climb about 50 percent cumulatively this year, and quoted rack prices have moved from $2.8 to $3.4 million for the current generation to $5 to $7 million for the next. A graphics vendor separately raised bundle prices about 10 percent for the same reason.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether buyers accept the higher prices or cut order volumes instead.

falsifiableTrigger: Mid-size cloud AI contract signings fall or capex drops below 20% of revenue for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Buyers who cannot get capacity from the largest clouds sign multi-year deals with smaller ones, which then spend heavily to build it.
rationale: One mid-size provider reported year-to-date multi-year contracts worth over $2.8 billion including one worth more than $600 million over four years, with cloud infrastructure revenue up 39 percent and capital spending at 32 percent of total company revenue. The pattern holds, but every figure comes from a single publisher.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to the largest clouds freeing up capacity, which would remove the reason to sign elsewhere.

falsifiableTrigger: Large US cloud server procurement growth returns above 5% quarter over quarter with accelerator-led servers taking a rising share for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Agent-style work leans more on ordinary processors and storage than on accelerators, so a shift toward it changes the mix of servers bought.
rationale: One report says agent-style adoption is shifting cloud deployments away from accelerator-led servers toward ordinary processors and storage, alongside a forecast slowdown in cloud server buying from 11.6 percent to 1.7 percent growth in the third quarter. The same publisher also names tight memory, processor and substrate supply as the primary brake, so the shift may be a supply effect rather than a change in what buyers want, and all three points come from one source.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to separating the workload shift from the parts shortage, which currently explains the same numbers.

falsifiableTrigger: Next-generation rack quotes settle below $4 million per unit, or quoted rack prices fall for 2 consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Each new rack packs more silicon, memory and power into the same cabinet, so the price of one unit of leading-edge capacity rises sharply between generations.
rationale: The one price comparison available puts current-generation racks at $2.8 to $3.4 million against pre-shipment inquiries of $5 to $7 million for the next generation, which is roughly double. It rests on a single source, and the same report ties part of the increase to a system price rise of more than 15 percent driven by memory costs.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to corroboration from a second publisher, since one set of pre-shipment quotes carries the whole claim.

detail.falsifiableTrigger: No named customer reports running two vendors' rack systems in one production cluster within 4 quarters.
detail.mechanism: Splitting a serving job across machines that are each good at a different part of it lets a buyer use whatever hardware it can actually get.
detail.sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the software to split work across vendors works well enough in production.
detail.statement: Buyers are beginning to run machines from competing vendors side by side inside a single cluster, with each vendor's system designed to hand work to the others.
detail.title: Clusters start mixing hardware from rival vendors

detail.falsifiableTrigger: No AI hardware supplier raises new equity or debt above $1 billion for capacity or customer financing for 2 consecutive quarters.
detail.mechanism: Building the factories and financing the customers costs more than these suppliers earn today, so the gap is filled with new shares and new debt.
detail.sensitivity: Most sensitive to how patient markets stay if the funded capacity fills more slowly than planned.
detail.statement: The companies selling AI hardware are themselves issuing shares and bonds to pay for the capacity they need, rather than funding it from what they earn.
detail.title: Chip suppliers now raise outside money to fund their own expansion

detail.falsifiableTrigger: The second design partner books no custom-silicon revenue from this buyer within 4 quarters, or the agreement lapses within 2 quarters.
detail.mechanism: A buyer that depends on one design partner for its own chips is exposed to that partner, so it hires a second one and plays them against each other.
detail.sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether this is genuinely new work or simply moved from the incumbent, which the reporting does not settle.
detail.statement: One of the biggest in-house chip programmes has added a second outside design partner alongside its incumbent, so even custom silicon now gets second-sourced.
detail.title: A large buyer adds a second designer for its own chips
